readPurposes.preparation: Reads that produce the input an owner prepares once and may transfer.
readPurposes.preservation: Reads that preserve unrelated or foreign content around an owner's write.
readPurposes.fresh-conflict-or-route-check: Reads that must observe live state under the lock or at the route boundary.
readPurposes.rollback-snapshot: Reads that capture a preimage so a failed closure can restore it.
readPurposes.integrity-validation: Reads that verify content against an expected digest or identity.
readPurposes.post-write-verification: Reads that verify what a publication actually wrote.
readPurposes.other: Reads whose purpose falls outside the named obligations; the note states it.

acquired-retirement.resource: Canonical acquired package directories under the acquired root, and their accepted lockfile entries, that no desired route reaches: sync's unreachable-acquisitions maintenance step (also planned, never applied, by check's convergence assessment) and the member retirement of a Pack disable (typed or root).
acquired-retirement.publication: Removal: under the workspace transition, recursive removal of each unshared, unreferenced canonical directory after a settlement protect snapshot, then removal of the accepted entries through the accepted-resolution writer; an already-settled entry is skipped.

reads.note: Planning reads the desired graph and every accepted lockfile row to decide which rows no desired route reaches, and checks each candidate canonical directory exists; a preview and check's convergence assessment run only this planning, once, and remove nothing.
Planning hashes an existing unshared canonical tree and refuses content that differs from the accepted tree integrity.
Planning finds native registrations that reference an MCP, Hook or Pack package's code; such packages are retained.
Under the transition, desired reachability and each accepted entry are re-read and must be unchanged.
Under the transition, native package references are observed again before removal; a new reference refuses.
Under the transition, the canonical tree integrity is recomputed immediately before removal.
The settlement protect observes and copies the canonical tree before it is removed.
Validation checks that each retired entry is gone from the lockfile and each removed canonical directory is absent.

acquired-retirement.existingSharing: The planned step carries the rows, canonical paths and planning verdicts it computed once; apply reuses them and rechecks only live state under the lock. Before prepared inputs were shared, each unreached row probed, hashed and scanned native package references for its canonical tree on its own, even when an earlier row of the same planning call bound that tree. Now unreached rows that bind one canonical tree share that tree's existence probe, integrity hash and native package reference scan within one planning call, and the retirement planning of a Pack disable hands the tree digests it verified to the disable.
acquired-retirement.preparedInputs: Each retirement planning call creates a memo, keyed by canonical path, of what it observed of each candidate tree: its existence, its integrity hash once an unshared row needs it, and its native package references once an MCP, Hook or Pack row needs them. Later unreached rows that bind the same tree consume that memo instead of probing, hashing or scanning again; each still validates its path, compares the digest with its own accepted tree integrity and keeps its own verified digest and copy of the references. The planned step carries the rows, canonical paths and planning verdicts, which apply consumes and the retirement artifact reports. A Pack disable also receives a lookup of the tree digests planning verified, by type and accepted row, and hands a digest to a kept member's retained-reference observation of the same root only when the disable is unblocked and its withdrawal description judged that root; sync and check's convergence assessment discard the lookup.
freshChecks: Desired reachability and accepted entries are re-read under the transition.
Native package references are re-observed before each removal.
Tree integrity is recomputed under the transition before removal.
The settlement protect snapshot precedes each removal.
Validation confirms lockfile entries and canonical directories are gone.
acquired-retirement.lifetime: The per-tree memo is created at the start of one planning call and released when that call returns; no other planning call and no transition sees it. The planned rows and verdicts live in the planned step and are released with its plan; no planning read substitutes for a check under the lock, and nothing is retained across invocations. The verified-digest lookup lives only for the Pack disable's settlement planning and never enters the step.

before-removing-unreachable-canonical-tr.basis: Before removing an unreachable canonical tree, retirement recomputes its aggregate integrity and the settlement protect then snapshots the same tree entry by entry for rollback.

check-s-convergence-assessment-plans-ret.basis: Check's convergence assessment plans the retirement of unreachable selected acquired packages once and removes nothing, probing and hashing each candidate canonical tree and observing its native package references once per tree, even when several unreached rows bind that tree.

native-package-references-found-planning.basis: Native package references found at planning are observed again under the lock before each canonical removal, so a registration that began referencing the package refuses its retirement.

preview-pack-disable-plans-retirement-on.basis: A preview of a Pack disable plans the retirement once and removes nothing: it hashes each unreachable canonical tree and observes its native package references once per tree, even when several unreached rows bind that tree.

sync-preview-hashes-each-unreachable-acq.basis: A sync preview plans the retirement and removes nothing: it probes and hashes each unreachable canonical tree and observes its native package references once per tree, even when several unreached rows bind that tree, so no tree's observation repeats before the preview returns.

rows-binding-one-canonical-tree-share-pl.basis: Within one retirement planning call, unreached accepted rows that bind the same canonical tree share its existence probe, integrity hash and native package reference scan, held in a memo that lives only for that call. Each row still validates its path, compares the digest with its own accepted tree integrity and keeps its own verified digest and copy of the references, and the transition repeats every observation under the lock before removal.

native-reference-scans-reread-native-con.basis: Within one retirement planning call, each unreached MCP, Hook or Pack row whose canonical tree no earlier row bound scans native package references on its own, probing, reading and parsing every agent's declared native MCP and Hook configuration files again although only the package root differs. On a Pack disable the scans run in the mutation's document-only prepare phase, where every probe, read and parse repeats; on sync and check the phase's observation view shares the probes and bytes and only the parses repeat, and a retained row's planning scan is the final judgement of its retention.
native-reference-scans-reread-native-con.openQuestion: May the retirement planning of a Pack disable, inside the mutation's document-only prepare phase, share the native MCP and Hook configuration bytes and their parses read for one unreachable row's native package reference inspection with the inspections of later rows in the same planning call, given that read-phases-have-bounded-lifetimes keeps document-only phases free of physical caching?

agent-output-cleanup.resource: AXM-owned skill and subagent outputs in agents' native directories (skill links, receipt-proven copied skill directories, rendered subagent files) that no desired agent or extension still needs, with the subagent projection rows withdrawn alongside them.
agent-output-cleanup.publication: Removal: an owned link is unlinked through the native entry removal capability, a copied skill directory is retired through its receipt, and an owned file is removed after a settlement protect snapshot; each removal is recorded as a footprint and emptied created parents are retired.

reads.note: The uninstall preparation captures native output ownership authority and inventories agent outputs, judged against the materialization agents and the proposal's expected names, once, where a removal description first needs them.
The cleanup step captures native output ownership authority once at planning, or accepts an uninstall preparation's, and passes it to its dry run and its apply run.

The planning dry run inventories agent outputs, or describes the inventory an uninstall preparation hands it, and observes artifact locations to preview removals and retentions; it is the only run in a preview and in check's convergence assessment, which remove nothing.

A cleanup reconciliation that takes its own first inventory of agent outputs keeps that inventory's skill entry and reader referent resolutions for its skill classification, and resolves the physical scope root once, at its first Subagent residue decision, for every later residue decision of that call.
The apply run inventories agent outputs again inside the transaction and decodes the lockfile's projection rows, so an unreadable lockfile refuses before any removal.
Each recorded subagent file is read and compared with its recorded row; a modified file is kept unless discarding modified files was requested.
Each removal first asserts its address lies within the native authority roots.
The settlement protect snapshots each entry before it is removed.
A second inventory after removal requires every retained desired output to remain and every retired output to be gone; withdrawn artifact locations are observed.

Each Subagent residue decision resolves the residue file's native entry live to key its projection row, because the inventory lists a linked file at its referent and an unresolved one at its raw path.

agent-output-cleanup.existingSharing: The ownership authority captured at planning already serves both the dry run and the apply run. An uninstall preparation now captures the ownership authority and inventories agent outputs once for every removal it describes, so its uninstall artifacts, cleanup dry runs and withdrawn-hook filter no longer each capture or inventory on their own. Within one cleanup reconciliation, the skill classification now takes the skill entry and reader referent resolutions and the copy-receipt presence that the call's own pre-removal inventory observed, and every Subagent residue decision keys beneath one resolution of the physical scope root.
agent-output-cleanup.preparedInputs: One uninstall preparation's native output ownership authority and agent output inventory are prepared once and handed out as separate copies: the inventory to each uninstall artifact, both to each cleanup step (its dry run describes the inventory and its apply run keeps the authority), and the authority to the withdrawn-hook filter. A cleanup reconciliation that takes its own first inventory of agent outputs keeps that inventory's skill entry and reader referent resolutions as a location set that is never mutated, and its skill classification consumes that set together with the copy-receipt presence the inventory just read; an inventory handed in already prepared lends no location set. The physical scope root, resolved at a cleanup reconciliation's first Subagent residue decision, is consumed by every residue decision of that call to key its projection row.
freshChecks: The apply run re-inventories outputs inside the transaction rather than reusing the dry run or an uninstall preparation's inventory.
The lockfile's projection rows are decoded before any removal.
Each removal asserts its address within the native authority roots and is protected first.
Post-removal inventory verifies retained and retired outputs.
A retired copied skill directory reads its receipt again before its listed contents are removed.
Withdrawn artifact locations are re-resolved live after removal.
Each Subagent residue decision resolves the residue file's native entry live, and a recorded residue file's bytes are read live.
The dry run and the apply run each resolve the physical scope root themselves.
agent-output-cleanup.lifetime: The ownership authority lives in the planned cleanup step and is released with its plan; an uninstall preparation creates its authority and inventory lazily where a removal description first needs them, its inventory serves only the descriptions that preparation makes, and each cleanup step keeps its copy of the authority for its apply run; every other inventory lives for one reconcile call, and the location set it lends and the physical scope root resolved at that call's first Subagent residue decision are released with that call; nothing is retained across invocations.

cleanup-step-observes-agents-owned-outpu.basis: The cleanup step observes the agents' owned outputs in a dry run while planning and observes them again under the transition lock before removing any, so an output changed in between is judged on its current state.

uninstall-preparation-inventories-every-.basis: One uninstall preparation derives the native output ownership authority and inventories every configured agent's native outputs once, where a removal description first needs them, and hands each uninstall artifact, cleanup dry run and withdrawn-hook filter its own copy within that preparation's document-only read phase. The cleanup step's apply run still inventories agent outputs live under the transition lock before and after removing.

cleanup-skill-classification-reuses-own-.basis: Within one cleanup reconciliation, the skill classification takes the skill entry and reader referent resolutions and the copy-receipt presence that the call's own pre-removal inventory just observed, held in a location set that is never mutated and lives only for that call; an inventory handed in already prepared lends nothing. Each removal still asserts its address within the native authority roots and is protected first, a retired copy re-proves its receipt, withdrawn locations are re-resolved live, and the post-removal inventory stays fresh.

residue-decisions-key-beneath-one-scope-.basis: One cleanup reconciliation resolves the physical scope root once, lazily at its first Subagent residue decision, and keys every later residue decision of that call beneath it; a root failure still refuses that first decision with the same error. The dry run and the apply run each resolve the root themselves, and each residue file's entry and bytes are still read live.

residue-decision-re-resolves-inventory-r.basis: Each Subagent residue decision resolves the residue file's native entry again to key its projection row, although the same call's inventory resolved the entry the file was listed from. The inventory lists a linked file at its referent and an unresolved one at its raw path, so the decision keys from its own live resolution of the listed path rather than from the inventory's entry.
residue-decision-re-resolves-inventory-r.openQuestion: Should a Subagent residue decision key a regular file from the native entry the same call's inventory resolved, while a linked or unresolved residue file keeps its live entry resolution?

archive-cache.resource: The user Registry archive cache: <axm cache root>/archives/<base64url sha512>.zip.
archive-cache.publication: Atomic replacement of a verified archive on a cache miss, access-time refresh on a hit, and removal of corrupt, expired or excess entries.

reads.note: Existence probe before a cache read: any probe failure is a miss, while a read failure after a successful probe is a cache error.
Existence probe before listing the cache directory: a failed probe yields an empty listing, while a failed directory read is a cache error.
A hit is read under the buffered-archive bound and hashed once into verification evidence; a mismatch removes the entry and the archive is fetched again.
A fetched miss is hashed once before it is written, and that hash becomes the evidence returned with the buffer.
Directory listing with one stat per entry for status, explicit prune and the automatic prune after every fourth write; archives in active use are skipped.
Cache verify reads and hashes each listed entry once and removes mismatches.

archive-cache.existingSharing: Concurrent loads of one selection and integrity were already coalesced through an invocation-owned in-flight table that holds only active calls, never completed bytes or failures.
archive-cache.preparedInputs: The verification evidence for the exact buffer the cache hashed (on a hit, or before writing a miss) is delivered with that buffer to the requester that ran the lookup, so Registry consumers skip their own hash; a freshly fetched miss buffer is handed to the atomic writer without a copy.
freshChecks: Every hit is read and hashed again against its integrity.
Every miss is hashed before it is written.
A coalesced follower receives a private copy without evidence, so its caller hashes it.
Each read and each listing probes its path first.
The cache root is created on every write because prune or another process may remove it.
Automatic prune lists the directory afresh after every fourth write.
Each write stats its target before the rename (declared Windows rename policy).
archive-cache.lifetime: The buffer and its evidence belong to the requester whose lookup produced them and are released when that fetch's consumer finishes; the in-flight table holds only active calls; nothing is retained across invocations.

automatic-prune-lists-shared-cache-direc.basis: Automatic prune lists the shared cache directory afresh after every fourth write, skipping archives in active use.

cache-hashes-hit-before-delivering-fetch.basis: The cache hashes a hit before delivering it and a fetched miss before writing it, each at its own boundary; only the caller's repeat hash was removed.

coalesced-archive-cache-follower-receive.basis: A coalesced archive-cache follower receives a private copy of the leader's verified buffer without evidence, so its caller hashes that copy.
coalesced-archive-cache-follower-receive.openQuestion: May a coalesced archive-cache follower receive verification evidence for its private copy of the leader's verified buffer without hashing it, relying on the leader's consumer not mutating the buffer before the copy is taken?

each-cache-listing-probes-cache-director.basis: Each cache listing probes the cache directory before reading it, because a failed probe yields an empty listing while a failed directory read is a cache error.
each-cache-listing-probes-cache-director.openQuestion: Should the archive-cache listing read its directory directly, reporting a failed inspection where a failed existence probe now yields an empty listing?

each-cache-write-stats-target-before.basis: Each cache write stats its target before the rename under the caller-declared Windows rename policy.
each-cache-write-stats-target-before.openQuestion: Should archive-cache and local Registry writes stat their target before the rename only on platforms where a rename cannot replace an existing file?

each-uncoalesced-archive-cache-load-prob.basis: Each uncoalesced archive-cache load probes the entry before reading it, because a failed probe is a miss while a failed read after a successful probe is a cache error.
each-uncoalesced-archive-cache-load-prob.openQuestion: Should the archive-cache read use one typed read-if-present instead of an existence probe followed by a read, accepting an explicit cache policy for stat failures?

every-cache-write-creates-cache-root.basis: Every cache write creates the cache root first, because an explicit prune or another process may have removed it since the last write.
every-cache-write-creates-cache-root.openQuestion: Should archive-cache writes stop creating the cache root after the first write of an invocation and instead create it and retry once when the write finds it missing?

freshly-fetched-archive-written-cache-fr.basis: A freshly fetched archive is written to the cache from the fetched buffer without the atomic writer copying it.

archive-extraction.resource: Files, directories and links under a caller-owned empty staging directory or scoped scratch directory.
archive-extraction.publication: Directory tree: decoded archive entries written, chmodded and linked into the caller's staging directory.

reads.note: The staging directory is listed once and must be empty before any entry is written.
Single execution: the ZIP central directory is parsed once per extraction and each member is read once from the verified buffer, so nothing repeats in extraction.
A deflated member's compressed bytes are copied once before inflation, because the module also runs on a runtime whose inflater has not been shown to accept an offset view.
Every created link is checked for containment, and chained links are read back after all links exist.

archive-extraction.existingSharing: The archive arrives in memory from the caller, is parsed once and each member is read once; a tree the workspace transition already extracted is copied into canonical staging instead of being extracted again.
freshChecks: The staging directory must be empty before extraction.
Links are checked for containment after all links exist.
An operation extraction slot is held while extracting.
Runs inside the caller's staging under the workspace lock or in a scoped scratch directory.
archive-extraction.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the extracted tree belongs to the caller's staging or scratch scope.

each-deflated-archive-member-copied-once.basis: Each deflated archive member is copied once before inflation, because the content module also runs on a runtime whose inflater is not shown to accept an offset view.
each-deflated-archive-member-copied-once.openQuestion: Does the workerd runtime's inflateRawSync decode a Uint8Array view at a non-zero byte offset identically to a copied buffer, so that deflated archive members may be inflated without copying them?

atomic-file-writer.resource: Single files published by atomic replacement (a uniquely named temp file beside the target, renamed over it) and existing native files updated in place without replacing the entry identity that insertion receipts bind.
atomic-file-writer.publication: writeFileAtomic writes the temp file and renames it over the target, optionally removing the target first when the caller declares that the host cannot rename over a file, skips identical content on request, and reports the staged identity and bytes to the caller's publication callback inside the uninterruptible rename; writeFilePreservingIdentity rewrites an existing file in place or delegates a new file to the atomic path; sweepStaleAtomicWriteTemps removes stale temp siblings of one target.

reads.note: Only with skipIfUnchanged: an existence check and a read of the target compare its content with the new bytes so identical content is left untouched; with ignore-read-errors an unreadable target counts as changed.

Only with a publication callback: a stat of the staged temp (through its retained handle on Windows, with the birth time refreshed after the rename) supplies the pre-publication identity the caller records with the intended bytes.
The identity-preserving writer stats the target before each write to choose the in-place or new-file branch and to bind the pre-write identity its in-place publication reports.
A stale-temp sweep, when a caller requests it before its write, lists the target's directory and removes only temp siblings of that exact target.

atomic-file-writer.existingSharing: The writer snapshots copied byte content once, so the comparison, the write and the publication witness observe one value, and it reports the staged identity to the caller instead of a post-rename stat of the target; before prepared inputs were shared, every successful write also attempted to remove its already-renamed temp.
atomic-file-writer.preparedInputs: Once the rename consumes the temp, the writer records that and performs no temp removal; cleanup runs only when the write or the rename failed or was interrupted before the rename. A caller that owns its byte buffer exclusively may transfer it, so the bytes are staged without a copy and without a comparison or publication witness.
freshChecks: Every write stages a new uniquely named temp file beside the target and renames it; nothing is reused across writes.
With skipIfUnchanged the target is read live at the call and compared with the new bytes.
The identity-preserving writer stats the target before each write.
A caller-declared target removal runs before each rename.
A failed or interrupted write or rename removes its temp file.
A stale-temp sweep lists the target's directory before each write that requests it.
atomic-file-writer.lifetime: The copied content snapshot, the staged identity and the consumed-temp flag are local to one write and are released when it returns, fails or is interrupted; a transferred buffer stays owned by the caller, which must not mutate it until the call completes; nothing is retained across writes or invocations.

atomic-file-publication-removes-temp-fil.basis: An atomic file publication removes its temp file only when the rename did not happen, so a successful write performs no temp removal.

identity-preserving-writer-stats-existin.basis: The identity-preserving writer stats the existing target before each in-place write, because that pre-write identity is the publication identity the write reports.

authored-step-preflight.resource: The read-only preflight of an authored-extension step (new, fork, adopt and native import): the workspace-wide materializability gate, the target's installed state, the prior desired graph and, for Hooks, Rules and Knowledge, the prior native output authority.
authored-step-preflight.publication: None: read-only owner; the step's transaction publishes through the scaffold, settings, lockfile and projection owners.

reads.note: Unless the step allows a configured source transition (fork, move adoption, and every native import except Subagents), the preflight lists every materializable package of the type, so an unresolvable same-type package refuses before scaffolding.
The target's installed state, the prior desired graph and, for Hooks, Rules and Knowledge, the prior output authority become the step's prior facts.
Inside the transaction, after scaffolding and marking it authored, every enabled same-type package is resolved again to find the target's ref.
The step's validate checks the target is installed and has a configured source.

authored-step-preflight.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, nothing was: each preflight reader decoded settings and the lockfile again before the transaction.
authored-step-preflight.preparedInputs: The preflight's four reads run in one document-only read view that shares decoded settings and lockfile cells, the desired evaluation and record rows; manifests, package hashes and tree integrity are still read physically, and the view closes before the transaction.
freshChecks: The transaction's readers and writers observe the workspace afresh.
The post-scaffold resolution inside the transaction still lists every enabled same-type package.
Package hashes and tree integrity in the preflight are computed physically.
A settings edit after the preflight is preserved by the writers' fresh reads.
authored-step-preflight.lifetime: The document view lives for the preflight and closes before the step's transaction opens; its frozen values are released at view exit and nothing reaches the transaction; nothing is retained across invocations.

authored-step-s-read-only-preflight.basis: The authored step's read-only preflight reads settings and the lockfile once in one document-only read view that closes before the step's transaction.

fork-move-adoption-skill-mcp-hook.basis: On fork, move adoption and Skill, MCP or Hook import, the in-transaction listing of every enabled same-type package is the only workspace-wide materializability check, so a broken unrelated package still refuses the command.
fork-move-adoption-skill-mcp-hook.openQuestion: May the authored step's post-scaffold resolution consider only the target on fork, move adoption and Skill, MCP or Hook import, where it is the only workspace-wide materializability check, so that an unrelated broken same-type package no longer refuses those commands?

inside-transaction-after-scaffolding-aut.basis: Inside the transaction, after scaffolding, the authored step resolves every enabled same-type package again to find the target, although the pre-transaction gate already listed them.
inside-transaction-after-scaffolding-aut.openQuestion: May the authored step's post-scaffold resolution consider only the target, so that an unrelated same-type package broken after the pre-transaction gate no longer rolls back new, in-place adopt or subagent import?

authoring-adopt.resource: An acquired package moved into workspace authorship (move mode), or an authored package declared where it already sits (in-place mode).
authoring-adopt.publication: Directory move: the acquired canonical directory is renamed into authored storage; in-place mode publishes only the settings declaration, through the settings owner.

reads.note: Preparation observes the install root once; that one inventory settles both the copy a move adopts and the in-place installed-copy refusal.
Per validity boundary the package manifest is read and its tree hashed at most once, by the first consumer, and shared by the native preflight and the package resolution.
Package resolution consumes the boundary's manifest and hash evidence; the full-tree hash remains the readability gate of each boundary.
Under the lock in-place adoption observes the install root, the declaration and the package afresh.

Under the lock each preflight run reads the package manifest and hashes its tree again, once for both the native preflight and the package resolution, because evidence read while preparing does not hold across the wait for the lock.

authoring-adopt.existingSharing: None before prepared inputs were shared: each boundary read the manifest and hashed the tree in the native preflight and again in the package resolution, and in-place preparation scanned the install root twice.
authoring-adopt.preparedInputs: Per validity boundary, one cached manifest read and one cached tree hash shared by the native preflight and the package resolution; in preparation, one install-root inventory shared by the move selection and the in-place refusal.
freshChecks: Each in-lock preflight run builds its own manifest and hash evidence.
Under the lock in-place adoption observes the install root and the declaration afresh.
Under the lock move adoption repeats the create-only check and resolves the acquired package.
authoring-adopt.lifetime: Evidence is cached per validity boundary: preparation's evidence serves only preparation's consumers and each in-lock run makes its own; the prepare inventory is frozen, searched in preparation only and never kept; nothing is retained across invocations.

each-validity-boundary-reads-package-man.basis: Each validity boundary reads the package manifest and hashes its tree at most once for both the native preflight and the package resolution, and in-place preparation observes the install root once.

under-transition-lock-each-adopt-preflig.basis: Under the transition lock each adopt preflight reads the package manifest and hashes its tree again, and in-place adoption observes the install root and the declaration again, because evidence read while preparing does not hold across the wait for the lock.

authoring-fork.resource: A new workspace-authored package directory forked from a managed package, with its settings declaration.
authoring-fork.publication: Directory tree: the source is copied into a scoped staging directory, its manifest is rewritten there, and the staged package is copied into a canonical directory under the lock.

reads.note: The source manifest is read for identity validation, then the source tree is copied into staging and the manifest rewritten.
The symlink containment walk lists the source recursively and reads every entry's link once, and the staging copy takes its directory listings and link values from that observation.
The staged package is hashed once while preparing and that hash is supplied to the prepare-time native preflight.
Under the lock an enabled fork's native preflight reads the staged manifest and hashes the staged package afresh.
After the copy into the canonical directory the published copy is hashed and compared with the prepared staged hash.

authoring-fork.existingSharing: The fork is staged once while preparing and the same staged package is copied at apply. This change hands the prepare-time native preflight the staged package hash and the manifest text the fork wrote instead of hashing the staging again and reading its manifest back, and lets the staging copy take its directory listings and link values from the symlink containment walk instead of listing the source and reading its links again.
authoring-fork.preparedInputs: The staged package hash is computed once while preparing and supplied to the prepare-time native preflight instead of a second hash; enabled preflight runs share one decoding of the workspace documents. forkExtensionPackage returns the exact manifest text it writes into the staging, and the prepare-time native preflight of an enabled Rule, Hook, Knowledge or Subagent fork decodes that text through readExtensionManifest instead of reading the staged manifest back. The symlink containment walk's recursive listing of the source and its link read of every entry form an immutable source observation that the staging copy consumes for its directory listings and link values.
freshChecks: Under the lock an enabled fork's native preflight reads the staged manifest, checks its identity and hashes the staged package.
Under the lock canonical recovery and the create-only check run before the canonical directory is created.
The published copy's hash is compared with the prepared staged hash.
Fork staging reads and parses the source manifest again after preparation's read phase is retired and refuses a source whose identity changed after resolution.

The staging copy stats every entry it does not copy as a link, enforces its entry and byte limits, checks each link it copies against the source root, and resolves the source and destination entries live for its overlap checks.
authoring-fork.lifetime: The staged package and its hash are held by the prepared candidate until apply completes; the staging root is a scoped temporary directory removed with the command's scope; the prepare-time preflight receives the hash and the written manifest text as values and the in-lock preflight receives nothing. The written manifest text lives only for the prepare call, and its decode is evaluated only by the prepare-time preflight of an enabled Rule, Hook, Knowledge or Subagent fork. The containment walk's source observation is passed by value to the one staging copy that immediately follows it and is not kept on the candidate.

apply-fork-copies-private-staging-into.basis: At apply, a fork copies its private staging into the canonical publication staging and hashes that copy to compare it with the package content hash pinned while preparing, before the swap. The copy drops some entries, keeps only permission bits and follows nested links, and the in-lock native preflight of an enabled Rule, Hook, Knowledge or Subagent fork hashes the private staging, a different tree, before that write, so this post-copy hash is the only check that the tree about to be swapped in carries the prepared content.

enabled-fork-hands-prepare-time-native.basis: An enabled fork hands its prepare-time native-reader preflight the staged package hash it just pinned instead of hashing the staging again.

source-manifest-without-owner-write-bit.basis: A source manifest without the owner-write bit is still copied into staging before the fork attempts its rewrite, so a non-root fork of a read-only manifest keeps refusing.
source-manifest-without-owner-write-bit.openQuestion: Should forking a package whose manifest is read-only succeed and stage a read-only rewritten manifest, instead of refusing for non-root users with 'Fork target manifest could not be written'?

staging-copies-source-manifest-fork-then.basis: Staging copies the source manifest and the fork then overwrites it with the rewritten manifest, because writing the rewrite during the copy changes which out-of-space refusal a fork reports.
staging-copies-source-manifest-fork-then.openQuestion: May an out-of-space failure while staging a fork be reported as a copy failure instead of a manifest-write failure, and may a fork that today runs out of space during the copy succeed when its rewritten manifest is smaller?

under-lock-enabled-fork-s-native.basis: Under the lock an enabled fork's native preflight hashes the private staging again, so a staged file made unreadable after preparation is reported as a package hash failure.
under-lock-enabled-fork-s-native.openQuestion: May the in-lock authored native preflight of fork and subagent import skip re-hashing the invocation-private staged package, so that a staged file made unreadable between prepare and apply is reported by the next reader instead of as PackageContentHashFailed?

under-lock-enabled-fork-s-native-2.basis: Under the lock an enabled fork's native preflight reads the staged manifest and checks its identity again, the earliest fresh refusal of tampered staging.

under-lock-fork-recovers-canonical-path.basis: Under the lock the fork recovers the canonical path and repeats the create-only check before createCanonicalDirectory performs its own recovery and existence check.
under-lock-fork-recovers-canonical-path.openQuestion: May fork, create and no-demand import rely on createCanonicalDirectory's own recover-then-exists check under the lock, accepting that a canonical-path probe failure there reports its own error vocabulary instead of the caller's create-only inspection error?

fork-copy-reuses-containment-walk-source.basis: Within one forkExtensionPackage call, the symlink containment walk's single recursive listing of the source and its link read of every entry become an immutable source observation, and the staging copy that immediately follows takes its directory listings and link values from it instead of reading them again. The observation is passed by value to that one copy and is not kept on the candidate, and every stat, entry and byte limit count, relocatable-link check, real path resolution, overlap and identity check, and write stays live.

fork-containment-walk-and-copy-link-chec.basis: While preparing, a fork's symlink containment walk resolves the real path of every link in the source and refuses an unresolved or escaping link before the staging copy starts, and the copy's own relocatable-link check then validates each link it copies against the source root. The two checks differ on .git entries, dangling links, absolute links, error vocabulary and precedence, so both run and only the listing and link values they share are read once.
fork-containment-walk-and-copy-link-chec.openQuestion: May fork rely on the copy's relocatable-link check alone and drop its own containment walk, so that dangling contained links and links inside .git no longer refuse and an escaping link reports ForkPackageFailed after the overlap check instead of ForkPackageInvalid?

fork-staging-reads-source-manifest-after.basis: Fork staging reads and parses the source manifest again and compares its identity with the resolved package's after discovery read it during resolution. Preparation's read phase is retired before staging, so the staging read observes live state and refuses a source manifest changed after resolution with 'Fork source changed after it was resolved'.
fork-staging-reads-source-manifest-after.openQuestion: May fork staging reuse the source manifest text read during resolution, even though the preparation read phase is retired before staging, so that a source manifest changed between resolution and staging is no longer refused with 'Fork source changed after it was resolved'?

enabled-fork-preflight-decodes-written-m.basis: Within one ForkExtension.prepare call, forkExtensionPackage returns the exact manifest text it writes into the private staging, and the prepare-time native preflight of an enabled Rule, Hook, Knowledge or Subagent fork decodes that text lazily through readExtensionManifest, with the same schema, identity and type checks and the same refusal, instead of reading the staged manifest back. The text lives only for that prepare call, and its decode is never evaluated for a disabled fork or a skill, pack or MCP server fork. The fork's own in-memory decode, the Subagent manager's contained package load, publication hash validation, and the in-lock preflight's fresh read, decode and hash of the staged package stay.

preflight-strictly-decodes-text-fork-alr.basis: The prepare-time native preflight of an enabled Rule, Hook, Knowledge or Subagent fork decodes the manifest text the fork wrote, although forkExtensionPackage has just decoded the same rewritten manifest in memory with its type's schema. The fork's decode is not strict for Hook manifests, checks no identity or type and refuses as an invalid fork target, so the preflight's strict decode with its identity and type checks is the prepare-time validation of the staged manifest the native readers see.
preflight-strictly-decodes-text-fork-alr.openQuestion: May the prepare-time native preflight of an enabled fork reuse the fork's own in-memory decode of the rewritten manifest instead of strictly decoding the written text again, accepting that a manifest the strict decode refuses would then pass preview and preparation and be refused only by the in-lock preflight?

authoring-hook-export.resource: A new native hook bundle directory outside the source package.
authoring-hook-export.publication: Directory tree: the prepared bundle files are written into staging and created as a canonical directory at the destination.

reads.note: The source manifest and declared resources are read once to render the bundle.
The source package is hashed before and after those reads; a differing hash refuses a torn read.

Under the lock the destination is checked again and the source is hashed and compared; this is the only source freshness check because the execution candidate's material path is the destination, not the source.

authoring-hook-export.existingSharing: The bundle bytes are rendered once while preparing and written verbatim at apply.
freshChecks: Under the lock the destination and its staging and backup siblings are checked again.
Under the lock the source package hash is compared with the prepared hash.
authoring-hook-export.lifetime: The prepared bundle bytes and source hash are held by the planned step until apply completes; nothing is retained across invocations.

native-bundle-bytes-rendered-once-while.basis: The native bundle bytes are rendered once while preparing and written verbatim when the destination is populated.

source-package-hashed-before-after-manif.basis: The source package is hashed before and after the manifest and resource reads to refuse a torn read, and under the lock it is hashed again as the only source freshness check.

under-lock-export-checks-again-destinati.basis: Under the lock the export checks again that the destination parent resolves to itself and that the destination and its staging and backup siblings are absent, after preparation made the same checks and before the create-only publication runs its own collision check.

authoring-import.resource: A workspace-authored package created or updated from native Skill, Subagent, Hook or MCP content, with its settings declaration.
authoring-import.publication: Directory tree: a converted skill or subagent is staged in a scoped temporary directory while preparing and copied into a new or replaced canonical directory; a hook or MCP conversion is written directly into the canonical directory's staging path when it is populated.

reads.note: The converted skill or subagent package is hashed and its manifest read once while preparing; the hash and manifest facts are supplied to the prepare-time subagent preflight.
The converted subagent staging is read back and validated.
Native hook bundle metadata is read first; an existence probe runs only when the read fails for a reason other than absence.
Importing into an existing authored subagent hashes the target while preparing and again under the lock, with a fresh declaration read.
Under the lock an enabled subagent import's preflight reads the staged manifest and hashes the staged package afresh.
The published copy of a converted skill or subagent is hashed and compared with the prepared staged hash.
The managed-package check stats and lists the native source once; the subagent definition-file selection and the skill copy choice take that inspection.

Importing into an existing authored subagent loads and validates the existing package's manifest and implementation sources inside the conversion boundary, after the prepare-time hash of that package, and then copies the whole tree into staging.

authoring-import.existingSharing: A converted skill or subagent is staged once while preparing and the same staging is copied at apply; a hook bundle or MCP manifest is converted once while preparing, held in memory, and first written when the canonical directory is populated, so these imports stage nothing while preparing. Within one preparation this change also shares the staged manifest text the hash walk decoded, the settled staged hash and manifest facts, one target existence probe, the resolved hook bundle root, and the managed-package check's inspection of the native source.
authoring-import.preparedInputs: The converted package's staged hash and immutable manifest facts are supplied to the prepare-time subagent preflight instead of a second hash and manifest read; hook import reads its bundle metadata once instead of probing first. The staged package hash walk hands the decoded text of the staged manifest to the converted manifest decoder, which reads the manifest from disk only when the walk did not see it as a regular file. The target existence probe that chooses between creating and updating the package also decides the prepare-time create-only refusal. Native hook import reads its resource closure against the bundle real path it resolved first. Within one native Skill or Subagent import call, the managed-package check's single stat and listing of the native source become a frozen inspection that the subagent definition-file selection and the skill copy choice take instead of inspecting the source again.
freshChecks: Under the lock canonical recovery and the create-only check (or the existing target's hash and declaration) run before publication, and creating the canonical directory probes the target again after its recovery.
Under the lock an enabled subagent import's native preflight reads and hashes the staged package.
The published copy's hash is compared with the prepared staged hash.
While preparing, the candidate seal reads a converted skill or subagent's native source and every staged file live as the material baseline that lock-time freshness recomputes.
In the authored step's transaction, the listing hashes the published canonical tree after the swap to resolve the workspace package.
The staging target conflict check and the skill copy's overlap checks and source root scan inspect live state rather than the managed-package check's inspection of the native source.

Inside the conversion boundary that retires preparation's read phase, importing into an existing authored subagent loads and validates that package's manifest and implementation sources, then copies the whole tree into staging.
authoring-import.lifetime: The staged package, its hash and its manifest facts are held by the prepared candidate until apply completes; the facts are immutable strings handed only to the prepare-time preflight; the staging root is a scoped temporary directory removed with the command's scope. The decoded staged manifest text, the target existence result and the resolved hook bundle root live only within the preparation call that creates them. The native source inspection is owned by the importNativeExtensionPackage call that creates it and does not outlive that call.

apply-after-native-skill-subagent-import.basis: At apply, a native Skill or Subagent import's publication validation hashes the copy at the publication staging path, the swap then renames that copy into the canonical path, and the authored step's in-transaction listing hashes the canonical tree again to resolve the workspace package. The swap is a write between the two reads, and the listing hash is the only read of the published canonical tree, so its value, not the pre-swap hash, becomes the recorded resolution.
apply-after-native-skill-subagent-import.openQuestion: Should an accepted requirement state that the resolution an authoring command records for a published canonical package comes from a read of that package after the swap, rather than from the content hash validated on its copy before the swap?

apply-skill-subagent-native-import-hashe.basis: At apply, a Skill or Subagent native import hashes the copy of its private staging in the canonical publication staging and compares it with the content hash pinned while preparing, before the swap. The lock-time refingerprint reads the private staging, a different tree, before the copy is written and compares a different digest, and the copy is not an identity copy, so this post-copy hash is the only check that the tree about to be swapped in has the prepared content.

converted-skill-subagent-package-staged-.basis: A converted skill or subagent package is staged once while preparing, and the same staging is copied into the canonical directory at apply.

converted-subagent-staging-read-back-val.basis: The converted subagent staging is read back and validated before it is published.

enabled-subagent-import-hands-prepare-ti.basis: An enabled subagent import hands its prepare-time native-reader preflight the staged hash and immutable manifest facts it already settled instead of a second hash and manifest read.

hook-import-reads-bundle-metadata-first.basis: Hook import reads its bundle metadata first and probes for existence only when the read fails for a reason other than absence.

hook-import-resolves-native-bundle-direc.basis: Native hook import reads its resource closure against the bundle real path that prepareNativeHookImport resolved earlier in the same call, so the bundle root is resolved once while preparing and that value lives only within the call. Each resource is still resolved, contained, type-checked and size-limited fresh, and hook export still resolves its own unresolved package root.

importing-into-existing-authored-subagen.basis: Importing into an existing authored subagent hashes the target while preparing and again under the lock with a fresh declaration read, a baseline the material fingerprint does not provide.

mcps-import-publishes-mcp-json-three.basis: mcps import publishes .mcp.json three times because the projection writer installs the converted package for managed validation and then withdraws it unless the package is enabled.

subagent-import-updates-existing-target-.basis: A subagent import that updates an existing target binds the pre-copy package with a lock-time package hash and the post-copy snapshot with the material fingerprint; each detects edits the other cannot.

under-lock-enabled-subagent-import-s.basis: Under the lock an enabled subagent import's native preflight hashes the private staging again, so a staged file made unreadable after preparation is reported as a package hash failure.
under-lock-enabled-subagent-import-s.openQuestion: May the in-lock authored native preflight of fork and subagent import skip re-hashing the invocation-private staged package, so that a staged file made unreadable between prepare and apply is reported by the next reader instead of as PackageContentHashFailed?

under-lock-enabled-subagent-import-s-2.basis: Under the lock an enabled subagent import's native preflight reads the staged manifest and checks its identity again, the earliest fresh refusal of tampered staging.

under-lock-import-create-mode-recovers.basis: Under the lock an import in create mode recovers the canonical path and repeats the create-only check before createCanonicalDirectory performs its own recovery and existence check.
under-lock-import-create-mode-recovers.openQuestion: May fork, create and no-demand import rely on createCanonicalDirectory's own recover-then-exists check under the lock, accepting that a canonical-path probe failure there reports its own error vocabulary instead of the caller's create-only inspection error?

when-metadata-read-fails-reason-other.basis: When the metadata read fails for a reason other than absence, an existence probe still runs so that a symbolic link loop keeps reporting the access failure as its cause.
when-metadata-read-fails-reason-other.openQuestion: May a hook bundle metadata read that fails for a reason other than absence report the read failure itself as its cause, so that the follow-up existence probe can be removed?

while-preparing-native-skill-subagent-im.basis: While preparing, a native Skill or Subagent import's staged package hash walk hands the decoded text of the staged manifest to the manifest decoder within the same conversion call, so the staged manifest is read once for the content hash, the package version and the manifest facts. A manifest the walk did not see as a regular file is read from disk as before, and the candidate seal and the in-lock native preflight still read and hash the staging fresh.

candidate-seal-fingerprints-native-sourc.basis: While preparing, the candidate seal of a native Skill or Subagent import reads the native source and every staged file again, after the staged hash walk, to fingerprint them as candidate materials in its own live observation. That fingerprint is the material baseline the lock-time freshness check recomputes and is hashed into the candidate identity, and it follows links and labels paths differently from the package hash, so taking it from earlier reads would make it a different check.

while-preparing-skill-import-subagent-im.basis: Within one native import preparation, the single target existence probe that chooses between creating and updating the package also decides the prepare-time create-only refusal, with the same subject, path and order, and the probe result is not kept beyond that preparation. Under the lock the create-only preflight and createCanonicalDirectory's recover-then-exists check still probe the target fresh.

native-import-reuses-managed-package-sou.basis: Within one native Skill or Subagent import preparation, the managed-package check's single stat and listing of the native source become a frozen inspection owned by that importNativeExtensionPackage call, and the subagent definition-file selection and the skill copy choice take it instead of inspecting the source again. The inspection does not outlive the call, and the target conflict check, the copy's overlap checks and root scan, and the candidate seal's read of the native source stay live.

subagent-import-reads-existing-package-t.basis: Importing a native subagent into an existing workspace-authored subagent hashes the existing package tree while preparing, then, inside the conversion boundary that retires preparation's read phase, loads and validates its manifest and implementation sources and copies the whole tree into staging. The hash is the baseline the lock-time hash compares against, the load refuses identity and occupied-slot conflicts before any copy failure, and the copy stages the package that is updated.
subagent-import-reads-existing-package-t.openQuestion: May native subagent import validate and copy an existing authored package in one scan inside the conversion boundary, even though copy failures (limits, link containment, overlap) would then outrank manifest, identity and slot refusals and the target hash failure would no longer come before source resolution failures?

authoring-pack-membership.resource: The authored pack manifest of a workspace-authored pack.
authoring-pack-membership.publication: Whole-file write of the pack manifest inside a workspace transaction.

reads.note: The pack manifest is read, parsed and decoded once while preparing; its text and decoded value are handed to the step.
Adding resolves member candidates from every workspace and accepted graph node before selector filtering; removal selects only from the prepared manifest's dependencies and observes no desired graph.
Under the lock the manifest is read and compared with the prepared text; a differing text refuses as stale.
After the write the manifest is read back, decoded and checked for the requested dependencies.
After the write the manifest is read back, decoded and checked for the removed dependencies.

authoring-pack-membership.existingSharing: The membership delta (additions or removals) was already computed once while preparing and passed to the step.
authoring-pack-membership.preparedInputs: The prepared pack manifest text and its decoded value are transferred to the locked step, which compares the locked text with it and edits the prepared value; the manifest digest and the locked re-parse are gone.
freshChecks: Under the lock the manifest text is read and compared with the prepared text.
After the write the manifest is read back and validated.
authoring-pack-membership.lifetime: The prepared text and decoded manifest have a single holder, the planned step, and are released when the execution plan completes; nothing is retained across invocations.

member-candidates-resolve-every-workspac.basis: Member candidates resolve every workspace and accepted graph node before selector filtering, so a resolution failure of an unrelated package still refuses the command.
member-candidates-resolve-every-workspac.openQuestion: May `packs add` stop refusing when an unrelated workspace or accepted package fails resolution?

prepared-pack-manifest-text-decoded-valu.basis: The prepared pack manifest text and decoded value are handed to the locked step, which compares the locked text with it and edits the prepared value, so no manifest digest or locked re-parse remains.

under-lock-pack-manifest-read-compared.basis: Under the lock the pack manifest is read and compared with the prepared text, and after the write it is read back and checked for the requested dependencies.

authoring-scaffold.resource: A new workspace-authored package directory created by '<type> new', with its settings declaration.
authoring-scaffold.publication: Directory tree: the rendered scaffold is populated into a staging directory and created as a canonical directory; rule, hook, knowledge and subagent scaffolds are also staged into a scoped OS temporary directory for the native-reader preflight, once while preparing and again under the lock (a hook scaffold is staged but not read).

reads.note: Native preflight reads the staged scaffold manifest and lets the rule, knowledge or subagent manager read the staged payload; the scaffold source hash is supplied by the caller instead of hashing the staging.
Each enabled preflight run decodes settings and the lockfile in one document phase (or the caller's phase).
Skill destinations are resolved once while preparing and that resolution is handed to the prepare-time destination check.

While preparing, the destination check classifies native locations from the entries its containment checks just resolved and a capture of the skill readers; a target missing from those entries is resolved live.
Each containment assertion of the prepare-time skill destination check resolves the native authority roots itself, so a shared workspace root is resolved once per target.
Under the lock the scaffold is staged again into a fresh temporary directory and the native preflight re-runs over exactly the bytes to be published.
Under the lock skill destinations are resolved afresh, an occupied native entry refuses, and the containment assertions and native location capture resolve every entry afresh.
Under the lock canonical recovery and the create-only check repeat before the canonical directory is created.

authoring-scaffold.existingSharing: None before prepared inputs were shared: the scaffold was rendered and staged for each use and each preflight hashed the staging it had just written. This change settles the scaffold source hash once for both native preflights, hands the prepare-time skill destination resolution to the prepare-time destination check, whose native location classification takes the entries its own containment checks just resolved, and shares one decoding of the workspace documents within each enabled native preflight run.
authoring-scaffold.preparedInputs: The scaffold source hash is settled once and supplied to both native preflights; the prepare-time skill destination resolution is handed to the prepare-time destination check; while preparing, the native entry each containment check of the destination check resolves is kept in a frozen list, and that list with a capture of the skill readers and their referents (no entries) is consumed by the same check's native location classification, which resolves a target missing from the list live; each enabled native preflight run shares one decoding of the workspace documents.
freshChecks: Under the lock the scaffold is restaged into a fresh temporary directory and the native preflight re-runs on it.
Under the lock skill destinations are resolved afresh, and the destination check's containment assertions and native location capture resolve every entry afresh.
While preparing, each containment assertion of the skill destination check resolves the native authority roots itself, once per target.
The final skill artifact resolves the skill destinations afresh.
Under the lock canonical recovery and the create-only check run before the canonical directory is created.
authoring-scaffold.lifetime: The scaffold source hash is held by the prepared step for both preflights and its own source ref; the frozen list of asserted native entries and the reader capture live for one prepare-time skill destination check and are dropped when it returns; each temporary staging directory is scoped to one preflight run and removed when that run ends; nothing is retained across invocations.

creating-subagent-reads-staged-manifest-.basis: Creating a Subagent reads the staged manifest once to resolve the package and again in the manager's projection observation, two owner calls per staging.

hook-scaffold-staged-into-os-temporary.basis: A hook scaffold is staged into an OS temporary directory for the native-reader preflight while preparing and again under the lock although no reader inspects it, because skipping it would let an unwritable temporary directory stop refusing the command.
hook-scaffold-staged-into-os-temporary.openQuestion: May `axm hooks new` skip its unread native-reader staging pass, so that an unwritable or full OS temporary directory no longer refuses preview and apply with 'Could not stage authored package preview'?

preparation-renders-scaffold-memory-prob.basis: Preparation renders the scaffold in memory and probes the destination once as the preview refusal; nothing is staged or hashed for this type.

scaffold-s-source-hash-settled-once.basis: The scaffold's source hash is settled once and supplied to the native-reader preflight while preparing and under the lock, so neither preflight hashes the staging it just wrote.

skill-destinations-resolved-once-while-p.basis: Skill destinations are resolved once while preparing and handed to the prepare-time destination check; the lock and the final artifact still resolve them afresh.

under-lock-authored-step-recovers-canoni.basis: Under the lock the authored step recovers the canonical path and repeats the create-only check immediately before createCanonicalDirectory performs its own recovery and existence check.
under-lock-authored-step-recovers-canoni.openQuestion: May fork, create and no-demand import rely on createCanonicalDirectory's own recover-then-exists check under the lock, accepting that a canonical-path probe failure there reports its own error vocabulary instead of the caller's create-only inspection error?

under-lock-scaffold-staged-again-into.basis: Under the lock the scaffold is staged again into a fresh temporary directory so the native-reader preflight inspects exactly the bytes about to be published.

skill-destination-classification-takes-a.basis: While a new skill is prepared, the prepare-time destination check classifies native locations from the target entry each of its containment checks just resolved, kept in a frozen list for that one check, plus a capture of the readers only; a target missing from the list is resolved live. Under the lock the destination check's containment assertions and native location capture resolve every entry afresh.

skill-destination-containment-resolves-r.basis: Each containment assertion of the prepare-time skill destination check resolves the native authority roots itself, so a workspace root that several targets share is resolved once per target within one check.
skill-destination-containment-resolves-r.openQuestion: Does a containment check that previews a skill destination before the lock count as an admission that must obtain fresh native-root observations under workspace/locations/resolution-cost-follows-path-depth?

authoring-version.resource: The authored manifest of a workspace-authored package.
authoring-version.publication: Whole-file write of the authored manifest inside a workspace transaction.

reads.note: The canonical observation reads the manifest and hands over its text; the version decision is decoded from that text.
Under the lock the manifest is read again, its version compared with the prepared one, and every other field preserved in the write.
After the write the manifest is read back and its version validated.

authoring-version.existingSharing: The version decision (from and to) was already settled once while preparing and carried into the transition, which compares it with the locked read.
authoring-version.preparedInputs: Preparation decodes the version from the manifest text the canonical observation already read, with no second read and no existence probes; nothing is transferred to the transition.
freshChecks: Under the lock the manifest is read and its version compared with the prepared version.
After the write the manifest is read back and validated.
authoring-version.lifetime: The captured manifest text is used only inside preparation; the prepared from and to versions are held by the planned step until the execution plan completes; nothing is retained across invocations.

preparation-decodes-version-decision-fro.basis: Preparation decodes the version decision from the manifest text the canonical observation already read, with no second read and no existence probes.

under-lock-manifest-read-again-version.basis: Under the lock the manifest is read again and its version compared with the prepared one, and after the write it is read back and validated.

boundary-claims.resource: The OS-principal coordination namespace under the account home: the active.json claim table, per-token lease lock directories and the admission lock directory; under Bun, a scoped temporary configuration file for the account-home lookup.
boundary-claims.publication: Atomic replacement of the claim table through a token-named stage, removal when it becomes empty, and removal of a reclaimed lease's stage; the account lookup's scoped temporary file.

reads.note: Per claim, under the admission lock: table read, strict decode and record validation, and the lease directory scan for unrecorded active leases.
Per other record: lease liveness by contending its lease lock, then overlap and ambiguous-spelling checks on fresh existence.
Once per top-level transaction: account home and namespace spelling checks that refuse a redirected coordination directory.

boundary-claims.existingSharing: One claims service per top-level transaction: its namespace, spelling checks, lease and admission directories are prepared once, and every protection and content claim of the transaction, nested joins included, uses them.
freshChecks: Admission lock acquisition per claim.
Table read, decode, validation and lease scan per claim.
Lease liveness, overlap and spelling checks per other record.
The claim table is rewritten on every claim.
boundary-claims.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the claims service and its lease live for one top-level transaction and are retired by its finalizer under one admission.

claim-adds-no-target-drops-no.basis: A claim that adds no target and drops no record still rewrites the claims table in canonical order and encoding.
claim-adds-no-target-drops-no.openQuestion: May a boundary claim that adds no target and drops no record leave the claims table's record order and encoding as found instead of rewriting it canonically?

each-boundary-claim-takes-admission-lock.basis: Each boundary claim takes the admission lock and reads, decodes and validates the claims table and checks each live record's overlap on fresh state, because a concurrent principal may have claimed since.

each-claim-scans-lease-directories-unrec.basis: Each claim scans the lease directories for unrecorded active leases on fresh state before admitting its targets.

every-boundary-claim-rewrites-claims-tab.basis: Every boundary claim rewrites the claims table atomically, even when the serialized table equals the bytes read in the same admission.
every-boundary-claim-rewrites-claims-tab.openQuestion: May a boundary claim whose table bytes are unchanged skip its rewrite, so that a write failure (unwritable namespace, ENOSPC) no longer fails the claim and a replaced or symlinked claims table is no longer normalized?

canonical-directory.resource: Canonical extension package trees and their sibling .axm-staging and .axm-backup directories.
canonical-directory.publication: Directory tree: a populated staging sibling swapped into place by rename, with interrupted-swap recovery, create-only publication behind a collision check, and removal of a superseded canonical tree.

reads.note: Interrupted-swap recovery probes the canonical and backup paths once before the reuse decision and again before every replacement stages; the reuse decision's recovery runs without the lexical path-safety checks that precede every other recovery.
Create-only publication recovers once, then probes the canonical path and refuses an occupied destination before staging.
Settlement snapshots staging, backup and canonical before a non-transient swap.
Staging is populated by copy, extraction or authored writes.
The staged tree is validated by the caller and, when the caller inspects it, hashed once; that digest is the tree integrity callers record.
A Knowledge commit passes its prepared tree integrity, and the staged hash refuses a copy that changed before publication.
Swap-time existence of the canonical path decides the backup rename.
Prior-tree digest after the canonical snapshot, taken only for a non-transient replacement over an existing tree, for the footprint byte-change decision.
Post-swap digest of the published tree, taken only when a prior digest exists, so the footprint reflects the bytes actually published.
A package already materialized in this acquisition is re-hashed before it is reused.

Canonical acquisition runs the caller's validation on a reused tree once at each reuse return; for a Registry skill that is the official AXM skill compatibility check, which reads skill.json and src/SKILL.md.
A self-copy hashes the canonical tree under the transition lock for the tree integrity the materialization records.
A fetched Registry archive is hashed before extraction only when the client's evidence does not cover that exact buffer and integrity.
Settlement records the canonical postimage by reading and hashing the published tree (settlement-owned).

After materialization or reuse, the Skill, Knowledge, Rule, Hook and Subagent managers hash the package again for the recorded package content hash, whose digest framing differs from the tree digest; an authored step's Rule, Hook or Subagent install of a workspace ref instead records the hash its in-transaction listing computed for the same root, except a Subagent install that wrote, bound or withdrew a native path inside the package, and any other workspace Rule or Hook install frames it from the strict walk that produces its tree integrity.

The reuse decision hashes an accepted tree before source work, except that a Knowledge sync restore refuses reuse from the differing digest the same loop iteration's observation computed of that root.

A workspace Rule or Hook install's strict walk of its package produces the tree integrity it records and, when no hash of that exact root was handed, frames the package content hash from the same bytes.
Only a workspace Pack's install probes its canonical Pack directory, after the workspace location check, and maps a failed probe to absence.
Pack validation decodes pack.json and compares its content identity, taking the text from the reuse decision's integrity walk for a tree that decision kept and reading the manifest live otherwise.

canonical-directory.existingSharing: The staged digest was already returned as the tree integrity and recorded by callers without hashing again; a package materialized earlier in the same acquisition is reused after a fresh re-hash; acquired temporary trees are copied instead of fetched again; one owner makes the reuse decision; an acquired Pack's install no longer probes its canonical Pack directory before canonical acquisition, which is the only observer of that directory.
canonical-directory.preparedInputs: Tree digests are computed only when a consumer needs them (no prior or post-swap digest for transient staging, and none for a create-only publication or any replacement with no prior tree); a Knowledge commit's prepared tree integrity is checked inside the staged hash; the reuse decision's recovery is passed once, as a single-use proof, to the pre-fetch recovery of the same path; create-only publication recovers once; materialization from a tree the transition already acquired takes no buffered-archive reservation; a fetched Registry archive with covering client evidence is not hashed again before extraction; Registry skill materialization relies on the official AXM skill compatibility check that canonical acquisition runs as the reuse validation of a reused tree, instead of checking that tree again; an authored step's in-transaction listing hands the package content hash it computed for a workspace ref, with that ref's root, to the Rule, Hook and Subagent install of the same ref, which records it without hashing the tree again; a workspace Rule or Hook install not handed a hash of its exact package root frames its package content hash from the same strict walk that produces its tree integrity, and records both; the reuse decision's integrity walk of a kept accepted Pack tree keeps the text of pack.json it read as a regular file at exactly that path and hands it to the Pack validation of that same tree; a Knowledge sync restore hands its reuse decision the differing digest the same loop iteration's observation computed of the canonical root, which refuses reuse from it instead of hashing that tree again.
freshChecks: Every replacement recovers its path again before it stages.
Create-only publication probes its destination after its one recovery.
Settlement snapshots staging, backup and canonical before a non-transient swap.
Swap-time existence of the canonical path.
A prior-tree digest and a post-swap digest decide the footprint of a replacement over an existing tree.
The reuse decision hashes an accepted tree before source work unless a Knowledge sync restore's same-iteration observation already found that root's digest different from the accepted integrity.
A reused package is re-hashed before reuse.

Canonical acquisition runs the caller's validation on every reused tree before returning it, so an incompatible reused Registry skill tree is still refused, and a fetched tree is still checked in staging before publication.
A self-copy, whose source is the canonical path itself, hashes that tree under the transition lock for the tree integrity it records.

A Rule, Hook or Subagent install hashes the package itself unless it is a workspace install handed a listed hash for exactly its own root, and a Subagent install also hashes it when a native path it wrote, bound or withdrew lies inside the package.
A workspace Rule or Hook install handed a hash of its exact package root still runs the strict walk for its tree integrity, and every Rule or Hook install reads its manifest live.
A workspace Pack's install probes its canonical Pack directory after the workspace location check and refuses a missing one.

The Pack validation of a kept tree still decodes pack.json and compares its content identity after the integrity walk, and reads a linked, missing, differently cased or non-file pack.json live with the same refusal.
A fetched archive without covering client evidence is hashed before extraction.
The caller holds the workspace transition lock; settlement records the postimage.
canonical-directory.lifetime: Digests and the recovery proof stay inside one acquisition under the transition lock; the proof is single-use, never cached or stored; the reused Registry skill tree's compatibility check runs within the one canonical acquisition and its result is not stored; the listed package content hash lives only within one authored step under the transition lock, from its in-transaction listing to that step's install; the buffered-archive reservation spans download through swap of one fetched archive; the bytes a workspace Rule or Hook install's strict walk reads stay local to that one digest computation within the install call; the pack.json text kept by the reuse decision's integrity walk lives within one acquisition call and reaches only the validation of the tree that decision kept; a Knowledge sync restore's observed differing digest lives within one loop iteration, with nothing written since that observation; nothing is retained across invocations.

acquired-temporary-tree-copied-into-cano.basis: An acquired temporary tree is copied into canonical staging instead of renamed, because it may sit on another filesystem and may serve several destinations.
