after-authoring-command-s-transaction-li.basis: An authored step's in-transaction listing computes the workspace package's content hash once and hands it, with the listed root, to the Rule, Hook and Subagent install of the same ref, which records it instead of hashing the canonical tree again; the hash lives only for that step under the transition lock. Each install uses it only when the ref's resolved root equals the listed root, and the Subagent install also only when no native path it wrote, bound or withdrew lies inside the tree; every other install, including sync and install plans whose refs were resolved in an ended read phase, hashes the package itself, and tree integrity, manifest read and destination checks keep their order.

after-materialization-reuse-extension-ma.basis: After materializing or reusing an acquired Registry, local, Git or HTTP package, the Hook and Rule managers hash the package root again for its recorded package content hash, an advisory change marker, and the Skill, Knowledge and Subagent managers hash their materialized packages the same way. The tree integrity these installs record comes from the acquisition, whether a reuse observation, the lock, staging or the copy, and not from a digest computation shared with that hash.
after-materialization-reuse-extension-ma.openQuestion: Should the package content hash these managers record after materializing or reusing a package keep its own walk of the package root, or be framed from the walk that produced its tree integrity when that walk covered the same root in the same call?

caller-s-staged-validation-reads-staging.basis: The caller's staged validation reads staging beside the staged hash, which digests the on-disk bytes after mode, link and case checks.

canonical-publication-computes-tree-dige.basis: Canonical publication computes tree digests only when a consumer needs them, and a Knowledge commit checks its prepared integrity inside the one staged hash.

canonical-publication-recovers-canonical.basis: A canonical publication recovers the canonical path's interrupted replacement in the reuse decision, whose judgement of the accepted tree depends on that recovery, and again when its replacement stages under the same transition lock. The replace-time recovery is the last one before staging: the publication relies on it for an empty staging directory and a prior tree restored from the backup, and the reuse decision's single-use recovery proof stands in only for an unstaged Registry publication's pre-fetch recovery.
canonical-publication-recovers-canonical.openQuestion: May a canonical replacement that follows the reuse decision's recovery of the same path under the same transition lock skip its own recovery before staging, given that this recovery is the last one before staging and the publication relies on it for an empty staging directory and a restored prior tree?

enabling-installed-mcp-server-publishes-.basis: Enabling an installed MCP server publishes no canonical tree: a non-Registry server's usable accepted tree is used as it is, and for a Registry server the reuse decision recovers the accepted path once and reuses the accepted tree.

package-already-materialized-acquisition.basis: A package already materialized in this acquisition, or a retained canonical binding, is hashed again before it is reused.
package-already-materialized-acquisition.openQuestion: May an acquisition reuse a package it already materialized, or a retained canonical binding, without hashing its tree again when no step wrote to it in between?

registry-materialization-from-tree-trans.basis: Registry materialization from a tree the transition already acquired copies it without taking a buffered-archive reservation; only a fetched archive holds one through staging and swap.

replacement-over-existing-tree-changed-c.basis: A replacement over an existing tree with changed content still hashes the published tree after the swap, so its footprint reflects the bytes actually published.
replacement-over-existing-tree-changed-c.openQuestion: May a changed-content canonical replacement record its modified footprint from the pre-swap staged digest instead of hashing the published tree, accepting that a foreign edit restoring the prior bytes between inspection and swap is then recorded as a modification?

reuse-decision-s-recovery-canonical-path.basis: The reuse decision's recovery of a canonical path stands in once for the back-to-back pre-fetch recovery of that path, and create-only publication recovers once.

reusing-accepted-registry-skill-tree-run.basis: Reusing an accepted Registry skill tree runs the official AXM skill compatibility check, which reads skill.json and src/SKILL.md, once: canonical acquisition runs it as the reuse validation at every reuse return, and Registry skill materialization relies on that check without storing its result. The check lives within the one canonical acquisition, an incompatible reused tree is still refused, and a fetched tree is still checked in staging before publication.

when-accepted-tree-has-drifted-reuse.basis: When an accepted tree has drifted, the reuse decision hashes it before source work, or, for a Knowledge sync restore, refuses reuse from the differing digest the same loop iteration's observation computed of that root, and the replacement hashes it again after the canonical snapshot, so foreign edits in between are reflected.

when-materialize-step-restores-local-sub.basis: When a materialize step restores a local Subagent from its usable accepted canonical tree, the self-copy hashes that tree again under the transition lock after planning's canonical observation hashed it to judge it usable. The planning digest belongs to the planning read phase, which ends before confirmation and the lock acquisition, while the self-copy digest is the only one taken under the lock and is the tree integrity the materialization records.

workspace-hook-rule-install-walks-packag.basis: A workspace Hook or Rule install without a handed hash of its exact package root frames its materialized-tree integrity and its package content hash from one strict walk of the package after the workspace location check, so it lists the package and reads each file once, and the walked bytes stay local to that one digest computation within the install call. A matching handed hash still runs the strict walk alone and hashes nothing, the manifest is still read live, and the strict walk stays the tree integrity the install records.

pack-install-probes-only-authored-pack-d.basis: A Pack's install operation probes the existence of its canonical Pack directory only for a workspace ref, after the workspace location check, and still maps a failed probe to absence. For a Registry, path, Git or HTTP Pack, canonical acquisition is the only observer of that directory, and its recovery, reuse decision and integrity checks are unchanged.

reused-pack-tree-validates-manifest-from.basis: When canonical acquisition keeps an accepted Pack tree, the reuse decision's strict integrity walk keeps the decoded text of pack.json it read as a regular file at exactly that path, and hands it only to the Pack validation of the tree that same decision kept, within one acquisition call. The integrity walk still runs first, the validation still decodes the manifest and compares its content identity, and a linked, missing, differently cased or non-file pack.json is read live with the same refusal.

canonical-observation.resource: The materialized canonical tree of a desired extension, judged against its accepted resolution: status, manifest, required payload and tree identity.

reads.note: Presence of the canonical root and of the type's required payload entry.

The manifest is read first and decoded once; only a read failure other than not-found probes the path, to tell an uninspectable location from an unreadable file. The capturing variant hands the text to the caller.
The required-payload check; for a subagent it loads the package through its contained, regular-file manifest read with strict decoding.

Tree identity of the canonical content compared with the accepted resolution's tree integrity, hashed unless the caller hands a digest it verified for the same root and accepted row in its read phase; a usable observation can hand its caller the strict walk or digests of that hash, and an owner-less Skill's matching walk that read SKILL.md stands for its readability read.
Tree identity for the decision whether an acquisition may keep the accepted canonical tree instead of materializing the requested ref again.
Workspace-authored ref resolution: presence probe, and the manifest read and package content hash unless the caller hands the decode or hash it settled for the same package root and type.

canonical-observation.existingSharing: Inside a physical observation phase, equivalent manifest reads and decodes coalesce; outside one, every observation reads live, and before prepared inputs were shared each consumer read the manifest again after the observation had read it. Now the observation's captured manifest decode and Subagent package load, its strict walk or digests of a usable accepted tree or the digest of a mismatched one, the lockfile its accepted-row lookup read, a tree digest or pre-content judgement its caller made earlier in the same read phase, and the observations, verdicts, decodes and accepted refs its callers make are handed to the next consumer inside the same call or read phase instead of being read, loaded or hashed again, and a caller that needs only the canonical root derives it without reading content.
canonical-observation.preparedInputs: A successful manifest read takes no presence probe; the capturing observation hands the calling owner the manifest text it read, with a lazily frozen decode, so hooks configuration, hook projection, Rule contributor selection, Knowledge discovery contributor selection, the knowledge corpus, Knowledge lint, visibility intent, publish identity and version preparation decode it instead of reading it again, and the usable accepted canonical lookup hands that decode to its workspace package resolution when it is the manifest of the resolved package directory and desired type; skill listing resolves each workspace-authored entry once per call through a prepared ref. Pack install graph selection, Pack member inspection and the step collection of a node no caller settled observe each desired node and resolve its usable package in one call that hands the workspace package resolution the same decode, and a bundled Skill's lookup or desired observation hands its bundled package resolution the skill.json decode of the same root. A non-forced install of a local, Git or HTTP sourced MCP server whose accepted tree is usable for the requested content selects its distribution and invocation from the mcp.json decode the MCP server manager's accepted canonical observation made at that root. The observation also hands back the Subagent package its payload check loaded, from which a Subagent uninstall or disable derives the native names to withdraw and orphan cleanup names each declared Subagent it observes at the same root. One Subagent package load reads each distinct source file once and hands that content to the core and every implementation that names it. An observation accepts a tree digest its caller verified for the same root and accepted row in place of hashing that tree: a Pack disable's retirement check hands the digests it verified to kept members' retained-reference observations, and Pack settlement observes no member whose root the retirement removes. Pack activation hands the observation of each kept member root the judgement it made of the member's accepted row before reading content, which stands in when the path service, layout, desired node and accepted row are the same values. A usable observation hands a caller that asks for them either its strict walk of the accepted tree, which source-switch classification's distribution tree digest of a Registry comparison replays, or the tree integrity of its walk with, when asked, the package content hash of the same bytes, which a Registry Hook's projection preparation takes for that root when the walk carries the content hash it asked for, or when its caller handed a content hash for the same root. An observation that hashed the accepted tree and found it different hands out that frozen digest, which a Knowledge sync's staged restore in the same loop iteration hands the reuse decision. When an owner-less Skill's strict walk matched the accepted tree integrity and read SKILL.md at exactly that path as a regular file, that read stands for the observation's own SKILL.md readability read. The canonical root an observation reports is derived from the desired node, accepted row and layout without reading content, and the MCP server manager's configured-agent outcomes take that root instead of observing the tree. Acquisition planning records each accepted ref it rebuilds from the planning read phase's accepted row, deep-frozen, and publisher trust and source-switch classification take a recorded ref only on an exact type and name match, rebuilding any other target themselves. Source-switch classification reads desired-node and accepted-row presence from the planning read phase's documents and takes or rebuilds the accepted ref before it decides whether to observe the accepted tree. Within one source-switch comparison of a non-Registry side with a Registry side, the side's distribution manifest bytes serve both its publication policy and that manifest's entry in the distribution tree hash, and the ignore observation takes the link and kind of each exactly named .gitignore its own walk listed. A distribution tree integrity computation carries each subdirectory listing taken for its emptiness test to the walk of that subdirectory. Outside a read phase, the accepted-row lookup of an MCP connection is keyed by the desired graph its caller just evaluated from the same desired-state reader, and an accepted-ref reconstruction builds the ref from the row its single lookup read. An accepted canonical observation hands the lockfile its accepted-row lookup read to its shared-package verdict. A lint run hands each Rule, Hook and Knowledge contributor selection of its projection invariant facts its own copy of the run's observation and captured manifest of the identical desired node. The lint run's authoring-folder observation also hands over each successful workspace-authored package resolution, with its root, deep-frozen manifest decode and content hash, through which the projection invariant facts resolve an enabled workspace-authored Subagent and the Hook contributor selection takes the content hash of the same package root. While the lint read model is populated, each selected installed Knowledge bundle's package inspection decodes the knowledge.json text its rule subject has just read through the same filesystem at the identical path, taking the canonical scan's deep-frozen parse when the scan parsed that exact text at that path. Within one inspection of an acquired directory or scan of an authored type, the canonical scan counts a portable skill's SKILL.md or an acquired subagent's subagent.json it has just read as present, and does not stat again a package directory its parent's classification stat'd. Leaf activation settlement hands its usable observation of an enabled Hook, or of a Rule or Knowledge subject the step-collection inventory lists as installed, to step collection. The satisfied-install check of an accepted Subagent that is not workspace-authored hands the frozen usable observation that gates its no-op to the Subagent configured-agent outcome observer, which derives the usable accepted ref from it. In configured-agent verification after apply, observeConfiguredTargets hands its frozen usable observation of each acquired Subagent to the Subagent configured-agent outcome observer, and its observation and captured manifest of each Rule, Knowledge and Hook subject to that type's projection-plan contributor selection. The Hook manager's projection preparation hands its caller a frozen record of each Registry Hook observation it made, the usable root and content key or unusable: planHookInstall's projected configured-agent outcome evaluation chooses the package root from it, and a Pack plan decides each Registry Hook member's acquisition from it and hands the records of the members it lists for acquisition to acquisition planning on the closure step. For each Hook read from its own location rather than a Registry root, the projection preparation also hands planHookInstall the deep-frozen hook.json decode it made, keyed by name and package root, which the projected outcome evaluation takes on an exact match. Within one Hook projection preparation, a Registry Hook whose accepted package is usable at the ref's content key takes the hook.json decode its accepted-canonical observation captured of that root, after any decode its caller handed in for the same root. Within one Pack install planning call that makes its own graph selection, the workspace authority scan hands the Knowledge, Rule and Hook projection preparations the manifest its observation captured for each usable, enabled workspace-authored member they receive, decoded into a fresh map, and each manager takes a decode only for the same package root and type. Configured-Pack recovery planning's reuse decision for a non-workspace member whose accepted ref has the same content key reads the status of the observation that refused differing content for that member. A targeted update of a Pack whose selected release is held by the minimum release age judges the desired Pack node's accepted tree once in its preservation check, and its closure check skips only that node. One Knowledge sync call records each usable enabled bundle's observation from its restore loop, its discovery selection takes a copy of it for the same layout, filesystem port and still-active read phase and a structurally equal node and accepted row, and with nothing restored the apply's discovery-region plan takes that frozen selection. Knowledge uninstall preparation hands each target's removal description the path, status and shared-package verdict its ownership check observed; Pack uninstall planning hands each selected acquired Pack's removal description the verdict its retirement check observed, and every ordered target's removal description the frozen projection invariant facts it evaluates once. An authored native preflight run hands the Hook, Rule or Knowledge manager it calls the deep-frozen staged manifest decode its identity check made, or that adopt's validity boundary read, and a Subagent projection observation that validates destinations refuses and reports from one package load. An MCP install without a native component hands the canonical mcp.json manifest it decoded, deep-frozen, to each manifest-backed agent sync of the same call. The canonical scan hands its JSON parse of each acquired Knowledge bundle's knowledge.json, deep-frozen, to the Knowledge inventory document's manifest reader, which decodes the manifest from it instead of parsing the text again.
freshChecks: Each observation reads the tree it judges and hashes it afresh unless its caller hands a digest verified in the same read phase for the same root and accepted row; the observation never retains a capture, so a later observation reads again.
A caller uses a capture only when it names the same manifest path and type; otherwise it reads the manifest itself.
The subagent payload check re-reads subagent.json through its contained read, which the lexical capture cannot satisfy.
Check assessments re-observe canonical content through their verifying content view.

An enabling leaf activation observes and hashes the accepted canonical tree while settling the request and again while collecting its materialize step, except that step collection takes settlement's observation of a Hook, or of a Rule or Knowledge subject the inventory lists as installed, for the same type, name and phase-cached accepted row, whose tree the Hook's projected outcomes or the shared projection exposure still judge later in the phase; a materialize step's reuse decision under the lock hashes it once more, and the execution review of an executable Registry package hashes it again in between.
Subagent rendering observes the canonical tree again after the local inspection's read phase has closed.

A workspace or bundled package resolution that takes the observation's manifest decode still checks path safety, probes the package's presence, compares owner and name and hashes the whole package, and a settled or foreign observation, or one taken elsewhere, still resolves by reading the manifest itself.

A contributor selection takes the lint run's observation only when the run's observation succeeded for every node, its observation phase is still active, the read goes through that phase's port and the accepted row and layout are identical; otherwise, and in check and --fix repairs, it observes and hashes the tree itself, and a sync takes no lint handover.

A kept Pack member's retained-reference observation takes the retirement's digest only for an unblocked disable whose withdrawal description hashes the same root later in the phase, and still compares it with the accepted tree integrity and checks manifest and payload; the retirement hash, the withdrawal-description hash and the retirement's locked recheck stay.
The MCP server manager's configured-agent outcomes still read the manifest at the derived root themselves, while settlement, step collection and the execution review observe and hash the tree.

Acquisition planning observes and hashes the accepted tree, unless a matching Pack plan record decides it, whenever the proposal's content key equals the accepted ref's or that ref cannot be rebuilt, and source-switch classification does so whenever the proposal leaves the accepted locator.

The Subagent configured-agent outcome observer trusts a handed accepted-package observation only when its own read phase returns the identical desired node and accepted row, otherwise observing the package live, and the projection observation still reads the package through its contained read.
The applied configured-agent outcome evaluation of a Hook install observes the accepted canonical tree afresh, and the install's satisfied-install check under the transition lock observes it again.

Acquisition planning uses a Pack plan's record only on an exact type and name match and observes any other package itself; under the transition lock, the candidate freshness check reads each member's accepted package again and each acquisition's reuse decision observes and hashes the accepted tree afresh.
A Subagent removal uses the handed-back package only at the root its observation judged and loads any other root itself, and orphan cleanup observes every other declared Subagent live.
A Knowledge removal description still probes the canonical root's presence.
Under the transition lock, Pack uninstall observes each selected acquired Pack's canonical package again and prepares the Rule, Hook and Knowledge projection plans afresh.

Under the transition lock, an uninstall step observes and hashes its target's accepted canonical tree again for the shared-package check, and a materialize step's reuse decision hashes it again after interrupted-swap recovery.
Each authored native preflight run under the transition lock reads and identity-checks its staged manifest itself, and a new Subagent's run loads its own staging.

An MCP install's native-target planning, competing-entry checks and locked native writes with their readback stay fresh, and direct sync callers and native-component installs read and decode mcp.json themselves.
The Knowledge manifest reader uses the scan's parse only for the identical manifest path and text; otherwise, outside a read phase or after a failed scan parse, it parses the text itself.

A handed authoring-folder resolution answers only while the lint observation phase is active; a failed resolution, an ended phase or a run without a handoff resolves and hashes the package afresh, and the handed Subagent resolution still runs its path safety, presence and identity checks.

Source-switch classification's distribution tree digest replays the observation's walk only from a matching walk of an observation that ended usable, still resolves each contained link live, and walks the tree itself otherwise.
The source-switch ignore observation still probes every other spelling and each ancestor its walk never listed live.
A distribution tree walk still passes every walked name through the segment, Git administration, link-containment, stat and selection checks and hashes the whole selected tree.
Read-phase readers, ended phases, other desired-state readers and proposed nodes evaluate their own desired graph for an MCP accepted-row lookup.

The rule subject of each selected installed Knowledge bundle still reads and parses knowledge.json itself, and its package inspection reads the manifest itself when the subject found it absent or unreadable, read it through another filesystem or path, or the text failed to parse.
When both skill/frontmatter-parseable and skill/frontmatter-standard-valid are configured, each reads and parses the same SKILL.md frontmatter itself, since each parse emits its own YAML warnings.

The canonical scan still probes an acquired subagent.json it could not read, stats an acquired root that itself holds a package manifest, and observes content beneath src, an authored subagent's manifest and every later scan directly.

An owner-less Skill observation reads SKILL.md itself whenever a verified digest was handed in or its strict walk failed, did not match the accepted tree integrity or did not read that file as a regular file.
One local inspection's Pack member evidence observes each desired member's tree again even when the same query inspected that member.

In configured-agent verification after apply, the Subagent outcome observer observes again an acquired Subagent whose verification observation is not usable, and the Hook outcome evaluation's contributor selection observes every enabled acquired Hook contributor again, the verified subject included.

A Knowledge sync's discovery selection observes a bundle live whenever its recorded observation's layout, port, read phase, node or accepted row differs or a restore ended that phase, and after a restored bundle is published the discovery-region plan observes and inspects every bundle afresh.

Configured-Pack recovery still observes each member against the proposed graph's node after graph selection hashed it against the current one, and its closure validation observes every member again after the write.
A held Pack update still observes every member and any other Pack node sharing the name before the update is preserved or blocked.

The Hook manager install of an enabled workspace-authored Hook reads and decodes hook.json again inside the transaction, and the authority rescan under the transition lock and the in-transaction manager installs of a Pack read each member manifest afresh.
Orphan cleanup loads the Subagent package itself for a different root or a missing capture, and the next Subagent package load of the same root resolves, checks and reads every source again.
canonical-observation.lifetime: A capture, including the Subagent package an observation loaded, is returned to the caller of one observation and never retained by it; it belongs to the caller's operation or read phase and is released when that call completes, so the decode a usable accepted canonical lookup hands its workspace package resolution lives for that one lookup. The decode a desired observation or bundled Skill lookup hands its package resolution lives for that one call, and a kept root's pre-content judgement for one owner call. A handed strict walk serves one step classification's distribution tree digest, a mismatched digest one restore loop iteration, a source-switch comparison's manifest bytes that comparison, the listed ignore facts the rest of that observation, a carried directory listing one tree integrity computation, and an owner-less Skill walk's SKILL.md read one observation call. A prepared workspace ref lives for one listing call. A derived MCP canonical root lives for one configuredAgentOutcomes call, an MCP caller's graph for one helper call, and the lockfile an accepted-row lookup read for one observation call. Acquisition planning's recorded accepted refs, which hold only successful reconstructions, live for one planning call. A lint run's observation handover, including its authoring-folder resolutions, is honoured only while its observation read phase is active, and the knowledge.json text the lint read model hands a Knowledge package inspection lives for that bundle's populate step. The canonical scan's own read and classification facts live for one inspectAcquiredDirectory or scanAuthoredType call. Settlement's handed leaf observation lives for the activation's preparation read phase; a Pack disable's verified digests live for its planning phase; and the satisfied-install observation lives for that check's read view under the transition lock. Verification's handed Subagent observations live for one observeConfiguredTargets call, and its handed aggregate subject observations for the provider's one manager call, both inside the verification's fresh observation read view. A Hook observation record, like a non-Registry Hook's handed decode, lives for one planHookInstall call, a Registry Hook's captured decode and digests for one per-ref scope of the preparation, and a Pack plan's records live until acquisition planning removes them before sealing, so none reaches execution. A Pack plan's authority-scan decodes live for one Pack install planning call, and the transition keeps only the scan's fingerprint. Configured-Pack recovery's member observations are frozen, keyed by member ref and owned by one Pack's planning call inside the sync preflight read phase, and a held Pack update's verdict lives for one preservation call inside the update's read phase. A Knowledge sync's observation record lives for that manager call and stands in only while the read phase it was made in stays active. An orphan cleanup capture serves one declared Subagent's naming, and a Subagent package load's source contents live for that one load. The Knowledge ownership-check record lives until uninstall preparation completes, and Pack uninstall's observed verdicts and projection facts live for one planning call. An authored native preflight's manifest decode belongs to its validity boundary, one preflight run or adopt's prepare phase, and a Subagent projection observation's package load to one manager call. The handed MCP manifest, like the decode a non-Registry MCP reuse selects from, lives for one install call, and the scan's Knowledge parse for the read phase that recorded it.

adding-coding-agents-observes-hashes-acc.basis: Adding coding agents observes and hashes the accepted canonical tree of each selected installed Subagent that is not workspace-authored in the materialization planning observation, and the detailed Subagent inventory, a separate WorkspaceRecords call, observes and hashes it again through its own live readers, with no write between them. No read phase spans the two calls, and sharing the observation would extend physical-observation reuse across owner calls outside any phase and require observing every selected node before the concurrently evaluated per-type inventory starts, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
adding-coding-agents-observes-hashes-acc.openQuestion: May agents add, whose materialization planning runs outside any read phase, hand the canonical observation it makes of each selected installed Subagent to the detailed Subagent inventory (a separate WorkspaceRecords call that outside a read view observes through its own live readers), given that doing so for every Subagent requires observing all selected nodes before the concurrently evaluated per-type inventory starts?

agents-add-execution-review-hashes-regis.basis: Adding coding agents hashes each installed Registry MCP server's accepted canonical tree in the materialization planning observation and again in the execution review, with no write between them. The review runs on live observations after the planning view has retired and inside the fingerprint bracket the seal checks, so it independently establishes the exact executable content and its unchanged-execution judgement shown for consent instead of resting on an observation made before that bracket opened.

after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.basis: After apply, configured-agent verification observes the canonical tree of each extension the operation leaves enabled again in a fresh observation read view, reading its manifest and hashing the tree, before judging the agents' current outcomes. It is the operation's post-write readback of what is on disk after its closures settle; the apply's writes lie between it and the tree digest the apply recorded, so that digest belongs to an earlier validity boundary.

apply-enabling-installed-skill-observes-.basis: On apply, enabling an installed skill observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree under the transition lock in the canonical reuse decision, the only place that decides whether the accepted tree may be kept, after the settlement and the step collection hashed it in a planning read phase that confirmation has ended. Restoring a local skill hashes the tree once more in the accepted local package check, the verification after materialization and before the resolution is recorded, which also checks the required payload and the desired constraint.

apply-enabling-installed-sourced-mcp-ser.basis: On apply, enabling an installed sourced MCP server checks its accepted tree under the transition lock once more after planning hashed it, through the reuse decision for a Registry server and through the accepted canonical observation for any other server, hashing the tree each time. The planning digest belongs to a read phase that ended before the lock was acquired and a possible confirmation, so the check under the lock is the last tree-identity check before the accepted tree is kept and projected to the agents.

apply-repeat-install-mcp-server-whose.basis: On apply, a repeat install of an MCP server whose accepted tree is usable hashes that tree again under the transition lock, through the reuse decision for a Registry server and through the install's accepted canonical observation for any other server, after planning already hashed it. Planning's read phase has ended before the lock is acquired and a confirmation of unbounded length may lie between them, so the hash under the lock is the last tree-identity check that decides whether the install keeps the accepted tree or restores the accepted content.

canonical-observation-subagent-reads-man.basis: The canonical observation of a subagent reads its manifest again through a contained real path with a regular-file check to judge the required payload, after the lexical manifest read.
canonical-observation-subagent-reads-man.openQuestion: May the subagent canonical observation judge its required payload from the manifest text it already read, giving up the contained real-path and regular-file check that the second read performs today?

collecting-subagent-enable-s-materialize.basis: Collecting a Subagent enable's materialize step reads the detailed Subagent inventory, whose configured-agent observation observes and hashes the accepted canonical tree of a subject that is not workspace-authored again, after the settlement and the materialize planner already observed that tree in the same documents-only read phase. Adopting the settlement's observation would carry a physical tree observation across owner calls inside a phase whose physical reads are deliberately live, and would drop that phase's last integrity validation of the tree, which the accepted read-phase requirement does not decide.
collecting-subagent-enable-s-materialize.openQuestion: May the detailed Subagent inventory of a Subagent enable, a WorkspaceRecords owner call inside the enable's documents-only read phase whose physical reads are deliberately live, adopt the canonical observation (usable status and tree digest) that the settlement made of the same subject in that phase instead of observing and hashing the accepted tree again?

configured-knowledge-update-sweep-plans-.basis: A configured Knowledge update sweep plans each entry in its own Knowledge manager call, and each call's discovery-region contributor selection observes the canonical tree of every other enabled bundle and checks its integrity again inside the one planning read phase, with no write in between. The calls run concurrently, so any call's observation of a bundle can be the last integrity validation that admits it into the discovery region or excludes it as package-invalid, and Pack-supplied, unselected, non-Registry, reinstall and failed entries get no later acquisition observation.
configured-knowledge-update-sweep-plans-.openQuestion: May the concurrent Knowledge manager calls of one update planning read phase rely on one integrity validation of each contributor bundle, although which call's observation comes last is known only after the calls finish and some bundles get no later observation?

configured-rule-update-sweep-plans-each.basis: A configured Rule update sweep plans each entry in its own Rule manager call, and each call's Rules-region contributor selection observes the canonical tree of every other enabled Rule and computes its integrity again, refusing the planned projection when that tree no longer matches its accepted tree integrity. The calls run concurrently inside one document-only planning read phase with no write in between, so any call's observation of a contributor can be the last integrity validation before its planned projection; the accepted requirements keep a document-only phase free of physical caching and do not decide whether the calls may be handed one validation.
configured-rule-update-sweep-plans-each.openQuestion: May the concurrent Rule manager calls of one update planning read phase rely on one integrity validation of each contributor Rule, although which call's observation comes last is known only after the calls finish?

disabling-acquired-hook-whose-withdrawal.basis: Disabling an acquired Hook whose withdrawal removes or rewrites its native registrations describes the execution withdrawal by hashing the Hook's accepted canonical tree and reading its manifest again, after the contributor selection of the planning passes already observed that tree, and trusts the manifest's execution declaration for the preview only when the tree still matches the accepted tree integrity. The planning phase is a document-only read phase that shares no physical observations, so this is a live integrity validation and the last one inside that phase, while the earlier observation decides the projection refusal.

disabling-hook-rule-knowledge-extension-.basis: Disabling a Hook, Rule or Knowledge extension, or a Pack with such members, selects the contributors of each shared projection in every manager pass of its planning (the Hook withdrawal observation and the after and before exposure passes), and each selection observes every acquired contributor's canonical tree and computes its integrity again, inside one read phase with no write between them. Removing the repeat would let a physical observation made by one manager call serve sibling manager calls inside a mutation's document-only planning phase, and the accepted bounded-lifetime requirement keeps compatible nested calls from upgrading a document-only phase to physical caching without deciding whether sibling manager passes of one planning may share such an observation; no existing bounded lifetime carries a canonical observation across these passes, and the before pass judges different desired nodes.
disabling-hook-rule-knowledge-extension-.openQuestion: May one mutation's document-only planning read phase reuse the canonical observation (tree walk and integrity hash) that one manager pass made of a contributor in the later manager passes of the same disable planning (the Hook withdrawal observation and the after and before exposure passes), given that read-phases-have-bounded-lifetimes keeps document-only phases free of physical caching?

each-authored-native-preflight-run-enabl.basis: Within one authored native preflight run of an enabled Hook, Rule or Knowledge fork, the Hook, Rule or Knowledge manager prepares its projection from the staged manifest decode that the run's identity check made for the same package root and type, instead of reading the manifest again. The decode belongs to that run and is released when it returns; a decode for another root or type is not used, and the run under the transition lock reads and identity-checks the staged manifest fresh.

locked-preflight-run-reads-staged-manife.basis: The authored native preflight that an enabled Hook, Rule or Knowledge fork runs again under the transition lock reads the staged manifest and checks its identity afresh, although its prepare run read the same staging. Confirmation and the transition lock acquisition lie between the two runs, so the locked read is the fresh refusal of a staged identity rewritten after preparation, before anything is published.

each-authored-native-preflight-run-new.basis: In each authored native preflight run of a new Knowledge bundle, the Knowledge manager inspects the bundle from the deep-frozen knowledge.json decode the identity check read from the same staging when the package root and type match exactly, so the staged manifest is read once per run. The decode lives for that run; bundle inspection, the description diagnostic, the overlap check and the instruction-entry decision still run in order, and the run under the transition lock reads its own staging.

each-authored-native-preflight-run-new-2.basis: In each authored native preflight run of a new Rule, the Rule manager prepares its projection from the deep-frozen rule.json decode the identity check read from the same staging when the package root and type match exactly, so the staged manifest is read once per run. The decode lives for that run; the manager still resolves the source file target, checks overlap, reads the rule body and builds the plan, and the run under the transition lock reads its own staging.

each-authored-native-preflight-run-new-3.basis: In each authored native preflight run of a new Subagent, the identity check reads the staged subagent.json lexically and the Subagent manager loads the package again from the same staging through its contained loader. The contained load's real-path, regular-file and strict-decode read is the run's only containment check of the staged manifest, which the lexical read cannot satisfy, so a symlinked or non-regular subagent.json still refuses.
each-authored-native-preflight-run-new-3.openQuestion: May a new Subagent's authored native preflight derive its identity facts from the Subagent manager's contained package load instead of a separate lexical read of the staged subagent.json, accepting that a symlinked or strictly invalid manifest then refuses with the package-load message instead of the prepared-manifest one?

new-subagent-preflight-loads-staged-pack.basis: In each authored native preflight run of a new Subagent, the Subagent manager's projection observation loads the staged package once through its contained loader and runs the refusing destination preflight before the reporting one from that load, instead of loading the package again after a separate destination validation. The loaded package lives for that one manager call, and the run under the transition lock loads its own staging.

each-hook-materializable-listing-resolve.basis: The usable accepted canonical lookup that each Hook materializable listing makes for every enabled workspace-authored Hook, as for every other workspace-authored type, resolves the workspace package ref from the manifest decode its own canonical observation captured for the same root and type instead of reading the manifest again; the capture belongs to that one lookup call and is released when it returns. Path safety, the presence probe, the manifest identity comparison and the package content hash still run afresh.

each-knowledge-materializable-listing-re.basis: Each Knowledge materializable listing resolves every enabled workspace-authored Knowledge bundle through the usable accepted canonical lookup, which hands its workspace package resolution the knowledge.json decode its canonical observation made of the same root and type, so the resolution no longer reads knowledge.json again. The decode lives for that one lookup, and the resolution still checks path safety, presence and identity and hashes the package.

knowledge-manager-install-inspects-autho.basis: The Knowledge manager install of a workspace-authored bundle reads knowledge.json once more for its package inspection after the materializable listing decoded it. The inspection is the bundle's last integrity validation inside the transaction, refusing a manifest error or OKF error diagnostics before the accepted resolution is recorded, in a different owner call that serves every ref type.
knowledge-manager-install-inspects-autho.openQuestion: Does an accepted requirement oblige the Knowledge manager install to validate a workspace-authored bundle's manifest and OKF diagnostics inside the transaction, or may it inspect the bundle from the decode the materializable listing already made?

each-rule-materializable-listing-resolve.basis: Each Rule materializable listing resolves every enabled workspace-authored Rule through the usable accepted canonical lookup, which hands its workspace package resolution the rule.json decode its canonical observation made of the same root and type, so the resolution no longer reads rule.json again. The decode lives for that one lookup, and the resolution still checks path safety, presence and identity and hashes the package; an observation that is not usable resolves nothing.

rule-manager-install-reads-authored-mani.basis: The Rule manager install of a workspace-authored Rule reads rule.json once more after the materializable listing decoded it. That read is the package's last decode validation inside the transaction, refusing an invalid Rule definition before the accepted resolution is recorded, in a different owner call that serves every ref type.
rule-manager-install-reads-authored-mani.openQuestion: Does an accepted requirement oblige the Rule manager install to validate a workspace-authored Rule's rule.json inside the transaction, or may it take the decode the materializable listing already made?

enabled-hook-rule-knowledge-authored-nat.basis: In each validity boundary of adopting an enabled Hook, Rule or Knowledge extension, the authored native preflight takes the manifest decode the boundary already read from the package root, identity-checks and deep-freezes it, and hands it to the manager it calls, which prepares its projection from it only when the package root and type match exactly. Adopt owns one decode per validity boundary, its prepare phase or one in-lock preflight run, and releases it when that boundary ends; the manager still validates package files, overlap and targets, and each preflight run under the transition lock reads the manifest once for itself.

enabling-installed-sourced-mcp-server-ob.basis: Enabling an installed sourced MCP server observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree while settling the request and again while collecting its materialize step, inside one preparation read phase with no write between them. The step-collection observation is the last judgement of that tree in the phase: its status decides whether the step refuses present acquired drift, which restoration ref it carries and whether it materializes.

mcp-configured-agent-outcomes-derive-can.basis: The MCP server manager's configured-agent outcomes derive each sourced server's canonical root from its accepted row and the workspace layout, by the same lookup and pre-content rule the canonical observation uses, instead of observing and hashing the tree; the root lives for one configuredAgentOutcomes call. Settlement, step collection and the execution review still observe and hash the tree.

mcp-enable-execution-review-hashes-revie.basis: The execution review of an enabled sourced MCP server hashes its package again under live observations after the preparation read phase has closed: a Registry server's accepted tree once, which stands for the reviewed package when it matches the accepted integrity, and any other server's payload as a scratch copy. That digest establishes the identity of the exact payload the review judges, and the review's own before-review and sealed material fingerprints bracket only the interval after it.

enabling-knowledge-bundle-selects-discov.basis: Enabling a Knowledge bundle selects the discovery region's contributors in the step collection's projection preparation (or the exposure pass when no prepared plan exists) and again when the execution candidate projects configured-agent outcomes, and each selection observes every enabled bundle's canonical tree and computes the integrity of each acquired one, inside one read phase with no write between them. Sharing it would carry a physical canonical observation across two owner calls and a provider port inside a mutation's document-only planning phase, and the accepted bounded-lifetime requirement keeps compatible nested calls from upgrading a document-only phase to physical caching without deciding whether separate owner calls of one planning may share such an observation; the two selections judge different desired nodes (the proposed and the current graph), and no existing bounded lifetime spans both.
enabling-knowledge-bundle-selects-discov.openQuestion: May an activation's document-only planning read phase reuse the canonical observation that its step collection or exposure pass made of each enabled Knowledge bundle when the execution candidate's configured-agent outcome projection selects the same bundles from the current graph, given that read-phases-have-bounded-lifetimes keeps document-only phases free of physical caching?

enabling-leaf-extension-observes-canonic.basis: Enabling a Skill, Subagent or MCP server, or a Rule or Knowledge subject that the step-collection inventory does not list as installed under its local name, observes the subject's canonical tree against the accepted resolution, hashing it, while settling the request and again while collecting its materialize step, inside one preparation read phase with no write between them. The step-collection observation is the last judgement of that tree in the phase, because no aggregate manager selects a Skill, Subagent or MCP server subject again and an unlisted Rule or Knowledge subject rematerializes as a prospective contributor whose source is fetched instead of its canonical tree judged; its status decides whether the step refuses present acquired drift.

step-collection-takes-settled-hook-rule-.basis: Leaf activation settlement prepares one usable canonical observation of an enabled Hook, or of a Rule or Knowledge subject whose memoized step-collection inventory read succeeds and lists it as installed under its local name, and hands it to step collection, which uses it instead of hashing the accepted tree again only for the same type and name and the same phase-cached accepted row, and otherwise observes the tree itself. The handed observation lives for the activation's preparation read phase, and later in that phase the Hook's projected outcomes or the shared projection exposure still select the subject and judge its tree fresh.

enabling-pack-observes-each-member-s.basis: Enabling a Pack observes each selected member's canonical tree against the accepted resolution, hashing it, while collecting the member's materialize step from the proposed graph, and for a member also declared directly or routed by another active Pack it observes the current-graph node again for the activation's retained canonical references, inside one read phase with no write between them. That observation evaluates a node with different origins and constraint, can reach a different status, and is the member's last tree-integrity validation in the phase. For a member only this Pack routes the work is not repeated, because the retained-reference lookup finds no node in the current graph and observes nothing.
enabling-pack-observes-each-member-s.openQuestion: May a Pack enable report the retained canonical reference of a member that is also declared directly or routed by another active Pack from the observation its materialize planning made of the proposed node, although the current-graph node the reference evaluates carries different origins and constraint and can reach a different status?

enabling-rule-selects-instructions-regio.basis: Enabling a Rule selects the instructions region contributors in the shared-projection exposure pass and again when the execution candidate projects configured-agent outcomes, and each selection observes every enabled Rule canonical tree and computes the integrity of each acquired one, after the settlement and the step collection already observed the enabled Rule, inside one read phase with no write between them. The two selections evaluate different graphs, the proposed and the current one, so their contributor sets differ by the Rule being enabled, and the execution candidate's selection is the last tree-integrity validation of the other enabled Rules in the phase, refusing a contributor whose tree does not match.
enabling-rule-selects-instructions-regio.openQuestion: May the execution candidate's instructions region contributor selection, the last tree-integrity validation of the other enabled Rules in the activation planning read phase, take the canonical observation the exposure pass made of each of those Rules instead of observing and hashing the same tree again?

every-knowledge-manager-call-selects-dis.basis: In every Knowledge manager call that selects discovery contributors, the package inspection of each usable enabled bundle decodes knowledge.json from the canonical observation's capture when the capture names the same root and type, instead of reading it again; the capture belongs to that bundle's selection step and is released when the step completes. The observation still reads the manifest and hashes the tree afresh, and the bundle-body inspection, the invalid-definition mapping, the missing-description diagnostic and the exclusion probe still run.

every-rule-manager-call-selects-rules.basis: In every Rule manager call that selects Rules-region contributors, the selection decodes each contributor's rule.json from the frozen capture its own canonical observation made of the same root and type, and reads the manifest with the same invalid-definition mapping only when no matching capture exists; the capture lives for that one selection call. The canonical observation's tree hash and the RULE.md read still run afresh in every selection.

hook-configuration-every-hook-manager-co.basis: Hook configuration and every hook manager contributor selection, for projection planning and for configured-outcome inspection, decode hook.json from the canonical observation's capture instead of reading it again.

hook-configuration-observes-configured-h.basis: Hook configuration observes the configured hook's accepted canonical tree, hashing it, to find the installed package, and every hook manager contributor selection that follows observes that tree and each other enabled acquired hook contributor's tree and computes its integrity again: in the planning projection, twice for each Hook ref the execution review evaluates, and on apply once more under the transition lock. Each later observation is the last tree-integrity validation, refusing a contributor whose tree does not match, in its own boundary: the planning read phase, the execution review that runs after that phase has ended and between material fingerprints, and the locked interval before the settings write and native apply.

hook-install-apply-observes-installed-ho.basis: A Hook install apply observes the installed hook's accepted canonical tree, hashing it, when the Hook projection run selects contributors and again when the install step's artifact evaluates the hook's current configured-agent outcomes. The accepted resolution is published to axm.lock and the transaction validates and commits between the two, so the later observation judges the tree against the persisted resolution in a new read boundary, and in deferred projection modes the projection run's observation is the last integrity validation of the contributors before native writes. The manager's projection record, the only channel between the two, outlives one closure, so carrying the observation through it would create a cache lifetime beyond the owning phase.

inspection-compatibility-convergence-ass.basis: The inspection, compatibility and convergence assessments each observe the selected canonical tree through the verifying content view, so a change between owners makes coverage partial.
inspection-compatibility-convergence-ass.openQuestion: May one bounded canonical observation answer every check assessment?

installing-mcp-connection-without-native.basis: Installing an MCP connection without a native component decodes its canonical mcp.json once to select and bind its invocation, deep-freezes that manifest and hands it to each manifest-backed agent sync in the same install call, which projects it instead of reading and decoding the file again for each projected name; the manifest lives for that install call. Native-target planning, competing-entry checks and the locked native writes with their readback stay fresh, and direct sync callers and native-component installs still read and decode the file themselves.

knowledge-inventory-document-decodes-kno.basis: Inside one read phase, the canonical scan cell keeps its successful JSON parse of each acquired Knowledge bundle's knowledge.json by exact path and text, and the Knowledge inventory document's manifest reader decodes the manifest from that deep-frozen value instead of parsing the same captured text again. The parse lives for the read phase and is answered only for the identical path and text; outside a phase, after the phase ends or after a failed scan parse, the reader parses the text itself, while the full schema decode, owner defaulting and read-error mapping stay with the reader. The physical read and the full decode are not repeated: the phase serves the second read of knowledge.json from the text it captured, and the scan decodes only the bundle identity.

knowledge-lint-selects-each-enabled-inst.basis: Knowledge lint asks its installed-bundle selection for the knowledge.json its canonical observation captured and inspects each bundle from that decode when it names the same package root and type, so the manifest is read once per installed bundle; the captures belong to the one lint call and are released when it returns. When the observation's read or decode failed or names another root, the inspection reads knowledge.json itself with the same KnowledgeCorpusUnavailable failure, and each later observation still reads and hashes the tree afresh.

lint-observes-each-desired-node-s.basis: Lint observes each desired node's canonical tree once per run and every rule that reports a canonical observation reads that one observation.

lint-run-instruction-files-enabled-instr.basis: In a lint run with instruction files enabled, the projection invariant facts call the Rule and Knowledge contributor selections, and each selection decodes every contributor's manifest from the frozen capture its own canonical observation made of the same root and type within that call, reading the manifest only when no matching capture exists. Nothing from the ended lint observation phase is reused: each selection still observes and hashes every acquired contributor's tree, and Knowledge inclusion, exclusion and bundle-body inspection still run.

lint-run-projection-invariant-facts-sele.basis: Within one lint run's observation read phase, the Rule, Hook and Knowledge contributor selections of the projection invariant facts take their own copy of the run's canonical observation and captured manifest of the identical desired node, so each acquired contributor's tree is observed and hashed once per run. The lint run owns the handover and builds it only when its observation succeeded for every node; a selection consults it only while that phase is still active, through the port lint observed through, against the identical accepted row and layout. The authored-contributor and identity checks still run first, the missing-resolution, workspace-authority definition and exclusion outcomes still derive from the observation, Knowledge package inspection is unchanged, and an ended phase, check and --fix repairs observe and hash the tree afresh; a sync takes no lint handover and observes each usable bundle itself, once per manager call until its read phase ends or a restored bundle is published.

manifest-reader-reads-file-without-prece.basis: The manifest reader reads the file without a preceding existence probe, and the capturing canonical observation hands the manifest text it read to the owner that decodes it.

observing-installed-package-not-workspac.basis: Observing an installed package that is not workspace-authored reads its manifest and then hashes the whole canonical tree against the accepted tree integrity, which reads the manifest again. The tree walk is the observation's last integrity validation of the bytes on disk and hashes what it reads itself; the earlier read keeps decoded manifest text, which cannot reproduce those bytes for the digest.

one-local-inspection-observes-canonical-.basis: One show or subagents show inspection, or a check whose requested assessments observe nothing after the inspection, observes the canonical tree of each inspected acquired Hook, Rule, Knowledge or Subagent package in the agent-outcome provider, through contributor selection or accepted-reference resolution, and again for its own document, computing the tree integrity each time through one observation view. The document's observation is the last tree-integrity validation in the inspection read phase, and nothing later in the query observes the package again.
one-local-inspection-observes-canonical-.openQuestion: May a show inspection, or a check whose requested assessments observe nothing after it, report each inspected package's canonical status from the observation the agent-outcome provider made through the same observation view, instead of computing the tree integrity again as the read phase's last tree-integrity validation?

check-inspection-document-observes-provi.basis: In a check with a compatibility or convergence assessment, the inspection document observes each inspected acquired package's canonical tree again through the verifying content view after the agent-outcome provider observed it through the phase's shared observation view, and the assessment then observes the same nodes once more, so the document's observation is not the last. Whether the document's canonical status may rest on the provider's non-verifying observation is not decided by the accepted check requirements, and the same inspection code also serves show, where the document's observation is the last.
check-inspection-document-observes-provi.openQuestion: In a check whose compatibility or convergence assessment re-observes the selected nodes later in the same verifying assessment view, may the inspection document report the canonical status that the agent-outcome provider observed through the phase's shared observation view, instead of re-observing the tree through the verifying content view?

one-skills-materializable-listing-resolv.basis: One Skills materializable listing resolves each workspace-authored skill once through a prepared ref instead of hashing its package twice.

pack-disable-planning-hashes-each-unreac.basis: Pack disable planning observes and hashes a kept member's canonical tree for the activation's retained canonical reference after the same planning phase already judged that tree, with no write between them: the retirement check hashes a Hook or MCP server member kept for native references, and the before-graph contributor selection of the shared projection exposure judges a Rule or Knowledge member. The retained-reference observation is the last judgement of the tree in the phase whenever no withdrawal description reads that tree afterwards (a Skill, Subagent, Rule or Knowledge member, a Hook or MCP server member whose withdrawal changes no native registration, and every kept member of a blocked disable), and its status decides whether the plan reports the content as retained or unknown.
pack-disable-planning-hashes-each-unreac.openQuestion: May a Pack disable report a kept member's canonical content as retained from an earlier judgement of the same root and accepted row in the planning phase, such as the digest its retirement check verified, when the retained-reference observation is the last judgement of that tree in the phase?

pack-disable-skips-retired-member-retain.basis: Pack disable settlement derives each member's canonical root from one graph lookup and one accepted-row read and observes the content only when that root is not a retirement target, because a retired member's root is reported as removed rather than retained, so the retirement check alone hashes that tree in the planning phase. The derived root lives for one Pack settlement, every other root is observed in full, and the retirement step still hashes the tree again under the transition lock before removing it.

pack-disable-kept-member-takes-retiremen.basis: The retirement check of a Pack disable returns, beside its step, the tree digests it verified, looked up by type and accepted row, and Pack settlement hands one to a kept member's retained-reference observation only for an unblocked disable whose digest names the observed root and accepted row and whose execution-withdrawal description hashes that same root later in the phase. The digest lives for that planning phase and stands in only for the hash: the observation still compares it with the accepted tree integrity and checks manifest and payload, while the retirement hash, the withdrawal-description hash and the retirement's locked recheck all stay.

pack-disable-withdrawal-description-hash.basis: Describing the execution withdrawal of a Pack's Hook or MCP server member whose withdrawal changes native registrations hashes the member's accepted canonical tree and reads its manifest again, after the retirement check verified that tree in the same planning phase with no write between them. It is the last judgement of the tree in the phase and gates trusting the canonical manifest: its result decides whether the previous execution declaration and secret references are reported as known or unavailable.
pack-disable-withdrawal-description-hash.openQuestion: May the execution-withdrawal description of a Pack member trust the canonical manifest from the digest the retirement check verified for the same root and accepted row in the planning phase, when no accepted requirement states whether the reported previous execution declaration needs its own tree judgement?

pack-install-observes-configured-package.basis: A Pack install observes the configured package of each workspace-authored member the Pack declares while planning, to settle workspace source authority, and again under the transition lock before the first write, refusing the apply when that authority changed in between. The second scan is the stale-candidate check under the lock for the authority fingerprint and its blockers, which the execution candidate's freshness check over settings, lockfile and material paths does not cover, and the planning scan belongs to a read phase that ended before the lock and a possible confirmation.

pack-uninstall-observes-each-selected-ac.basis: Pack uninstall observes each selected acquired Pack's canonical package while planning and again under the transition lock before the first write, so a package whose readability changed in between refuses the apply instead of being retired on the planned decision.

pack-uninstall-planning-observes-each-se.basis: Pack uninstall planning describes each selected acquired Pack's removal from the path, status and shared-package verdict its retirement check observed in the same planning call, so the Pack's canonical tree is observed and hashed once while planning; workspace-authored Packs and member targets observe for themselves. The observed verdict lives for that planning call, and under the transition lock Pack uninstall still observes each selected acquired Pack's canonical package fresh before the first write.

pack-uninstall-planning-evaluates-projec.basis: Pack uninstall planning evaluates the projection invariant facts once per planning call and hands the frozen facts to the removal description of every ordered target, so the shared Hook, Rule and Knowledge contributors those facts select are observed and hashed once instead of once per removed target. The facts live for that planning call, and under the transition lock Pack uninstall still prepares the Rule, Hook and Knowledge projection plans fresh.

pack-uninstall-planning-selects-contribu.basis: The shared-projection exposure review of Pack uninstall preparation selects the contributors of each shared Hook, Rule and Knowledge projection in its current and proposed passes, observing and hashing each enabled acquired contributor's canonical tree again after Pack uninstall planning's projection facts observed it. The review is a separate owner call inside a documents-only planning read view whose physical ports stay live, and the proposed pass judges different desired nodes whose Pack origins and constraint can change, so sharing an observation or a tree digest across them is a new reading of the planning phase that the accepted requirements do not decide.
pack-uninstall-planning-selects-contribu.openQuestion: May one Pack uninstall preparation share each contributor's canonical observation, or its tree digest by canonical root, between Pack uninstall planning's projection facts and the separate shared-projection exposure review, and between that review's current and proposed passes, inside the documents-only planning read view?

planning-configured-hook-update-observes.basis: When a configured Hook update proposes a Registry ref whose content key equals the accepted ref's, acquisition planning observes and hashes each selected accepted Hook tree after the Hook install planning of that entry already observed it, inside the preparation read phase with no write between them. That observation decides between reusing intact accepted content and reacquiring edited content, and it is the last judgement of the tree in the planning read phase.

hook-update-version-advance-skips-accept.basis: For a Registry proposal of a sourced node, acquisition planning reconstructs the accepted ref from its accepted row, read from the planning read phase's documents, before it observes anything, and observes and hashes the accepted tree only when that ref's content key equals the proposal's; a configured Hook update that advances a version therefore acquires without observing the accepted Hook tree. An equal-key proposal, and any node that is not sourced or whose accepted ref cannot be reconstructed, still observe the tree fresh in that phase.

hook-update-entries-reselect-retained-ho.basis: Each updated entry's projection preparation selects the retained Hook contributors by observing every other acquired Hook's accepted tree and computing its integrity again, inside the same preparation read phase. Each selection decides whether that entry's projection plan renders or refuses with a contributor tree mismatch, and the entries are planned concurrently, so no shared judgement of a contributor is guaranteed to follow the others.
hook-update-entries-reselect-retained-ho.openQuestion: May the concurrently planned entries of a configured Hook update share one judgement of each retained Hook contributor's accepted tree, given that each entry's projection plan refuses on a contributor tree mismatch?

planning-pack-install-observes-registry-.basis: Within one Pack install planning read phase, the Pack plan decides each Registry Hook member's acquisition from the usable observation of its accepted canonical tree that the Hook projection preparation made in the same call, and observes and hashes only a member that preparation did not observe, such as one disabled in the proposed graph. The Pack plan hands a frozen type, name and usable record for each member it lists for acquisition on the closure step, and acquisition planning uses a record only on an exact type and name match, keeps its content-key test and accepted-resolution comparison, and removes the records before trust, source-switch, gating and sealing, so no observation reaches execution. Under the transition lock, the candidate freshness check reads each member's accepted package again and each acquisition's reuse decision observes and hashes the accepted tree afresh.

planning-pack-update-observes-each-uncha.basis: Within an update's planning read phase, each Pack plan decides whether an unchanged Registry Hook member's accepted content may be reused from the observation its own Hook projection preparation made of a member with the same type and name in the same call, instead of observing and hashing that tree again; sibling Pack plans never see each other's observations. The observation lives for that one Pack plan call and its acquisition settlement, which removes it before sealing, and under the transition lock the candidate freshness check reads each member's accepted package again and each acquisition's reuse decision observes and hashes the accepted tree afresh.

pack-update-contributor-selections-reobs.basis: Each updated Pack's Hook, Rule and Knowledge projection preparation selects the retained contributors by observing every other acquired contributor's accepted tree and computing its integrity again, although sibling Pack plans in the same update planning read phase observe the same contributors. The Pack plans run concurrently, each judges contributors against its own proposed graph, whose desired node for a contributor can differ, and sharing them would need an observation memo keyed by desired node and accepted entry in a document-only planning phase, which the accepted read-phase requirement does not provide for.
pack-update-contributor-selections-reobs.openQuestion: May each updated Pack's Hook, Rule and Knowledge contributor selection in one update planning phase reuse a canonical observation that another Pack's plan made of the same retained contributor with an equal desired node and accepted entry, given that the phase is document-only and each plan judges contributors against its own proposed graph?

planning-repeat-install-registry-package.basis: Source-switch classification reads desired-node and accepted-row presence from the planning read phase's documents and takes the accepted ref that acquisition planning recorded for the same type and name, or reconstructs it, before it observes anything, and runs the accepted-content observation only once the proposal leaves the accepted locator; a repeat install of a Registry package at its accepted locator therefore classifies without observing or hashing the accepted tree again. Acquisition planning's reuse decision remains the judgement of that tree in the phase.

source-switch-classification-observes-ac.basis: When an install's proposal leaves the accepted source locator, source-switch classification observes and hashes the accepted canonical tree after any observation the install's step planning made of it in the same planning read phase. Its status refuses replacement of locally modified acquired content, its path feeds the switch artifact and content comparison, and when that comparison is with a Registry its strict walk also serves the distribution tree digest, so nothing later in the phase judges that tree again.

render-subagent-s-canonical-tree-observe.basis: With --render, the subagent's canonical tree is observed again through the accepted canonical observation after the local inspection observed it and its read phase closed. The inspection's read phase has ended, so rendering from its observation would extend an ended phase; the render observes live state, and the rendered package bytes are read after that observation.

repeat-install-accepted-registry-skill-r.basis: A repeat install of an accepted Registry Skill, Rule, Hook, Knowledge package, Subagent, MCP server or Pack observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree in the selection read phase to settle the accepted request, and again in the planning read phase to decide whether acquisition may reuse that content. The selection read phase has retired before planning opens its own, so its verdict cannot stand in for the reuse decision; where the migration of a deprecated Registry extension plans its replacement install inside one read view, the planning observation is still the last judgement of that tree in that view.

resolving-workspace-authored-package-rea.basis: Resolving a workspace-authored package reads its manifest and then hashes the whole tree, which reads the manifest again, because the full-tree hash is the resolution's readability gate.
resolving-workspace-authored-package-rea.openQuestion: Should computePackageContentHash accept the manifest bytes the same workspace package resolution already read, changing its directory walk?

rule-knowledge-subagent-managers-read-th.basis: Rule, Knowledge and Subagent managers read their package manifest once per owner call inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase.
rule-knowledge-subagent-managers-read-th.openQuestion: May an owner-call dry-run preimage map share native file bytes inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase?

under-transition-lock-each-hook-manager.basis: Under the transition lock, each Hook manager run of a Hook uninstall (the refusal observation of the proposed graph, the withdrawal run and the re-render after the settings removal) selects the Hook contributors again, and each selection observes every acquired contributor's canonical tree and computes its integrity again; that observation is the only judge of whether accepted content may be rendered. The withdrawal run's selection is the last integrity validation before its native write, and the re-render follows the transition's own writes to native configuration, the canonical tree, settings and lockfile, so it judges the remaining desired routes against the state those writes produced.

under-transition-lock-each-rule-manager.basis: Under the transition lock, each Rule manager run of a Rule uninstall (the refusal observation of the proposed graph before the first write and the region re-render after the settings removal) selects the Rule contributors again, and each selection observes every acquired remaining contributor's canonical tree and computes its integrity again.
