The transition's own canonical retirement, settings removal and accepted-resolution removal lie between the two runs, so the re-render judges contributors against the written state, proves that the retirement left shared package roots usable, and is the last integrity validation before the region write.

under-transition-lock-install-repeats-ac.basis: Under the transition lock, an install that repeats an accepted extension from the same exact source observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree again in the satisfied-install check, after the candidate freshness check under the same lock has already read every file of that tree as a material path. The satisfied-install check is the no-op decision and its last identity and integrity check in that boundary: planning's usable verdict belongs to a read phase that ended before the lock was acquired, and an unchanged fingerprint does not establish the same verdict when a symlinked canonical root was retargeted, which would turn a required restore into a no-op.

under-transition-lock-removing-direct-ro.basis: Under the transition lock, removing the direct route of an extension that an installed Pack still reaches observes the accepted canonical tree for the shared-package check, observes it again when the retained materialization looks up the usable accepted ref, and for a Registry package hashes the same tree once more in the canonical reuse decision. The settings write that removes the direct route lies between the first observation and the later ones, so the retained materialization judges the Pack-only route against the desired node that write produced, and the reuse decision is the only place the decision to keep an accepted tree is made and the last integrity validation before materialization.

under-transition-lock-satisfied-install-.basis: Under the transition lock, the satisfied-install check of a repeat install of an accepted Subagent that is not workspace-authored hands the usable accepted-package observation that gates its no-op, frozen, to the Subagent configured-agent outcome observation it requests, which derives the usable accepted ref from it instead of observing and hashing the accepted tree again. The handoff lives for that one check's read view, and the observer uses it only when its own read phase finds the same desired node and accepted row, observing the package live otherwise; the no-op usability gate and the projection observation's contained package read stay.

under-transition-lock-uninstall-step-obs.basis: Under the transition lock, an uninstall step observes its target's canonical tree for the shared-package check before the transaction begins, and the target's manager observes and hashes the same tree again inside the transaction to decide which canonical path to retire and whether another accepted binding still shares it. The manager's observation is the last route and identity check before the destructive retirement and, for Hooks and Packs, before the native package reference refusal, so it runs under the transaction's rollback protection and, for Hooks, after the manager withdraws the native Hook registrations.

uninstall-planning-observes-target-s-acc.basis: Uninstall planning observes and hashes the target's accepted canonical tree to describe the removal, and under the transition lock the uninstall step observes and hashes the same tree again for its shared-package check. The planning read phase has ended and a confirmation of unbounded length and the lock acquisition lie between them, so the step's observation is the fresh check inside the locked boundary that no other accepted binding still owns the package before canonical content is removed.

uninstall-preparation-knowledge-bundle-o.basis: Knowledge uninstall preparation hands the removal description of each target bundle the path, status and shared-package verdict its ownership check observed over the current graph, as an immutable record the Knowledge uninstall planner creates and the preparation releases when it completes, instead of observing and hashing the target's tree again. The removal description still probes the canonical root's presence, and other types, Pack member removals and targets without a prepared observation observe the tree themselves.

knowledge-uninstall-exposure-passes-obse.basis: In Knowledge uninstall preparation, the Knowledge contributor selections of the exposure review's proposed and current passes and of the projection invariant facts each observe every enabled acquired bundle's canonical tree and compute its integrity again, inside one document-only read phase with no write between them. They are separate owner calls over different desired graphs and service contexts, so sharing their observations needs a phase-scoped observation store, and whether such a keyed handoff upgrades the document-only phase to physical caching is not decided by the accepted read-phase requirement.
knowledge-uninstall-exposure-passes-obse.openQuestion: May one Knowledge uninstall preparation share each enabled bundle's canonical observation and tree integrity across the exposure review's proposed and current passes and the projection invariant facts, given that workspace/workspace-state/read-phases-have-bounded-lifetimes forbids upgrading a document-only phase to physical caching?

uninstalling-hook-observes-each-acquired.basis: Uninstalling a Hook observes each acquired Hook contributor's canonical tree and checks its tree integrity in every contributor selection of its preparation (the after and before exposure passes and the invariant-fact Hook participant), observes the removed Hook's tree once more to describe its removal, and evaluates each Hook ref twice more in the execution review's current-outcome evaluation. Each selection's observation is the integrity validation that admits a tree as projection input, refusals between the selections make an earlier one the last validation of the read phase, and the removal description's observation decides whether the tree becomes a removal target; the review evaluations run after the preparation read phase has ended.
uninstalling-hook-observes-each-acquired.openQuestion: May the later Hook contributor selections and the removal description of one Hook uninstall preparation rely on an earlier integrity validation of the same tree in that read phase, although refusal paths leave no selection that every execution reaches last?

uninstalling-rule-observes-each-acquired.basis: Uninstalling a Rule observes each acquired Rule contributor's canonical tree and checks its tree integrity in every Rule contributor selection of its preparation (the exposure review's proposed and current passes, the invariant-fact Rule participant and, for a Rule an installed Pack still reaches, the retained native-output capture and the configured-agent outcome projection), and observes the removed Rule's tree once more to describe its removal, inside one read phase with no write between them. Each observation is the integrity validation of that tree: the last selection is the outcome projection or the invariant-fact participant, while refusals and failures between the selections, or an outcome evaluation without configured agents, make an intermediate one the last, and the removal description's observation decides whether the tree is a removal target.
uninstalling-rule-observes-each-acquired.openQuestion: May the later Rule contributor selections and the removal description of one Rule uninstall preparation rely on an earlier integrity validation of the same tree in that read phase, although refusals and skipped outcome projections leave no selection that every execution reaches last?

unpack-observes-pack-against-accepted-re.basis: Unpack observes the Pack against its accepted resolution while planning, hashing an acquired tree, to prove its accepted identity readable, and the Pack uninstall step observes the same tree again under the transition lock. The planning read phase ends before confirmation and the promotion steps write settings before the step runs, so the locked observation is the fresh ownership and identity check before the canonical Pack is removed and decides its shared-package retention.

unpack-proves-each-workspace-authored-pa.basis: Unpack proves each workspace-authored Pack or member usable through the usable accepted canonical lookup, which hands its workspace package resolution the manifest decode its canonical observation captured when the capture sits at the resolved package directory for the desired type, so the resolution does not read the manifest again. The decode lives for that one lookup call, and the resolution still probes the package's presence, checks path safety, compares owner and name and hashes the whole package.

updating-registry-mcp-server-whose-selec.basis: Updating a Registry MCP server whose selected version is the accepted one observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree while planning to decide that acquisition may reuse it, the execution review hashes it again, and an apply hashes it once more in the reuse decision under the transition lock. The execution review is an independent observation after the planning read phase has ended, and the locked reuse decision runs after confirmation and lock acquisition as the last integrity validation before the accepted tree is kept, so a tree edited before apply is re-acquired instead of becoming accepted authority.

when-installed-pack-still-reaches-enable.basis: When an installed Pack still reaches the enabled Subagent an uninstall removes, preparation observes and hashes the Subagent's accepted canonical tree to describe the removal, and the Subagent configured-agent observation observes and hashes it again for the retained-output capture and once more for the execution candidate's outcome projection, inside one read phase with no write between them. The outcome projection's observation is the last integrity validation of the tree in the phase, and the retained-output capture's is the last when a cleanup refusal or an outcome evaluation without configured agents leaves the projection out; that capture also chooses the ref whose native outputs become the retention evidence closure validation consumes.
when-installed-pack-still-reaches-enable.openQuestion: May the retained-output capture and the outcome projection of a Subagent uninstall that an installed Pack still reaches rely on the integrity validation that describing the removal made earlier in the same read phase, although either of them can be the last validation of that tree?

when-materialize-step-s-registry-subagen.basis: When a materialize step's Registry Subagent ref names the accepted version, the reuse decision under the transition lock hashes the accepted canonical tree again after planning's canonical observation already hashed it to judge it usable. Keeping the accepted tree is a prepared no-op that passes the same freshness boundary as a write: planning's digest belongs to an ended read phase on the far side of a confirmation and the lock acquisition, and interrupted-swap recovery may write the judged tree in between.

when-proposed-registry-hook-same-name.basis: When a proposed Registry Hook of the same name is already installed, the Hook manager's projection preparation observes and hashes its accepted canonical tree once and hands the calling planHookInstall a frozen record of each Registry Hook observation it made: the usable root and the content key of the ref it restores, or unusable. The projected configured-agent outcome evaluation of the same call applies the same content-key test to that record to take the accepted root or fetch the source, still reads the manifest from the chosen root, and observes any Hook the preparation did not observe. The record lives only for that planning call and never carries fetched directories; the applied outcome evaluation observes the tree afresh, and the install's satisfied-install check under the transition lock observes it again.

withdrawing-subagent-s-native-outputs-ob.basis: An uninstall or disable of a Subagent observes its accepted canonical tree once under the transition lock, and that one observation names the native outputs to withdraw, from the Subagent package its payload check loaded at the same root, and for an uninstall also decides canonical retirement. The package is handed only to the removal and released when it returns; on any other root the removal loads the package itself, a package that cannot be loaded or a manifest that escapes its package falls back to the Subagent's own name, and orphan cleanup still observes every other declared Subagent live.

desired-observation-resolves-usable-pack.basis: Pack install graph selection, Pack member inspection and the step collection of a node no caller settled observe each desired node and resolve its usable package in one call, which hands the workspace package resolution the manifest decode the observation made of the same root and type, so the resolution does not read and decode the manifest again. The decode lives for that one call, and the resolution still checks path safety, probes presence, compares owner and name and hashes the whole package, while a settled or foreign observation still resolves by reading the manifest itself. Inside a planning or inspection read view the saving is one cached text request and its decode, and outside one it is a physical manifest read.

bundled-skill-resolution-takes-observati.basis: The usable accepted canonical lookup of a bundled Skill, and the observation of a desired bundled Skill that resolves its usable package in the same call, hand the bundled package resolution the skill.json decode the observation made of the same root, so the resolution does not read and decode skill.json again. Only the manifest decode is handed, never a hash, and it lives for that one call; the resolution still checks path safety, probes presence, compares owner and name and hashes the whole package, and an observation taken elsewhere still resolves by reading the manifest itself.

kept-root-observation-reuses-pre-content.basis: Pack activation derives each member's canonical root for its retained references by judging the member's accepted row before any content is read, and the observation of a kept root reuses that judgement when the path service, layout, desired node and accepted row are the same values it was made from, judging again otherwise. The judgement is a pure derivation that lives for one owner call, and the presence probe, the content reads, the payload checks and the tree-integrity check still run.

acquisition-planning-shares-reconstructe.basis: Within one acquisition planning call, the reuse decision for a sourced Registry node records each accepted ref it reconstructs from the planning read phase's accepted row, deep-frozen, and takes its usable verdict from the accepted-content observation without rebuilding that ref; publisher trust and source-switch classification use a recorded ref only on an exact type and name match and reconstruct any other target with their own error mapping and order. Only successful reconstructions are recorded, the record list lives for that one call, and every observation and hash of the accepted tree still runs.

lint-knowledge-inspection-decodes-subjec.basis: While the lint read model is populated, each selected installed Knowledge bundle's package inspection decodes the knowledge.json text its rule subject has just read through the same filesystem at the identical path, taking the canonical scan's deep-frozen parse when the scan parsed that exact text at that path and parsing the text itself otherwise, instead of reading and parsing the manifest again. The lint read model owns the handed text, which lives for that one bundle's populate step; when the subject found the manifest absent or unreadable, or read it through another filesystem or path, the inspection probes and reads it itself, and a failed parse is never shared, so after invalid JSON the inspection parses the text itself. Schema decode, the missing-description diagnostic and the inspection's failure handling are unchanged.

lint-knowledge-subject-parses-manifest-a.basis: The rule subject of each selected installed Knowledge bundle reads and JSON-parses knowledge.json itself, although the read model's canonical scan, and in a lint run the run's canonical observation, already parsed the identical text; inside an active observation phase the phase serves the subject's read from the bytes it already read, and outside one the file is read again. The subject's parse is the mutable loose manifest value the Knowledge rules receive, and invalid JSON keeps its parse-failure marker, so taking the scan's deep-frozen identity parse would change what the rules receive.
lint-knowledge-subject-parses-manifest-a.openQuestion: May the Knowledge rule subject take the canonical scan's deep-frozen parse of knowledge.json in place of its own read and parse, given that the rules would then receive a frozen manifest value instead of their own mutable one?

accepted-row-lookup-keys-mcp-by-caller-g.basis: Outside a read phase, an accepted canonical observation or accepted-ref reconstruction of an MCP connection evaluates the desired graph once: the live lockfile reader keys the connection's accepted row by the graph its caller just evaluated without options from the same desired-state reader, and an accepted-ref reconstruction builds the ref from the row its single lookup read. The graph lives for that one helper call; read-phase readers, ended phases, other desired-state readers and proposed nodes evaluate their own graph, and the lockfile row read, the canonical observation, the source and settings entry reads and the graph-then-lockfile failure order stay.

shared-package-verdict-takes-row-lookup-.basis: An accepted canonical observation's accepted-row lookup hands the lockfile it read to the same call, and the shared-package verdict judges other package bindings against that lockfile instead of reading axm.lock again, reading one itself only when the lookup read none. The lockfile lives for that one observation call, so under the transition lock the verdict still rests on a lockfile read in that call, after the tree observation it follows.

pack-member-evidence-observes-inspected-.basis: One local inspection's Pack member evidence observes each desired member's canonical tree and computes its tree integrity, even when that member is also an inspected item whose canonical observation the same query already made, as when show selects several subjects or check expands its scope to Pack members. That member observation may be the last tree-integrity validation of the member in the query.
pack-member-evidence-observes-inspected-.openQuestion: May one local inspection's Pack member evidence reuse the canonical observation it already made of a member that is also an inspected item, instead of computing that member's tree integrity again?

distribution-tree-walk-lists-each-direct.basis: A distribution tree integrity computation lists each directory of its walk once: a subdirectory's listing, taken when its emptiness is tested, is carried with its pending entry and walked directly, and lives only for that one computation. Every walked name still passes the segment, Git administration, link-containment, stat and selection checks in listing order, and the whole selected tree is still hashed.

source-switch-comparison-reads-distribut.basis: When source-switch classification compares a non-Registry side with a Registry side, it reads that side's distribution manifest once, and within that one comparison the bytes serve both its publication policy and, as a copy, the manifest's entry in the distribution tree hash. The hash takes those bytes only for a regular file at exactly the manifest's root-relative path, after its listing, link-containment, stat and selection checks, and reads every other entry as before.

hook-install-planning-takes-prepared-man.basis: Within one planHookInstall call, the Hook manager's projection preparation hands its caller a frozen list of the deep-frozen hook.json decodes it made, each keyed by name and package root, for every Hook read from its own location rather than from a Registry root (a local, workspace, Git-hosted or HTTP Hook), and the projected configured-agent outcome evaluation of the same call takes a decode only on an exact name and root match instead of reading and decoding the manifest again. Registry Hooks, whose root may be a fetch released with the preparation, and unmatched refs still read the manifest, and the decodes live only for that planning call. The applied outcome evaluation after the write reads hook.json afresh, and execution reads the package again under the transition lock.

knowledge-sync-observes-each-usable-bund.basis: One Knowledge sync call observes each usable enabled bundle's canonical tree once in its restore loop, recording the observation only while the read phase it was made in stays active, and its discovery selection takes a copy of that observation and a fresh manifest capture for the same layout, filesystem port and still-active read phase (or no phase on either side) and a structurally equal node and accepted row; with nothing restored, the apply's discovery-region plan takes that frozen selection instead of selecting again. The record lives for that manager call, a selection that misses any of those conditions observes live, each usable bundle's package inspection still runs once in the discovery selection, and after a restored bundle is published the plan observes and inspects every bundle afresh.

sync-apply-observes-usable-bundles-after.basis: When a sync apply publishes a restored Knowledge bundle, the discovery-region plan resolves, selects and observes the published state for itself, so each usable bundle's canonical tree is observed and inspected again after the publication although the publication did not write it.
sync-apply-observes-usable-bundles-after.openQuestion: May a sync apply's post-publication discovery-region plan reuse the pre-publication observation of a usable Knowledge bundle that the publication of a restored bundle did not write?

ended-sync-read-phase-observes-bundle-li.basis: When restoring a Knowledge bundle writes through the read phase's filesystem port and so ends the phase in which the restore loop observed a usable bundle, the discovery selection observes that bundle's canonical tree live again, because an observation recorded for an ended phase no longer stands in.

non-registry-mcp-reuse-selects-observati.basis: A non-forced install of a local, Git or HTTP sourced MCP server whose accepted canonical tree is usable for the requested content selects its distribution and invocation from the mcp.json decode that the MCP server manager's accepted canonical observation made at that canonical root, instead of probing, reading and decoding the manifest again; the captured manifest lives for that one install call. The observation's tree hash under the transition lock stays the last integrity check, and forced, acquiring, Registry, workspace and native-component installs still read the manifest themselves.

hook-manager-install-reads-authored-mani.basis: The Hook manager install of an enabled workspace-authored Hook reads and decodes hook.json once more after the materializable listing in the same transaction decoded it. That read is the package's last decode validation inside the transaction, refusing an invalid Hook definition before the accepted resolution is recorded, in a different owner call that serves every ref type.
hook-manager-install-reads-authored-mani.openQuestion: Does an accepted requirement oblige the Hook manager install to validate a workspace-authored Hook's hook.json inside the transaction, or may it take the decode the materializable listing already made of the same root?

lint-frontmatter-rules-each-parse-skill-.basis: When the lint configuration defines both skill/frontmatter-parseable and skill/frontmatter-standard-valid, each of the two rules reads, decodes and YAML-parses the same skill's SKILL.md frontmatter on one rule context in one run, after skill/skill-md-present probed the file. Each YAML parse emits the frontmatter's YAML warnings on standard error, so sharing one parse would change the warning output.
lint-frontmatter-rules-each-parse-skill-.openQuestion: May axm lint emit a SKILL.md frontmatter YAMLWarning on stderr once per skill instead of once for each configured frontmatter rule (skill/frontmatter-parseable and skill/frontmatter-standard-valid), or must each rule's parse keep emitting its own warning?

canonical-scan-reuses-own-reads-and-clas.basis: Within one inspection of an acquired directory, a portable skill's SKILL.md or an acquired subagent's subagent.json that the canonical scan has just read successfully counts as present without another existence probe, and a pack, MCP server or subagent package directory that its parent's classification stat'd as a directory, like an authored package directory the authored root's classification just stat'd, is not stat'd again. These facts live for one inspectAcquiredDirectory or scanAuthoredType call inside the read model's cached canonical scan, so occurrences, subject-file presence and diagnostics are unchanged, while content beneath src, an authored subagent's manifest and every later scan are still observed directly.

canonical-scan-probes-unreadable-subagen.basis: When the canonical scan cannot read an acquired subagent's subagent.json, building its occurrence still probes the same path for existence, because a failed read does not tell an absent manifest from one that is present but unreadable, such as a directory named subagent.json or a file the scan may not read.
canonical-scan-probes-unreadable-subagen.openQuestion: May the canonical scan decide an acquired subagent's subject-file presence from the cause of its failed manifest read instead of probing the same path again?

canonical-scan-stats-enumerated-acquired.basis: When the acquired root itself holds a pack, MCP server or subagent manifest, the canonical scan stats the root as that package's content directory after its own listing of the root has succeeded, because the root, unlike every directory beneath it, was enumerated rather than classified by a stat.
canonical-scan-stats-enumerated-acquired.openQuestion: May the canonical scan treat an acquired root whose directory listing has just succeeded as a directory, without stat'ing it again, when the root itself holds a package manifest?

pack-recovery-reuse-reads-member-blockin.basis: Configured-Pack recovery planning observes each member's canonical tree once against its proposed node and accepted row to refuse present content that differs, and the reuse decision for a non-workspace member whose accepted ref has the same content key reads that observation's status instead of hashing the tree again. The observations are frozen, keyed by member ref and owned by one Pack's planning call inside the sync preflight read phase. Lock-time acquisition and reuse of the members it lists, and the recovery closure's validation, which observes every member again after the write, stay fresh.

verification-hands-usable-subagent-obser.basis: In configured-agent verification after apply, observeConfiguredTargets hands its frozen usable observation of each acquired Subagent it verifies, on that Subagent's request row, to the Subagent configured-agent outcome observer, which derives the usable accepted ref from it instead of observing and hashing the accepted tree again. The handoff lives for one observeConfiguredTargets call inside the verification's fresh observation read view, and the observer takes it only when its own phase readers return the identical desired node and accepted row, observing the package live otherwise. The verification's own post-write observation and integrity comparison, the projection observation's contained package read, and the observer's own observation of workspace-authored and bundled Subagents stay.

verification-outcome-observer-reobserves.basis: In configured-agent verification after apply, an acquired Subagent whose observation is not usable carries no handed observation, so the Subagent configured-agent outcome observer observes its accepted tree and hashes it again in the same fresh observation read view before concluding that it has no usable accepted ref. The verification's own observation stays the post-write integrity check, and the observer's second observation reads the same shared physical reads of that phase.
verification-outcome-observer-reobserves.openQuestion: May the Subagent configured-agent outcome observer take the verification's own observation of an acquired Subagent it found unusable, as it does for a usable one, instead of observing and hashing the accepted tree again in the same fresh observation read view?

verification-hands-aggregate-subject-obs.basis: In configured-agent verification after apply, observeConfiguredTargets hands its own observation and captured manifest of each Rule, Knowledge and Hook subject it verifies to that type's projection-plan contributor selection, which takes its own copy instead of decoding the manifest and hashing the tree again. The live provider installs the handoff around that one manager call for captures from its own active fresh observation phase, a selection uses it only through that phase's port against the identical accepted row and layout, and every other contributor is still observed. Unlike a show inspection, whose document observation is the read phase's last tree-integrity validation, the handed observation is itself the verification's post-write integrity check, and the phase's memoized readDirectory, lstat, readLink, readFile and readFileString would return the same bytes to a second observation.

verification-hook-outcomes-selection-reo.basis: In configured-agent verification after apply, the Hook configured-agent outcome evaluation that follows the projection-plan observation in the same provider call takes no handed observation, so its contributor selection observes and hashes the canonical tree of every enabled acquired Hook contributor again, the verified subject included, in the same fresh observation read view. The handoff covers only the projection-plan selection, and the verification's own observation stays the post-write integrity check.
verification-hook-outcomes-selection-reo.openQuestion: May the Hook configured-agent outcome evaluation inside post-apply verification take the verification's own observation of each selected Hook subject, as the projection-plan selection of the same provider call does, instead of observing and hashing its canonical tree again in the same fresh observation read view?

usable-registry-hook-preparation-takes-o.basis: Within one Hook projection preparation, a Registry Hook whose accepted package is usable at the ref's content key takes the hook.json decode its accepted-canonical observation captured instead of reading and decoding the manifest again, only for the hook.json of the usable root that observation chose in the same per-ref scope, and a decode the caller handed in for the same root still comes first. A content-key mismatch fetches the release and reads its own manifest, the decode lives only for that per-ref scope, and package-file validation, the strict tree walk, the outcome evaluation's own manifest read, materialization and every locked observation still read the package live.

source-switch-ignore-observation-probes-.basis: When source-switch classification discovers a non-Registry side's ignore inputs, the ignore observation takes the link and kind of each exactly named .gitignore its own walk listed from that walk instead of calling readLink and stat on it again, and keeps those facts only for the rest of that observation. Other spellings and the ancestors the walk never listed are still probed live, and each ignore file's contents are read once as before.

held-pack-update-observes-accepted-pack-.basis: A targeted Pack update whose selected release is held by the minimum release age judges the desired Pack node's accepted canonical tree once in its preservation check, probing, reading the manifest and hashing it once, and its closure check skips only that same node of the graph it read. The verdict lives for that one preservation call inside the update's read phase; every member and any other Pack node sharing the name are still observed, in the same order, before the update is preserved or blocked.

orphan-cleanup-names-declared-subagent-f.basis: When a recorded Subagent file stem is no declared name, orphan cleanup in a Subagent projection observation or output retirement observes each declared Subagent live through the capturing accepted canonical observation and derives that Subagent's own and native names from the package its payload check loaded at the same root, instead of loading that package again. The captured package serves only that one declared Subagent's naming; a different root or a missing capture loads the package itself, and each declared Subagent still gets its own live manifest read, contained package load and tree hash on every call.

subagent-package-load-reads-each-source-.basis: One Subagent package load resolves each distinct source string, checks that it is a contained regular file and reads it once, keeping the content in a map private to that load, so the core and every implementation that name the same source take that content instead of reading the file again. The map lives for one load and holds only successful reads; the next load of the same root resolves, checks and reads every source again, and each implementation is still parsed on its own.

drifted-knowledge-restore-takes-observat.basis: When one Knowledge sync call's restore loop observes an enabled Registry bundle whose canonical tree hashes differently from its accepted tree integrity, the observation reports that frozen digest beside its materialization-mismatch status, and the bundle's staged restore in the same loop iteration hands it to the reuse decision, which refuses reuse for that exact root and accepted integrity instead of hashing the tree again. The digest is never reported after a failed walk and never keeps a tree, every gate before the reuse decision still runs, any other root or accepted integrity is hashed as before, and the fetched bytes are still checked against the archive, staged-tree and expected publication integrity.

ownerless-skill-observation-reads-skill-.basis: Observing an accepted Skill without an owner runs the strict tree walk before its SKILL.md readability read, and when that walk matched the accepted tree integrity and read SKILL.md at exactly that path as a regular file, the walk's read stands for the readability read within that one observation call. The presence probe and the integrity walk stay, a verified digest handed in by the caller still leaves the readability read to the observation, and the incomplete, corrupt, mismatch and usable statuses keep their precedence.

drifted-ownerless-skill-observation-read.basis: When the strict walk of an owner-less Skill's canonical tree fails or does not match its accepted tree integrity, the observation reads SKILL.md itself after the walk, so an unreadable SKILL.md is still judged corrupt before the tree is judged a materialization mismatch, and a walk that read SKILL.md leaves that file read twice in one observation call.
drifted-ownerless-skill-observation-read.openQuestion: May the observation of an owner-less Skill whose tree differs from its accepted integrity take the walk's read of SKILL.md as its readability check instead of reading SKILL.md again?

source-switch-registry-digest-replays-ac.basis: When source-switch classification keeps the extension identity and compares content with a Registry, the accepted canonical observation hands out its strict walk of the accepted tree beside the observation, only from a matching walk of an observation that ended usable and with copies of the bytes it read. That one step classification's distribution tree digest replays the walk's listings, entry facts and bytes instead of listing and reading the accepted tree again, contained-link validation still resolves each link live, the observation's strict walk stays the integrity validation, and an observation that did not walk the tree leaves the digest to walk it live.

lint-facts-take-authoring-folder-package.basis: Within one lint run's observation read phase, the authoring-folder observation keeps each successful workspace-authored package resolution, with its root, deep-frozen manifest decode and content hash, and lint hands them over through its canonical-observation handoff: the projection invariant facts resolve an enabled workspace-authored Subagent through those prepared inputs, and the Hook contributor selection takes the handed content hash for exactly the same package root. A handed resolution answers only while that phase is active, the Subagent resolution still runs its path safety, presence and identity checks, and a failed resolution, an ended phase or a run without a handoff resolves and hashes the package afresh.

pack-plan-projections-take-authority-sca.basis: Within one Pack install planning call that makes its own graph selection, the workspace authority scan hands the Knowledge, Rule and Hook projection preparations the manifest its observation captured for each usable, enabled workspace-authored member they receive, decoded into a fresh map for that call, and each manager takes a decode only for the same package root and type instead of reading and decoding knowledge.json, rule.json or hook.json again. The concept documents, the Rule body and the package content hash are still read, and a Pack plan given a configured update's prepared selection, sync recovery and a member disabled in the proposed graph take no decode and read the manifest themselves. The transition keeps only the scan's fingerprint, so the authority rescan under the transition lock and the in-transaction manager installs read each manifest afresh.

pack-recovery-reobserves-member-selectio.basis: Configured-Pack recovery planning renders Pack graph selection, whose accepted-member resolver observes and hashes each accepted member's canonical tree against the current desired graph's node, and recovery's blocking loop then observes and hashes the same member again against the proposed graph's node to refuse present content that differs. The two observations judge against different desired nodes whenever prospective Pack manifests change the graph, and the member resolver returns only the selected ref, so recovery keeps its own observation.
pack-recovery-reobserves-member-selectio.openQuestion: Should the Pack member resolver hand the frozen accepted-package observation it made to the selection's caller, so that recovery can reuse it for the same member when its proposed desired node is the very node the resolver observed against?

closure-postconditions.resource: Post-write verification of a reconciliation closure and of a materialize, install or uninstall operation: native outputs the closure must leave in place, retention witnesses captured before its first write, and the installed state of the extension the operation wrote.
closure-postconditions.publication: None: read-only owner; it verifies what the projection, materialization and settlement owners published.

reads.note: Planning observes the required existing native units of the retained subjects (with instruction units when configured agents are given), excluding units the closure plans to change, so the closure knows what must stay.
Inside the transition, before the first write, the closure captures retention witnesses of retained shared native units as their preimage.
After the closure's last write, every captured retention witness is validated against current native content.

After the last write, required native units are observed through the record rows of the verified types, with instruction readback when instruction propagation is required, in the same fresh phase as the witness validation.
After a materialize operation's writes, its validate checks the extension is observably installed in its own fresh phase.

After an install or uninstall operation's writes, its validate checks the target's installed state with no shared phase (an install skips this when an enclosing closure verifies that type); the check builds the whole inventory of the target's type.

After a coding-agent removal's cleanup step removes the departing agents' outputs, it observes the native outputs the remaining agents still require, reports their current state and refuses when they cannot be verified.

After a skill operation commits, the apply-time artifact rebuilds the planning artifact: it reads settings, reads the skill's native name from SKILL.md again (planning reads it too when the content is already on disk) and re-probes planned native skill locations whose result the materialization's observed locations then replace (presentation).

closure-postconditions.existingSharing: Retention witnesses captured before a closure's first write are carried to its validate, and a closure check with neither retained witnesses nor required units reads nothing; beyond that, each check's readers decoded settings and the lockfile independently before prepared inputs were shared, and each closure check and each materialize-operation presence check now shares one fresh observation phase among its readers. Each retention-witness capture and each retention-witness validation now reads every referent file its retained units share once and parses it once per grammar, instead of once per unit.
closure-postconditions.preparedInputs: Each closure check with retained witnesses or required units, and each materialize-operation check, runs inside one fresh observation phase opened after the last write: the closure check shares one physical observation of settings, lockfile, record rows and observed native files across witness validation, native-output observation and instruction readback, and the materialize-operation presence check shares one observation among its readers. Each retention-witness capture and each retention-witness validation prepares the cached text of every referent file its retained units share and runs its units inside a native-config observation view that parses each such text once per grammar; every retained unit of that pass consumes them, each receiving its own parse copy. An install or uninstall operation's presence check opens no shared phase. No value passes between checks.
freshChecks: Every retention witness is compared whenever any was captured, even when no unit is required.
Retention-witness validation captures a fresh location set and reads every referent file again after the last write, reusing no text or parse from the capture.
Within a retention pass, whole-file hashes, directory walks and stats still read per retained unit, and each unit keeps its own error mapping.
Every required native unit is compared after the last write.
The materialize-operation presence check runs after the operation's writes in its own phase.
An install operation's presence check runs after its writes unless an enclosing closure verifies that type, and an uninstall operation's presence check always runs after its writes.
A coding-agent removal's cleanup step observes the retained native outputs again after its removals and refuses when they cannot be verified.
Operation validate, apply-time artifact and closure validate remain separate post-write segments.
A check with no demand opens no phase and reads nothing.
A failed phase capture maps to the same refusal as a failed live read.
Verification still rebuilds the whole read model of each verified type.
closure-postconditions.lifetime: Each observation phase lives for one validate call after the last write and is released on success, failure or interruption; retention witnesses live from capture to the closure's validate; each retention pass's cached referent-file text and the parses of the native-config observation view it opens live only for that capture or validation pass and are released when it ends; nothing crosses checks, closures or invocations, and no text or parse crosses from capture to validation.

after-skill-operation-commits-apply-time.basis: After a skill operation commits, the apply-time artifact re-probes every planned native skill location although the materialization's observed locations replace that result, and a failed probe still refuses the closure.
after-skill-operation-commits-apply-time.openQuestion: May the apply-time skill artifact reuse the materialization's observed native locations, so that a failing re-probe no longer refuses the closure with 'Cannot observe planned native Skill locations'?

closure-keeps-three-post-write-segments.basis: A closure keeps three post-write segments (operation validate, apply-time artifact and closure validate), owned by different transactions and separated by other steps' writes.

closure-postcondition-validates-retentio.basis: The closure postcondition validates retention witnesses, observes required native outputs and reads back instructions in one fresh observation phase after the closure's last write, and opens none when nothing is retained or required.

coding-agent-removal-captures-native-out.basis: A coding-agent removal captures the native outputs the remaining agents still require while planning its cleanup step, again under the transition lock before its first write as the retention preimage, and once more in its cleanup step after removing the departing agents' outputs, where it reports their current state and refuses when they cannot be verified. The planning capture belongs to a read phase that has ended, and the cleanup's removals write the observed native directories between the pre-write capture and the last one.

each-closure-s-native-output-postconditi.basis: Each closure's native-output postcondition observes the configured agents' native outputs itself after that closure's writes, because those writes, and any earlier closure's, changed what planning observed.

each-post-write-check-still-rebuilds.basis: Each post-write check still rebuilds the whole read model of the verified type, reading every installed package manifest of that type, because a subject's row also carries diagnostics and identity occurrences found elsewhere.
each-post-write-check-still-rebuilds.openQuestion: Should selected-subject post-write verification ignore read-model diagnostics and identity occurrences outside the subjects' expected paths, accepting that such states no longer refuse?

inside-transition-before-first-write-clo.basis: Inside the transition and before its first write, a closure captures retention witnesses of retained shared native units as the preimage its validate compares.

materialize-operation-s-presence-check-o.basis: A materialize operation's presence check observes the installed extension in its own fresh observation phase after the operation's writes.

under-lock-hook-uninstall-reads-agent.basis: Under the lock, Hook uninstall reads the agent's native settings for the candidate fingerprint, the retention-witness capture, the projection runs and the first-touch snapshot, each a fresh check, preimage or snapshot.

retention-pass-reads-shared-referent-fil.basis: Each retention-witness capture and each retention-witness validation keeps its own cached text of every referent file its retained units share and runs its units inside a native-config observation view, so one pass reads a shared native file once and parses it once per grammar, with each unit receiving its own parse copy. The reads live only for that pass and nothing crosses from capture to validation, which still captures a fresh location set inside its fresh observation phase; whole-file hashes, directory walks, stats and each unit's error mapping stay per unit.

container-receipts.resource: The workspace receipt store .axm/projection-containers.json (container identities, structural inverses and created-directory proofs), with the identity-capture and structural-inverse primitives its entries are built from.
container-receipts.publication: Locked read-modify-write of the store: each physical step publishes the next store, retires an emptied store with its proven empty created directories, or creates a missing store ancestor, through the caller's write, retire and createDirectory callbacks under the caller's store lock.

reads.note: Locked read and strict decode of the store under the store lock, the base of every update; a store that is not an ordinary file is refused.
Each later physical step of one update sequence re-reads the store under the same hold, so retiring an emptied store sees the created directories the preceding publication persisted.
Anchor capture of the nearest existing store ancestor on every changed write, re-verified only around creating a missing ancestor.
Inherited and recorded created-directory identities are verified before they are merged into the store or retired, and a directory is retired only when empty.
Container identity capture and verification resolve the native root, parents, entry and aliases live on every call.
Structural inverse application compares the stored digest with a digest bound to the exact text and hashes each restored candidate.

A settings or lockfile round trip's preparation reads the store once, before the locked update, to select the receipts of its document; a single execution per preparation, and the locked update reads afresh.

container-receipts.existingSharing: An update whose receipt entries equal the locked store's entries returns without calling the writer, and the decoded locked store feeds both the merge and the publication; before prepared inputs were shared, the writer read the store text again itself. Within one container identity capture, a native root that is the identity owner root now takes its directory check and identity from the owner's stat, and the container entry takes its shape check and identity from the followed stat its resolution made, instead of statting either again.
container-receipts.preparedInputs: The exact store text read under the lock, or its absence, is handed to the writer with the next contents; one update sequence applies several receipt changes over one locked read; a text digest is bound to its exact string for inverse application; the structural-insertion predicate computes no digest. The owner's live stat is the native root's stat when the native root is the identity owner root, and the capture's root directory check and root identity consume it. Entry resolution yields the identity values of the followed stat that produced the entry's address, and the capture's entry shape check and entry identity consume them.
freshChecks: Every update reads and strictly decodes the store under the store lock.
The next store is decoded before it is persisted.
The store ancestor anchor is captured on every changed write and re-verified around any ancestor creation.
Created and inherited directory identities are verified live before merge or retirement, and only empty directories are retired.
Every inverse application checks the stored before and after digests and hashes each restored candidate.

Every identity capture and verification resolves and stats its identity owner live, resolves and stats a native root that is not the identity owner root on its own, takes the entry's stat from the entry's live resolution, and stats each parent and resolves each alias live; the next capture observes afresh.
container-receipts.lifetime: The locked text, decoded receipts and sequence states live inside one update under the store lock and are released when it returns, fails or is interrupted; digest-bound texts live for the owner call that produced them; the owner's stat and the entry resolution's followed stat live only within the one container identity capture that made them; nothing is retained across invocations.

changed-receipt-store-write-re-verifies.basis: A changed receipt store write re-verifies the store's ancestor anchor only around creating a missing ancestor; with nothing missing the single anchor capture is the proof.

inverse-application-during-native-insert.basis: Inverse application during a native insertion withdrawal binds each digest to its exact text, so stacked inverses compare digests without hashing the same text again.

receipt-store-update-hands-writer-exact.basis: A receipt store update hands its writer the exact store text it read under the store lock, so a changed store is published without the writer reading it again.

receipt-store-update-reads-decodes-store.basis: A receipt store update reads and decodes the store under its lock after a caller's preparation read, the read-modify-write base of a store shared by several owners.

structural-insertion-judgment-settings-s.basis: Structural-insertion judgment for settings saves, MCP config insertion and managed .gitignore patterns computes no receipt digest.

capture-takes-equal-native-root-from-own.basis: When the native root is the identity owner root, one container identity capture builds the root's directory check and identity from the owner's live stat, which lives only within that capture. Every capture and verification still resolves and stats the owner live, and the next capture observes afresh.

capture-takes-container-entry-identity-f.basis: Entry resolution also yields the identity values of the followed stat that produced its address, and one container identity capture builds the entry's shape check and identity from them at the same point instead of statting the entry again; the values live only within that capture. Every later capture or verification resolves and stats the entry afresh, and the owner, root, parent and alias observations stay live.

copied-directory-receipts.resource: Copied native directories (the copy fallback for skill outputs when links are unavailable) and their sibling management receipt .<name>.axm-copy.json listing the copied files, links and directories with identities and integrity.
copied-directory-receipts.publication: Exclusive creation of the sibling receipt beside a staged copy, and receipt-limited retirement that removes only unchanged listed entries, empty listed directories and the receipt, through the caller's settlement retirement or direct removal.

reads.note: Walk of the staged copy, hashing each file and capturing file, link and directory identities that the new receipt binds, each file and directory identity from the followed stat that resolved it.

Receipt read: directory resolution (or the caller's admitted entry address) and ordinary receipt-file resolution, decode, a directory stat after the decode for the root identity match, and relative path safety.
Live check of each listed file (identity and integrity hash) and link (identity, then link text).
Currency decision: a walk of the canonical source tree compared with the receipt so a current copy is not rewritten.
One copied-tree walk resolves its root referent once, at its first link with a relative target, for the containment check of each of its links.
Replaceability proof at the replace decision: a second file and link pass and a walk of the copied tree for foreign additions.
Retirement reads the receipt again and re-proves every listed entry before removing it.
The workspace inventory reads each copied skill directory's receipt once to name its source and runs no currency, ownership or link check; a single execution.

Native retention fingerprinting reads a retained copied directory's receipt once per witness capture to list its entries; a single execution per capture, and the validation after mutation captures afresh.

Native location capture classifies a copied skill entry from its caller's receipt-presence fact for that entry and otherwise reads the receipt once for presence; the classification is not write authority.

copied-directory-receipts.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, every currency, replaceability, ownership and retirement check and every native location classification read and decoded the sibling receipt itself. Now the replaceability check and some currency checks take a receipt their caller has just read, and native location classification can take a receipt-presence fact from its caller in place of its own receipt read. A skill inspection's copy currency check and a non-directory entry's ownership decision take the entry address the write admission just returned instead of resolving the entry again, each copied-directory entry check takes a file or directory entry's identity from the followed stat of its own resolution, and one copied-tree walk resolves its root referent once for all of its links with a relative target.
copied-directory-receipts.preparedInputs: A receipt the caller has just read, with only pure steps since, is consumed by the replaceability check in skill materialization, by the currency check of a copied skill observation row and by the currency check of skill install planning's target-state check. A receipt-presence fact, never the receipt itself, crosses to the native location capture from skill install planning's target-state check, from the agent output inventory of skill removal and from the post-write agent output inventory of skill materialization for the entries a rename leaves behind; the capture uses it only when its directory is the entry the capture resolves and otherwise reads the receipt itself. The entry address a skill inspection's write admission returns is consumed by that inspection's copy currency check and by the ownership decision of a non-directory entry. The followed stat that resolves a copied file or directory entry is consumed as that entry's identity by the same entry check. The root referent a copied-tree walk resolves at its first link with a relative target is consumed by the containment check of that link and of every later link of that walk.
freshChecks: Each receipt read still checks directory kind, ordinary receipt file, root identity and path safety.
The currency check reads its own receipt when target hashing or a source walk separates it from a later read.
The replaceability check repeats the file and link pass and walks the copied tree after the currency check.
Link checks read the link text after the link identity check.
Retirement reads the receipt and proves each entry again; creation refuses an occupied receipt sibling.
Skill removal's canonical-source check reads its own receipt under the transition lock before protecting a copied skill.
Each receipt read stats the directory again after decoding the receipt, so a directory replaced during the read fails the root identity match.
A skill inspection's write admission stays its route check, and the ownership read of a directory entry resolves that entry live.
No entry observation crosses from one entry check to another, and the capture stats an entry that is neither a link, a file nor a directory live.
Each copied-tree walk still resolves every link's own directory and target segments and checks their containment live.
copied-directory-receipts.lifetime: A shared receipt lives within one inspection or one observation row and is released when that call returns; it is never carried into retirement or across invocations. A receipt-presence fact lives within one skill install inspection, or within one skill removal call before its first write, and is released when that call returns. Within one skill materialization, a receipt-presence fact from the post-write inventory lives until the classification of the entries a rename leaves behind returns, before those entries are removed. An admitted entry address lives for one skill inspection and is released when that inspection returns. A followed-stat observation of an entry lives within the one entry check that resolved it. A walk's root referent lives for that one copied-tree walk and is released when the walk ends.

copied-link-check-reads-link-text.basis: A copied link check reads the link text after the link identity check, the last observation of the target text, which can change in place without a new identity.

copied-skill-s-sibling-receipt-caller.basis: A copied skill's sibling receipt that the caller has just read, with only pure steps since, is consumed by the replaceability check of skill materialization and by the currency check of a copied skill observation row.

enable-new-skill-entry-has-no.basis: With --enable: A new skill entry has no prior copy, so its receipt is probed once and written only by the copy fallback on filesystems without directory links.

replaceability-check-copied-skill-repeat.basis: The replaceability check of a copied skill repeats the file and link pass after the currency check and walks the copied tree, the pre-mutation proof at the replace decision taken after the source walk.

skill-install-planning-probes-reads-copy.basis: Skill install planning's target-state check reads each directory target's copy receipt once, decides currency from it, and hands only a receipt-presence fact to the native location capture of the same inspection, where the fact lives until the inspection returns. Apply-time skill materialization still reads the receipt fresh for currency, replaceability and retirement.

skill-materialization-reads-copied-skill.basis: Skill materialization reads the copied skill's receipt for its currency check and again for ownership because target hashing and a source walk run between the two reads.

skill-removal-capture-takes-inventory-re.basis: Within one skill removal call and before its first write, an output that the agent output inventory owns through its copy receipt passes only a receipt-presence fact for its directory to the native location capture, which classifies the removal target from it when the directory matches the entry it resolves and otherwise reads the receipt itself. The removal's canonical-source check and the receipt-limited retirement still read the receipt fresh.

withdrawing-copied-skill-projection-read.basis: Withdrawing a copied skill projection reads and decodes its copy receipt in the agent output inventory and again when receipt-limited retirement re-proves the receipt's binding to the current directory and every listed entry after the rollback protection. The retirement read runs under the transition lock after that protection and after earlier outputs' removals in the same call, and is the last integrity validation before receipt-limited removal, because captured location facts are not write authority.

copied-skill-removal-source-check-reread.basis: Copied skill removal's canonical-source check reads and decodes the copy receipt again and resolves the Skill's canonical source to decide whether to protect and retire the copy, although the agent output inventory already compared them before the first write. It runs under the transition lock, after earlier outputs' removals in the same call, as the last comparison of the receipt's source with the canonical source before mutation, since receipt-limited retirement proves the receipt and its entries but not the source.
copied-skill-removal-source-check-reread.openQuestion: Must copied skill removal prove under the transition lock that the copy receipt names that Skill's canonical source, or does a valid receipt bound to the current directory identity suffice as ownership proof for retirement?

renamed-skill-classification-takes-inven.basis: Within one skill materialization, a renamed copy that the install's post-write agent output inventory owns through its copy receipt passes only a receipt-presence fact to the classification of the entries the rename leaves behind, which uses it when the directory matches the entry it resolves and otherwise reads the receipt itself. The removal's canonical-source check and the receipt-limited retirement still read the receipt fresh.

copied-entry-check-takes-identity-from-i.basis: Each copied-directory entry check (capture, currency, replaceability, ownership and retirement) takes a file or directory entry's identity from the followed stat its own resolution just made and still stats any other entry kind live; no observation crosses from one entry check to another. Retirement still re-proves each entry right before removing it.

receipt-read-stats-copied-directory-afte.basis: Reading a copied directory's receipt resolves the directory and stats it again after reading and decoding the receipt, to compare the directory's current identity with the identity the receipt names. That later stat is the identity proof that lets retirement refuse a directory replaced while its receipt was read.
receipt-read-stats-copied-directory-afte.openQuestion: May reading a copied directory's receipt take the directory's identity from the resolution made before the receipt read, even though a directory replaced during that read would then pass retirement's identity proof?

skill-inspection-decides-copy-currency-f.basis: Within one skill inspection, the copy currency check and a non-directory entry's ownership decision take the entry address the write admission just returned, with only reads of other paths since, instead of resolving the entry again; the address lives for that inspection. The admission under the transition lock stays the route check, and a directory entry's receipt read, identity stat, file hashes, link text, source walk and later replaceability and retirement reads stay live.

copied-tree-walk-resolves-root-once-for-.basis: One copied-tree walk (the capture of a new copy, or the source walk of a currency check) resolves its root referent once, at its first link with a relative target, and keeps that value for the rest of that walk only. Each link's own directory, segment and containment checks stay live, and a walk with no relative link resolves no root.

copied-linked-outputs.resource: Native link entries (instruction alias links and skill directory links) and the bounded copied skill directories used where links are unsupported.
copied-linked-outputs.publication: Copy or link: relative symlinks to canonical content, or staged copied directories swapped in.

reads.note: Resolves the target referent and the link entry before any decision.
Decides create, replace or no-op from the resolved link address when the link is its exact absolute spelling; otherwise inspects with readLink and stat.
An existing link's target is resolved fresh and compared with the desired target.
Settlement snapshot of the link and of created parent directories.
Currency check of a copied skill: receipt read and hash of the copied files.
Ownership read of the copy receipt and the replaceability proof before replacing a copied skill.
Per-file recheck when a copied directory is retired.
The copy receipt binds the staged bytes.

Skill removal's target classification takes the skill-container, entry and canonical-source resolutions its agent output inventory retained, failures included, instead of resolving them again; any other path resolves live.
Before each unlink, skill removal admits the entry within the native authority roots and resolves the canonical source and the link's immediate target live to prove the exact link.
Skill install planning captures each target entry, a link entry's immediate target and the canonical skill source once for its target-state check and its native location classification.

Skill install planning resolves each configured skills directory when it groups targets by physical directory, and again with the shared .agents/skills directory as reader and shared referents in its classification capture.
Skill materialization names the native directory from the compatibility check's SKILL.md read when that check read the same path, and reads SKILL.md itself for any other content root.
The post-write agent output inventory reads each expected source's SKILL.md native name again.

The classification of the entries a renamed skill leaves behind takes the skill-container referents and entries the post-write agent output inventory resolved, failures included; any other path resolves live.
A renamed-skill removal admits the obsolete entry and reads its copy receipt's source or its link's immediate target once, then resolves each candidate source in order until one proves ownership.
Bundled AXM skill readiness reuses the native authority root resolutions and canonical source referent of its first successful inspection for each later distinct skills directory.
Each in-transaction bundled skill ensure resolves the native authority roots, the canonical source and the target entry under the lock.
Setup planning resolves each bundled-skill target entry once in its plan rows and hands frozen copies keyed by exact path to its output-concern observation.

copied-linked-outputs.existingSharing: Each link creation resolves its target and its entry once before deciding; a copied skill's ownership and replaceability proofs are each taken once per replace inspection. Link creation now decides from the entry address it already resolved, bundled AXM skill readiness inspects each exact repeated skills-directory spelling once per readiness run and reuses the native authority root resolutions and canonical source referent of its first successful inspection for every later distinct skills directory, and skill removal's target classification answers from the resolutions its agent output inventory just made. Skill install planning resolves each target entry, a link entry's immediate target and the canonical skill source once, in one planning capture that serves both its target-state check and its native location classification. Skill materialization names a skill's native directory from the SKILL.md read of the compatibility check that canonical materialization just ran, classifies the entries a renamed skill leaves behind from the resolutions its post-write agent output inventory just made, and removes each obsolete renamed entry with one admission and one copy-receipt or immediate-link read across its candidate sources. Setup planning hands the bundled-skill target entries its plan rows resolved to the output-concern observation of the same planning call, and a preview carries them to its report.
copied-linked-outputs.preparedInputs: Link creation decides from the entry address it already resolved when the link is its exact absolute spelling; a copied skill's receipt is read once and shared only across the pure steps of one replace inspection; bundled AXM skill readiness keeps the skills-directory spellings it has inspected and skips an exact repeat, and keeps the native authority root resolutions and canonical source referent of its first successful inspection for each later distinct directory's inspection; skill removal's target classification answers from the skill-container, entry and canonical-source resolutions its agent output inventory retained, failures included; skill install planning's capture of each target entry, a link entry's immediate target and the canonical skill source is consumed by its target-state check and its native location classification; the SKILL.md read outcome of the AXM skill compatibility check, for an authored package or a reused Registry tree, is consumed by skill materialization to name the native directory; the skill-container referents and entries that the install's post-write agent output inventory resolved, failures included, are consumed by the classification of the entries a renamed skill leaves behind; a renamed-skill removal's admission of the obsolete entry and its read of the copy receipt's source or the link's immediate target are consumed by each candidate source's ownership check; setup planning's frozen bundled-skill target entries, keyed by exact path, are consumed by the output-concern observation of the same planning call and by the preview report.
freshChecks: Runs inside the caller's transition; the link and its created parents are protected before the uninterruptible remove, mkdir and symlink.
An existing link's target is resolved fresh; a link reached through an aliased parent keeps the readLink and stat inspection.
A copied skill's currency and replaceability proofs are separate observations around intervening I/O.
Bundled AXM skill readiness resolves the target entry of every other skills-directory spelling, aliases included, on its own, and runs again when the install is applied.
Each in-transaction bundled skill ensure under the lock resolves the native authority roots, the canonical source and the target entry afresh.
Skill removal's target classification resolves live any path its agent output inventory did not resolve.
Skill removal's write admission, its exact-link proof against the canonical source before each unlink, the protection of each removed entry and the retirement observation run live.
Skill install planning reads copy receipts and copy currency live, and apply-time skill materialization and its write admission resolve every entry afresh.
Skill materialization reads SKILL.md live for any content root the compatibility check did not read, and the native location capture and post-write verification read SKILL.md themselves.
A renamed skill's classification of its new locations, its removal admission, the exact-link proof before each unlink and the retirement observation resolve live.
A renamed-skill removal keeps the receipt-limited retirement's own fresh receipt re-proof, and every candidate source after a write is removed afresh through the single-source removal.
Setup resolves user-scope readers and unplanned paths live, and every report status other than a preview resolves the bundled-skill entries again.
copied-linked-outputs.lifetime: Link creation's resolved entry address and a copied skill's receipt live inside one link creation or one replace inspection and are released when it returns; bundled AXM skill readiness's inspected spellings, root resolutions and canonical source referent live for one readiness run and are never carried from planning to apply; skill removal's retained resolutions are created by its agent output inventory within one skill removal call, are used before its first write, and are released when that call returns; skill install planning's capture is local to one inspection and is released when it returns; the compatibility check's SKILL.md outcome lives within one skill materialization call with nothing written in between; a renamed skill's classification resolutions are created by the post-write agent output inventory within one skill materialization call and are released when that call returns; a renamed-skill removal's admission and receipt or link read live within that removal and are released at its first write; setup's frozen bundled-skill entries are created by one planning call and, for a preview, travel on its transition to the preview report; nothing else is retained across calls, and nothing is retained across invocations.

bundled-axm-skill-readiness-inspects-eac.basis: Bundled AXM skill readiness inspects each exact repeated skills-directory spelling once per readiness run; other spellings, aliases included, are still inspected.

bundled-skill-install-re-reads-configure.basis: The bundled skill install re-reads configured agents and re-resolves their skills directories before its transaction to fix the protected targets.
bundled-skill-install-re-reads-configure.openQuestion: May the bundled skill install fix its protected target directories from the readiness snapshot instead of re-reading configured agents before the transaction?

bundled-skill-readiness-runs-when-instal.basis: Bundled skill readiness runs when the install is planned and again when it is applied, on opposite sides of the planning and apply boundary, so a conflict written between them is refused under the lock.

each-closure-re-inventories-agents-skill.basis: Each closure re-inventories the agents' skills directories, because ownership is proven only by a link target or copy receipt after that closure's writes.

each-skill-materialization-inventories-e.basis: Each skill materialization inventories every configured agent's skills directory after its canonical swap, because ownership is proven by link target or copy receipt and each closure's writes change the directory.

link-creation-decides-create-replace-no.basis: Link creation decides create, replace or no-op from the entry address it already resolved when the link is its exact absolute spelling, instead of inspecting the same entry again.

lone-skill-md-native-name-read.basis: A lone SKILL.md native name is read for preparation, again in the native-location capture and again in post-write verification, at boundaries separated by projection writes.

setup-resolves-skills-directories-from-s.basis: Setup resolves skills directories from its selection before settings exist, while the bundled skill install runs after setup writes settings and re-reads the persisted agents, re-reading them again under the lock.

skill-removal-classification-reuses-inve.basis: Within one skill removal call and before its first write, the removal-target classification answers from the skill-container referents, entries and canonical-source referent that the agent output inventory just resolved, failures included, and resolves any other path live. Write admission, the exact-link proof before each unlink, protection and the retirement observation still resolve live.

withdrawing-linked-skill-projection-reso.basis: Withdrawing a linked skill projection resolves the canonical skill source and the link's immediate target in the agent output inventory and again in the removal's exact-link proof before the unlink. The proof is the last check under the transition lock that the immediate link reaches that Skill's canonical source, since write admission does not compare them and earlier unlinks and parent retirements in the same call write between the reads.

skill-install-planning-captures-targets-.basis: Skill install planning resolves each target entry, a link entry's immediate target and the canonical skill source once, in one planning capture local to the inspection that serves both the target-state check and the native location classification; nothing is captured when no target is named. Copy receipts and copy currency are still read live, and apply-time skill materialization and its write admission resolve every entry afresh.

skill-install-planning-resolves-skills-d.basis: Skill install planning resolves each configured skills directory when it groups install targets by physical directory, and resolves those directories and the shared .agents/skills directory again as reader and shared referents in the capture that classifies native locations.
skill-install-planning-resolves-skills-d.openQuestion: May skill install planning classify its readers and the shared skills directory from the skills-directory resolutions its target grouping made in the same inspection, instead of resolving those directories again in its reader capture?

renamed-skill-classification-reuses-inst.basis: Within one skill materialization, the classification of native entries that a renamed skill leaves behind answers from the skill-container referents and entries that the install's post-write agent output inventory just resolved, failures included, and resolves any other path live; nothing is classified when the install renames no entry.
