Removal admission, the exact-link proof before each unlink, the retirement observation and the classification of the new locations still resolve live.

skill-native-name-from-compatibility-che.basis: Skill materialization names a skill's native directory from the SKILL.md read outcome of the AXM skill compatibility check that canonical materialization just ran, for an authored package and for a Registry tree that acquisition reused when the check read the same path; absence keeps the package-name fallback and an unreadable file still refuses as an invalid skill identity. The outcome lives within the one materialization call with nothing written in between, any other content root is read live, and the native location capture and post-write verification still read SKILL.md themselves.

bundled-readiness-reuses-first-inspectio.basis: One bundled AXM skill readiness run keeps the native authority root resolutions and the canonical source referent from its first successful inspection and reuses them for every later distinct skills directory, while each directory's own target entry is still resolved on its own. The values live within the one readiness run and are never carried from planning to apply, and each in-transaction ensure under the lock resolves the roots, the source and the entry afresh.

renamed-skill-removal-admits-entry-once-.basis: When a new skill version renames its native entry, the removal of the obsolete entry admits it once and reads its copy receipt's source or its link's immediate target once, then resolves each candidate source (each previously accepted source, then the current one) in order until one proves ownership; these values live within that removal and are released at its first write. The owner's receipt-limited retirement keeps its own fresh receipt re-proof, and every candidate source after a write is removed afresh through the single-source removal.

setup-plan-hands-bundled-skill-entries-t.basis: Setup planning resolves each bundled-skill target entry once, in its plan rows, and hands frozen copies keyed by exact path to the output-concern observation of the same planning call; a preview carries them on its transition, so the preview report describes those planned entries without resolving them again. User-scope readers and unplanned paths still resolve live, every other report status resolves the entries again, and the bundled skill install's in-transaction ensure resolves each target afresh under the lock.

credentials-store.resource: The restricted credential file ~/.config/axm/credentials.json with its lock directory and refresh.lock, and the OS keychain entry for each Registry origin.
credentials-store.publication: Atomic 0600 replacement of credentials.json under the credential lock, removal of the file when its last Registry is erased, and keychain writes and deletes.

reads.note: Host facts for tier selection and persistence policy (container markers, CI, SSH, root, generic Bun executable) are read once when the store is built; the WSL marker is not read here.
The gate read of a save or clear (read, permission stat, decode) runs before any keychain or file mutation and refuses storage it cannot read or decode.
After each attempted keychain call or write-side keychain module load, a fresh read is the merge base for the fallback write or the plaintext removal, so other Registries' concurrent updates survive.
The load fallback reads the restricted file when the keychain holds no entry or is unavailable.
The permission stat taken with each read decides the overly-permissive warning; a served snapshot replays that warning at the position of the read it stands in for.
Renewal reloads the stored session under the refresh lock so a session another invocation rotated is observed before the refresh token is spent.
Sign-out reloads the stored session under the refresh lock before revoking and erasing it.

Each lock acquisition ensures the credential directory and resolves its lock target again; sign-in loads and saves under two acquisitions separated by the device flow, and renewal saves under a credential lock taken after the refresh round trip.

credentials-store.existingSharing: The session layer memoizes each origin's stored session for the invocation, so sign-in checks and request authorization share one load while reload bypasses the memo; after its first successful load the keychain module is served from the runtime's module cache to later keychain calls.
credentials-store.preparedInputs: One restricted-file snapshot (raw text and permission flag) per keychain-free segment of a locked save or clear, served to that segment's later consumers, each of which decodes its own value. Building the store reads no WSL marker; only sign-in strategy selection reads it, once.
freshChecks: The gate read precedes any keychain or file mutation with the same refusal on read, stat or decode failure.
A fresh read follows every attempted keychain call and every write-side keychain module load attempt.
The credential directory is ensured for each lock acquisition and again just before the atomic 0600 write.
The credential lock covers the whole save or clear, and lock compromise races the operation.
Renewal and sign-out take the separate cross-process refresh lock and reload inside it.
credentials-store.lifetime: A snapshot is a local value of one locked section and is dropped when the section ends in success, failure, interruption or lock compromise; the per-origin session memo lives as long as the invocation's session layer.

after-failed-keychain-write-write-side.basis: After a failed keychain write or write-side module load, a fresh credential-file read is the merge base for the fallback write.

building-credential-store-command-reads-.basis: Building the credential store for a command reads no WSL marker; sign-in strategy selection alone reads it, with one read.

credential-directory-ensured-restricted-.basis: The credential directory is ensured and restricted to 0700 again right before the credential file is published, after the ensure each lock acquisition makes.

credential-file-read-follows-every-attem.basis: A credential-file read follows every attempted keychain read, write or delete under the credential lock, because a native keychain call can outlast the lock's stale threshold.

each-credential-refresh-lock-acquisition.basis: Each credential or refresh lock acquisition resolves its lock target again, because each acquisition is its own lock precondition.

keychain-tier-save-whose-read-side.basis: A keychain-tier save whose read-side keychain module load fails reads the credential file again for its load fallback instead of reusing the gate read.
keychain-tier-save-whose-read-side.openQuestion: Is a failed keychain-module load attempt a validity boundary for credential-file reads under the credential lock, or may a save reuse its gate read across it?

locked-credential-save-clear-reads-restr.basis: A locked credential save or clear reads the restricted credential file once per keychain-free segment and serves that segment's later consumers from the snapshot.

owner-required-refusal-new-command-loads.basis: On the owner-required refusal, a new command loads the stored session for the default Registry once to name the signed-in handle and sends no authorized request, so nothing renews, saves or clears credentials.

per-origin-stored-session-memo-serves.basis: The per-origin stored-session memo serves signed-in checks and every authorized request of the invocation from one load.

session-renewal-reloads-stored-session-u.basis: Session renewal reloads the stored session under the refresh lock, and its save then reads the credential file under a credential lock taken after the refresh round trip.

sign-loads-stored-session-under-one.basis: Sign-in loads the stored session under one credential lock and saves under another, separated by the device-flow round trips, so the save's gate read is a new observation.

sign-out-loads-stored-session-then.basis: Sign-out loads the stored session, then reloads it under the refresh lock before revoking and erasing it.

token-show-loads-stored-session-most.basis: Token show loads the stored session at most once through the session memo and sends no authorized Registry request, so nothing renews, saves or clears credentials.

demote-authored-retirement.resource: The workspace-authored package directory of the demoted extension (the type's authored root joined with its name), project scope only.
demote-authored-retirement.publication: Recursive removal of the authored directory as the last action of the demote step, after the replacement install and any disabled-state restoration succeed; the removal is a plain filesystem remove whose failure, including an already-absent directory, is ignored.

reads.note: The removal reads nothing; the authored path it removes is computed once at prepare from the workspace layout and carried by the planned step.

demote-authored-retirement.existingSharing: Nothing to share at this owner: the removal reads nothing, and the demote prepare that computes the authored path runs once in one read view and seals one execution candidate.
freshChecks: The removal runs only inside the planned step, after the execution candidate passes its freshness check under the transition lock.

The removal is not protected by a settlement snapshot; it runs after the replacement install and the disabled-state restoration have succeeded, and a failed removal is ignored because the acquired package is already authoritative.
demote-authored-retirement.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the authored path computed at prepare is captured by the planned step and released when the execution candidate resolves.

demoted-authored-directory-removed-once-.basis: The demoted authored directory is removed once in the replacement step and nothing is read for it; no repeated work was identified here.

reads.note: Full replacement during workspace initialization: existence probe, then read of the prior under the file lock, with one parse that keeps tool values lossless.
Patch commit: re-read of the current lockfile under the keyed file lock, parsed and decoded once, so the base-to-next patch merges against current state.
Prior binding and projection unit keys are derived from the writer's own parse instead of a second parse of the prior.
Parse of the emitted TOML for the after units of the receipt.
Parse of a restored image before a withdrawal accepts it.
Settlement snapshot of axm.lock before replacement.
Reader loads refuse a legacy lockfile beside it, probe existence, then read and decode once per loader.
Accepted-resolution state probe reports a missing lockfile to planning before the legacy refusal; a probe failure carries its own step label.

desired-lockfile.existingSharing: The writer decides a no-op from its own parse before rendering, the patch path parses once and decodes that parse, and tool values are parsed once per write.
desired-lockfile.preparedInputs: The writer derives independently owned, frozen prior unit keys from its own parse and hands them with the raw prior to the round trip.
freshChecks: Every commit re-reads the lockfile under the keyed file lock inside the uninterruptible write.
The round trip revalidates identity and bytes immediately before publication.
Settlement snapshots axm.lock before replacement, and stale atomic-write temps are swept before every write.
Fresh setup publishes an empty lockfile before instruction sync and commits the instruction rows afterwards.
desired-lockfile.lifetime: The prior unit keys are strings owned by one lockfile write under its file lock and are released when it returns; no object of the writer's parse is shared.

changed-lockfile-commit-hands-round-trip.basis: A changed lockfile commit hands the round trip the prior unit keys derived from the writer's own parse, so the prior image is not parsed a second time.

export-reads-decodes-selected-lockfile-o.basis: The export reads and decodes the selected lockfile once and reaches no lockfile writer.

fresh-setup-instruction-sync-writes-empt.basis: Fresh setup with instruction sync writes an empty lockfile and later commits the instruction projection rows, so axm.lock is published and re-read twice.
fresh-setup-instruction-sync-writes-empt.openQuestion: May fresh setup with instruction sync publish its lockfile once after instruction sync, so that an interrupted setup leaves no axm.lock and a lockfile write failure is rolled back after the instruction writes?

full-lockfile-replacement-during-workspa.basis: A full lockfile replacement during workspace initialization probes axm.lock existence before reading its prior, keeping the check-target and read-target failure labels distinct.
full-lockfile-replacement-during-workspa.openQuestion: May a full lockfile replacement report a non-NotFound failure of its prior read under one step label instead of distinguishing the existence check from the read?

lockfile-writer-reads-current-lockfile-b.basis: The lockfile writer reads the current lockfile before writing an entry, to preserve the other resolutions and to skip a write that changes nothing.

planning-probes-lockfile-s-existence-bef.basis: Planning probes the lockfile's existence before reading accepted resolutions, and a first-use settings write probes axm.json before deciding whether to create the runtime ignores.
planning-probes-lockfile-s-existence-bef.openQuestion: May the documents adapter derive initial-settings and accepted-resolution presence from a typed read, given that probe failures would then carry the read's step label and cause?

workspace-authored-mcp-server-records-no.basis: A workspace-authored MCP server records no accepted resolution and the recorder skips MCP servers, so no lockfile image is rendered.

desired-settings.resource: The project or user settings document (axm.json).

reads.note: Caller intent read of the project and user settings in one serialized declaration; outside a read phase each document is decoded once per call and a sourced MCP declaration evaluates its desired graph over those decodes, inside a phase it uses the phase's documents.

One serialized MCP undeclaration decodes the selected settings once for its desired graph, its removal decision and its settings removal; the graph reads the inherited settings and the lockfile itself.
Owner live read of the prior text (existence probe, then read) for the formatting-preserving render, the no-op decision and the round-trip baseline.
One frozen parse of the prior image, shared by the render and the round trip.
Parse of the rendered edit proves it equals the target; when the edited text is published, the same parse is the round trip's after image.
Settlement snapshot of axm.json before replacement.
Stale atomic-write temps beside axm.json are swept before every write, including temps leaked earlier in the same invocation.
Existence probe on a first-use write decides whether runtime ignores are created; a probe failure fails the write.
Each loader read probes existence, then reads and strictly decodes the document once per loader; the probe keeps its own failure cause.

An MCP install's live read of its settings entry carries the entry's preferences forward and, when the enclosing enable or authored import or fork just published that entry, decides that an equal entry is not set again.

An uninstall step reads its target's configured source from the settings once before its transaction; when the target's manager has no configured query of its own, whether the target is configured is derived from that read.
The uninstall transaction's validation reads, after the write, whether the target is still configured, where its manager exposes a configured query or source, and whether it is installed, both live.
The skills handoff first-use observation probes axm.json once and, when it runs interactive setup, hands a path it found absent to setup preparation.

Setup preparation probes axm.json itself unless it is handed an absence observed at the same path, and its transaction reads the settings again under its lock; on the install route preparation probes again after the selection prompt.

desired-settings.existingSharing: The owner's live read serves the no-op decision, render and round-trip baseline without reopening the file, and the render is validated once; declarations inside an active read phase share the phase's decoded documents.
desired-settings.preparedInputs: Within one settings write, the prior image and the published edit are each parsed once and the frozen parses are handed to the round trip; within one declaration outside a read phase, the project and user settings are decoded once and shared by the intent read, the source lookup and, for a sourced MCP declaration, the desired graph that decides its round-trip flag; within one serialized MCP undeclaration, the selected settings are decoded once and shared by the desired graph, which decides whether the accepted resolution is removed, and by the decision and edit that remove the settings entry; within one uninstall step, the configured source read from the settings before the transaction also decides whether the target is configured, unless the target's manager has its own configured query; within one skills handoff first-use wrapper call, the settings path its first-use observation found absent is handed to setup preparation, which takes that absence in place of probing axm.json again only when the path equals the one it computes; within one closure settlement, the fact that an MCP server enable or an authored import or enabled fork published a connection's settings entry under its own name as the closure's last axm.json write is handed to that connection's install, which does not set again an entry equal to its own live read.
freshChecks: The owner live read runs inside the uninterruptible write under the workspace transition; a prepared no-op is decided from it.
The round trip revalidates identity and bytes immediately before publication.
Settlement snapshots axm.json before replacement, and stale atomic-write temps are swept before every write.
Each declaration's caller read is a strict decode that fails corrupt settings before writing; its decoded settings are not reused across a write, the writer mutex or calls.
An MCP undeclaration's desired graph still reads the inherited settings and the lockfile itself, and the lockfile read and commit after its settings write stay live.
An uninstall step's own configured query, where its manager has one, still runs, and the post-write configured readback and isInstalled checks read live state.

First-use setup reads the settings again under its transaction lock, takes the transaction's snapshots and rechecks at apply time, and on the install route it probes axm.json again after the selection prompt.

An MCP install's live read of its settings entry runs after every earlier publication in the closure; an equal entry is skipped only from that read and only after the enclosing enable or authored import or fork published it, a distribution the install newly selects is still published, sync sweeps, Pack routes and ordinary installs still set and normalize the entry, and the install's re-read of the declared entries for projection stays fresh.
An authored owner-only write, each agent's membership and each final authored declaration stay separate publications with their own receipts.
Package discovery reads axm.json live as a source workspace after location construction has released its loaders.
desired-settings.lifetime: Parsed images belong to one settings write and are released when it returns (the restoration closure keeps the after image until finish completes); a declaration's decoded settings, and a sourced MCP declaration's desired graph over them, belong to that serialized call, are used only before its first write and are released when it returns; an MCP undeclaration's selected-settings decode belongs to that serialized call and is released when it returns; an uninstall step's configured source and the configured state derived from it live only for that step's run; the observed settings absence lives for one first-use wrapper call and is never forwarded into initialization; the published-entry fact is derived when an enable prepares its realization from the activation proposal, or set by an authored import or fork for its one install call, and lives only for that closure settlement, while the install's live read of its entry is released when that install call returns.

after-authored-step-final-declaration-se.basis: After an authored step, the final declaration is a separate settings publication with its own receipt, or a no-op decided from the settings owner's fresh live read.

authored-mcp-package-step-import-enabled.basis: An authored MCP package step, on import or on an enabled fork, declares the package settings entry through the settings writer before materialization, and the install operation it runs in the same closure under the transition lock compares the entry it would set with its own live read of that entry and does not set an equal one again, so the settings writer no longer reads, renders and compares axm.json for that no-op. The skip is decided inside that one install call and only for these two authored routes: a distribution the install newly selects is still published, every other install still sets and normalizes the entry, and the install's re-read of the declared entries, the final authored declaration and the transaction's validation stay fresh.

creating-mcp-server-declares-package-set.basis: Creating an MCP server declares the package settings entry before materialization, and the install operation that materialization runs sets the entry again inside the same closure with the distribution it selected, so the settings writer reads, renders, compares and publishes axm.json a second time with a real change. Folding both into one insertion is not decided by the accepted requirements: the single insertion would record an exact-withdrawal receipt that the second, modifying publication otherwise erases, which is a reading of the exact-withdrawal requirement its text does not settle, and materialization resolves the reference from the declaration before the distribution is selected.
creating-mcp-server-declares-package-set.openQuestion: May creating an MCP server publish its workspace declaration together with the distribution the install operation selects as one settings insertion, so that axm.json is published once and the creation records an exact-withdrawal receipt that the second, modifying publication otherwise erases?

declaration-s-strict-caller-read-setting.basis: A declaration's strict caller read of the settings is a separate corruption gate from the settings owner's live read, which alone feeds preservation, the no-op decision and the round-trip baseline.

each-added-agent-s-membership-own.basis: Each added agent's membership is its own settings publication with its own prior read, because each single insertion records its own exact-withdrawal receipt.

each-departing-agent-withdrawn-own-setti.basis: Each departing agent is withdrawn in its own settings publication with its own prior read, because a publication applies a recorded receipt's exact inverse only when it withdraws a single unit.

each-settings-loader-read-settings-write.basis: Each settings loader read, and the settings writer's prior read, probes existence before reading content, because the two steps report distinct failure causes and step labels.
each-settings-loader-read-settings-write.openQuestion: May the --verbose/--debug cause, the settings writer's debug reason and the runtime-ignore step label for a non-NotFound failure come from the content read instead of the existence probe?

each-settings-write-like-each-lockfile.basis: Each settings write, like each lockfile write, sweeps stale atomic-write temps beside the document first, which also removes temps leaked earlier in the same invocation.
each-settings-write-like-each-lockfile.openQuestion: May a settings or lockfile write skip the stale atomic-write temp sweep when an earlier write in the same invocation already swept that directory, leaving temps leaked after that sweep until a later write?

each-settings-write-parses-prior-image.basis: Each settings write parses its prior image and its published edit once and hands both frozen parses to the round trip instead of parsing them again.

enabling-sourced-mcp-server-publishes-se.basis: Enabling a sourced MCP server publishes its settings entry through the activation, and the enable route's materialize step carries the fact that this activation published the connection's entry under its own name as the last axm.json write of the same closure under the transition lock, when it publishes no removal. The install operation that step runs compares the entry it would set with its own live read of that entry and does not set an equal one again, so the settings writer no longer reads, renders and compares axm.json for that no-op; the fact lives only for that closure settlement. A changed entry is still published, sync sweeps, Pack routes and ordinary install routes still set and normalize the entry, and the install's live read, its re-read of the declared entries for projection, change classification and the transaction's validation stay fresh.

hook-install-consumer-configuration-decl.basis: A Hook install with consumer configuration declares the hook settings entry and then sets the same entry again with the configuration inside the same closure, so the settings writer reads, renders and publishes axm.json twice for one hook, and the second publication adds the configuration. Writing both as one entry is not decided by the accepted requirements: a first declaration would then record an exact-withdrawal receipt that the second publication otherwise erases, and a reinstall with the same configuration would leave axm.json untouched and could report the install as unchanged instead of updated.
hook-install-consumer-configuration-decl.openQuestion: May a Hook install with consumer configuration write its declaration and configuration as one settings entry, accepting that a first declaration then records an exact-withdrawal receipt that the second publication otherwise erases, and that a reinstall with the same configuration no longer rewrites axm.json and may report the install as unchanged instead of updated?

registry-sourced-mcp-declaration-outside.basis: A Registry-sourced MCP declaration outside a read phase decodes the project and user settings once for its intent read and its source lookup.

share-reads-decodes-project-settings-doc.basis: Share decodes the project settings document during location construction for the workspace layout, and package discovery then probes, reads and decodes the same axm.json again as a source workspace to learn the owner, the distribution opt-outs and the authored directories. The two reads lie in different validity boundaries: construction's loaders are released when construction returns and the Git repository and origin lookups run before discovery, so discovery observes live state instead of extending an ended read phase. Discovery also decodes through its own lenient cross-version source settings view and reports its own source resolution failures.

unpack-promotes-each-pack-member-workspa.basis: Unpack promotes each Pack member that the workspace does not declare directly in its own settings publication and removes the Pack declaration in another, and each publication's live read and readback follow the previous publication's write to axm.json, so none of them rereads unchanged state. Publishing them as one is not decided by the accepted requirements: the Pack removal would have to read promotions still pending in a closure-scoped settings document, one closure receipt would replace the single-insertion receipt each promotion records, and a promotion's settings failure would no longer surface at that member before the Pack uninstall runs.
unpack-promotes-each-pack-member-workspa.openQuestion: May unpack buffer its member promotions and the Pack removal into one settings publication under a closure document batch, so that the Pack removal reads the pending promotions and the closure records one receipt outcome, instead of publishing and reading back axm.json once per promoted member and once for the Pack removal?

when-new-command-establishes-authoring-o.basis: When the new command establishes the authoring owner, the owner-only settings write is the exact baseline of the declaration's insertion receipt, so owner and declaration stay two settings writes.

mcp-declaration-graph-reads-call-decoded.basis: Outside a read phase, a sourced MCP declaration decodes its selected and inherited settings once each through its call-local cached documents and evaluates the desired graph for its round-trip flag over those decodes, instead of the graph reading both documents again. The decodes belong to that serialized call and are used only before its first write; inside a read phase the graph reads the phase's documents, and the settings owner's live read, no-op decision and round-trip proof at publish stay.

uninstall-step-derives-configured-state-.basis: Before its transaction, an uninstall step reads its target's configured source from the settings once and derives whether the target is configured from that read, unless the target's manager has its own configured query, which still runs. The derived value lives only for that step's run, and the post-write configured readback and the isInstalled checks still read live state.

mcp-undeclaration-graph-reads-call-decod.basis: One serialized MCP undeclaration decodes the selected settings once before its first write and evaluates the desired graph over that decode, which also decides whether the entry is removed, instead of the graph reading the document again; the decode belongs to that call and is released when it returns. The graph still reads the inherited settings and the lockfile itself, and the settings owner's live read, no-op decision and round-trip proof, and the lockfile read and commit after the settings write, stay live.

first-use-handoff-setup-takes-observed-s.basis: When the skills handoff command runs interactive, non-preview first-use setup in a scope without axm.json, the first-use wrapper hands the settings path its own first-use observation found absent to setup preparation, which takes that absence in place of probing axm.json again only when the path equals the one it computes after the user-scope refusal and the user workspace root resolution. The observation lives for that one wrapper call and is never forwarded into initialization, so the settings checks under the workspace transition lock, the transaction's snapshots and the apply-time rechecks stay fresh.

first-install-setup-probes-settings-afte.basis: When an interactive, non-preview install runs first-use setup in a scope without axm.json, the install observes the settings absence before its selection prompt, and setup preparation probes axm.json again after that selection. Setup decides from its own probe, so settings written elsewhere while the selection is open complete setup without a transaction instead of being taken as absent.
first-install-setup-probes-settings-afte.openQuestion: May first-use setup on the install route take settings absence from the observation made before the selection prompt instead of probing axm.json again after it?

diagnostic-export.resource: A user-named export destination file, and the local diagnostic record it copies after review.
diagnostic-export.publication: A staged copy written create-only and linked into place create-only; the staged name is removed.

reads.note: Each review makes one bounded read of the record, decodes it strictly, checks its event id, renders it canonically and hashes it once.

diagnostic-export.existingSharing: Export reviews the record once and writes exactly the reviewed content.
freshChecks: The supplied SHA-256 must equal the fresh review's hash before anything is written.
The create-only link fails with conflict when the destination exists.
diagnostic-export.lifetime: The reviewed content lives for one show or export and is not transferred between owners.

after-chunked-review-read-enforces-recor.basis: After the chunked review read enforces the record's size bound, it copies the chunks into one buffer and decodes that buffer once.

reviewing-diagnostic-record-reads-decode.basis: Reviewing a diagnostic record reads, decodes, renders and hashes it once, and export writes exactly the reviewed content.

showing-diagnostic-record-reviews-once-o.basis: Showing a diagnostic record reviews it once: one bounded read, one strict decode and one canonical rendering, from which both the displayed record and its reported SHA-256 come.

directory-copy.resource: A destination tree: canonical staging, scratch captures of path sources, authoring targets, and the staged copy of a skill into an agent skills directory where directory links are unsupported.
directory-copy.publication: Directory tree: a scanned source copied entry by entry after source and target identity checks.

reads.note: One scan of the source admits its bytes and entries against the copy limits before any write.
A fork's containment walk lists the source tree and reads each link value once, and the copy that immediately follows takes them from its observation.
Source and target identities are resolved once each before any write, refusing overlap, aliases and hard links.
Source bytes are streamed once into each target file, then the source mode is restored.

directory-copy.existingSharing: The source tree was already scanned once before any target write, and the identities of the whole read set are captured once and checked against every target. Now one copy also resolves its source root once for every overlap check, each source file once in its read set and each target once where its first overlap check needs it, and a fork's staging copy takes its link values and directory listings from the containment walk that immediately precedes it instead of listing the tree and reading its links again.
directory-copy.preparedInputs: A fork's staging copy accepts the source observation that the fork's containment walk records with observeCopySource, and the copy's scan consumes its link values and directory listings. Within one copy, the source root's address is consumed by every overlap check of that copy, each source file's address by the read-set identity checks and its target's overlap check, and each target's address by its overlap, identity, hardlink or workspace-conflict check.
freshChecks: The caller's lock or scratch scope.
Source and target identity checks before the first write.
With a fork's source observation, the scan still stats every entry that is not a link, checks each link's containment and reads live the link value or listing of any entry the walk did not list.
The streamed byte count is re-checked against the copy limit while copying.
directory-copy.lifetime: A fork's source observation is created by its containment walk, passed to the copy that immediately follows with no write in between and not used after that copy; the copy ignores an observation of a different source root. The source root, source file and target addresses are created within one copy call, used before its first write and released when the call returns. No other value is transferred between owners.

acquired-tree-budget-walk-copy-s.basis: The acquired-tree budget walk and the copy's own scan with source and target identity checks run at different boundaries.

installing-hook-from-source-other-than.basis: Installing a Hook from a source other than the Registry copies its package into a scratch snapshot for the execution review; acquisition then captures a path source into scratch before confirmation, and the apply copies the acquired package again into canonical staging under the transition lock. The review snapshot is scoped to the review and removed when it ends, and acquisition, a confirmation of unbounded length and the transition lock acquisition separate it from the publication.
installing-hook-from-source-other-than.openQuestion: May a Hook install keep the execution review's package snapshot past the review, through acquisition, a confirmation of unbounded length and the transition lock acquisition, and publish from it instead of from the source content acquired after the review?

installing-updating-mcp-server-from-sour.basis: Installing or updating an MCP server from a source other than the Registry copies its package into a scratch snapshot for the execution review; acquisition then captures a path source into scratch before confirmation, and the apply copies the acquired package again into canonical staging under the transition lock. The review snapshot is scoped to the review and removed when it ends, and acquisition, a confirmation of unbounded length and the transition lock acquisition separate it from the publication.
installing-updating-mcp-server-from-sour.openQuestion: May an MCP install or update keep the execution review's package snapshot past the review, through acquisition, a confirmation of unbounded length and the transition lock acquisition, and publish from it instead of from the source content acquired after the review?

copy-resolves-source-root-and-each-targe.basis: One directory copy resolves its source root once in its opening overlap check, each source file once in its read set and each target once where its first overlap check needs it, and runs every overlap, identity, hardlink and workspace-conflict check on those resolutions in the same order. The addresses live within that copy call and are used before its first write; every target still gets a live resolution before any directory or file is written.

document-round-trip.resource: The exact-withdrawal receipts that record a desired document's structural inverse, kept in the workspace receipt store beside axm.json and axm.lock.
document-round-trip.publication: Atomic replacement of the receipt store, plus creation of its directory, through the container-receipt mutation.

reads.note: Admits the document's route inside the native root once and captures an existing document's prior identity from that admission's resolutions, or captures its parent's identity afresh when the document is absent.
Stored receipts for the unit prefix and physical path.
Each matching withdrawal receipt's identity is verified again before its inverse is applied.
A stored inverse is applied only to its matching postimage.
Revalidation immediately before publication: identity and bytes still equal the writer's before image.
Finish captures identity, compares the route and reads back the published bytes before recording receipts.
Structural inverse derivation and its hashes, now only for a publication that can record a receipt.
Locked read-modify-write of the shared receipt store at finish, even when no receipt is recorded.
Existence of the receipt store, read only on the byte-equal no-op path for the footprint change kind.

document-round-trip.existingSharing: The round trip receives the exact before and after strings from the document writer and returns the content, revalidation and finish steps to it, without reading the document itself to prepare.
document-round-trip.preparedInputs: The structural inverse and its hashes are derived only after the identity, route and readback checks, and only when the publication can record a receipt; the receipt-store update at finish consumes the store text read under the store lock instead of reading it again, except on the byte-equal no-op path. For an existing document, preparation's single content-mutation admission hands its physical root, physical owner root, entry address and followed stat to the prior-identity capture, which observes the owner, root, entry, parents and aliases from them instead of resolving and admitting the document again.
freshChecks: Revalidation runs inside the uninterruptible document write immediately before publication.
Finish verifies identity, route and published bytes before recording receipts.
A withdrawal recaptures the container identity before applying each matching receipt's inverse.
The receipt store is read, modified and written under its per-file lock at every finish, even when no receipt is recorded; the byte-equal no-op path re-reads it after protection.
document-round-trip.lifetime: Identities, baselines, stored receipts and the locked store text belong to one document publication (prepare, revalidate, finish) and are released when it completes; a document batch's visited paths live for that batch. The admission resolutions that the prior-identity capture continues from live only within that preparation call; revalidation and finish each capture the document afresh.

each-settings-lockfile-publication-captu.basis: Each settings or lockfile publication captures the document's container identity at preparation and verifies it again before publication and at finish.

publication-whose-finish-records-no-rece.basis: A publication whose finish records no receipt still locks, reads and decodes the shared receipt store, which is the store's last integrity check before the publication completes.
publication-whose-finish-records-no-rece.openQuestion: May a document publication whose finish records no receipt skip the receipt-store read, so that a store corrupted after preparation no longer fails that publication?

round-trip-finish-derives-structural-inv.basis: Round-trip finish derives the structural inverse and its hashes only for a publication that can record an exact-withdrawal receipt.

withdrawal-recaptures-document-s-contain.basis: A withdrawal recaptures the document's container identity for each matching receipt although preparation captured it moments earlier.
withdrawal-recaptures-document-s-contain.openQuestion: May a withdrawal compare the identity captured at preparation instead of recapturing it before applying the receipt's inverse?

existing-document-preparation-captures-i.basis: Preparing a settings or lockfile round trip over an existing document admits the document once for a content mutation and captures its prior container identity from that admission's root and entry resolutions within the same preparation call, so the admission's refusals still come first and the owner, root, entry, parent and alias observations keep their order. Revalidation before publication and finish each capture the document afresh, and an absent document's parent capture is unchanged.

execution-candidate.resource: A plan's sealed execution candidate (material paths, material fingerprint and the identity derived from them), its external execution review of non-workspace Hook and MCP refs, and the apply-time validation that rechecks the candidate under the workspace transition lock.
execution-candidate.publication: Directory tree: a scoped temporary review snapshot (axm-execution-review-*) of a reviewed local, Git or HTTP source, copied so the review hashes the payload materialization would copy, and removed when that ref's review scope closes; Registry refs are reviewed in place and nothing else is published.

reads.note: Planning runs in one document read view: lockfile reconciliation, configured agents when a plan carries configured-agent operations (read in preview too, although only post-apply verification consumes them), and current-state agent outcomes only for steps whose owner plan supplied none.
A plan with a non-workspace Hook or MCP exposure ref fingerprints its materials before the review; the seal must match it or preparation is stale.

Each reviewed ref per step is fetched and admitted (or its accepted canonical tree is reused when the locked integrity matches, the digest of that comparison then serving as the reviewed tree digest when that tree is the reviewed package root), snapshotted when not a Registry ref, tree-hashed and its manifest read to state the exact executable content; an exact, warning-free Registry ref listed again in the same step outside an operation unit is reviewed once, and local names of one such MCP package share its fetch, tree digests and decoded manifest within the step.
A repeated ref in one step is fetched and reviewed again when its fetch can log a lifecycle warning or publish progress under an operation unit, or when it is not an exact Registry ref.
The seal fingerprints settings, lockfile and every step and artifact material path recursively (link text, mode, bytes) under live observations, independently of the planning view.
A composite child plan without a review observes only its own materials; the composite's seal covers the settings and lockfile and derives the only identity.

Under the transition lock the candidate fingerprint is recomputed before apply, followed by the caller's additional freshness check; for sync the paths both checks cover are read once in one fresh observation.
A pre-apply gate, such as publish's revalidation of the prepared distribution, is bracketed by a candidate fingerprint before and after it.
Registry exposure is revalidated after confirmation and again after waiting on lock contention.
After apply, configured-agent outcomes of enabled operations are read back in one fresh observation phase that also shares one MCP inspection read view.

The placement preflight resolves each distinct retained package destination under the acquired root, with the .axm-staging and .axm-backup boundaries of a package without accepted ownership, and each distinct local source's filesystem identity once per call, and adds the selected packages' destinations, those boundaries and the local source paths to the candidate's material paths.

execution-candidate.existingSharing: Steps whose owner plan already supplied agent outcomes are not re-observed; a plan-level apply transaction claims no default targets and leaves the shared settings and lockfile to each closure's first-touch protection; the post-apply readback runs in one fresh observation; a review reuses an accepted canonical tree whose integrity matches instead of fetching.
execution-candidate.preparedInputs: Sync's candidate check and its additional preflight check read the paths both cover once, in one fresh observation per validation pass under the lock; an exact, warning-free Registry Hook or MCP ref listed twice in one step is fetched and reviewed once when no operation unit is current; a migration's review-free child plans derive no discarded identity and do not fingerprint the settings and lockfile the migration's own seal covers; an accepted canonical Registry tree that matches the locked integrity and is the reviewed package root supplies its digest as the reviewed tree digest, and its frozen decoded Hook or MCP manifest, with the settings entry already read for review, for the previous input requests; within one step, local names of one exact, warning-free Registry MCP package reviewed outside an operation unit share the fetched directory by source content key, and tree digests and the frozen decoded manifest by path, for each name's own review; a same-source Registry Hook or MCP ref whose accepted canonical tree the review hashed before fetching and found to differ from the locked integrity carries that verdict in its review scope, from which the previous input requests are left unavailable; within one placement preflight, the destination resolution of each distinct retained package claim (package key and address), with the .axm-staging and .axm-backup boundaries of a package without accepted ownership, and the filesystem identity of each local source path that several refs list are each made once at their first position, and the selected packages' destinations, those boundaries and the local source paths with their filesystem identities join the candidate's material paths, which the seal and the under-lock refingerprint consume.
freshChecks: The seal fingerprints every material physically, independent of the planning view.
With a Hook or MCP review, the pre-review fingerprint must equal the seal.
Under the lock the candidate is refingerprinted before apply and after any pre-apply gate; a mismatch is a stale candidate with no writes.
Only paths that both sync validation checks cover share one read; other materials are read unshared, and a failed capture runs both checks unshared.
Registry exposure is rechecked after confirmation and after lock contention.

Distinct refs, warning-bearing, inexact or in-unit duplicates, and cross-step repeats are each fetched (or reuse a matching canonical tree) and reviewed, except that local names of one exact, warning-free Registry MCP package reviewed outside an operation unit share one fetch per step.

Local names sharing an MCP source whose fetch can log a warning or publish progress, or that is not an exact Registry ref, share no fetch, digest or manifest: each is fetched, snapshotted or reused from its canonical tree, hashed and decoded on its own; every local name, shared or not, keeps its own reuse decision, lock entry, configuration and target review.

A reused canonical tree's digest is compared with the locked integrity on every review, and the acquired-directory lookup still runs; that digest serves as the reviewed tree only when the reviewed package root is that canonical path.

When previous input requests are needed, the reviewed package root is not the reused canonical tree and the review has not already hashed that canonical tree and found it diverged before fetching, the canonical tree's existence is checked, it is hashed again and compared with the locked integrity, and its manifest is read again, also after a failed first hash; any failure leaves the previous input requests unavailable.
A child plan with an execution review keeps its own seal and review bracket.

Each placement preflight validates the address of every accepted and selected claim, keeps its overlap, absence and staging-boundary refusals with their details and order, and captures each local ref's source directory with its own error mapping; distinct claims and distinct source paths are each resolved.
execution-candidate.lifetime: The preparing use case owns the sealed candidate from prepare through preview, confirmation and apply of one invocation; the shared validation observation lives for one validation pass under the lock and closes before any gate or write; each fetched or snapshot tree, with a reused canonical digest, frozen manifest and diverged-canonical verdict, lives in its per-ref review scope, while a shared exact MCP fetch and its tree digests and decoded manifests live in a step scope created when that step's review begins and released when its refs are reviewed, before a later step fetches; the reviewed-ref key set lives for one step; the placement preflight's sets of examined claims and resolved source paths live for one preflight call and are not retained, while the material paths it returns live with the sealed candidate; nothing is retained across invocations.

after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.basis: After apply, configured-agent verification of each enabled Knowledge operation runs the Knowledge manager's discovery-region observation again in a fresh observation phase, selecting every enabled bundle and reading the instruction file, after the operation's own region write already read that file back to record its insertion. That readback saw only its own closure's write and its read phase ended with the closure's settlement, while other closures' writes or rollbacks can still change the combined region, so only the fresh observation states the final per-agent outcomes that are reported and decide the convergence failure.

after-apply-resolution-verifies-each-ena.basis: After apply, the resolution verifies each enabled configured-agent operation in its own fresh observation phase, observing the subject's canonical tree and running the Subagent manager's projection observation of its native files again after the operation's writes and its own post-write presence check. The closure's settlement and later closures' writes or rollbacks to the same agents' files lie between them and the operation's read phase has ended, so only the fresh observation states the final per-agent outcomes that are reported and decide the convergence failure.

after-applying-operation-leaves-subject-.basis: After applying an operation that leaves its subject disabled, configured-agent verification opens a fresh observation phase and evaluates the desired graph, reading and decoding the settings, the inherited user-scope settings, the lockfile and authored Pack manifests again, although no canonical or native observation follows. Apply's settings and lockfile writes, lock acquisition and confirmation lie between the planning reads and this readback, which is the last post-write read of the desired state, and its read or decode failure fails the apply.
after-applying-operation-leaves-subject-.openQuestion: Must an apply that leaves no subject enabled still fail when its final readback cannot read or decode the settings, the inherited user-scope settings, the lockfile or an authored Pack manifest?

after-applying-removal-whose-subject-lea.basis: After applying a removal whose subject leaves the desired state, configured-agent verification opens a fresh observation phase and evaluates the desired graph, reading and decoding the settings, the inherited user-scope settings, the lockfile and authored Pack manifests again, although no operation leaves a subject enabled for it to observe. The removal's settings and lockfile writes and the transition lock lie between the planning reads and this readback, which is the last post-write read of the desired state, and its read or decode failure fails the apply.
after-applying-removal-whose-subject-lea.openQuestion: Must a removal whose every operation plans its subject absent still fail when its final readback cannot read or decode the settings, the inherited user-scope settings, the lockfile or an authored Pack manifest?

after-knowledge-uninstall-whose-bundle-i.basis: After a Knowledge uninstall whose bundle an installed Pack still reaches, configured-agent verification observes the bundle's canonical tree and runs the Knowledge manager's discovery-region observation of the instruction file again in a fresh observation phase, after the uninstall step rendered the region and checked the bundle's presence under the same lock. The closure's settlement, a later closure re-rendering the same discovery region and a failed closure's rollback lie between them, and the uninstall step's read phase has ended, so only the fresh observation states the final per-agent outcomes that are reported and decide the convergence failure.

candidate-preparation-reuses-agent-outco.basis: Candidate preparation reuses agent outcomes its owner plan already projected, and a plan-level apply transaction claims no default targets, leaving the shared settings and lockfile to each closure's first-touch protection.

candidate-seals-live-settings-lockfile-b.basis: The candidate seals the live settings and lockfile bytes at preparation and checks them again under the transition lock before applying.

each-migration-child-plan-keeps-own.basis: Each migration child plan keeps its own placement preflight, exposure review, child-path coverage, outcome projection and withdrawals inside the migration's candidate.
each-migration-child-plan-keeps-own.openQuestion: May migrate fold its child plans' placement preflights, exposure reviews and child-path coverage into the migration's own seal, accepting deduplicated risk conditions and a changed identity and consent detail of the candidate for identical inputs?

execution-review-fetches-exact-hook-mcp.basis: The execution review fetches the exact Hook or MCP archive again after the extension-kind plan has released its own per-call tree, as the kernel's independent observation of executable content before sealing.

execution-review-fetches-reviews-exact-w.basis: The execution review fetches and reviews an exact, warning-free Registry Hook or MCP ref that one step lists twice only once when no operation unit is current.

migration-child-plans-skip-computing-the.basis: Migration child plans skip computing their own discarded candidate's identity and the settings and lockfile coverage that the migration's own seal already provides.

plan-exposes-non-workspace-hook-mcp.basis: A plan that exposes a non-workspace Hook or MCP ref fingerprints its materials before the execution review and again at the seal, which must match.

plan-level-apply-transaction-claims-no.basis: A plan-level apply transaction claims no default targets, leaving the shared settings and lockfile to each closure's first-touch protection.

pre-acquisition-observation-check-guards.basis: The pre-acquisition observation check guards the no-op decision with its own refusal.

preview-candidate-configured-agent-opera.basis: A preview of a candidate with configured-agent operations reads configured agents at resolve although only post-apply verification consumes them.
preview-candidate-configured-agent-opera.openQuestion: May a preview skip the resolve-time configured-agents read that only post-apply verification consumes, so that a settings document corrupted after candidate sealing no longer fails the preview?

publish-apply-fingerprints-materials-und.basis: Publish apply fingerprints its materials under the lock both before and after its read-only revalidation gate, on top of the seal.
publish-apply-fingerprints-materials-und.openQuestion: May publish apply skip the pre-gate material fingerprint for a gate declared read-only, so that an edit made during the gate that also fails the gate is reported as stale material rather than as the gate's source-changed failure?

publish-keeps-each-package-s-whole.basis: Publish keeps each package's whole directory among its candidate materials, so the final material check detects edits to excluded files, version-control metadata, links and modes that a rebuild would not.

ref-repeated-one-step-still-fetched.basis: A ref repeated in one step is still fetched and reviewed again when it carries lifecycle warnings, lacks an exact integrity, or is reviewed under an operation unit whose fetch publishes progress.
ref-repeated-one-step-still-fetched.openQuestion: May the execution review skip a repeated exact Registry ref in one step even when its fetch would log a lifecycle warning or publish progress, so that the warning and progress appear once rather than once per listing?

registry-exposure-plan-s-registry-refs.basis: Registry exposure of a plan's Registry refs is revalidated after confirmation and again after waiting on lock contention.

same-hook-mcp-ref-listed-two.basis: The same Hook or MCP ref listed by two steps is reviewed per step, because each step's targets, outcomes and native locations differ and a shared fetch would hold every extracted tree until the review loop ends.

seal-fingerprints-settings-lockfile-phys.basis: The seal fingerprints the settings and lockfile physically after the planning view has closed, independently of the decoded documents planning used.

under-lock-candidate-refingerprints-nati.basis: Under the lock the candidate refingerprints its native targets and other materials before the first write, a fresh conflict check against the sealed preimage.

under-lock-hook-configuration-re-hashes.basis: Under the lock, hook configuration re-hashes the package content as the stale-content check, because the seal records a symbolic-linked package root only as link text.

under-lock-skill-subagent-native-import.basis: Under the lock, a Skill or Subagent native import refingerprints the staged tree its candidate sealed after the copy, a fresh conflict check no earlier read replaces.

under-transition-lock-sync-s-candidate.basis: Under the transition lock, sync's candidate check and its preflight freshness check read the settings, lockfile and other paths both cover once, in one fresh observation that ends before any write.

when-execution-review-reuses-accepted-ca.basis: When the execution review reuses an accepted canonical Registry tree, the digest it computes to compare that tree with the locked integrity is also the reviewed tree digest whenever the reviewed package root resolves to that same canonical path, so the tree is hashed once within the ref's review scope. The comparison with the locked integrity and the acquired-directory lookup still run before that reuse, and an acquired or fetched package root is hashed as reviewed content with its existing error mapping.

when-reviewed-hook-ref-s-configuration.basis: When a reviewed Hook ref's configuration differs from the accepted one while every target's registration is current and the reviewed package root is the reused canonical tree, the execution review establishes the previous input requests from the frozen hook manifest and the accepted configuration it already read for review, within that ref's review scope. A canonical tree the review already hashed and found diverged before fetching leaves the previous input requests unavailable without another hash; every other path, including a fetched ref whose earlier canonical hash failed, checks that the canonical tree exists, hashes it against the locked integrity and reads its hook manifest again, treating any failure as unavailable.

when-reviewed-mcp-ref-s-configuration.basis: When a reviewed MCP ref's configuration differs from the accepted one while every target's registration is current and the reviewed package root is the reused canonical tree, the execution review establishes the previous input requests from the frozen decoded mcp.json and the previous settings entry it already read for review, within that ref's review scope. A canonical tree the review already hashed and found diverged before fetching leaves the previous input requests unavailable without another hash; every other path, including a fetched ref whose earlier canonical hash failed, checks that the canonical tree exists, hashes it against the locked integrity and decodes its mcp.json again, treating any failure as unavailable.

when-several-enabled-local-names-share.basis: When several enabled local names share one exact, warning-free Registry MCP package reviewed outside an operation unit, the execution review of a step fetches the package once by source content key, hashes each tree path once and decodes each manifest once, holding the fetched directory in a step scope that is released when that step's refs are reviewed and keeping only successful results. Each name still makes its own canonical reuse decision and reviews its own lock entry, configuration, preferences, agent targets and previous inputs, and a later step fetches again.

warning-or-unit-mcp-source-fetched-per-n.basis: When local names share an MCP package whose fetch logs lifecycle warnings, or the review runs under an operation unit whose fetch can publish download progress, the execution review fetches, hashes and decodes the package once per name. Sharing the fetch would emit each warning and progress event once instead of once per name, and the accepted requirements do not decide whether that output may shrink.
warning-or-unit-mcp-source-fetched-per-n.openQuestion: May the execution review of one step fetch an exact Registry MCP package once for every local name that shares it even when that fetch logs lifecycle warnings or publishes progress under an operation unit, so that the warnings and progress appear once rather than once per name?

non-pinned-mcp-source-reviewed-per-local.basis: When local names share an inexact Registry MCP source, or a local, Git or HTTP source reviewed through a per-ref snapshot copy, the execution review resolves or snapshots and hashes that source once per name. An inexact fetch is a fresh remote resolution and a local source is live, user-mutable content, and the accepted requirements do not decide whether one review may state every name's executable content from a single read of it.
non-pinned-mcp-source-reviewed-per-local.openQuestion: May the execution review of one step fetch or snapshot an inexact Registry, local, Git or HTTP MCP source once for every local name that shares it, reviewing each name against that one tree instead of reading the source again per name?

fetched-review-settles-diverged-canonica.basis: When the execution review of a same-source Registry Hook or MCP ref has checked that the accepted canonical tree exists, hashed it before fetching and found it differs from the locked integrity, it leaves the previous input requests unavailable from that per-ref verdict, held in the ref's review scope, without checking or hashing that tree again. A failed first hash, a non-Registry or different-source ref, and every other path that needs previous input requests still check that the canonical tree exists and hash it against the locked integrity.

placement-preflight-resolves-each-retain.basis: Within one placement preflight, each distinct retained package claim (package key and address) resolves its destination under the acquired root, and for a package without accepted ownership its .axm-staging and .axm-backup boundaries, once at its first position, so an accepted binding and a selected component of the same package, or several components of one package, share that resolution. The set of examined claims is local to that preflight call and is not retained. Address validation over every claim, the overlap, absence and staging-boundary refusals with their details and order, and the apply-time revalidation of the returned material paths still run.

placement-preflight-resolves-each-local-.basis: Within one placement preflight, a local source path that several refs list (its acquisition ref and its exposure refs, such as one per active MCP server name, in one step or across steps) has its filesystem identity resolved once, at its first listing; the set of resolved source paths is local to that preflight call and is not retained. Every ref still captures its source directory with its own error mapping and runs its address claim, snapshot and destination checks in the same order, distinct source paths are each resolved, and the apply-time revalidation of the returned material paths still runs.

execution-directory.resource: The directory an invocation runs from, selected by --directory or -C or the launch directory, resolved to its canonical native spelling.

reads.note: One strict realPath of the selection, then the canonical port's spelling of the real path.
The canonical port compares the opened handle's identity with the spelled path's identity.
Where the port is absent or cannot spell the path, the real path is resolved again before the listing walk, which follows no links.
A stat admits the canonical path as a directory and a stat of its dot entry confirms it can be entered, failing with usage otherwise.

execution-directory.existingSharing: The resolved directory is provided to the command once as the execution directory service.
execution-directory.preparedInputs: The real path of the selected directory, handed from the strict realPath to the canonical port inside one resolution.
freshChecks: Missing, file, untraversable and dangling selections still fail with usage before the command runs.
Where the port cannot answer, the real path is resolved again before the listing walk.
Workspace location construction resolves its project root again as its own validity boundary.
execution-directory.lifetime: The resolved path lives for one command and is not persisted.

after-canonical-port-s-identity-check.basis: After the canonical port's identity check, the runtime stats the canonical path to admit a directory and fail a file with usage.

every-command-runs-through-command-runti.basis: Every command that runs through the command runtime resolves its selected directory with one strict real-path lookup when the canonical native path port spells it.

where-canonical-port-absent-cannot-spell.basis: Where the canonical port is absent or cannot spell the path, the real path is resolved again before the listing walk, which follows no links.

git-locator-discovery-checkout.resource: The source view of a root locator install: scoped temporary shallow Git checkouts (axm-source-discovery-*) keyed by url, ref and transport context, plus the per-probe-loop local walk and retained-tree verdicts.
git-locator-discovery-checkout.publication: Directory tree: a scoped temporary shallow checkout, created on first lookup and removed when its scope closes or its clone fails.

reads.note: One shallow clone per url, ref and transport context and one broad convention discovery per checkout and subpath answer every type probe.
One broad walk of a local source path per unfiltered probe loop; each typed probe receives a fresh filtered array in walk order.

A retained canonical tree of a local, HTTP or Git source is verified against its accepted snapshot once per probe loop, with or without selectors, keyed by binding, canonical path, accepted tree integrity and package root.
With explicit selectors each selected type runs its own filtered walk, whose outcomes depend on the filter.

git-locator-discovery-checkout.existingSharing: One Git checkout and one broad discovery already served every type probe of a locator install, and the selection already carried the same source view into planning. This change also shares one broad local walk per unfiltered probe loop and one verification of each retained local, HTTP or Git package tree per probe loop, with or without selectors.
git-locator-discovery-checkout.preparedInputs: One scoped shallow Git checkout per url, ref and transport context and one broad convention discovery per checkout and subpath answer every type probe of a root locator install, and the selection carries that source view into planning. Within one unfiltered probe loop, one broad local walk answers every typed probe with a fresh filtered array in walk order, including the typed discovery of each verified retained local, HTTP or Git tree at its discovery root. Within one probe loop, with or without selectors, the retained-verdict map records each retained local, HTTP or Git package tree once its accepted snapshot is established, and later probes of the loop reuse that verdict instead of hashing the tree again; failures are never kept.
freshChecks: A failed checkout or discovery is not cached and is retried by the next lookup.
A failed broad walk answers nothing; each typed probe then walks on its own and fails or drops out as it would alone.
With explicit selectors every type keeps its own filtered walk.
A retained tree with a different binding, canonical path, accepted integrity or package root is verified again.
A retained Git tree whose hash does not match or cannot be computed is hashed again by each later probe, which then discovers from the Git source at the accepted commit.
Acquisition later fetches by commit and checks the accepted tree.
git-locator-discovery-checkout.lifetime: Checkouts live in the scope that created the locator source view, which spans selection and planning, and are removed when it closes; the walk map and verdict map live for one probe loop; nothing is retained across invocations.

explicit-selectors-each-selected-type-ru.basis: With explicit selectors each selected type runs its own filtered walk of a local source, because duplicate rejection, MCP gating, marketplace names and source-path matching depend on the filter.

one-git-checkout-one-broad-convention.basis: One Git checkout and one broad convention discovery answer every type probe of a root locator install, and the selection carries the same source view into planning.

root-locator-install-without-selectors-w.basis: A root locator install without selectors walks a local source once per probe loop and verifies each retained tree once, instead of once per probed type.

retained-git-tree-hashed-once-per-probe-.basis: A root locator install of a Git source, with or without selectors, hashes each retained Git package tree from the same clone URL once per probe loop: the loop's retained-verdict map records the tree only after its hash matches the accepted tree integrity, keyed by binding, canonical path, accepted integrity and package root, and later probes skip that hash while each still asks for its own typed discovery of the tree, which an unfiltered probe loop answers from one broad walk. A mismatch or failure is never kept, the map ends with the probe loop, and acquisition later fetches by commit and checks the accepted tree.

handoff-manager-lock.resource: The foreign Skills-manager lock file: skills-lock.json in a project workspace, or .skill-lock.json under the user state home (or .agents) in user scope.
handoff-manager-lock.publication: Atomic replacement of the manager lock with the transferred entry removed and every other entry and unknown field preserved, after a settlement snapshot, recorded as a modified footprint.

reads.note: The manager lock is read and decoded once at prepare; its entries select names and become each step's comparison baseline.
Each catalog agent's effective skills directory is resolved once per prepare, and each supported exact spelling joins the base .agents/skills directory in one first-seen list.
Source discovery runs once per selected name; a Git source is cloned once per name.
The upstream package is fetched once per name and its materialized-tree integrity is computed.

Each listed skills directory's entry is resolved fresh once per name, and the resolution that classifies a present entry also follows it to its physical referent, so a retargeted alias resolves to a new referent; a dangling link is followed live.

Each distinct referent's materialized-tree integrity is compared with the upstream, and the manager's published project hash with the recorded hash when one is recorded; the two digests differ in selection, ordering and failure precedence.

The shared skill install planner reads the upstream skill again to plan each name's install step, because discovered references do not carry decoded skill documents across the source and extension-kind contracts.
Each step re-reads the manager lock under the transition lock, refuses a changed entry, and preserves the current unrelated entries.
The lock path is protected by a settlement snapshot before the atomic write.
The modified footprint records the published postimage for settlement.

handoff-manager-lock.existingSharing: The lock read at prepare was already transferred to every step as its comparison baseline, and the atomic writer publishes without reading the destination. Prepare now builds one list that holds each exact skills-directory spelling once and uses it for every selected name, reuses the physical referent that the native entry resolution of a present copy already followed, and computes each distinct referent's digests once per selected name for every alias that resolves to it.
handoff-manager-lock.preparedInputs: Within one selected name, the materialized-tree integrity and the manager project hash of each distinct resolved referent are computed once and reused for every alias that resolves to it; each alias is still compared and refused on its own. The skills-directory list holds each exact spelling once, in first-seen order, from the base .agents/skills directory and every catalog agent's supported effective skills directory, and every selected name's iteration resolves its native entry in each listed directory. The referent that native entry resolution follows for a present copy keys that name's referent digests, is digested when it is new, and is recorded among the step's material paths without being resolved again.
freshChecks: Every alias is resolved to its referent fresh and compared against this name's upstream integrity and recorded hash.
A dangling link at a selected name's native entry is followed live so it is refused with its own location error.
Each selected skill is its own plan step, and each step re-reads the manager lock under the transition lock before retiring targets and writing.
The execution candidate's fingerprint over the lock and every target is checked again at apply.
handoff-manager-lock.lifetime: The referent digest map is local to one selected name's iteration of prepare; the prepare-time lock document is captured by the planned steps and released when the execution candidate resolves; nothing is retained across invocations. The skills-directory list is built afresh by each prepare call and released when that call returns. A present copy's referent is used within one directory iteration of prepare, after which it remains only as a key of that name's referent digests and among the step's material paths.

each-distinct-referent-digested-twice-on.basis: Each distinct referent is digested twice, once as a materialized tree and once with the manager's published project-hash algorithm, because the two digests differ in selection, ordering and failure precedence.

each-step-re-reads-manager-lock.basis: Each step re-reads the manager lock under the transition lock, refuses a changed entry and preserves the current unrelated entries before it writes.

handoff-computes-materialized-tree-integ.basis: Handoff computes the materialized-tree integrity and manager project hash of each distinct installed referent once per selected skill, and still compares and refuses every alias on its own.

handoff-from-git-source-discovers-fetche.basis: Handoff from a Git source discovers and fetches the upstream once per selected name, so names that share one URL and revision clone and fetch separately.
handoff-from-git-source-discovers-fetche.openQuestion: May skills handoff verify every selected name that shares one Git (url, ref) against a single discovery checkout, instead of a separate discovery clone and commit fetch per name, accepting that a moved branch or a remote refusing commit fetches changes the outcome?

shared-skill-install-planner-reads-upstr.basis: The shared skill install planner reads the upstream skill again for each selected name, because discovered references do not carry decoded skill documents across the source and extension-kind contracts.
shared-skill-install-planner-reads-upstr.openQuestion: May skills handoff hand each discovered skill document to the shared install planner instead of the planner reading the upstream skill again, accepting that discovered references then carry decoded skill documents across the source and extension-kind contracts?

handoff-reuses-entry-resolution-referent.basis: Handoff preparation follows each present native copy to its physical referent once per selected name and directory, in the native entry resolution that also classifies the entry, and digests and records that referent without resolving it again; a dangling link is still followed live so it is refused with its own location error. The referent is a string used within one directory iteration of prepare, every alias is still resolved fresh in that prepare, compared against the upstream integrity and recorded hash and refused on its own, and the manager-lock re-read under the transition lock and the candidate fingerprint check at apply stay fresh.

handoff-resolves-each-distinct-skills-di.basis: Skills handoff lists each exact skills-directory string once, in first-seen order, from the base .agents/skills directory and every catalog agent's effective skills directory, so a native entry that several agents share is resolved once per selected name.
