The list is built afresh by each prepare call; lexically distinct directories, including aliases of one physical directory, are still resolved, digested, compared and refused on their own, and the manager-lock re-read under the transition lock and the candidate fingerprint check at apply stay fresh.

hook-native-config.resource: An agent's JSON or JSONC settings file that holds native Hook registrations under its settings key (for example .claude/settings.json), whose physical file other native readers may share.
hook-native-config.publication: Under the physical file's exclusive write: rollback protection, parent creation and one identity-preserving write of the whole planned document recorded as created or modified, followed by a string readback against the planned text.

reads.note: Every run admits each distinct spelling of the target and its aliases once against the planned physical file, a dry run's own target spelling through the unlocked admission that selected it, and checks each declaration root for overlap against one resolution of the settings file before reading; escaping aliases and overlapping declarations are refused.
One read of the physical file per run (a dry run reads unlocked, an apply reads under the exclusive write); every decision of that run uses this text.
Renders the planned document from the raw text and the declared owners, validating whole-file grammar of raw and planned text before any write; each render is one native render fact.
Reader preflight captures which native readers share the physical file and checks raw and planned text against each reader's grammar; under the lock it is the fresh route check.

Observes the declared units in the raw text with the JSONC grammar and, when none are declared, whether foreign content remains; per-owner subset renders run only in dry runs, to report owners that are already current.
The write authority protects the file before the first write so a failed closure restores it.
After the write, one fresh read compared as a string with the planned text; it is never parsed.
Native package references read the settings file on their own: once as planning evidence for an uninstall and once on the post-image as the fresh check before canonical retirement.

The hook manager's eager pre-write observation of each plan is held for the immediate consumer inside the same owner call; a take returns it at most once, and a second take or a take after the consumer returns observes fresh.

Under the transition lock and before the first write, an uninstall observes the hook plans of the proposed graph on the pre-withdrawal file as its refusal; the later run observes the text the settings write produced.
Separate hook manager calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase each read the settings file live; that phase never caches file bytes across owner calls.

Each hook manager call that selects contributors hashes every contributor package it was not handed a prepared hash for and whose canonical observation framed none from its strict walk, projection preparation frames each proposed root's tree integrity and package content hash from one strict walk, its own or its accepted-canonical observation's, unless it was handed that root's hash, and each call reads each contributor's fixture-evidence receipt at most once, so separate projection runs and outcome evaluations of one invocation still hash and read unchanged packages again.

Each hook projection plan build and each configured-agent outcome evaluation that holds no writer routes this manager issued for the same configured agents resolves the configured Hook writer routes, checking each configured agent's settings path against the native authority roots.

hook-native-config.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, each run already read the physical file once and fed that text to rendering, reader preflight and unit observation, and its post-write readback was a single string comparison; parses were not shared, so one run parsed its two or three distinct texts 5 to 11 times, and callers repeated a whole dry run to observe plans the manager had just observed. Within one inspection, native package-reference evidence reads and parses each native configuration file once through the inspection's shared reference view. This change shares exact-text parses, each distinct spelling's admission and one resolution of the settings file for its overlap checks within one run, hands the hook manager's eager observation of each plan to its immediate consumer, and within one hook manager call shares the writer routes, the configured Hook entries, one desired-state evaluation, the validated package root's real path, the package content hashes and tree digests a walk already framed, fixture-receipt statuses and projected outcomes, while one native package-reference inspection shares each path probe.
hook-native-config.preparedInputs: Within one run, exact (format, text) parses are shared through a private syntax view whose per-consumer copies equal an unshared parse: a dry run joins an enclosing observation view, and a locked apply always opens fresh cells under the exclusive write. Apply runs skip the dry-run-only per-owner renders. Each native Hook settings run admits each distinct spelling of the target and its aliases once, and its overlap checks share one resolution of the settings file through a checker that lives for the run. The hook manager hands its eager dry-run observation of each plan to the immediate consumer in the same owner call instead of a second dry run, and the before and after exposure passes share one syntax observation view. Hook configuration hands its verified package content hash to the hook manager's contributor selection, and an enabled Hook authored native preflight hands its package content hash for the staged root to the hook manager's projection preparation; the manager uses a handed hash only on an exact package-root match. Within one hook contributor selection, an acquired retained contributor the caller handed no hash for takes the package content hash its canonical observation framed from the strict walk of the accepted tree at its exact package root. Within one hook projection preparation, one strict tree walk frames both the materialized-tree integrity and the package content hash of each proposed package root that was not handed a hash, and a Registry Hook whose accepted package is usable at the ref's content key takes those digests from the strict walk its accepted-canonical observation made of the same root, the package content hash only when no hash was handed in and the accepted row selects exactly the ref's content. Within one hook projection preparation, the projected configured-agent outcome evaluation records a deeply frozen fixture-receipt status for each prospective contributor, each prepared contributor takes a structured copy of the deeply frozen outcomes that evaluation computed for it, matched by position, and a prepared contributor that evaluation left out takes a copy of the status recorded for the same root, content hash and configuration hash. A hook projection preparation resolves the configured Hook writer routes once for its plan observation and its prepared contributors' outcomes and hands them, frozen, to its caller; Hook install planning passes them to each selected ref's projected configured-agent outcome evaluation, which uses them only when the same manager issued them for the same configured agents in the same order. The hook manager's runtime-file validation of a package returns the real path of the package root it resolved lazily once every declared file was found contained in it, and a contributor's fixture-evidence receipt key in the same call takes that real path on an exact match with its canonical root instead of probing and resolving the root again. Within one hook projection plan build or configured-agent outcome evaluation, contributor selection and the projected outcome evaluation share one lazy read of the configured Hook entries in axm.json, and each native observation or apply of a plan shares one lazy read of its own among every contributor and every reader of the settings file it renders. A hook projection plan build that reads desired state live through the manager's own reader, outside a read phase and without a handed desired graph, derives its output authority from its one desired-state evaluation, and a Hook uninstall that withdraws native registrations, or a Hook deactivation, hands its one evaluation to its own projection run, which takes its graph and output authority from it. Within one native package-reference inspection, each successful existence and real-path probe of an absolute path is kept for the rest of that call.
freshChecks: Every run admits each distinct spelling of the target and its aliases against the planned physical file, a dry run letting the unlocked admission that selected the target stand for its own spelling and a locked apply admitting every spelling again under the exclusive write, and every declaration still resolves its own root and gets its own overlap verdict.
Each run reads the physical file fresh; a locked apply never reuses the eager observation or another run's parses.
Reader route capture and per-reader grammar preflight run in every run.
Planned output of new text is validated before any write.
Rollback protection, parent creation, identity-preserving write and footprint record run under the exclusive write.
The post-write string readback runs after every write.
The eager pre-write refusal still observes every plan; a handed-over observation that is taken twice, or after its consumer returns, is observed fresh.
The in-transition pre-write refusal under the transition lock and the post-image package-reference check stay separate observations.

Consumers that receive no handed-over observation observe their plans fresh: materialization's retained plans from an earlier owner call, the sync closure planner, the hook install step's re-plan, the authored native preflight and the invariant-fact participants.

The strict materialized-tree walk runs for every prepared hook package root, including one whose package content hash was handed in, either in the preparation or as its accepted-canonical observation of that same root, and a drifted, absent or other-version accepted package and a fetched or local root keep their own strict walk.
Hook configuration and each in-lock authored preflight hash the package again under the transition lock instead of reusing a preparation hash.

Every later projection preparation, in-lock run, configured-agent outcome call and plain projection-plan call reads fixture receipts fresh, and an outcome evaluation that fails hands no recorded statuses on.
The candidate freshness check, the satisfied-install check, the reuse decision and the refusal of a Hook changed after projection preparation observe afresh.
Every later contributor selection observes and hashes afresh, and the strict walk stays each retained contributor's integrity check that refuses a drifted tree.
The applied outcome evaluation, Pack member steps and every later preparation resolve the writer routes afresh, and the native reconciliation's own route checks run on every observe and apply.

Every native observation and every locked apply of a plan reads the configured Hook entries live for itself, a locked apply before its own native write, as do use callbacks, the per-ref preparation and plans observed or applied after their producing call returned.

A package without runtime files, a local or fetched source root and every later owner call probe the package root and resolve its real path again for the fixture-receipt key, and every later contributor selection or projection preparation resolves the root again in its own runtime-file validation.

Plans in a read phase, plans handed a desired graph and plans under a different ambient desired-state reader evaluate the graph and capture the output authority separately, and a withdrawal's route checks, contributor selection, native observe and apply reads and post-write readback run live.
Every native package-reference inspection, including the one under the transition lock before canonical retirement, probes each distinct path live again.
hook-native-config.lifetime: Syntax cells belong to one run, or to the enclosing observation view a dry run joins, and are cleared when it exits on success, failure or interruption; each consumer receives its own copy. Spelling admissions and the overlap checker's resolution of the settings file belong to one run. A handed-over plan observation exists only while the consumer callback runs inside the same owner call and is taken at most once. A handed package content hash, and a package content hash or tree integrity an observation framed from its walk, lives only for the hook manager call it is handed to, and tree-walk bytes stay local to one digest computation. Recorded fixture-receipt statuses and projected outcomes are created by the projected outcome evaluation of one projection preparation and released when that call returns. Writer routes a preparation resolves live for that preparation and its caller's planning call. A validated package root's real path lives for its validation call and the owner call it is returned to. A shared read of the configured Hook entries lives for one owner call, or for one observe or apply execution of a plan. A desired-state evaluation lives for one plan build, or for one withdrawing manager call under the transition lock, where it precedes the first write. Native path probes live for one native package-reference inspection. Nothing crosses the transition lock, a read phase or an invocation.

after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.basis: After apply, configured-agent verification of a Hook the operation leaves enabled runs the hook manager projection observation again in a fresh read view, reading, parsing and rendering each agent hook settings file once more after the locked run has written it and read it back. The locked readback proves only that one closure's write landed as planned, while verification is the last observation of every left-enabled Hook against the final desired state, separated from that readback by the release of the exclusive write, closure settlement or rollback, and later closures' writes.
after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.openQuestion: Should an accepted requirement state that the configured-agent outcomes an operation reports for a Hook it leaves enabled come from a fresh observation after every closure settles rather than from a closure's locked readback?

after-hook-write-one-fresh-read.basis: After a Hook write one fresh read is compared as a string with the planned text and never parsed.

each-hook-manager-call-selects-contribut.basis: Hook manager calls in different validity boundaries each hash their contributor packages and read their fixture-evidence receipts again: the prepare-time projection and the in-lock re-plan or locked run, calls before and after closure writes, post-apply verification in its fresh read view, the execution review after preparation's read phase is retired, and separate authored preflight runs that each end their own read view. A lock acquisition, a write or an ended read phase lies between each pair, and an ended phase is never reused.

hook-manager-calls-joined-by-document-on.basis: Hook manager calls by different owners that share only a mutation's document-only prepare phase, such as set-activation's configured-agent outcomes and a later projection observation, each hash their contributor packages and read their receipts live. That phase shares document decoding only, so sharing a hash derived from package bytes across its owner calls would upgrade it to physical caching.

prospective-hook-contributor-receipt-rea.basis: Inside one hook projection preparation, the projected outcome evaluation reads the fixture receipt and checks the canonical root once for each prospective contributor and records a deeply frozen status keyed by package root, content hash and configuration hash; the prepared contributors take that evaluation's outcomes, and an evaluation in the same call of a prepared contributor it left out takes a copy of a matching recorded status instead of reading the receipt and checking the canonical root again. An unreadable receipt is recorded as invalid like any other status, an evaluation that fails hands no statuses on, and the recorded statuses are released when that call returns, so every later preparation, in-lock run, configured-agent outcome call and plain projection-plan call reads receipts fresh.

provider-and-observation-phase-hook-mana.basis: The two hook manager calls inside one configured-agent outcomes provider call, a projection-plan observation followed by a configured-agent outcome evaluation, and separate manager calls inside one pure-query observation read phase each hash every contributor package and read its receipt again. The accepted requirements do not decide whether that read, when the provider serves post-apply verification, is a post-write readback or advisory evidence that may be shared, and the calls select contributors from different graphs and agent lists.
provider-and-observation-phase-hook-mana.openQuestion: Is the hook package-content hash and fixture-receipt read that a provider or observation-phase call performs after apply a post-write readback that each manager call must repeat, or advisory evidence that later manager calls in the same provider call or observation phase may reuse by exact package root?

each-hook-projection-run-parses-every.basis: Each Hook projection run parses every exact settings text once through a private syntax view whose per-consumer copies equal an unshared parse; a locked apply opens fresh cells under the exclusive write.

enabled-hook-authored-native-preflight-h.basis: An enabled Hook authored native preflight hands the package content hash it computes for the staged root to the hook manager's projection preparation through its prepared content hashes, and the manager uses that hash on an exact package-root match instead of framing its own. The handed hash is the advisory fixture-receipt key and lives only for that preflight run; the strict materialized-tree walk still runs at the same position, and each in-lock preflight hashes its own staging.

every-hook-run-captures-which-native.basis: Every Hook run captures which native readers share the physical file; under the lock this is the fresh route check.

hook-configuration-hands-verified-packag.basis: Hook configuration hands its verified package content hash to the hook manager's contributor selection instead of the manager hashing the package again.

hook-manager-hands-eager-pre-write.basis: The hook manager hands its eager pre-write observation of each plan to the immediate consumer in the same owner call, and the before and after exposure passes share one syntax observation view, removing one dry run per immediate consumer.

hook-projection-preparation-hashes-each-.basis: Hook projection preparation frames each proposed package root's materialized-tree integrity and package content hash from one strict tree walk and one read of each file, and the bytes stay local to that one digest computation. The walk's failures and their order are unchanged, and the tree integrity stays the baseline that locked materialization compares to refuse a Hook changed after projection preparation.

invariant-fact-participants-observe-each.basis: Invariant-fact participants observe each hook plan again after the manager's eager observation, one extra dry run per plan per call.
invariant-fact-participants-observe-each.openQuestion: May the projection participant contract, and the planning-observations specification's participant example, gain an observed-plans member so invariant facts consume the manager's eager observation?

locked-hook-apply-skips-per-owner.basis: A locked Hook apply skips the per-owner subset renders that only a dry run reports.

native-package-references-read-from-sett.basis: Native package references are read from the settings file as uninstall planning evidence and again on the post-image as the fresh check before canonical retirement.

pack-uninstall-planning-sync-closure-pla.basis: The sync closure planner, the hook install step's re-plan, materialization's retained plans and the authored native preflight still observe projection plans the managers already observed. Pack uninstall planning uses the managers' eager observation only as its native-withdrawal refusal and does not observe those plans again.
pack-uninstall-planning-sync-closure-pla.openQuestion: May the sync closure planner, the hook install step's re-plan, materialization's retained plans and the authored native preflight consume the projection managers' eager observation instead of observing their plans again?

projection-s-eager-observation-locked-ru.basis: A projection's eager observation and its locked run parse and render the same settings text separately, because syntax results belong to one observation or one locked publication.
projection-s-eager-observation-locked-ru.openQuestion: Should the native syntax contract admit an owner-call lifetime so a projection's eager observation and its locked run share exact-text parses?

separate-hook-manager-calls-inside-mutat.basis: Separate hook manager calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase each read the settings file live.
separate-hook-manager-calls-inside-mutat.openQuestion: May an owner-call dry-run preimage map share native file bytes inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase?

under-transition-lock-before-first-write.basis: Under the transition lock and before the first write, uninstall observes the hook plans of the proposed graph on the pre-withdrawal file; the later run observes the text the settings write produced.

when-plan-exposes-enabled-non-workspace.basis: When a plan exposes an enabled non-workspace Hook ref, the execution review evaluates that Hook's current outcomes by running the hook manager's projection observation again for the reviewed targets, reading and parsing native hook settings files that planning's projection already read. Planning observed the proposed graph's plans and handed that observation only to its immediate consumer, while the review asks whether the current files realize the prior graph's contributors and starts after preparation's read phase has been retired.

execution-review-observes-current-outcom.basis: Within one execution review, the same current-outcome observation repeats for each reviewed hook ref whose targets and prior graph agree. The review reads live state with no read phase, and the previous ref's source fetch or copy can run between the observations, so the accepted requirements do not decide whether a later ref's exposure decision may rest on an earlier observation.
execution-review-observes-current-outcom.openQuestion: May one execution review reuse a single live current-outcome observation across several reviewed hook refs that share targets and prior graph, even when another ref's source fetch or copy runs between them?

within-one-inspection-native-package-ref.basis: Within one inspection, native package-reference evidence reads and parses each native configuration file once through the inspection's shared reference view, however many inspected packages it checks.

hook-preparation-resolves-writer-routes-.basis: A Hook projection preparation resolves the configured Hook writer routes, which check each configured agent's settings path against the native authority roots, once for its plan observation and its prepared contributors' outcomes, and hands them, frozen, to its caller. Hook install planning passes them to each selected ref's projected configured-agent outcome evaluation, which reuses them only when the same manager issued them for the same configured agents in the same order and otherwise resolves them itself; they live only for that planning call. The applied outcome evaluation, Pack member steps, later preparations and the native reconciliation's own route checks on observe and apply still resolve the routes afresh.

hook-preparation-hands-projected-outcome.basis: Inside one Hook projection preparation, each prepared contributor takes the deeply frozen outcomes the projected configured-agent outcome evaluation computed for it, matched by position and returned as structured copies in the shared sort order, instead of a second read of the hook settings entries, configuration resolution, configuration hash and per-agent outcome evaluation. A prepared contributor that evaluation left out, such as a withdrawn one, is evaluated on its own with the fixture-receipt statuses the call read and the same error mapping. The outcomes live for that call, and projection plans and every other outcome evaluation still evaluate afresh.

hook-run-admits-each-distinct-spelling-o.basis: Each native Hook settings run admits each distinct spelling of the target and its aliases once, in first-occurrence order: a dry run lets the unlocked admission that selected the target stand for its own spelling, and a locked apply admits every distinct spelling again under the exclusive write before reading the file. The overlap checks of one run share one resolution of the settings file through a checker that lives only as long as the run, while every declaration still resolves its own source and gets its own overlap verdict. The escape, alias-change, scope, reader preflight, write and readback checks still run in every run.

hook-package-validation-resolves-root-on.basis: The Hook manager's validation of a Hook package's runtime files resolves the package root's real path lazily, the first time a declared file reaches that step, holds it for that validation call and returns it to its owner call only once every declared file was found contained in it; every later contributor selection or projection preparation resolves the root again. Every declared asset and handler entrypoint still gets its own lexical containment check, existence check, real path, containment check against the resolved root and file-type check, with the same failures in the same order.

hook-fixture-evidence-probe-resolves-pac.basis: When a Hook manager call (a projection plan build, a configured-agent outcome evaluation or a projection preparation) evaluates the fixture evidence of a contributor it holds no recorded receipt status for, the receipt key takes the package root's real path that the runtime-file validation in the same call resolved, handed on as a frozen list only when every runtime file it checked was contained in that root and used only on an exact match with the contributor's canonical root, instead of probing the root's existence and resolving its real path again. A prepared package hands its root only when it was read from its canonical root, and a package without runtime files, a local or fetched source root and every later owner call probe and resolve the root as before; the containment checks stay in the validation, and a symlinked root still keys its receipt by its real path.

one-inspection-probes-each-native-path-o.basis: Within one native package-reference inspection, the successful existence and real-path probe of each absolute path is kept for the rest of that sequential call, so a native configuration file that several catalog readers declare, and each candidate path of its parsed value, is probed once instead of once per reader. Every reader is still recorded, a failed probe still aborts the inspection with the same error, and every inspection, including the one under the transition lock before canonical retirement, probes each distinct path live again.

retained-hook-selection-frames-hash-from.basis: Within one Hook contributor selection, an acquired retained contributor the caller handed no package content hash for takes the package content hash its canonical observation frames from the strict walk of the accepted tree, handed only to that selection and only from a usable observation whose walk matched the accepted tree integrity at the contributor's exact package root, instead of hashing the same package again. A handed hash for the exact root still comes first, and workspace-authored, handed-over and unaccepted contributors hash their package as before; the hash lives for that manager call, the strict walk stays the contributor's integrity check that refuses a drifted tree as a contributor tree mismatch, and every later selection observes and hashes afresh.

usable-registry-hook-preparation-takes-o.basis: Within one Hook projection preparation, a Registry Hook whose accepted package is usable at the ref's content key takes the tree integrity its accepted-canonical observation verified in its strict walk of that root, and, when no hash was handed in and the accepted row selects exactly the ref's content, the package content hash framed from the same walk, instead of walking the accepted tree again; the digests are handed out only from a walk that matched the accepted tree integrity, only for the usable root chosen in that per-ref scope, and the bytes stay inside the walk. A drifted, absent or other-version accepted package and a fetched or local root keep their own strict walk, and the tree integrity stays the baseline that locked materialization compares, while the candidate freshness check, the satisfied-install check, the reuse decision and the refusal of a Hook changed after projection preparation observe afresh.

hook-withdrawal-hands-desired-evaluation.basis: A Hook uninstall that withdraws native registrations, and a Hook deactivation, evaluate the desired state once under the transition lock through the Hook manager's own reader outside a read phase, derive the withdrawn declarations from that frozen evaluation and hand it to their own projection run, which takes its graph and output authority from it instead of evaluating the desired state again. The evaluation lives for that one manager call and precedes its first write; under a read phase or a different ambient desired-state reader each step evaluates as before, an uninstall that retains native registrations evaluates nothing here, and route checks, contributor selection, the native observe and apply reads and the post-write readback still run live.

live-hook-plan-derives-authority-from-gr.basis: A Hook projection plan build that reads desired state live, outside a read phase, without a handed desired graph and through an ambient desired-state reader that is the manager's own, evaluates the desired state once and derives its output authority from that frozen evaluation instead of evaluating again to capture it; the evaluation lives for that plan build. Plans in a read phase, plans handed a desired graph and plans under a different ambient reader still evaluate the graph and capture the authority separately, and the plan's native observation, locked apply and readback still read live.

hook-projection-run-reads-configured-ent.basis: Within one Hook projection run or one configured-agent outcome evaluation, contributor selection and the projected outcome evaluation share one lazy read of the configured Hook entries in axm.json, made where the first of them needs it, and each native observation or apply of a plan makes one lazy read of its own that every contributor and every reader of the shared settings file it renders takes; the shared value is the reader's frozen document or a frozen copy, and a failing read fails its first consumer with the same error. Each read lives for one owner call or one observe or apply execution, so every observation and every locked apply still reads the entries live before its own native write, and use callbacks, the per-ref preparation and plans observed or applied after their producing call returned read them live.

hook-test-receipt.resource: The local hook test receipt under the workspace runtime directory, mode 0600.
hook-test-receipt.publication: Atomic replacement of the hook test receipt.

reads.note: The hook manifest is read once as bytes before execution for both the manifest and the first package content hash, which decodes the first fixture's declared files for that fixture's reads.
The package is hashed before and after fixture execution; a changed package writes no current-content receipt.
Each fixture resolves its entrypoint inside the package afresh, and each fixture after the first reads its input and expected output files afresh, after earlier fixtures have run.

hook-test-receipt.existingSharing: No receipt is read back: each run hashes, executes and writes one receipt without reading a previous one. Within one run, the hook.json bytes read for the manifest and the first fixture's files decoded by the content hash are now shared with their later readers instead of being read again.
hook-test-receipt.preparedInputs: The hook.json bytes the manifest reader reads feed the first package content hash for the root hook.json entry when lstat reports a regular file, and that hash walk decodes the first selected fixture's declared input and expected output files for that fixture's reads when the resolved file is one of them.
freshChecks: The package hash after execution reads the package live and is compared with the hash before execution.
Each fixture's entrypoint is resolved and contained afresh.
Each fixture file, including the first fixture's files whose text comes from the content hash, is resolved, contained and size-checked live before use.
Each fixture after the first reads its input and expected output files live after the previous hook process has run.
hook-test-receipt.lifetime: The hook.json bytes and the first fixture's decoded files are created and held inside one TestHook.run call and are not transferred between owners; the decoded files are cleared before the first hook process starts, and the bytes are released when the run returns.

fixture-execution-reads-hook-json-before.basis: Within one hooks test run, hook.json is read once as bytes for the manifest, the first package content hash uses those bytes for the root hook.json entry when lstat reports a regular file, and that hash walk decodes the first selected fixture's declared input and expected output files for that fixture's reads. These values stay private to the run and the decoded files are cleared before the first hook process starts; each resource is still resolved, contained and size-checked, refusals still come before any hash, and the after-run hash reads live.

later-fixtures-read-resources-live-after.basis: Each fixture after the first reads its input and expected output files again and resolves, contains and stats its entrypoint again after an earlier fixture's hook process has run package code in the package root. That execution is a validity boundary because it may rewrite the package, so each later fixture's resources are read, contained, bounded and validated against the live package before that fixture executes.
later-fixtures-read-resources-live-after.openQuestion: Should the accepted hooks test requirement state that each fixture's input, expected output and entrypoint are read, contained and validated against the live package after any earlier fixture's hook process has run?

package-hashed-before-after-fixture-exec.basis: The package is hashed before and after fixture execution because execution may change it, and a changed package writes no current-content receipt.

inspection-content-reads.resource: Content bytes of the files one local inspection or check assessment reads, keyed by physical path and file identity.

reads.note: Each read resolves the physical path and compares the file identity before and after reading; an alias or content change during the inspection is reported as a changed read, which makes check coverage partial.
Captured bytes of a physical file are reused within one view while its identity is unchanged.

inspection-content-reads.existingSharing: One view reuses the captured bytes of a physical file whose identity is unchanged; check's assessment view routes later owners' reads through the identity check as well.
freshChecks: Each read re-resolves the path and compares the file identity before reusing captured bytes.
An inspection nested inside check opens its own content view over check's assessment view, so its reads repeat the path resolution and identity checks.
inspection-content-reads.lifetime: Captured bytes and diagnostics live for one inspection or assessment view and are released when it returns.

one-inspection-reuses-captured-bytes-eac.basis: One inspection reuses the captured bytes of each physical file whose identity has not changed.

install-metadata.resource: ~/.axm/install-meta.json, the record of how this installation was installed (under AXM_USER_HOME when set).
install-metadata.publication: Atomic replacement of the install metadata document after a verified script or package-manager upgrade records the new method.

reads.note: Owner detection reads install metadata once through a read-if-present read and keeps the found, missing, invalid and unreadable statuses as evidence.
The store's own reader also reads if present and maps every non-found outcome to none; no command calls it.
Owner detection resolves the real path of each distinct executable path and of the script bin directory once; a single execution, so its real-path lookups repeat nothing.
A verified upgrade writes the install metadata once with the new method and reads nothing; it is a single execution and does not reuse the detection read.

install-metadata.existingSharing: Owner detection runs once per upgrade preparation, and apply consumes that preparation.
install-metadata.preparedInputs: The metadata text, read once by a read-if-present read instead of an existence probe followed by a read; it stays inside detection.
freshChecks: Each upgrade preparation reads the file fresh.
The record written after a verified script or package-manager upgrade describes the new method and does not reuse the detection read.
install-metadata.lifetime: The text is released when detection returns; nothing is retained across invocations.

upgrade-owner-detection-reads-install-me.basis: Upgrade owner detection reads install metadata once through a read-if-present read and keeps its found, missing, invalid and unreadable statuses.

instructions.resource: Instruction alias files AXM maintains beside the canonical instruction file (copies, or symlinks published through the shared link publisher), the managed alias-ignore region of the workspace .gitignore, and the scratch entries of the symlink capability probe.
instructions.publication: Copies: protection of created ancestors and of the target, parent creation and an identity-preserving write recorded as created or modified. Symlink aliases go through the shared symlink publisher. .gitignore pattern changes run under the file's exclusive write with a native-insertion capture and record per pattern. The capability probe creates and removes a scratch directory, file and link inside the workspace root.

reads.note: One observation reads each admitted referent once: planned items and the project-scope missing-source check share one completed content admission per resolved roots, path and owner root, every other call keeps its own admission and roots, and all of them share the referent's bytes, so decisions, planned items and content witnesses bind the same bytes.
Witnesses capture each input's entry admission, anchor and container identities and a content digest.

The symlink capability probe writes and removes a scratch link in the workspace root once per observation unless the caller passes a capability; as a mutation it retires an enclosing observation phase.
Prepare re-observes each target live and re-derives ownership from fresh content; alias items that share a source read it once per prepare call, before any write.

Apply re-takes the witnesses fresh (whole set, per target, and the ignore file) and refuses any change; a copy publishes the bytes its passing source witness read when the referent and a fresh address-only admission match, and reads fresh otherwise.
The deletion guard re-reads target and source bytes before removing a stale alias; modified copies are retained.
writeFile probes whether the target exists to label the footprint created or modified, before the identity-preserving writer's own stat.
Readiness walks for Git management and strictly admits and reads the ignore file; directly after an observation of the same working tree it consumes that observation's strict admission instead.

When apply plans a .gitignore change, its managed region dry run walks for Git, strictly admits and reads the .gitignore and refuses malformed fences once before any alias write; the locked region write walks for Git and admits the file again before its exclusive write and reads it under that write.
The ignore file is read under its exclusive write; each eligible pattern insertion is checked with the digest-free structural predicate.

Each pattern's insertion capture and record re-read and prove the file and its receipts; a withdrawal resolves and retires under one live gate and forgets removed patterns in one receipt-store update.
Reconciliation re-reads the projection rows and observes the projection after applying, and fails unless it is current.

instructions.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, reconciliation already reused the preflight's symlink capability for its post-transition observations and read-back, sync reused it for its read-back, and the sync instruction step passed an observed capability on; copy content and ownership were decided from the observation snapshot. One observation still read the same referent two to five times, and apply read a source again right after verifying its witness.
instructions.preparedInputs: Admitted referent bytes are shared inside one observation, one prepare call and one apply iteration (the source witness's read is the publication read). Planned items and the project-scope missing-source check of one observation share one completed content admission per resolved roots, path and owner root. Readiness consumes the observation's strict ignore-file admission when it directly follows an observation of the same working tree. When instruction disable removes no alias and its in-lock observation found a complete region in a Git working tree, its region removal takes its Git management, strict admission and unlocked read from that observation. An observation asked for a prior membership derives that membership's route targets for the agent-addition planning step. Enable planning for a changed configuration hands the desired observation's symlink capability to the superseded-configuration preflight, and reconciliation hands the preflight's symlink capability to the superseded configuration's removal under the transition lock. Ignore-file withdrawal resolves and retires under one live gate and forgets removed patterns in one receipt-store update, and the insertion predicate no longer hashes. Within one link classification, a link whose referent is the source's own path resolves that entry once for both sides. Across the planned items of one observation, completed link-classification entry resolutions are shared through the admission cells under their own key. Within one target classification, a target that is not a link is classified absent or an unowned directory from the entry kind its own content admission resolved. The row key that classification computed for a planned copy, an unowned file or a stale recorded copy, including a computed absence of key, is carried with the observed item to the orphan-row decision. Each prepare iteration measures its target's row key from the entry path its own target entry admission returned. When apply plans a .gitignore change, its managed .gitignore dry run is its one unlocked fence check before any alias write.
freshChecks: Witness entry and content admissions, alias evidence, the stale-candidate stage, the user-scope missing-source check, prepare and apply each keep their own admission and native roots before any shared bytes are consulted.
Witnesses are re-taken fresh at apply (whole set, per target, ignore file) with unchanged hash counts per witness.
Prepare re-observes each target live; the deletion guard re-reads before removal.
Each prepare iteration admits its target's entry live; that admitted entry addresses the target's later writes and removals, and its row key is measured from it with the scope root resolved live.
Link classification still probes whether the resolved referent exists, and a target whose content admission refuses it or whose readable bytes cannot be read is still probed for existence and stat.
The superseded configuration's removal keeps its own in-lock observation.

Readiness runs live when no matching observation precedes it, and when apply plans a .gitignore change its unlocked fence check is the managed region dry run, which walks for Git, admits and reads the .gitignore live before any alias write.

Instruction disable keeps its live fence check; its region removal walks for Git, admits and reads the .gitignore live after any alias removal or when the observation found no matching complete region, and the region write always walks for Git and admits the file before its exclusive write and reads it under that write.
An observation without a passed capability probes symlink support itself.
Agent-addition planning resolves each prior route target live, and observes the prior membership separately when the observation cannot derive its route targets from its own facts.
Each ignore pattern keeps its own insertion capture, record and post-write proof.
The post-write observation must find the projection current.
The managed .gitignore dry run evaluates the structural predicate at its own unlocked boundary, records nothing, and is never reused by the locked write.
A closure that touches the instruction surface probes symlink capability before its source write and again in the alias reconciliation after it.
instructions.lifetime: Read cells belong to one observation call or one prepare call and are cleared when it exits; admission cells belong to the planned-item and missing-source stages of one observation call and are cleared when those stages end; link-classification entry resolutions live in those cells under their own key and are cleared with them; carried row keys live only for one observation call and never reach the snapshot or the status shape; a link classification's shared source entry and a target classification's admitted entry kind are consumed within that classification; a prepare iteration's admitted target entry keys that target and addresses its later writes and removals in the same operation; the fence dry run is consumed in the same apply call before its first alias write; a source witness's bytes are consumed in the same apply iteration and released after its write or record; the strict admission and region facts are a small immutable record on the snapshot, consumed only by a readiness check with no write in between or by a disable's region removal under the same transition lock when no alias removal precedes it; prior route targets are an immutable array on one observation's snapshot, consumed by the agent-addition planning step that asked for them; the symlink capability is a boolean held from an enable's desired observation to its superseded-configuration preflight during planning, and for one reconciliation under the transition lock. Nothing crosses lock acquisition, a preview and apply boundary, or an invocation.

applying-instruction-projection-changes-.basis: Applying an instruction projection with changes verifies every witness once, then verifies each stale target, written target and the .gitignore witness again immediately before that mutation, so the witnesses of the first mutation are admitted, identity-captured and read twice with no write between. The per-mutation verification is the last fresh conflict check before each removal or write under the transition lock and preserves changes made after the observation, while the full pass refuses with the first changed witness in sorted order before any write; for a written copy, the per-target pass also supplies the source bytes it publishes.

before-removing-each-owned-instruction-c.basis: Before removing each owned instruction copy under the transition lock, the deletion guard reads the copy and its source again after the prepare step and the witness pass read them, and removes the copy only when those bytes are what AXM last wrote or the current source. That read is the last preservation check before the copy is retired; the witness pass only compares each path with the observation's digest and returns no bytes, so it cannot stand in for the guard's decision.

closure-changes-instruction-region-probe.basis: A closure that changes an instruction region probes symlink capability when it records copies before the source write and again in the alias reconciliation after it, both under the transition lock.
closure-changes-instruction-region-probe.openQuestion: May recording instruction copies before a source write hand its symlink capability to the alias reconciliation that follows that write in the same transaction?

configuration-changing-instruction-enabl.basis: A configuration-changing instruction enable observes the superseded configuration again under the transition lock before removing its aliases.
configuration-changing-instruction-enabl.openQuestion: May instruction enable remove a superseded configuration's aliases from its in-lock preflight observation, accepting the changed outcome for foreign alias edits between preflight and removal?

disabling-instruction-management-under-t.basis: Disabling instruction management under the transition lock checks the .gitignore region fences live, walking for Git, strictly admitting and reading the ignore file, before its in-lock observation walks for Git and reads the ignore file again. Taking the fence refusal from the observation would let a lockfile or settings read failure take precedence over the malformed-fence refusal and would run the symlink probe's scratch create and remove before a refusal, which the accepted requirements do not decide; the observation cannot take its read from the fence check either, because the probe writes under the workspace root between them and the observation's read is the .gitignore witness baseline.
disabling-instruction-management-under-t.openQuestion: May instruction disable run its malformed-fence refusal after the in-lock observation, using that observation's strict .gitignore admission, accepting that a lockfile or settings read failure then takes precedence over the fence refusal and that a refused disable has already run the symlink probe's scratch create/remove?

disable-without-alias-removal-reuses-obs.basis: When instruction disable removes no alias and its in-lock observation found a complete alias region with a matching strict referent in a Git working tree, the region removal takes its Git management, strict admission and unlocked read from that observation, which the disable holds for its one closure under the transition lock with no write between. The region write still walks for Git, admits the file and reads it fresh under its exclusive write before refusing a malformed region or rendering the removal.

disable-after-alias-removal-rereads-giti.basis: When instruction disable removed an owned alias, the region removal walks for Git, strictly admits and reads the .gitignore again after the in-lock observation did. The alias file removal and created-directory retirement write to the observed workspace between the two, so the observation no longer stands for the live file.

disable-rechecks-gitignore-region-withou.basis: When the in-lock observation found the workspace outside Git, no complete alias region, a failed strict admission or a different referent, the region removal walks for Git and reads the .gitignore live again, and that live walk and read decide whether it reports the region unchanged or goes on to the region write. They are the last fresh check behind the unchanged result, so the prepared no-op passes the same freshness boundary as a write.
disable-rechecks-gitignore-region-withou.openQuestion: May instruction disable report its region removal unchanged from its in-lock observation's .gitignore facts when it removed no alias and that observation found the workspace outside Git, no region, a failed strict admission or a different referent?

gitignore-region-write-rereads-under-fil.basis: The region write walks for Git and strictly admits the .gitignore again before taking its exclusive write, then reads the file again under that write. The walk and admission are the last route check before the file lock and name the locked file, and the locked read is the fresh read that feeds the malformed-region refusal, the preservation of foreign entries and the rendered write.

disabling-observes-instruction-targets-a.basis: Disabling observes the instruction targets again under the lock, after planning observed them, so only aliases that are still owned are removed.

each-instruction-copy-gitignore-write-pr.basis: Each instruction copy or .gitignore write probes whether its target exists to label the footprint before the identity-preserving writer's own stat.
each-instruction-copy-gitignore-write-pr.openQuestion: May instruction file writes lose the distinct 'Failed to inspect instruction file' diagnostic and its failure order so the created or modified label comes from the identity-preserving writer's own stat?

each-managed-gitignore-pattern-insertion.basis: Each managed .gitignore pattern insertion keeps its own pre-image and post-image receipt.

enabling-changed-instruction-configurati.basis: Enabling a changed instruction configuration probes symbolic-link capability once before the lock and hands it to the superseded-configuration preflight.

instruction-management-enabled-install-p.basis: With instruction management enabled, install planning observes the instruction projection in the Rule, Knowledge or Pack projection plan, probing symlink capability and reading the admitted referents, and observes it again for instruction readiness after the plan is assembled, inside the same planning read phase. The plan's observation includes prospective roots and refuses through its own error, so readiness decided from it can refuse or pass differently and report a different failure; readiness still observes when no plan observation ran, and a hand-over of only the symlink capability crosses source resolution that may run between the two probes, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
instruction-management-enabled-install-p.openQuestion: May install planning decide instruction readiness, or at least take its symlink capability, from the instruction observation a Rule, Knowledge or Pack projection plan made earlier in the same planning read phase, accepting that this observation uses prospective roots and that source resolution may run between the two?

instruction-management-enabled-local-ins.basis: With instruction management enabled, a local inspection that reports both Rule and Knowledge agent outcomes observes the instruction projection once for the Rule outcomes and again for the Knowledge outcomes, probing symbolic-link capability and reading the admitted referents in each observation. The first observation's symlink probe writes through the inspection's observation read phase and retires it as a mutation, so the second observation reads live state and no bounded owner holds both values without extending an ended phase.

instruction-management-enabled-one-instr.basis: With instruction management enabled, one instruction observation reads each admitted referent once and the apply publishes the bytes its passing source witness read.

instruction-management-enabled-planning-.basis: With instruction management enabled, planning a coding-agent removal observes the remaining agents' instruction projection twice with no write between: once in the cleanup step's capture of the native outputs those agents still require, and again in the instruction step. The two observations take equivalent inputs, but planning the cleanup step from the instruction step's observation reports a lockfile read failure ahead of the cleanup step's ownership, presence and retained-output refusals, and handing the cleanup step's observation to the instruction step needs a planning lifetime spanning both step collections that no read phase, owner call or lock provides; the accepted requirements decide neither.
instruction-management-enabled-planning-.openQuestion: May agents remove plan its cleanup and instruction steps inside one planning lifetime so that the instruction step consumes the remaining membership's instruction snapshot (re-flagged with the posture overrides) that the cleanup step's retained-output capture just observed, given that no read phase, owner call or lock currently spans the two collections?

instruction-management-enabled-preparing.basis: With instruction management enabled, preparing the withdrawal of a Rule or Knowledge contribution whose region keeps other contributors observes the instruction projection in the exposure review's proposed pass and again in its current pass, inside one document-only read phase with no write between them. The two passes are separate manager owner calls whose prospective roots can differ, and the accepted requirements do not settle whether handing one pass's physical observation, including its symlink probe result, to the other upgrades the document-only phase to physical caching.
instruction-management-enabled-preparing.openQuestion: May one shared-projection exposure review reuse its proposed pass's instruction projection observation for its current pass when both are called with identical observation arguments inside the same document-only read phase, given read-phases-have-bounded-lifetimes forbids upgrading a document-only phase to physical caching?

instruction-management-enabled-rule-know.basis: With instruction management enabled, a Rule or Knowledge activation observes the instruction projection for its readiness gate and again in each pass of its shared-projection exposure review, probing symlink capability and reading the admitted referents each time, inside one document-only read phase with no write between them. The exposure passes observe with prospective roots the gate does not use, so routes built from the gate's observation differ when the canonical instruction file is absent or empty, and even a hand-over of only the symlink capability crosses materialization planning that may wait on source acquisition; whether a document-only phase may carry these physical observations across owner calls is not decided by the accepted requirements.
instruction-management-enabled-rule-know.openQuestion: May a Rule or Knowledge activation's exposure review build its instruction routes from the readiness gate's instruction observation, or at least reuse the symlink capability the gate probed, across the intervening materialization planning inside one document-only read phase, even though the exposure passes observe with prospective roots the gate does not use?

instruction-management-enabled-rule-mana.basis: With instruction management enabled, the Rule manager observes the instruction projection after each region write to report which agents read the target, probing symlink capability and reading the admitted referents, and when the region changed the alias reconciliation that follows observes the same tree again. The alias reconciliation observes with its own membership and withdrawn sources, may follow other region writes or alias writes, and does not run when aliases are deferred or no region changed, so taking the report from it changes the agents and targets that install and projection steps report; the accepted requirements do not decide that change.
instruction-management-enabled-rule-mana.openQuestion: May the Rule manager's reported readers of its instruction target be taken from the in-lock preflight of the alias reconciliation that follows in the same closure, accepting that the report then reflects that reconciliation's membership and withdrawn sources and any region writes made between, and must still be observed by the manager itself whenever aliases are deferred or no reconciliation follows?

instruction-prepare-re-derives-ownership.basis: Instruction prepare re-derives ownership from fresh content, while the witness pass compares identity and bytes with the snapshot.

instruction-projection-runs-managed-giti.basis: Instruction projection runs its managed .gitignore update first as a dry run outside the file's exclusive write, before writing any alias, judging each added eligible pattern with the structural-insertion predicate and resolving removed patterns' inverses; the update under the exclusive write after the alias writes reads the file, judges and resolves again.

instruction-readiness-directly-after-obs.basis: Instruction readiness directly after an observation of the same working tree consumes that observation's strict .gitignore admission instead of walking for Git and reading the ignore file again.

instruction-reconciliation-reuses-prefli.basis: Instruction reconciliation reuses its preflight's symlink capability for its transition and read-back, setup's instruction sync reuses it for its read-back, and the sync instruction step passes its observed capability on.

lint-fix-reads-instruction-rows-observes.basis: lint --fix reads the instruction rows and observes instruction targets again under the transition lock before and after repair.

one-instruction-observation-admits-same-.basis: One instruction observation admits each source and target path once for its planned items and its project-scope missing-source check, sharing one completed content admission per resolved roots, path and owner root that the observation call owns and clears when those stages end. The witnesses, alias evidence, the stale-candidate stage, prepare and apply still admit fresh. The user-scope missing-source check is not a repeat of the item admission, because it admits under workspace-only authority while the items admit under the scope's captured native roots, so it admits on its own.

instruction-witnesses-admit-entry-and-co.basis: Each instruction witness admits its path again as an entry and again for its content after the planned items admitted it. The witness admissions are the observation's last route and identity capture: their address, parent and leaf identities and content digest form the fingerprint that apply re-takes and compares to refuse later changes, and the entry boundary and the content boundary with its hardlink refusal are distinct checks.

symlink-capability-probed-before-lock-ag.basis: Symlink capability is probed before the lock and again under the transition lock, and a closure's required native outputs are captured before its writes and validated after them; each probe serves its own validity boundary.

unattended-setup-apply-probes-symlink-ca.basis: Unattended setup apply probes symlink capability again instead of reusing a positive plan-time probe.
unattended-setup-apply-probes-symlink-ca.openQuestion: May unattended setup apply reuse a plan-time positive symlink probe, accepting that a capability lost between plan and apply then fails and rolls back instead of falling back to a copy?

when-agents-added-instruction-management.basis: When agents are added with instruction management enabled, step planning observes the instruction projection once, and that observation derives the prior membership's route targets from its own per-item source and target observations, alias evidence and discovery tree. The derived targets live on that observation's snapshot for the one planning step; the step still resolves each prior target live, observes the prior membership separately when the resulting membership does not contain it, and the in-lock apply still checks the eligible targets.

when-instruction-enable-changes-configur.basis: When instruction enable changes the configuration, the superseded configuration's removal under the transition lock reuses the preflight's symlink capability instead of probing again.

link-classification-resolves-shared-sour.basis: Within one link classification, a link whose referent is the source's own path resolves that entry once for both sides, in the planned-item and stale-candidate stages alike. Across the planned items of one instruction observation, completed link-classification entry resolutions are shared through that stage's admission cells under their own key and cleared when the stage ends. The existence probe, content admissions, witnesses and prepare's live per-item classification under the transition lock stay fresh.

orphan-row-decision-reuses-classificatio.basis: Within one instruction observation, the row key that classification computed for a planned copy, an unowned file or a stale recorded copy, including a computed absence of key, is carried with the observed item and reused for the orphan-row decision; targets that classification never keyed are keyed as before. The carried keys live only for that observation call and never reach the snapshot or the status shape, and prepare keys each target afresh under the transition lock.

apply-checks-gitignore-fences-once-befor.basis: Instruction apply checks the .gitignore fences once before any alias write: the managed region dry run walks for Git, strictly admits and reads the .gitignore and refuses malformed fences, as the readiness check does, instead of a separate fence check repeating the same walk, admission and read just before it. Apply still re-takes the ignore-file witness, and the locked region write still walks for Git, admits the file and reads it again under its exclusive write.

target-classification-uses-own-admission.basis: Within one instruction target classification, a target that is not a link is classified absent, or an unowned directory, from the entry kind its own content admission just resolved, instead of probing the path's existence and stat again. The existence and stat probes still run when that admission refuses the path or a readable entry's bytes cannot be read, files keep their content judgment, observation and prepare each still admit the target, and the witnesses are unchanged.

prepare-keys-each-target-from-entry-admi.basis: Within one prepare iteration, the target's row key is measured from the entry path that the iteration's own target entry admission returned, instead of resolving the target entry again. The scope root is still resolved live for the key, and that admission stays the last resolution of each prepared target before later writes and removals address it.

knowledge-corpus.resource: The installed Knowledge corpus selected for a concept query: the enabled bundles of the selected workspace, their manifests and their captured source bytes.

reads.note: The desired graph and the accepted resolutions that select enabled bundles are read in one documents-only workspace read phase per capture.
One canonical observation per selected bundle, which also captures and decodes its knowledge.json.
Each bundle manifest is taken from the observation's capture when it is the knowledge manifest at the expected package path; otherwise it is read live.
The corpus source bytes are read twice and compared, so a changing corpus is reported instead of indexed.
The capabilities report reads the desired graph and the knowledge lock entries again after the capture, outside its read phase, to name bundles the other scope also installs.

knowledge-corpus.existingSharing: Each query already built one index snapshot from one captured corpus. This change also reads the bundle selection's settings and lockfile in one read phase per capture, hands the observation's knowledge.json decode to the capture, hashes each source of the settled capture once, and computes the corpus fingerprint once per index snapshot.
knowledge-corpus.preparedInputs: The bundle selection reads its settings and lockfile in one documents-only read phase, and the knowledge.json decode its canonical observation made is handed to the corpus capture instead of being read again. The corpus capture hashes only its settled capture into source revisions, which travel with the captured sources to the index snapshot as each concept reference's content revision. The index snapshot computes the corpus fingerprint once over the captured sources; the capabilities report, the query page and its cursor, and the related output consume it as the snapshot fingerprint, and the concept references of a lone bundle use it as their bundle fingerprint, while each bundle of a multi-bundle corpus gets its own fingerprint over its own sources.
freshChecks: Each capture opens its own read phase, so a second capture in one invocation observes a changed selection.
The corpus bytes are captured under a double read that reports a changing corpus.
A capture attempt whose confirming read differs hashes nothing and retries the complete capture, up to its attempt limit, before the changing corpus is reported.
A manifest the observation did not capture, at a different path or of another type, is read live and fails as before.
The capabilities report's cross-scope collision check reads the desired graph and knowledge lock entries again after the capture.
knowledge-corpus.lifetime: The read phase's documents end with the bundle selection; the captured manifest decode lives in the selection result for one capture; the source revisions are created by the capture call once its confirming read settles and live in the captured sources until the index snapshot records them; the corpus fingerprint is created by the snapshot call and lives in the snapshot; the index snapshot lives for the query or capabilities report that captured it.

after-corpus-capture-cross-scope-collisi.basis: After the corpus capture, the cross-scope collision report reads the desired graph and the Knowledge lock entries again. The bundle selection's documents-only read phase ends before the capture, which runs between the two reads, so the report observes the selected scope's configured and locked names in a later read instead of reusing an ended phase.

corpus-capture-decodes-each-bundle-s.basis: The corpus capture decodes each bundle's knowledge.json from the canonical observation's capture instead of reading it again.

corpus-capture-reads-selected-bundle-sou.basis: Corpus capture reads the selected bundle sources twice and compares them, so a changing corpus is reported instead of indexed.

cross-scope-collision-report-reads-decod.basis: The cross-scope collision report reads and decodes the unselected scope's settings and lockfile after workspace location construction decoded the settings of both scopes for the layout. The construction's loaders belong to its own call and are released when it returns, and the bundle selection's read phase begins and ends in between, so the report reads live state in its own read; the two reads also compute different values, since construction defaults absent settings and fails on malformed ones while the report treats an absent or unreadable scope as not determined and also reads that scope's lockfile.

installed-corpus-selected-one-documents-.basis: The installed corpus is selected in one documents-only read phase per capture, so the lockfile is read and decoded once.

corpus-capture-hashes-settled-sources-on.basis: Each corpus capture attempt only reads the selected sources, and after the confirming read and the byte compare succeed the settled capture is hashed once into source revisions, owned by that one capture call. The confirming read, the byte compare, the retry count and the changing-corpus refusal stay, and an attempt that does not settle hashes nothing.

index-snapshot-fingerprints-captured-cor.basis: The index snapshot computes the corpus fingerprint once over the captured sources, as an immutable value local to that snapshot call, and uses it as the bundle fingerprint when it indexes exactly one bundle, while the corpus capture returns only its sources and hashes no corpus fingerprint. Each bundle of a multi-bundle corpus still gets its own fingerprint over its own sources, the snapshot and bundle fingerprint values are unchanged, and the capture's confirming read, byte compare, retry and changing-corpus refusal stay.

lint-git-index-snapshot.resource: A private scoped temporary directory (axm-lint-git-index-*) holding a byte-exact copy of the stage-0 Git index entries: files with their modes, symbolic links, and gitlink directories.
lint-git-index-snapshot.publication: Directory tree: staged index entries written into a scoped temporary directory, created once per lint run and removed with its scope.

reads.note: The Git root is detected from the selected path, and unmerged index entries are refused.
The index listing is collected once, hashed once for the index fingerprint, decoded once and parsed.
One blob batch over the unique object ids, held as one buffer and sliced into per-blob views.
Lint reads the materialized snapshot back through its host-faithful observation boundary, as it reads a live workspace.

lint-git-index-snapshot.existingSharing: One blob batch already covered the unique object-id set, and the index fingerprint was already hashed once from the listing.
lint-git-index-snapshot.preparedInputs: Blob contents are written from views into the private batch buffer instead of copies, and each distinct parent directory is created once per materialization by a cached creation that an entry runs or joins only after its own containment check.
freshChecks: Each entry's lexical containment is checked before its parent directory is created or its content written.
Unsupported modes and non-UTF-8 symbolic-link targets are refused per entry.
There is no workspace transition lock: the view is read-only and is identified by the index fingerprint carried in the native view.
A Git-index view of the user scope never shares the observation phase's settings and lockfile cells with lint's read model.
lint-git-index-snapshot.lifetime: The blob views and the parent-directory memo live for one materialization call; the snapshot directory is released with the lint scope.

staged-every-stage-0-index-entry.basis: With --staged, every stage-0 index entry is written into a private snapshot and lint reads back what it needs, because the snapshot is a host-faithful view with its own physical boundary.

staged-staged-blobs-written-from-views.basis: With --staged, staged blobs are written from views of the one batch buffer and each snapshot parent directory is created once per materialization.

local-inspection.resource: The local inspection document for selected subjects: inventory rows, canonical observations, manifests, native placements, MCP facts and native package references, built per query.

reads.note: One query resolves its selection and builds the detailed document inside one observation read phase with MCP inspection and native package reference views.

When check's scope expands to pack members or contributors, a second query builds the detailed document for every expanded subject, including the requested ones, so a change between the two reads is reported as a changed read.
The expanded query drops the type filter and assigns its own result-local subject, request and native ids, so the first query's items are not transferred into it.

A Pack's member inspection reads pack.json again after its item's canonical observation read it; inside check that read is the last identity check of the manifest in the inspection's content view, so a rewrite after the observation is reported as a changed read.

MCP package facts read and decode mcp.json again from the inventory row's paths with the MCP server manifest grammar, and fail the query with an MCP configuration error where the observation records the package as corrupt.

local-inspection.existingSharing: One query builds its document inside one read phase and one content view; check's queries share check's assessment view. Inside a query's observation read phase, through that phase's own observation port, an enabled installed Knowledge bundle's complete package inspection is also shared, once per exact package root. Each item whose canonical observation captured the manifest at the inspected root takes its manifest version from that capture and that observation's decode of it, instead of reading and parsing that manifest again. A Pack item's member inspection reuses that decode when the pack.json text it reads is exactly the captured text and the decode is a Pack.
local-inspection.preparedInputs: Each Knowledge package inspection outcome, success or failure, by exact package root, that the Knowledge manager's discovery contributor selection makes for an enabled installed bundle through the query's observation read phase, consumed by the inventory document, which counts the bundle's concepts and diagnostics from it; each consumer applies its own mapping. Each item's capture of the manifest text its canonical observation read at the inspected root, with that observation's decode of it made at most once on first use, is consumed by the item's manifest version, which applies the type and name guard to the decode or parses the captured text when that decode failed, and by a Pack item's member inspection, which uses the decode only for exactly the captured text and only when it is a Pack.
freshChecks: Each query captures or joins a read phase; a query after that phase ends observes again.
A scope-expanding check builds the requested subjects' detailed document again in its expanded query.
The Knowledge manager still observes each enabled bundle's canonical package in each discovery contributor selection a query makes; only the package inspection after it is shared.
An inspection through any port other than the read phase's own observation port, including check's assessment view, inspects the Knowledge package again.
Each item stats its inspected root before it takes a manifest version, and an item whose observation captured no manifest at that root reads and parses the manifest itself.
A Pack's member inspection reads pack.json again for every Pack item and decodes the text it read itself when that text differs from the captured text or the captured decode is not a Pack.
An MCP server item's package facts read and decode mcp.json again from the inventory row's paths with the MCP server manifest grammar.
local-inspection.lifetime: The document is returned to its caller; nothing is retained across queries. The Knowledge package inspection outcomes are held in a map the workspace read view creates with each observation read phase and clears when that phase closes. Each item's manifest capture and its cached decode are created with that item's canonical observation and are released when that item's inspection completes.

expanded-check-inspection-drops-type-fil.basis: The expanded check inspection drops the type filter and assigns its own result-local ids, so the first query's items are not transferred into it.

inside-check-local-inspection-opens-own.basis: Inside check, local inspection opens its own content view over check's identity-checking filesystem, so each inner read repeats the path resolution and identity checks.
