inside-check-local-inspection-opens-own.openQuestion: May LocalInspection inside check rely on check's assessment view for identity diagnostics, changing the per-query diagnostic scope reported in check output?

local-inspection-enabled-installed-knowl.basis: Inside one active observation read phase, the outcome of a complete Knowledge package inspection, success or failure, is prepared once per exact package root when the Knowledge manager selects discovery contributors for an enabled installed bundle; the read phase owns it and releases it when it closes, and the inventory document counts the bundle's concepts and diagnostics from that outcome while each consumer keeps its own mapping. Only inspections through the phase's own observation port receive it: the manager's package-tree check still reads in every selection, and staged, prepared and check's assessment-view inspections, which read through other ports, inspect the package again.

when-check-s-scope-expands-pack.basis: When check's scope expands to pack members or contributors, the expanded inspection builds the requested subjects' detailed document again.
when-check-s-scope-expands-pack.openQuestion: When check expands its scope, may it build the requested subjects' detailed inspection once, so that an edit between request resolution and the single detailed inspection is observed once instead of being reported as a changed read?

manifest-version-takes-item-observation-.basis: Each local inspection item takes its manifest version from its own canonical observation's decode of the manifest at the inspected root, made at most once and released with the item, instead of reading and parsing that manifest again, with the same type and name guard after the root's stat succeeds. When that decode failed the captured text is parsed for the identity, with no capture the manifest is read as before, and the root's stat and the observation's own read stay.

mcp-package-facts-read-mcp-json-again.basis: Local inspection's MCP package facts read and decode mcp.json again after the item's canonical observation read it, because they choose the root from the inventory row's paths, decode the MCP server manifest grammar, and fail the query with an MCP configuration error where the observation records the package as corrupt.
mcp-package-facts-read-mcp-json-again.openQuestion: May local inspection's MCP package facts reuse the item's canonical observation of mcp.json, given that they choose the root from the inventory row's paths, decode McpServerManifestSchema, and fail the query with McpConfigInvalid or McpConfigIoFailed where the observation records corrupt?

pack-member-evidence-reuses-observation-.basis: A Pack's member inspection still reads pack.json itself on every route, and reuses its item's canonical observation decode of that manifest, which lives for that item, only when the text it read is exactly the captured text and that decode is a Pack, instead of parsing and decoding the manifest again. Otherwise it decodes the text it read with the same failure text, so a manifest rewritten after the observation yields members from the rewritten bytes.

pack-member-evidence-reads-pack-manifest.basis: A Pack's member inspection reads pack.json again after its item's canonical observation read it: in show the observation phase's cell serves the read, and in check it re-resolves the path and compares the file identity through the inspection's content view as the last identity check of that manifest for the item, so a rewrite after the observation is reported as a changed read.
pack-member-evidence-reads-pack-manifest.openQuestion: May a Pack's member evidence take pack.json from its item's canonical observation instead of reading it again, given that inside check that read is the last identity check of the manifest in the inspection's content view?

local-registry-publication-lock.resource: <extension dir>/.publish.lock, its .recovery gate, and a private .publication-* owner-record directory.
local-registry-publication-lock.publication: Copy or link: an owner record written once and published by an exclusive hard link, removed on release.

reads.note: Release re-reads the lock and removes it only while it still carries this owner's token.
Reclaiming a stale lock re-reads the current owner and the recovery gate before removing anything.

local-registry-publication-lock.existingSharing: The owner record was already written once and hard-linked for each acquisition attempt.
freshChecks: A filesystem lock across processes and clients.
Release and reclaim re-read the owner token.
local-registry-publication-lock.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the owner record directory is removed when the lock scope closes.

reclaiming-dead-holder-releasing-publica.basis: Reclaiming a dead holder and releasing the publication lock re-read its owner record to prove which token holds the lock.

local-registry-store.publication: Atomic replacement of the archive and then the index on publish, under the publication lock; a plain index rewrite, outside the publication lock, on a visibility change.

reads.note: Index lookups, scans, catalogs, callback archive reads, publish and the publication preview probe the path before reading it, so absence stays distinct from an inspection failure.
Admission reads index.json again after selection read it, for the publisher binding and integrity current at admission, then reads the archive and hashes it once.
A read inside a content callback probes, reads and hashes the admitted archive again, refusing bytes that changed after admission.
A read of a ref that names no integrity selects a version from index.json, and its admission reads index.json again for the identity check.
Publish re-reads the current index under the publication lock and recomputes the preview condition before writing.

Outside an open Registry read phase, or after it has ended, the publication preview probes and reads each target and pack-dependency index.json itself; inside one it takes each index from the phase, which already holds the indexes the preparation's batched selection read, and publish revalidates it under the lock.

local-registry-store.existingSharing: Index lookups and selections requested through the Registry client factory run inside the Registry read phase, which reads each index once per phase; a local publish already wrote the caller's archive bytes and recorded integrity without reading or hashing them again; a batch admission admitted each item once per content callback.
local-registry-store.preparedInputs: A single-item exact read returns the bytes and verification evidence its admission produced instead of probing, reading and hashing the archive again; admitted and callback reads return verification evidence that Registry consumers accept instead of hashing; a published archive is handed to the atomic writer without a copy; inside an open Registry read phase, a file Registry's publication preview takes each target and pack-dependency index from the phase, which already holds the indexes the preparation's batched selection read, instead of reading index.json itself.
freshChecks: Every admission re-reads index.json after selection, then re-reads the archive and hashes it.
Every read inside a content callback re-reads and re-hashes the admitted archive.
A read of a ref that names no integrity re-reads index.json at admission after selecting from it.

The publication preview probes and reads each target and pack-dependency index.json itself only when no Registry read phase is open or the phase has ended; inside an open phase it takes each index from the phase, so each index.json is read once per phase.
Publish re-reads the index and recomputes the preview condition under the publication lock.
Existence probes precede index lookups, scans and callback archive reads so absence stays distinct from failure.
local-registry-store.lifetime: Admitted bytes and their evidence belong to the single read that returned them and are released by its consumer; publish borrows the caller's archive for the write only; the index answers the publication preview takes from the phase belong to the Registry read phase that publication preparation's workspace read view opens and are released when that phase ends; nothing is retained across invocations.

each-file-registry-index-archive-read.basis: Each file Registry index or archive read is preceded by an existence probe so that an inspection failure keeps its own error detail apart from a read failure.
each-file-registry-index-archive-read.openQuestion: Should the local Registry replace its exists-then-read probes with typed reads, accepting a merged inspection and read error detail and a retargeted local-storage-failures specification binding?

file-registry-batch-admission-later-cont.basis: With a file Registry, batch admission and the later content-callback read of the same archive each read and hash it, so a change after admission is refused.

file-registry-each-exact-content-admissi.basis: With a file Registry, each exact-content admission reads and hashes the archive as well as index.json, so an apply that admits its Registry refs before acquisition and again after confirmation reads and hashes each admitted archive at every admission, although it acquires nothing.

file-registry-evaluation-reads-extension.basis: With a file Registry the evaluation reads the extension index once and writes nothing.

file-registry-exact-admission-reads-inde.basis: With a file Registry, an exact admission reads index.json again after the selection read it, so the publisher binding and integrity it admits are the ones the Registry holds at admission.

file-registry-index-json-read-once.basis: With a file Registry, index.json is read once per boundary: at resolution, at each admission's identity check and at the re-admission after confirmation.

file-registry-publication-preview-reads-.basis: Inside an open Registry read phase owned by the Registry client factory, a file Registry's publication preview takes each target and pack-dependency index from the phase, which already holds the index the preparation's batched selection read, so each index.json is probed and read once per phase. The phase lives for the publication preparation and ends with it; with no phase, or one that has ended, the preview reads index.json itself, and publish still re-reads the index under the publication lock and recomputes the preview condition.

file-registry-read-ref-names-no.basis: A file Registry read of a ref that names no integrity selects a version from index.json and then reads index.json again at admission for the identity check.
file-registry-read-ref-names-no.openQuestion: May the local Registry admit a range-selected identity against the index it just read for selection instead of re-reading index.json at admission?

file-registry-single-exact-read-returns.basis: With a file Registry, a single exact read returns the bytes and evidence its admission verified instead of probing, reading and hashing the archive again.

file-registry-update-re-reads-extension.basis: With a file Registry the update re-reads the extension index the evaluation read, to refuse the write when the visibility revision changed after that evaluation.

file-registry-update-re-reads-extension-.basis: With a file Registry the update re-reads the extension index the evaluation read, to refuse the write when the visibility revision changed after that evaluation.

local-publish-writes-archive-from-caller.basis: A local publish writes the archive from the caller's buffer without a defensive copy.

under-publication-lock-publish-reads-ind.basis: Under the publication lock, publish reads the index the preview read again and recomputes the preview condition against live state.

mcp-config-writer.resource: Agent MCP configuration files (JSON, JSONC, TOML, YAML, Starlark or VS Code settings) whose servers container one or more native readers may share.
mcp-config-writer.publication: Once per planned physical file under its exclusive write: rollback protection, parent creation, a transient backup of the locked preimage, one identity-preserving write recorded as created or modified, then a readback of the declared consumers' containers.

reads.note: Validation re-resolves every declared alias that planning resolved to the planned physical path before any native write, and applying the writes re-resolves them again; a retargeted alias is refused.

Validation reads each planned file once, preflights co-readers on the preimage and on the rendered proposal, checks Pi name collisions, and keeps the proposal, the preimage and whether the server already existed.

Under the exclusive write the writer re-resolves the path and reads the preimage fresh; it uses the validated proposal only when path, full preimage text and write inputs are identical and renders again otherwise; the change label and backup content always come from this read.
With an adoption, the locked read is compared with the expected entry before rendering; no validated proposal is used on that path.

Renders preserve other native values and refuse a new-server insertion that would change unrelated content; the structural predicate is evaluated once when the formatted edit was already judged on the same pair.
Removal target resolution reads competing entries as precedence evidence before planning.

Removal preparation reads every group, or takes the targets and bytes a disabled connection's inspection observed in the same read, and preflights its co-readers before any later work; then every withdrawal re-checks routes per group and reads the container once for the removal render and the second co-reader preflight.
Every removal, a dry run included, re-reads the file and re-renders all selected keys under the exclusive write and preserves other values; a dry run skips only the write.
A transient backup is written from the locked preimage text (no extra read) and removed after the write, retained when the write fails.
After publication the file is read back and each configured consumer's container is decoded.
An install reads and decodes its canonical manifest once for distribution selection and invocation resolution, freezes it and hands it to the manifest-backed agent sync of every name it projects.

The locked adoption freshness check and the adoption step read and hash every adopted source and refuse one that changed after discovery; preparation inside discovery's read phase uses discovery's fingerprints instead.

Configured MCP target resolution admits each declared route live once per call and reads the bytes and resolves the referent of each exact path spelling once per call for the competing-entry checks of every member that declares it; adoption preparation and import discovery read them although discovery read the same physical document.

Discovery checks the route of, reads and fingerprints each native MCP file once per call for every configured agent that declares it, and hands its texts to the in-order target validation of the same read phase.
In-order adoption validation reads each target file discovery did not read once per call and validates a write at a path discovery read against discovery's text.
A Pack disable reads and preflights each container once in its removal preparation, and each MCP member's dry-run withdrawal plans from those frozen facts.

mcp-config-writer.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, multi-server removal already rendered every selected key and published each physical file once; validation, locked writers and readback each parsed inside one syntax read view; the transient backup came from the locked preimage text. This change hands each validated write preparation to the locked writer, reads each removal group's container once for its render and co-reader check, judges an identical insertion pair structural once, hands an install's decoded canonical manifest to its agent syncs, and lets adoption preparation rely on discovery's source fingerprints; import discovery no longer re-reads and hashes the selected native MCP file to compare it with the fingerprint it just took. It also resolves the configured MCP targets once for every candidate of one adoption preparation or import discovery and validates a write at a path discovery read against discovery's text, lets the members of one configured MCP target resolution share each declared route's admission and each path spelling's competing-entry bytes and referent, lets the configured agents that declare one native MCP file share its route check, read and fingerprint within one discovery, prepares a Pack disable's MCP withdrawal once for all its MCP members, and parses a same-grammar competing location that names the target file once.
mcp-config-writer.preparedInputs: Validation hands the writer one frozen preparation per planned write (physical path, exact preimage text with absence as empty, rendered proposal, whether the server existed, and the write inputs), consumed under the exclusive write only for an identical path and preimage. Removal planning reads each group's container once in its co-reader step and renders from that text. A formatted JSON-like insertion already judged structural on the identical pair skips the second predicate, and the predicate no longer hashes. An install hands the canonical manifest it decoded, frozen, to the manifest-backed agent sync of every name it projects, which decodes the file itself when none is handed over. Adoption preparation relies on the source fingerprints discovery took in the same read phase, and the prepared candidate carries no source text. Discovery hands the texts it read to the in-order target validation of the same adoption preparation or import discovery call and to nothing else. In-order validation resolves the configured MCP targets once for that call, gives each candidate its own copy of the resolved groups, and serves each candidate's planned write from discovery's frozen text at the exact physical path discovery read, or from one read per other target file for that call; each candidate's plan consumes its copy of the groups, and its co-reader preflights, Pi name-collision check and render consume the preimage. Within one configured MCP target resolution, members that share a declared route consume one successful live admission, and their competing-entry checks consume the shared bytes and referent of each exact path spelling. Within one native MCP discovery call, the configured agents that declare the same native MCP file consume one route check, one read and one fingerprint of it, and the native configuration observation view parses each exact text once per grammar and hands every reader its own copy. A Pack disable with an MCP member resolves the configured targets, reads their competing entries and checks each container against its co-readers once, and freezes the resulting per-container facts (path, agents, configured consumers, declared targets, aliases, writer target, servers container and activation field), from which each MCP member's dry-run withdrawal plans afresh. Within one competing-entry read, the location's own parse of a spelling that resolves to the target file under the same servers container stands for the target's parse when both grammars are equal.
freshChecks: Every declared alias is re-resolved by validation, again before the first write and again before each removal.
Both co-reader preflights run for every write and every removal group.
Pi name-collision check runs during validation.
The writer re-resolves its path, takes the exclusive write and reads the preimage fresh; the no-op decision, change label and backup content come from that read.
Adoption writes compare the locked read with the expected entry and never use a validated proposal.

Removal preparation reads every group's container and preflights its co-readers before any per-group render; a disabled connection's withdrawal preview takes the targets and bytes its inspection observed in the same read instead, and a Pack disable runs this preparation once for all its MCP members.

Every withdrawal planned from prepared removal facts, each Pack MCP member's included, rechecks every declared route and renders and preflights its co-readers against the live container before any physical target changes.
Every removal under the exclusive write, a dry run included, re-reads and re-renders; planning text and renders are never carried into it.
Rollback protection, transient backup, identity-preserving write and footprint record run under the exclusive write.
Readback of the declared consumers' containers runs after every publication.

The structural insertion predicate still runs whenever the guard sees a different string pair (a blank file, an unformatted fallback edit, TOML and YAML insertions): it is the refusal gate on the published bytes.
The adoption freshness check and the adoption step, both under the transition lock, read and hash every adopted source again and refuse a changed one.
After the adoption writes, transaction validation reads each adopted native MCP file back for the co-reader check of the original text against the result.
Within one configured MCP target resolution, an alias spelling is still read as itself and each member decodes competing entries with its own grammar and error wording.

Inline target resolution in adoption preparation and import discovery reads the competing entries at each declared location itself, although discovery read the same physical document in that read phase.
The locked freshness check and the adoption step each resolve the configured MCP targets and validate every candidate on its own.
mcp-config-writer.lifetime: A preparation lives for one call that applies planned writes and is released after its write. A removal group's text and parses live only for that group's co-reader step; no container text is stored on prepared removal groups or carried into the locked removal, and nothing is retained across invocations. A Pack disable's frozen removal preparation is created when its disabled realization is prepared, serves the dry-run withdrawal of every MCP member, and is released when that realization preparation returns. An install's handed-over manifest is created when the install decodes it and released when that install call returns. Discovery's source fingerprints stand in for a source read only within the read phase that took them, and every later phase reads the source again to compare with them. Discovery's texts, the resolved groups and the preimage texts of an in-order validation live only for that adoption preparation or import discovery call, and each candidate's copy of the groups only for its own validation. The admissions, bytes and referents shared within a configured MCP target resolution, and the routes, reads and fingerprints shared within a native MCP discovery, live only for that call and keep only successes, because any failure ends it. The location's parse that stands for a same-grammar target parse is used only within that competing-entry read and is not cached.

adoption-locked-mcp-writer-compares-lock.basis: With an adoption, the locked MCP writer compares the locked read with the expected entry and renders again; no validated proposal is used.

adoption-preparation-reads-hashes-each-a.basis: Adoption preparation relies on the fingerprints discovery took of each adopted native MCP file in the same read phase instead of reading and hashing the file again; discovery's texts reach only the in-order target validation of that call, and the prepared candidate carries no source text. The locked freshness check and the adoption step still read and hash every adopted source and refuse a changed one in the same per-candidate order.

after-adoption-writes-transaction-valida.basis: After the adoption writes, transaction validation reads each adopted native MCP file to confirm the adopted entry and reads it again for the co-reader check of the original text against the result, beside the inspection readback, with no write between the reads. The later read is the last post-write readback of the file before the transaction settles and the only one that feeds the check that the adoption kept every existing invocation and its meaning, so serving it from the earlier read would remove that last readback.

after-settings-write-retires-read-phase.basis: After the settings write retires the read phase, the MCP sync re-observes competing native entries, a different validity boundary from the locked freshness check.

discovery-hashes-each-native-mcp-source.basis: Discovery hashes each native MCP file once, and every source discovered from that file carries that fingerprint, which adoption uses to refuse a source changed after discovery.

each-planned-mcp-file-handled-once.basis: Each planned MCP file is handled once per call: validation and each write or removal, a dry run included, parse it inside one read view, a removal renders every selected key into one result, and a write takes its transient backup from the locked preimage text without another read.

every-declared-mcp-alias-planning-resolv.basis: Every declared MCP alias that planning resolved is re-resolved by validation before any native write, and again when the writes are applied, the fresh route check before publication.

every-mcp-removal-dry-run-included.basis: Every MCP removal, a dry run included, re-reads the file and re-renders every selected key under its exclusive write after removal planning has read and rendered it; planning text and renders are never carried into it.

import-discovery-no-longer-re-reads.basis: Import discovery no longer re-reads the selected native MCP file to compare it with the fingerprint it just took.

import-preparation-keeps-adopt-s-inline.basis: Import preparation keeps adopt's inline-target validation as its only native projection preflight, so its refusals stay visible in preview.
import-preparation-keeps-adopt-s-inline.openQuestion: May `mcps import` skip adopt's inline-target validation, moving its refusals from preview to apply or replacing it with a managed-package projection preflight?

importing-mcp-server-writes-native-mcp.basis: Importing an MCP server writes the native MCP configuration three times, two of them cancelling, because the projection writer performs the transition so the native configuration is replaced only after managed validation.
importing-mcp-server-writes-native-mcp.openQuestion: May `mcps import` skip the projection install-and-withdraw pair for a package it imports disabled, accepting different native configuration bytes and no managed validation of that transition?

inserting-new-mcp-server-into-non.basis: Inserting a new MCP server into a non-blank JSON-like config evaluates the structural-insertion predicate once when the refusal guard would judge the same before and after text.

installing-manifest-backed-mcp-server-re.basis: Installing a manifest-backed MCP server decodes its canonical manifest once to select the distribution and resolve the invocation, freezes it and hands it to the manifest-backed agent sync of every name the install projects, for that install call only. The sync decodes the manifest itself only when none is handed over, as for a native component's preference entry. Canonical integrity verification before the decoded manifest is used and every publish-side check of the sync, including co-reader validation and the locked writer's fresh read, stay.

locked-mcp-writer-consumes-proposal-vali.basis: The locked MCP writer consumes the proposal validation rendered when the physical path, the full preimage text and the write inputs are identical, instead of parsing and rendering again.

materialization-plans-mcp-removal-previe.basis: Materialization plans an MCP removal in its preview phase and again in its run phase; each phase observes the containers itself.

mcp-removal-planning-reads-each-group.basis: MCP removal planning reads each group's container once in its co-reader step and renders the removal from that text.

mcp-writer-s-refusal-guard-evaluates.basis: The MCP writer's refusal guard evaluates the structural-insertion predicate on the published pair when it differs from the pair the insertion judged (blank config, unformatted fallback, TOML or YAML).

removal-planning-keeps-first-loop-read.basis: Removal planning keeps its first-loop read and co-reader preflight of every group before any per-group render, so no group is changed before every co-reader and outgoing entry is checked.

removal-target-resolution-reads-competin.basis: Removal target resolution reads competing MCP entries as precedence evidence, with its own failure vocabulary, before removal planning reads the groups.

under-transition-lock-adoption-step-prep.basis: Under the transition lock the adoption step prepares its targets again right after the locked freshness check prepared them.
under-transition-lock-adoption-step-prep.openQuestion: May mcps adopt reuse the target preparation proven by its locked freshness check, so that a foreign edit landing between that check and the adoption step is refused as 'changed before import' rather than 'changed after discovery'?

adoption-candidates-share-one-target-res.basis: Inside one adoption preparation or import discovery call, in-order validation resolves the configured MCP targets once, gives each candidate its own copy of the resolved groups, and validates a planned write at the exact physical path of a document discovery read in that call against discovery's frozen text, reading any other target file once for that call. Each candidate keeps, in order, its plan, the re-resolution of every declared alias, both co-reader preflights, the Pi name-collision check and the rendered proposal, and the first refusal stops the run. The locked freshness check and the adoption step still validate each candidate on its own and re-read and hash every adopted source.

adoption-target-resolution-rereads-disco.basis: Inline target resolution in adoption preparation and import discovery reads the competing entries at each declared location as precedence evidence, with its own failure vocabulary, although discovery read the same physical document in that read phase. The read is keyed by the declared location spelling, and target resolution learns that the spelling names a document discovery read only after resolving it.
adoption-target-resolution-rereads-disco.openQuestion: May inline target resolution during adoption preparation and import discovery take a declared location's competing entries from the text discovery read at the same physical path in that read phase, instead of reading the declared location itself as precedence evidence?

target-resolution-shares-admissions-read.basis: Within one configured MCP target resolution, members that share a declared route reuse one successful live admission, and their competing-entry checks share the bytes and the referent of each exact path spelling, so a native MCP file several agents share, such as project .mcp.json, is admitted, read and resolved once per call. The shared values live only for that call and keep only successes, because any failure ends it; each member still decodes with its own grammar and error wording, and an alias spelling is still read as itself. Validation, the locked writer and every removal still re-resolve each declared alias at their own boundaries.

discovery-shares-native-file-several-age.basis: Within one native MCP discovery call, configured agents that declare the same native MCP file share its route check, its read and its fingerprint, and each exact text is parsed once per grammar through the native configuration observation view, which hands every reader its own copy; every agent keeps its own source with its own servers value. Only successes are shared, so a refused route or an unreadable or invalid file still ends discovery where it first occurs. Adoption preparation, the locked freshness check, the adoption step and transaction validation still read the file themselves.

pack-disable-withdraws-mcp-members-from-.basis: Preparing a Pack disable resolves the configured MCP targets, reads their competing entries and reads and checks each container against its co-readers once, and only when the Pack has an MCP member; each member's dry-run withdrawal then plans afresh from those frozen facts, which live only until that realization preparation returns. Every member still rechecks each declared route, renders and checks its co-readers against the live container, and reads the container back in its own dry run.

competing-entry-check-parses-same-gramma.basis: Within one competing-entry read, a location whose spelling resolves to the target file under the same servers container is parsed once when its grammar equals the target's, because the location's own parse already accepted the same bytes; nothing is shared or cached. A location whose grammar differs from the target's, JSON against JSONC, still parses the bytes again under the target's grammar, and the referent resolution and its failure mapping stay.

mcp-inspection.resource: Detailed inspection of desired MCP servers against the agents' native MCP configuration.

reads.note: The review reads an already-enabled server's current configured-agent outcomes live to find its verified targets, keyed by type, name, sorted targets and installed state, so a later step listing the same server reuses a copy; a provider failure yields no verified targets.
One detailed inspection of an enabled connection reads each projected native file once through a lazy cached read, and each agent sharing that file decodes its own entry from it.
An enabled sourced connection without a native component reads each candidate's mcp.json until one is present, and the text of that read is the manifest the inspection decodes.

When a candidate's mcp.json read fails for a reason other than absence, the inspection probes the file's existence to decide whether the candidate is skipped or selected with the read failure raised at the manifest decode.
A disabled connection's inspection reads each configured target's native file once, and the withdrawal preview plans from a copy of those bytes.

mcp-inspection.existingSharing: Detailed observations are cached per server within one query and an enclosing view of the same phase is inherited. Activation planning and adding coding agents read inventories for presence only, so they compute no detailed MCP inventory inspection of pre-change configured-agent outcomes; one execution review observes each server's current registrations once per distinct target set and installed state. Within one MCP inspection read view, inspections of different connections now plan against one configured target resolution; one detailed inspection of an enabled connection skips re-admitting the targets its own resolution admitted and reads each projected native file once for all its agents; an enabled sourced connection without a native component decodes the manifest text of the read that selects its root; and a disabled connection's inspection hands the targets and native bytes it observed to the materialize step collection's withdrawal preview.
mcp-inspection.preparedInputs: The detailed inspection of each desired MCP server, which each later request with the same inputs in the same read phase receives as its own copy; within one execution review, the verified targets of a server's current-registration observation, which later plan steps that list the same server with the same targets and installed state receive as a copy. Within one MCP inspection read view, the configured target resolution per agent set, scope, workspace root, native directory inputs and native resolution root, which each inspection planning against those inputs receives as its own copy of the resolved groups, without admission keys. Within one detailed inspection of an enabled connection, the admission keys of its own target resolution, which its planned agents consume to skip re-admitting the same scope, native root and physical path, and one lazy cached read per projected native file, which every agent of that inspection decodes with its own format and servers path. Within one detailed inspection of a sourced connection without a native component, the text of the mcp.json read that selects the manifest root, which the manifest decode consumes. For a disabled connection, the configured targets its inspection resolved and the bytes it read of each target's native file, which the materialize step collection's withdrawal preview receives as a copy when that inspection is not current.
freshChecks: An inspection requested after the read phase ends is observed live.
The execution review of an already-enabled server inspects its current registrations live after the planning read phase has ended, once per distinct target set and installed state.
Sync's freshness check observes the detailed MCP inventory again before it writes and refuses the candidate when it differs from the inventory it planned over.
After apply, configured-agent verification inspects the native configuration of each server the operation leaves enabled, in a fresh observation phase.
An inspection outside an active MCP inspection read view, or on a file system other than the one the view's resolution first ran on, resolves its configured targets live.

A detailed inspection of an enabled connection that plans against the view's shared resolution still admits each planned agent's target live, as does one whose own resolution did not admit that target under the same scope, native root and physical path.
When a candidate's mcp.json read fails for a reason other than absence, the inspection still probes the file's existence, which decides whether the candidate is skipped or selected.

The withdrawal preview of a disabled connection still runs every removal check in order, with the live render, co-reader preflights, alias recheck and dry-run readback, and the disable step's run resolves and reads its targets live.
mcp-inspection.lifetime: Cached inspections live for the enclosing read phase and are cleared when it closes. The execution review creates a server's verified targets at its first current-registration observation and releases them when the review returns. The view's configured target resolution is reused only while the view and its read phase are active and is cleared when the view closes. An inspection's own admission keys, its shared native file reads and the selected manifest text are local values of that inspection call and are released when it returns. A disabled connection's observed targets and native bytes live in its inspection cell for the enclosing MCP inspection read view, or only for that connection's step planning when no view is in scope, and the preview's copy is made only when the connection is not current.

adding-coding-agents-inspects-each-insta.basis: Adding coding agents plans its materialization over inventories that the materialize step collection reads for presence only within one planning call, so the detailed MCP inventory's inspection of pre-change configured-agent outcomes, which agents add never consumes, is not computed. The currency judgment for the resulting membership still inspects each installed sourced server's native configuration, and sync preparation still plans over detailed inventories and rechecks them before it writes.

agents-add-execution-review-inspects-cur.basis: The execution review of each enabled server from a source outside the workspace inspects its current configured-agent outcomes again after the planning inspections. The planning read phase has ended when the review runs, and the review observes live state between its before-review fingerprint and the seal, so it cannot reuse a planning inspection.

review-observes-current-registrations-on.basis: Within one execution review, the verified targets of a server's current-registration observation are kept as a frozen list keyed by type, name, sorted targets and installed state, and each later plan step that lists the same server receives a copy, so the review inspects that server's native configuration once per distinct target set and releases the list when it returns. Each step still fetches its reviewed package, a provider failure still yields no verified targets, and the seal still fingerprints the reviewed materials.

after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.basis: After apply, configured-agent verification inspects the native configuration of each MCP server the operation leaves enabled once more, inside one MCP inspection view, after planning inspected the containers the writes then changed. The native writes lie between the two inspections, and this readback is the post-write verification that judges each agent's entry current from its decoded native value rather than from the writes' own results.

detailed-inspection-desired-mcp-server-c.basis: Detailed inspection of a desired MCP server is cached for the run and retires with its phase.
Detailed inspection of a desired MCP server is cached for the query and retires with its read phase.

enabling-pack-mcp-server-members-inspect.basis: Enabling a Pack collects its materialize step through activation's presence-only inventory reads within one planning call, so the detailed MCP inventory's inspection of every active desired MCP server, including members already enabled through another origin, is not computed, and each member's currency inspection stays. A member reached only through the Pack being enabled is not repeated work, because the pre-change graph holds no node for it and only its currency inspection reads its native configuration.

local-inspection-enabled-mcp-server-acce.basis: A local inspection of an enabled MCP server with an accepted resolution inspects the server's native configuration in the agent-outcome provider against the accepted canonical path and again for the inspection document against the inventory row's observed paths. The two requests can select different manifest roots, so sharing one inspection changes the shown outcomes where the observed paths select a different or no manifest root, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
local-inspection-enabled-mcp-server-acce.openQuestion: May the local inspection judge an accepted MCP server's shown per-agent outcomes against the accepted resolution's canonical path, as the agent-outcome provider does, instead of the inventory row's observed paths, accepting a changed outcome where those paths select a different or no manifest root?

planning-mcp-server-s-enable-inspects.basis: Planning an MCP server's enable inspects its native configuration for the projected configured-agent outcomes while settling and again to judge its materialization currency while collecting its step, judging different nodes, settings entries and states outside any MCP inspection view. Only the native-configuration and manifest reads repeat, and sharing them needs a faithful parse view or running activation planning as an observation phase, which the accepted read-phase requirement does not decide.
planning-mcp-server-s-enable-inspects.openQuestion: May activation planning share physical native-configuration and manifest reads across its projected-outcome and currency MCP inspections within its planning read phase, by running that phase as an observation phase or under a faithful parse view, although those inspections judge different nodes, entries and states?

mcp-enable-planning-reads-inventories-fo.basis: Activation's step collection reads each type's inventory for presence only within one planning call and the activation realization carries no inventory, so the detailed MCP inventory's inspection of pre-change configured-agent outcomes, which activation never consumes, is not computed. The currency judgment, the projected-outcome inspection and the execution review still inspect the server's native configuration.

enable-execution-review-inspects-already.basis: The execution review of a server that is already enabled inspects its current configured-agent outcomes once more after the planning inspections. The planning read phase has closed when the review runs, and the review observes live state between its before-review fingerprint and the seal, so it cannot reuse a planning inspection.

planning-mcp-update-inspects-each-update.basis: Planning an MCP update inspects each updated server's native configuration for the candidate's configured-agent outcomes and, for a server that is already enabled, again in the execution review, outside any MCP inspection view. The planning read phase has ended and its materials are fingerprinted when the review runs, so the review observes live state for its own request rather than reusing the planning inspection.

planning-uninstall-mcp-server-installed-.basis: Planning the uninstall of an MCP server that an installed Pack still reaches inspects the server's native configuration for the retained native outputs and again for the candidate's configured-agent outcomes, both outside any MCP inspection view and with no lock, write or confirmation between them. Both run in uninstall's document-only planning phase, and sharing them needs a phase-scoped cache or a value handoff of a physical native observation in that phase, which the accepted read-phase requirement does not support as written.
planning-uninstall-mcp-server-installed-.openQuestion: May uninstall planning reuse one detailed MCP inspection of a Pack-retained server between the retained native-output capture and the candidate's configured-agent outcome projection, by a phase-scoped cache or a value handoff, although both run in a document-only planning phase that compatible nested calls may not upgrade to physical caching?

sync-planning-inspects-each-desired-mcp.basis: Sync planning inspects each desired MCP server inside its MCP inspection view, and the execution review of a reconciled MCP server that is already enabled inspects its current outcomes again after that view has closed. The planning read phase has ended, a fresh revalidation and a new planning phase lie between them, and the review observes live state inside its own fingerprint bracket.

disabled-inspection-hands-withdrawal-pre.basis: A disabled MCP connection's inspection keeps the configured targets it resolved and the bytes it read of each target's native file, and when the connection is still active natively the materialize step collection hands the withdrawal preview a copy of them instead of resolving the targets and reading the files again. The observation lives in the connection's inspection cell for the enclosing MCP inspection read view, or only for that connection's step planning when no view is in scope, and a current inspection copies nothing. Every later preview check still runs in order (unverified readers, the shared-container conflict, the co-reader preflights, the alias recheck, the live render and preflight, and the dry-run readback), and the step's run resolves and reads its targets live.

inspection-view-shares-one-configured-ta.basis: Within one MCP inspection read view, inspections of different connections plan against one configured target resolution per agent set, scope, workspace root, native directory inputs and native resolution root, and each inspection receives its own copy of the resolved groups. The resolution is reused only while the view and its read phase are active and only through the file system it first ran on, carries no admission keys so each inspection of an enabled connection still admits its planned agents' targets live, and is cleared when the view closes. An inspection outside an active view resolves live, and each later view, such as sync's freshness check or after-apply verification, resolves again.

one-inspection-admits-reads-each-native-.basis: One detailed inspection of an enabled MCP connection skips re-admitting a planned agent's target only when its own target resolution admitted that exact scope, native root and physical path live in the same call, and agents that share a projected native file read it through one lazy cached read owned by that call. Each agent still decodes its own entry with its own format and servers path, a reader under another native root is still admitted under its own root, and a projected-state inspection reads no native file. Sync's freshness check, the execution review and after-apply verification still inspect live at their own boundaries.

inspection-selects-canonical-manifest-fr.basis: Within one detailed inspection of an enabled sourced MCP connection without a native component, the manifest root is selected from the read of each candidate's mcp.json: an absent file moves on to the next candidate, and the text the read finds is the one decoded, with no preceding existence probe. The text lives only in local values of that inspection call, and a native component's root is still selected by its existence probe.

manifest-read-failure-keeps-existence-pr.basis: When a candidate's mcp.json read fails for a reason other than absence, the inspection still probes the file's existence, which decides whether the candidate is skipped, with a source diagnostic carrying the probe's own failure when the probe fails, or selected with the read failure raised at the manifest decode.
manifest-read-failure-keeps-existence-pr.openQuestion: May a canonical mcp.json read that fails for a reason other than absence fail the inspection or become a source diagnostic from the read failure alone, without a follow-up existence probe?

native-config-syntax.resource: Parsed views of one agent native configuration text (JSON, JSONC, TOML or YAML) used by native readers, by the MCP validator, writer, readback and inspection, and by Hook runs and their exposure passes.
native-config-syntax.publication: None: read-only owner. It decides which exact parse results one observation or one locked publication may share and how each consumer receives its own copy.

reads.note: Parses one exact (format, text) pair once per view (one native parse fact); an empty text yields an empty document without parsing; syntax and shape failures are mapped by each consumer's own vocabulary.

MCP validation, each locked write, removal and retirement, each readback and each inspection parse inside one structured-copy read view; TOML documents are copied with their date kinds. This sharing predates the run views and is unchanged.
MCP removal planning's per-group co-reader step parses its container once through an observation view, for the removal render and the second co-reader preflight.
A Hook dry run joins an enclosing observation view or opens a private one; a locked apply always opens a fresh publication view under the exclusive write.
The before and after exposure passes run inside one observation view, so a before-pass document whose text the after pass already parsed receives a copy of that parse.

The agent output inventory's hook settings observation parses one settings text once and validates its shape, deriving the declared AXM hook units and the unowned-footprint registration presence from that parse; a blank text yields an empty document without parsing.

native-config-syntax.existingSharing: MCP readers and writers already share exact parses inside one structured-copy read view per validation, per locked write, removal or retirement, per readback and per inspection (TOML documents copied with their date kinds); that sharing is unchanged on every MCP route. Before prepared inputs were shared, Hook runs, the hook exposure passes and MCP removal planning's per-group co-reader step parsed without any view. The agent output inventory parsed a hook settings text once for its declared AXM hook units and again, when it held none, to find any registration for the unowned footprint; it now derives both from one parse.
native-config-syntax.preparedInputs: Two run entries beside the existing structured read view: an observation view that joins an enclosing active view or opens a private one whose faithful copies equal an unshared parse (prototype-carrying members, null-prototype records, own __proto__ keys and TOML date kinds preserved; YAML keeps structured cloning), and a publication view that always opens fresh cells for one locked publication while keeping the enclosing view's copy mode. Hook runs, the hook exposure before and after passes, and MCP removal planning's per-group co-reader step use them; MCP validation, locked writes and readback keep the structured read view. The agent output inventory's hook settings observation parses each settings text once and gives its declared AXM hook units to the inventory's declared hook outputs and whether its settings key holds any registration to the inventory's unowned hook footprint.
freshChecks: A locked publication never reuses parse results from another run or from the eager observation.
Each format is its own key: JSON and JSONC results of one text are never substituted for each other.
Each consumer maps failures through its own vocabulary.
A view that has exited parses live.
The agent output inventory reads each hook settings file itself on every inventory.
native-config-syntax.lifetime: Cells belong to the view that opened them and are cleared when its effect exits on success, failure or interruption; a joined observation releases with its enclosing view; every consumer owns the copy it receives. The hook settings observation's parsed document lives only inside that one helper call, and the inventory keeps only the units and registration presence it returns.

hook-runs-parse-through-observation-view.basis: Hook runs parse through an observation view (dry run) or a publication view (locked apply) whose faithful copies keep each consumer's value semantics.

json-jsonc-parses-one-settings-text.basis: JSON and JSONC parses of one settings text stay separate results, so sharing never substitutes a weaker reader or its error vocabulary.

mcp-removal-planning-s-per-group.basis: MCP removal planning's per-group co-reader step parses its container once through an observation view for the removal render and the second co-reader preflight.

mcp-validation-each-locked-write-removal.basis: MCP validation, each locked write, removal and retirement, readback and inspection parse inside one structured-copy read view, unchanged by the hook run views.

syntax-results-stay-scoped-one-observati.basis: Syntax results stay scoped to one observation or one locked publication, so an eager observation and the locked run that follows it parse separately.
syntax-results-stay-scoped-one-observati.openQuestion: Should the native syntax contract admit an owner-call lifetime so a projection's eager observation and its locked run share exact-text parses?

agent-output-inventory-parses-hook-setti.basis: The agent output inventory parses each hook settings text once and derives from that one parse both its declared AXM hook units and whether it holds any registration for the unowned footprint. The parsed document lives only inside that one helper call, and the inventory still reads each settings file itself.

native-entry-removal.resource: Single native entries a caller has proven: links, files and empty directories.
native-entry-removal.publication: Removal: an uninterruptible unlink of the entry itself, never its referent, or an atomic empty-only directory removal.
native-entry-removal.existingSharing: Not applicable: each removal is one system call and the owner reads nothing.
freshChecks: Callers prove identity, emptiness and settlement protection before each removal.
Empty-directory removal refuses atomically when a child exists.
native-entry-removal.lifetime: No value is prepared or transferred; each removal is one uninterruptible system call.

each-entry-removed-once-after-identity.basis: Each entry is removed once after its identity proof.

native-insertion-receipts.resource: Insertion proofs for native agent files (inserted-key, created-file and created-directory receipts) and the parent directories AXM creates for native writes, persisted as entries of the workspace receipt store.
native-insertion-receipts.publication: The native write authority's store writer atomically replaces the receipt store after authorization and settlement protection; the authority also creates store and native parent directories and retires created files and directories through settlement retirement.

reads.note: Witnessed admission of the target against the native root witnesses before each read, directory creation, store write and retirement.
Live read of the native file compared with the caller's before bytes at capture and with the caller's bytes at a withdrawal gate; absent and empty stay distinct.
A second witnessed admission after the read supplies the identity context of the captured container.
Container identity capture of the native file and of its nearest existing ancestor.
Receipt store read and decode to select the receipts that address the physical path.
One digest of the current text per call, compared with each path-matching receipt's content digest.
One live identity proof (witnessed admission plus identity verification) per distinct stored identity per call.
Readback of the written native file, post-write identity capture and anchor verification before persisting proof.
One post-write recapture per distinct prior receipt identity, using the aliases stored in that receipt.
Created-directory identity proof before recording or retiring it, and a store read after retiring a created file to select its created-directory receipts.
Entry-mode admission of a forget, addressing the receipts it drops.
Settlement protection of the store and of each created or retired directory before the mutation.
Only when the next store bytes equal the locked text: an existence probe and a re-read after protection before skipping, so a foreign deletion or replacement of the store heals.
Each store publication is recorded against the intended bytes and the staged entry identity.

native-insertion-receipts.existingSharing: The native root witnesses are captured once when the authority is built and compared at every admission, and a capture carries the before text, before identity, ancestor anchor and valid receipts into the matching record. This change shares one pre-read admission, one digest of the current text, one proof per distinct stored identity and one recapture per distinct prior identity within each authority call, one live gate for a withdrawal's resolution and retirement, and one store update sequence under one lock for a record with its forgets or for a set of forgets.
native-insertion-receipts.preparedInputs: Within one authority call: the pre-read admission's address and native root feed the capture's read, physical path and selected context; one digest of the current text is compared with every path-matching receipt; one live verdict per distinct stored identity decides each receipt that carries it; one post-write recapture per distinct prior identity refreshes every receipt of that identity; and the digest derived with the inverse, or one digest of the written text, is the content digest of every refreshed prior and of a new inserted-key or created-file receipt. Within one withdrawal, one live gate (content match, identity, valid receipts and digest) feeds both resolution and retirement, and each restored text carries its verified digest into the next round. A record and the forgets it carries, when the forget's entry-mode admission addresses the verified container, or a set of forgets, apply as one store update sequence under one lock, starting from one locked read, and the store writer receives the store text read under the lock.
freshChecks: Every capture, withdrawal gate and record reads the native file live and compares it with the caller's bytes.

Every capture and withdrawal gate keeps its witnessed admission before the read and, whenever it captures the file's identity, a second witnessed admission for its identity context; a record keeps its witnessed admission before the readback.
Each distinct stored identity is proven live in each call; no verdict is carried across calls.
A capture after a withdrawal that did not retire keeps its own live read and gate.
A record reads back the written file and verifies identity, anchor and each distinct prior before persisting proof.
A forget keeps its entry-mode admission; a record and its forgets share one store update only when that admission addresses the verified container.
Retiring a created file reads the store again afterwards and proves each created directory live and empty before retiring it.
The store writer authorizes and protects before every write and re-reads before skipping identical bytes.
A resolution-only dry run of the managed .gitignore update keeps its own live gate, and the later withdrawal under the exclusive write proves the file again.
native-insertion-receipts.lifetime: Admission results, digests, identity verdict and recapture maps, and the withdrawal gate state are local to one authority call, which for a native file insertion, withdrawal or forget runs under the caller's exclusive write except for a dry run's resolution, and are released when it returns, fails or is interrupted; a capture is held by the caller until its matching record; the locked store text and the states of one update sequence live for one hold of the store lock; only the native root witnesses live as long as the authority's workspace layer; nothing is retained across invocations.

building-workspace-layer-captures-native.basis: Building the workspace layer captures the native authority root witnesses twice, once for the workspace transaction scope and again for the native write authority, resolving the same native roots and observing their anchor and parent directory identities each time, also on a route that writes nothing. Sharing them would keep one live identity observation for the whole workspace layer and would move the refusal of a root retargeted between the captures from settlement protection or retirement to the authority's admission, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
building-workspace-layer-captures-native.openQuestion: May the native write authority use, for the lifetime of the workspace layer, the native root witnesses the workspace transaction scope captured at layer construction, so that a root retargeted between the two captures is refused by the authority's admission (NativeWriteRefused, native-root-changed) instead of later by settlement protection or retirement, and a layer without a transaction scope keeps its own capture?

capture-after-withdrawal-did-not-retire.basis: A capture after a withdrawal that did not retire the file reads the file live and compares it with the caller's before bytes immediately before the caller writes.

forget-native-insertion-receipts-keeps-o.basis: A forget of native insertion receipts keeps its own entry-mode admission, and shares one store update with the record only when that admission addresses the verified container.

hook-settings-write-admits-target-protec.basis: A Hook settings write admits its target for protection and again for parent creation, the last witnessed route check before parent creation and the write, after the rollback snapshot.

inside-one-native-admission-identity-cap.basis: Inside one native admission or identity capture the root is resolved again during the target walk when the child directly under the root is absent or a link, the last fresh observation of the root before the target route is accepted.
inside-one-native-admission-identity-cap.openQuestion: May one native admission or identity capture reuse the root spelling it resolved at its start for its own target walk, so that a root replaced during the walk is refused by the next admission (possibly after the write) instead of by this one?

managed-region-write-admits-target-prote.basis: A managed region write admits its target for protection and again for parent creation, the last witnessed route check before parent creation and the write, after the rollback snapshot.

mcp-configuration-write-admits-target-th.basis: An MCP configuration write admits its target through the native write authority for protection and again for parent creation, the last witnessed route check before parent creation and the write, after the rollback snapshot.

native-insertion-capture-resolution-reti.basis: Native insertion capture, resolution and retirement keep a second witnessed admission after reading the file, the last root-witness, root-selection and ancestor-marker check inside the call.
native-insertion-capture-resolution-reti.openQuestion: Should native insertion capture, resolution and retirement rely on a later witnessed admission (parent creation or protection) instead of re-checking their root witness after reading the file, making that admission a documented precondition of the native write authority port?

native-insertion-withdrawal-resolves-inv.basis: A native insertion withdrawal resolves its inverses and retires an AXM-created file from one live gate, and a record with forgotten units, or a set of forgets, updates the receipt store under one lock and one locked read.

one-native-insertion-authority-call-admi.basis: One native insertion authority call admits its target once before the read, digests the current text once, proves each distinct stored identity once and recaptures each distinct prior identity once after the write.

recording-managed-gitignore-pattern-deri.basis: Recording a managed .gitignore pattern derives the receipt's structural inverse again from the authority's own post-write readback after the caller's eligibility predicate.

recording-native-insertion-captures-cont.basis: Recording a native insertion captures the container with the caller's aliases separately from the prior receipts' recaptures, which use each receipt's stored aliases.

recording-native-insertion-reads-back-wr.basis: Recording a native insertion reads back the written file and verifies its identity and ancestor anchor before persisting proof.

skill-link-admits-native-entry-through.basis: A Skill link admits its native entry through the native write authority when it captures the missing parent directories and again when it creates them, and, when it created any, again when it records them, each the witnessed route check of its own step before or after the link is written.

subagent-file-write-admits-target-throug.basis: A Subagent file write admits its target through the native write authority for protection and again for parent creation, the last witnessed route check before parent creation and the write, after the rollback snapshot.

when-next-receipt-store-bytes-equal.basis: When the next receipt store bytes equal the locked text, the store writer probes and re-reads the store after protection, the only observation that heals a foreign deletion or replacement of the store on a no-op.

when-subagent-file-write-creates-missing.basis: When a Subagent file write creates missing parent directories, recording them admits the target through the native write authority again and verifies the captured ancestor anchor and each created directory's identity after the write, apart from the admission that captured the missing directories before protection.

native-location-set.resource: Read-phase observations of declared native reader, instruction, skill, hook and MCP locations: entry and referent addresses with canonical spellings.
native-location-set.publication: None: a capture is read-phase evidence only, never mutation authority.

reads.note: realPath, stat, readLink and readDirectory of the requested targets and their direct link targets, shared within one capture including failures.
Canonical spelling through the canonical-path port (on Linux an O_PATH open, a descriptor readlink and two stats), shared per distinct path within one capture.
The canonical-path port compares the opened descriptor's identity with the named path's and refuses a removed or replaced path.
Referent and canonical spelling of each identical skills-directory spelling, resolved once within one install target grouping and never kept on failure.
SKILL.md existence probe of each exact path, kept on success within one configured Skill location observation.
Referent of each exact skill read-directory spelling, resolved once within one setup output-concern observation.
The stat a native Subagent entry's resolution makes classifies a regular file; only a symbolic link with a referent is stat'ed again for its referent's type.
An existing leaf whose referent differs from its lexical spelling has its parent resolved, its link read, and is stat'ed and resolved again at its physical spelling.

native-location-set.existingSharing: Identical realPath, stat, readLink and readDirectory reads, including failures, are shared within one capture; before prepared inputs were shared, the canonical spelling port still ran once per requested target. This change resolves the canonical spelling of each distinct existing path once per capture, and a lint run's ownership issues no longer take a second agent-output inventory. It also describes every removal of one skill uninstall planning call from one physical grouping of its install targets, resolves each identical skills-directory spelling once within one install target grouping, probes each SKILL.md path once within one configured Skill location observation, resolves each exact skill read-directory spelling once within one setup output-concern observation, and admits a regular native Subagent file from the file kind its entry resolution already observed.
native-location-set.preparedInputs: The canonical spelling, refusal or missing answer for each distinct existing path is prepared at its first resolution in a capture and reused by later targets of the same capture. A lint run's single agent-output inventory supplies both the agent-output facts and the ownership issues its workspace rules read. A skill uninstall planning call's physical grouping of its configured install targets is prepared when the first removal needs it and is consumed by every removal's removed and retained artifact descriptions, each artifact with its own consumer lists. Within one install target grouping, the referent of each identical skills-directory spelling is prepared at its first resolution and reused as the grouping key of later targets with that spelling. Within one configured Skill location observation, each successful SKILL.md existence probe is prepared at its first position and reused by the readers, the owned-entry check and the link checks that name the same path. Within one setup output-concern observation, the grouping key of each exact skill read-directory spelling is prepared at the first selected agent that declares it and reused for later agents. The file kind that a native Subagent entry's resolution observes is consumed in the same agent output inventory iteration to admit a regular file without a second stat.
freshChecks: Each new capture resolves every path afresh.
The canonical-path port's opened-versus-named identity check runs once per distinct path per capture.
Settlement, write admission and identity capture keep live resolution outside any capture.
Validation of each planned MCP write captures the declared reader locations again for the co-reader preflight of the proposed text.

Each install target grouping call resolves its skills-directory spellings again, distinct spellings and aliases still resolve on their own in the same order, and a failed resolution is never kept, so a retarget between grouping calls is observed.
Skill uninstall unmaterialization takes its native observations live at apply time.
Each configured Skill location observation probes SKILL.md afresh, and a failed probe ends that call without being kept.
Each setup output-concern observation, including the re-observation for setup's applied report, resolves its read directories again, and user-scope entries resolve live.
A native Subagent entry that is a symbolic link with a referent still takes the stat that checks its referent's type.

An existing leaf reached through a linked ancestor or a case alias is stat'ed and resolved again at its physical spelling before its address is returned, in captures, in the native authority root capture that building the workspace layer runs, and in live write and settlement admissions alike.
native-location-set.lifetime: Shared reads and spellings live in maps local to one capture and are dropped when it returns, fails or is interrupted; only the captured addresses reach the caller's read phase, and nothing outlives the invocation. A lint run's agent-output inventory is created in its observation read phase and released with it. A skill uninstall planning call's target grouping is created when its first removal needs it, is shared by that call's removals and is released with that planning call. The referent map of one install target grouping is local to that grouping call. The SKILL.md probe map is created inside one configured Skill location observation call and is never returned. The read-directory map of one setup output-concern observation is local to that call. A Subagent entry's observed file kind is used only within its own agent output inventory iteration.

lint-run-inventories-agents-native-outpu.basis: A lint run takes one agent-output inventory of the agents' native outputs in its observation read phase and derives its ownership issues from that inventory with a pure function, because ownership issues never consult the desired agents or the expected names; the derived issues keep the MCP and Hook exclusion and both detail strings. The inventory lives only for that read phase, and each new capture still resolves every path afresh.

sync-probes-each-planned-native-skill.basis: Sync probes each planned native skill location at planning, at the pre-lock no-op validation, under the lock before the first write, and once more as the manager's post-write native evidence, each at its own boundary.

validating-each-planned-mcp-write-captur.basis: Validating each planned MCP write captures the native location set of every catalog agent's declared MCP, Hook and permission readers twice, once to preflight the co-readers against the current text and again to preflight them against the proposed text, with no write between the two captures. Under the transition lock the second capture is the last co-reader route check and the last canonical-path identity check of every declared reader alias before the write, because the locked writer re-resolves only its own target. Reusing the first capture would remove both checks, and moving the first preflight after the name-collision check and the render would change which refusal comes first.

within-one-native-location-set-capture.basis: Within one native location-set capture the canonical spelling of each distinct existing path is resolved once and reused by the capture's other targets.

skill-uninstall-planning-groups-install-.basis: Each skill uninstall planning call groups its configured install targets by physical directory once, lazily when the first removal needs it, and describes every removal's removed and retained artifacts from that grouping, each artifact with its own consumer lists. The grouping lives for that planning call, a grouping failure is reported as the failure of the removal that awaited it, and a call that plans no removal never runs it; unmaterialization's apply-time native observations stay live.

target-grouping-resolves-each-skills-dir.basis: Within one install target grouping, each identical skills-directory spelling resolves its referent and canonical spelling once, in a map local to that grouping call. Distinct spellings and aliases are still resolved live in the same order, failures are never kept, and each separate grouping call resolves again, so a retarget between calls is observed.

skill-location-observation-probes-each-s.basis: One configured Skill location observation call keeps a private map of successful SKILL.md existence probes keyed by exact path, so catalog readers that share a location, an owned entry and links that share one canonical source probe each SKILL.md once instead of once each. The map is created inside the call and never returned; each distinct path is still probed at its first position and in the same order, a failed probe ends the call with the same error and is not kept, and every new observation probes afresh.

aliased-existing-leaf-reobserved-at-phys.basis: Resolving an existing leaf reached through a linked ancestor or a case alias stats and resolves it at its lexical spelling and then, because its referent differs from that spelling, resolves its parent and reads the link, stats and resolves the same leaf again at its physical spelling before returning its address. That physical observation lets every alias of one entry in a capture share one set of physical reads and one refusal, so a refusal at the physical spelling refuses every alias, in captures and in live write and settlement admissions alike.
aliased-existing-leaf-reobserved-at-phys.openQuestion: May an existing leaf reached through a linked ancestor or a case alias be admitted from its lexical-spelling stat and realPath without re-observing its physical spelling, even though aliases in one captured phase would then stop sharing one physical observation and refusal?

setup-concerns-resolve-each-shared-read-.basis: Within one setup output-concern observation, each exact skill read-directory spelling that several selected agents declare is resolved once, in a map local to that call, and its grouping key is reused for the later agents. Other spellings, proposed entries the caller did not plan and user-scope entries still resolve live, and each observation call, the post-apply report's re-observation included, builds its own map, so a retarget between calls is observed.

inventory-admits-regular-subagent-file-f.basis: The agent output inventory admits a regular native Subagent file from the file kind its native entry resolution observed in the same loop iteration instead of taking a second stat of the path. Only a symbolic link with a referent still takes the stat that checks its referent's type, and removal paths still resolve each Subagent entry live.

native-managed-region.resource: A fenced Rule or Knowledge region inside the instruction file the selected scope's settings plan (for example AGENTS.md), beside foreign content.
native-managed-region.publication: Under the physical file's exclusive write: insertion capture, rollback protection, parent creation and an in-place write of the whole rendered file recorded as created or modified, then the insertion record and a string readback; a withdrawal that empties the file retires it through the insertion authority instead.

reads.note: Each run admits the planned target at the start of the region reconciliation; a dry run then rechecks only its alias against that physical file, apply rechecks the target and its alias under the exclusive write, and every run checks ownership roots for overlap.
One read of the physical file per run (unlocked for a dry run, under the exclusive write for apply) feeds fence inspection, the render, verification of the rendered region and the reader preflight.
An explicit adoption compares this read with the bytes observed when the adoption was planned.
Reader preflight checks raw and rendered text for every reader of the physical file.
A withdrawal resolves the unit's insertion and decides retirement from one live gate that re-reads the file and proves its receipts.
