Insertion capture keeps its own live read compared with the pre-image before the write.
The write authority protects the file before writing.
The insertion record reads back and proves what was written, forgetting a withdrawn unit in the same receipt-store update.
A string readback after the write must equal the rendered text.
The Rule and Knowledge managers' eager pre-write region observation is held for the immediate consumer inside the same owner call and is taken at most once.
Separate manager calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase each read the instruction file live; that phase never caches file bytes across owner calls.

The authored native preflight of an enabled Rule or Knowledge package dry-runs the proposed region while preparing and again in the step's preflight under the transition lock, before the package source is published.
A configured-agent membership change observes the region plans before its first write and again in its post-write check.

After apply, configured-agent verification dry-runs each selected kind's region once in a fresh observation phase, so its per-agent outcomes reflect every closure's writes to the instruction file and its alias routes.
The satisfied-install check of a repeated Rule or Knowledge install dry-runs the region from the live instruction file to decide whether the install is a no-op or restores accepted content.

A Rule projection preparation reads the instructions configuration and admits the instruction source target once for its inputs' overlap checks and its plan, and a live Rules plan build evaluates desired state once for its graph and its output authority.

A Knowledge preparation or sync reads the desired graph, the Knowledge lock and settings entries and the discovery and instructions configuration, and admits the instruction target, once for its source checks, its discovery dry run and its plan.
Each Knowledge link-base validation resolves the native referent of each exact target live once and compares every configured reader's instruction parent with the source's.

A region row key is measured from the target entry the same call's route admission resolved, or beneath the scope-root referent the same reconciliation's link-base validation resolved, and otherwise from live resolutions of both.

native-managed-region.existingSharing: Before prepared inputs were shared, one read under the exclusive write already fed fence inspection, rendering, region verification, the reader preflight and the adoption check; callers repeated a whole region dry run (one instruction-file read) to observe plans the manager had just observed, and a withdrawal passed the same text through separate resolve and retire gates. This change hands the managers' observation to the immediate consumer instead and joins the withdrawal's gates into one live gate. It also hands the discovery dry run of a Knowledge deactivation, a catalog refresh or a sync apply that restored nothing to the instruction-surface apply and the Knowledge manager's eager observation to a coding-agent removal's instruction step, resolves a Rule preparation's instruction source target and a Knowledge preparation's or sync's projection inputs once for their source checks, dry run and plan, lets a dry run's admission of the planned target stand as its target route check, keys region rows from the entry the same call's target admission resolved or beneath the scope-root referent the same reconciliation's link-base validation resolved, resolves each exact target's referent once per link-base validation, and derives a live Rules plan's output authority from its one desired-state evaluation.
native-managed-region.preparedInputs: The Rule and Knowledge managers hand their eager dry-run observation of each region plan to the immediate consumer in the same owner call; a withdrawal resolves and retires from one live gate, and the withdrawn unit is forgotten in the record's single receipt-store update. A coding-agent removal's instruction step consumes the Knowledge manager's eager observation of its region plans when the caller supplies no Knowledge facts. A Knowledge deactivation and a catalog refresh hand the discovery plan's eager dry run to the instruction-surface apply as its alias-reconciliation decision, and a Knowledge sync apply with nothing restored and its projection inputs shared hands it the discovery dry run it made before any publication. A Rule projection preparation resolves the instruction source target at its first demand, after the first input's source is fetched, and hands the frozen target to its later inputs' overlap checks and to its plan. A Knowledge preparation resolves its projection inputs, including the instruction target's route check, once and hands the frozen record to each source's overlap and inclusion checks and to its discovery-region plan. A Knowledge sync resolves its projection inputs once after its restore loop and hands that record to its discovery dry run and, when nothing was restored and the record is shareable, to its apply's discovery-region plan together with that dry run's selection. A Rule region plan keeps the entry its instruction target admission resolved for its eager observation to key the region row, and each Rule or Knowledge region generation keys its row from its own call's target admission. A Knowledge link-base validation keeps each exact target's resolved referent for the rest of that validation and answers the scope root's referent, beneath which the same reconciliation keys the region's instruction target. A region dry run's admission of the planned target stands as the target route check for the rest of that run. A Rules region plan that reads desired state live through the manager's own reader takes its graph and its output authority from one desired-state evaluation.
freshChecks: A dry run's admission of the planned target at the start of the region reconciliation is its target route check and the alias is rechecked against it; apply rechecks the target and its alias under the exclusive write, and ownership-root overlap checks run in every run.
Each run reads the physical file fresh; locked applies never consume a planning observation.
The reader preflight runs on raw and rendered text in every run that renders the region.
Insertion capture keeps its own live read after a withdrawal that did not retire.
Rollback protection precedes the write; the witnessed parent-creation admission is the last route check before writing.
The insertion record's proof and the string readback run after every write.

Consumers that receive no handed-over observation observe their region plans fresh: the prepared plans materialization retains from an earlier owner call, Pack uninstall planning, the authored native preflight and the invariant-fact participants.
A dry run returns before any insertion authority call.
Post-apply configured-agent verification observes the region in a fresh observation phase after every closure settles, never from an operation's observation or readback.
The satisfied-install check of a repeated install dry-runs the region from the live file under the transition lock, never from planning's observation.
Each Rule or Knowledge preparation input runs its own overlap check against the instruction target.

An observation or apply that holds no admitted entry resolves the region row key's target entry live, and the scope root is resolved live unless the same Knowledge reconciliation's link-base validation resolved it.
The dry run and the locked apply each run their own link-base validation from live referents, and every configured reader is compared and refused on its own.
After a sync apply publishes a restored Knowledge bundle, the discovery-region plan resolves its projection inputs, admits the instruction target and observes the region again.
native-managed-region.lifetime: A handed-over plan observation exists only while the consumer callback runs inside one owner call and is taken at most once; the live gate's resolution is consumed in the same run under the exclusive write. A Rule preparation's frozen target is created at its first demand and taken only while the same read phase, or none, is current, and a failed resolution is never kept. A Knowledge preparation's record lives for that owner call and reaches its plan only while the read phase current at the start of the call is still current and only for a desired graph the caller supplied or its reader froze. A Knowledge sync's record lives for that manager call until a restored bundle is published, and the dry run it hands over lives only while the apply callback runs inside that call under the transition lock. The frozen Rule target and Knowledge record go no further than the call that resolved them and the plan it returns, whose observations and apply still admit the target and its alias for themselves. A Rule plan holds its admitted entry only until its eager observation takes it or its producing call ends, and a region generation's admitted entry and a dry run's target admission serve only their own call. Link-base validation referents live for that one validation, and the scope-root referent serves only the reconciliation that resolved it. A live Rules plan's desired-state evaluation lives for that plan build. Nothing else is retained after its owner call or across the transition lock.

adoption-dry-run-re-reads-route.basis: The adoption dry run re-reads the route-checked physical file after the feature's read, so a region changed since adoption was planned is refused before the lock.

after-apply-configured-agent-verificatio.basis: After apply, configured-agent verification dry-runs the Rules region once for all selected enabled Rule operations, in a fresh observation phase after every closure has settled, although each operation already observed the region under the transition lock and read back what it wrote. The operation's readback covers only the bytes it wrote at that moment and its pre-write observation describes a state its own write replaced, so the verification is the apply's last post-write verification and alone reflects later closures' writes to the same file and its alias routes in the per-agent outcomes it reports and fails on.

after-every-region-write-insertion-recor.basis: After every region write the insertion record reads the file back and proves what was written.

authored-native-preflight-dry-runs-propo.basis: The authored native preflight dry-runs the proposed Rule or Knowledge region while preparing and again under the lock before the package source is published, and after the declaration is committed the apply reads the native file again under its exclusive write and publishes the region.

configured-agent-membership-change-obser.basis: A configured-agent membership change observes the Rule and Knowledge region plans before its first write and again in its post-write check, two validity boundaries separated by the change's own writes.

configured-knowledge-update-sweep-plans-.basis: A configured Knowledge update sweep plans each entry as its own single-bundle install, so each updated bundle's closure selects the discovery-region contributors and reads, renders and writes the instruction file itself, and each render is the last route recheck, reader preflight and readback of its own closure's state. Rendering the region once from the complete contributor set requires planning the sweep as one multi-bundle install with a trailing projection step, which adds a progress unit, changes each bundle step's artifact and moves a region refusal out of the failing bundle's best-effort closure, and the accepted requirements do not decide that change.
configured-knowledge-update-sweep-plans-.openQuestion: May a configured Knowledge update sweep plan its updated bundles as one multi-bundle install whose discovery region is rendered once in a trailing projection step, given that this adds a progress unit, changes the per-bundle artifacts, and moves a region refusal out of the failing bundle's own best-effort closure into a step that runs after every bundle has committed?

configured-rule-update-sweep-plans-each.basis: A configured Rule update sweep plans each entry as its own single-rule install, so each updated rule's closure selects the Rules-region contributors and reads, renders and writes the instruction file itself, and each render is the last route recheck, reader preflight and readback of its own closure's state. Rendering the region once from the complete contributor set requires planning the sweep as one multi-rule install with a trailing projection step, which adds a progress unit, changes each rule step's artifact and moves a region refusal out of the failing rule's best-effort closure, and the accepted requirements do not decide that change.
configured-rule-update-sweep-plans-each.openQuestion: May a configured Rule update sweep plan its updated rules as one multi-rule install whose Rules region is rendered once in a trailing projection step, given that this adds a progress unit, changes the per-rule artifacts, and moves a region refusal out of the failing rule's own best-effort closure into a step that runs after every rule has committed?

dry-run-re-reads-route-checked.basis: The dry run re-reads the route-checked physical file after the feature's read so a region changed since adoption was planned is refused, and apply reads it again under the exclusive write lock.

each-region-write-re-reads-file.basis: Each region write re-reads its file under the exclusive write lock and re-checks its route before publishing.

invariant-fact-participants-observe-each.basis: Invariant-fact participants observe each Rule and Knowledge region plan again after the manager's eager observation, one extra instruction-file read per plan per call.
invariant-fact-participants-observe-each.openQuestion: May the projection participant contract, and the planning-observations specification's participant example, gain an observed-plans member so invariant facts consume the manager's eager observation?

rule-knowledge-managers-hand-their-eager.basis: The Rule and Knowledge managers hand their eager pre-write region observation to the immediate consumer in the same owner call, removing one region dry run (one instruction-file read) per immediate consumer.

separate-rule-knowledge-manager-calls-in.basis: Separate Rule and Knowledge manager calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase each read the instruction file live.
separate-rule-knowledge-manager-calls-in.openQuestion: May an owner-call dry-run preimage map share native file bytes inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase?

under-transition-lock-before-first-write.basis: Under the transition lock and before the first write, uninstall observes the region plans of the proposed graph on the pre-withdrawal instruction file; the later run observes the file after the settings write.

under-transition-lock-install-repeats-ac.basis: Under the transition lock, an install that repeats an accepted Registry or Git Rule or Knowledge extension from the same exact source dry-runs the shared instruction region from the live instruction file again in the satisfied-install check, after planning already observed that region. The check decides whether the repeated install is a no-op or restores accepted content, so it passes the same freshness boundary as a write: planning's read phase has ended, its observation rendered a proposed region with a prospective package rather than the current per-agent outcomes, and the candidate fingerprint does not cover canonical package content, reader and alias routes outside the planned paths, or instruction-file writes by earlier closures of the same apply.

when-installed-pack-still-reaches-remove.basis: When an installed Pack still reaches the removed Knowledge bundle, its uninstall step renders the discovery region through the retained materialization and then again through the step's aggregate re-render, both from the same desired graph under the transition lock. The aggregate re-render follows the retained render's write and is the uninstall closure's last route and alias recheck, fresh read under the file's exclusive write, reader preflight and readback, and it alone reports the step's projection exclusion warnings, while the retained render checks a narrower ownership set and can refuse where the aggregate would not.

rule-preparation-resolves-instruction-so.basis: A Rule projection preparation resolves the instruction source target, from the instructions configuration and the instruction file's route within the native authority roots, at its first demand after the first input's source is fetched, and its later inputs and its plan take the frozen result while the same read phase, or none, is current; a failed resolution is never kept. The target lives for that one preparation call. Each input still runs its own overlap check against the target, and the plan's observe and apply route and alias rechecks, region generation and every other Rule manager call still resolve the target for themselves.

agent-removal-instruction-step-consumes-.basis: When a coding-agent removal must create or update an instruction copy and the caller supplies no Knowledge facts, the instruction step consumes the eager pre-write observation the Knowledge manager makes of its region plans within one observedProjectionPlans owner call, instead of observing the same plans a second time, removing one Knowledge discovery dry run (one instruction-file read, one lockfile read and one canonical bundle stat) during planning. The observed plans live only for that owner call; a failure of the eager observation still becomes the instruction files error step, and the step's apply under the transition lock still observes fresh.

knowledge-preparation-resolves-projectio.basis: One Knowledge preparation call resolves its projection inputs (the desired graph, the Knowledge lock and settings entries, the discovery and instructions configuration, and the instruction target's route check) once and hands the same frozen record to each source's overlap and inclusion checks and to its discovery-region plan, removing one instruction-target route resolution per call and, where no read phase serves the documents, one read of each of those documents. The record lives for that owner call and reaches the plan only while the read phase current at the start of the call is still current and only for a desired graph the caller supplied or its reader froze; otherwise the plan resolves its own inputs. Each source's overlap check, the region dry run's target and alias route checks at observe and apply, and every other caller's own resolution still run fresh.

knowledge-sync-apply-hands-discovery-dry.basis: With nothing restored and its projection inputs shared, a Knowledge sync apply hands the discovery-region dry run it made before any publication, with cloned native locations and the plan's exclusions, to the instruction-surface apply as the plan's pre-write observation, taken at most once, instead of observing the same region twice more; when a restored bundle was published, it hands the post-publication plan observation instead. The handed observation lives only while the apply callback runs inside that manager call under the transition lock, and the apply's own route re-resolution, its re-read under the exclusive write, its reader preflight and its readback stay fresh.

restoring-sync-apply-dry-runs-region-twi.basis: When a sync apply publishes a restored Knowledge bundle, the discovery dry run before the publication and the projection plan's observation after it both render the region and read the instruction file, because the publication and the changed contributor set lie between them; the earlier dry run keeps the pre-write refusal ahead of the publication.
restoring-sync-apply-dry-runs-region-twi.openQuestion: May a restoring sync apply drop the discovery dry run it makes before publishing a restored Knowledge bundle, given that the post-publication plan observation renders the region again before the write?

knowledge-sync-resolves-projection-input.basis: One Knowledge sync call resolves its projection inputs (the desired graph, the Knowledge lock and settings entries, the discovery configuration and the instruction target's route check) once after its restore loop and hands that record, frozen when its graph is shareable, to the discovery dry run and, when nothing was restored and the record is shareable, to the apply's discovery-region plan. The record lives for that manager call until a restored bundle is published; the region dry run's own target and alias route checks at observe and apply still run fresh, and an unwritable target is refused the same way in preview and apply.

published-restore-resolves-knowledge-pro.basis: After a sync apply publishes a restored Knowledge bundle, the discovery-region plan resolves its projection inputs again, including the instruction target's route check, because the publication opens a new validity boundary.
published-restore-resolves-knowledge-pro.openQuestion: May a restoring sync apply's post-publication discovery-region plan reuse the projection inputs and instruction-target route resolution made before the publication, given that the region reconciler re-checks the target and alias routes itself?

link-base-validation-resolves-each-refer.basis: One Knowledge link-base validation resolves the native referent of each exact target once, so the scope root that the declared instruction file and every root-level configured reader's primary instruction file share is resolved once per validation instead of once per reader. The resolutions live only for that validation call and failures are never kept; every configured reader is still compared and refused on its own, and the dry run and the locked apply each validate against live resolutions of their own.

rule-region-key-reuses-target-admission-.basis: A Rule region plan keeps the entry its instruction target admission resolved, and its eager observation, the first dry run in its producing owner call, keys the region row from that entry instead of resolving the target entry again; region generation keys its row from its own admission within the same call. The plan holds the entry only until that eager observation takes it or the producing call ends, and the scope root is always resolved live. Later observations, any second observation inside the producing call and apply resolve the row key live.

rule-dry-run-readmits-admitted-instructi.basis: A Rule region dry run admits the planned physical file again at the start of the region reconciliation after the Rule manager admitted the instruction source while planning, with only reads between them. The reconciliation admits the referent rather than the planned spelling, maps a failure to an inspection failure rather than an invalid Rule definition, and its admission is the route check every caller of the shared region reconciliation relies on.
rule-dry-run-readmits-admitted-instructi.openQuestion: May a Rule region dry run take the Rule manager's planning admission of the instruction source as its target route check, accepting that the shared region reconciliation would then skip its own admission of the referent and its inspection-failure mapping for Rule plans?

dry-run-admits-planned-target-once.basis: In a region dry run, the admission of the planned target at the start of the region reconciliation stands as the target's route check for that one call, and the run rechecks only the alias against the physical file it resolved. A dry run takes no write lock and writes nothing between that admission and its run; apply still rechecks the target and its alias under the exclusive write.

dry-run-rechecks-alias-against-admitted-.basis: A region dry run admits its alias, the display path resolved beneath the workspace root, after admitting the planned target and refuses when the alias no longer reaches the same physical file. It is the run's only alias recheck; when the alias spells the planned target itself, it repeats the target admission within the same call, with no write lock or write between the two.
dry-run-rechecks-alias-against-admitted-.openQuestion: May a region dry run skip its alias recheck when the alias spells the same path as the planned target it has just admitted, accepting that the alias-changed refusal then cannot arise in that dry run?

live-rules-plan-derives-authority-from-g.basis: A Rules region plan build that reads desired state live, outside a read phase, without a handed desired graph and through an ambient desired-state reader that is the manager's own, evaluates the desired state once and derives its output authority from that frozen evaluation instead of evaluating again to capture it; the evaluation lives for that plan build. Plans in a read phase, plans handed a desired graph and plans under a different ambient reader still evaluate the graph and capture the authority separately, and the region dry run's route checks, the locked apply's re-read under the exclusive write and the readback still run live.

knowledge-deactivation-apply-takes-disco.basis: A Knowledge deactivation, which an install or update that leaves its bundle disabled and the retained materialization of an uninstall run, and a catalog refresh hand the discovery plan's eager dry run, made in the same Knowledge manager call with nothing written since, to the instruction-surface apply as its alias-reconciliation decision, taken at most once and only inside that call, instead of observing the region again. The apply's route re-resolution, its re-read under the exclusive write, its reader preflight and its readback still run, and every later call observes the instruction file live.

knowledge-region-generation-keys-from-ta.basis: The Knowledge region generation keys its region row from the entry its own call's instruction-target route admission resolved, with only reads between them, instead of resolving the target entry again, and resolves the scope root live. Plans, their dry runs, apply and every other call key the row from a live resolution.

knowledge-region-keys-target-beneath-val.basis: Knowledge link-base validation answers the scope root's referent when it resolved exactly that path, and the same reconciliation keys the Knowledge region's instruction target beneath that referent instead of resolving the scope root again; the target's entry is still resolved live. A reconciliation whose validation did not resolve the scope root keys through projection unit-path keying as before, and the dry run and the locked apply each validate and key against resolutions of their own.

pending-login-store.resource: ~/.axm/pending-login.json, the pending device sign-in record, which holds the device code.
pending-login-store.publication: Atomic replacement after a stale-temp sweep, then a 0600 mode normalization; removal when the sign-in clears it or when the record is invalid.

reads.note: One observation of the pending record decides whether a sign-in that names no flow resumes, and is handed to a device flow reached directly from strategy selection.
Starting a device sign-in decides re-emit, restart, conflict or a new record from the handed observation, or from its own load when none is handed.
The wait loads the record again after a browser handoff, after a loopback attempt, on an expiry retry or when called on its own, and checks its Registry before polling.
Each save sweeps stale atomic-write temps beside the record once, as that save's precondition, and a device sign-in start saves its record once; a single execution, not a repeat.
After each save the record's mode is set to 0600 once, restoring what the creating umask may have reduced; it repeats no read and is a single execution.

pending-login-store.existingSharing: None before prepared inputs were shared: each sign-in step loaded the record from disk.
pending-login-store.preparedInputs: The pending-record observation and the record a device sign-in started or re-emitted, handed from strategy selection to the device flow and from its start to its wait when no browser handoff, loopback attempt or retry runs between them.
freshChecks: Registry match, expiry against the clock and every clear still run on the handed record.
A wait after a browser handoff, a loopback attempt or an expiry retry, and a standalone resume, load the record again.
The store has no lock; an invalid record is removed and fails once, at the first read.
pending-login-store.lifetime: The handed record lives for one device-flow attempt and is released when its wait completes, fails or is interrupted; it never reaches outcomes, output or trace attributes.

device-flow-wait-follows-browser-handoff.basis: A device-flow wait that follows a browser handoff, a loopback attempt or an expiry retry loads the pending sign-in again before polling.
device-flow-wait-follows-browser-handoff.openQuestion: Must a wait that follows a browser handoff, or a device sign-in started after a loopback attempt, in the same invocation observe the pending sign-in again?

one-observation-pending-sign-serves-each.basis: One observation of the pending sign-in serves each uninterrupted device-flow segment, from strategy selection to the device flow and from its start to its wait.

projection-invariant-facts.resource: Projection invariant facts (whether each projection unit is current, stale, missing or obsolete against its desired contributors) that a local check evaluates for its declared subjects and that its convergence assessment evaluates for its selection, within check's read phase, that a lint run evaluates for the workspace for its projection-ownership and projection-contributor rules, and that an uninstall plan builder evaluates for the targets it describes.

reads.note: Check evaluates projection facts once for its declared subjects to expand the scope to connected contributors; when a scoped convergence assessment follows, the facts are frozen and offered with their read phase, location, graph and participant selection key.

The local materialization assessment uses the offered facts only while the producing read phase is still active for the same location and graph and the selection key (subject types plus subagent names) matches; otherwise it evaluates.
An unfiltered convergence assessment observes every aggregate participant, including units with no desired contributor, so it is never served from check's declared-scope facts.

A lint run evaluates the facts once inside its observation read phase, observing every participant's plans and each enabled subagent's projection, and the projection-ownership and projection-contributor rules read the same frozen facts.

Each removed target's description reads the plan builder's unfiltered facts and keeps those for its own aggregate units when its enabled state changes, to describe the projection files and managed regions the removal updates.

projection-invariant-facts.existingSharing: Check and its convergence assessment already ran inside one observation read phase, so their participant observations shared that phase's cached reads; the facts themselves were evaluated twice. A lint run's rules already ran inside lint's observation read phase, but each rule that read the facts evaluated them itself, and each uninstall target description evaluated the facts for itself. Now a scoped check that requests convergence, a lint run and each uninstall plan builder evaluate the facts once and hand the same frozen facts to their consumers.
projection-invariant-facts.preparedInputs: A scoped check that requests convergence evaluates projection facts once and hands the frozen facts to the convergence assessment, which reuses them when phase, location, graph and selection key match. A lint run evaluates the projection facts once through a lazy accessor inside its observation read phase and hands the same deep-frozen facts to the projection-ownership and projection-contributor rules. Each uninstall plan builder, for leaf removals and for Pack removals together with the exclusive members they withdraw, evaluates the unfiltered projection facts once at the first removed target's description and hands the same frozen facts to every later target in that call, each target filtering them by its own type and enabled change.
freshChecks: The convergence assessment re-evaluates when the producing phase has ended, the graph or location differs, or the selection chooses other participants, such as a different subagent name set.
An unfiltered check never offers its facts, and an empty declared scope offers none.
Sync preparation and its fresh observation check never receive prepared facts.

A lint demand for the projection facts outside the run's active observation read phase evaluates them afresh, and facts whose evaluation did not finish inside that phase are not kept for later demands.
Uninstall's in-lock transition observes projections again under its lock instead of reading the plan builder's facts.
projection-invariant-facts.lifetime: The frozen facts are owned by the check call that evaluated them and are released when the check returns; reuse is bounded by the producing read phase. A lint run's facts accessor is created inside its observation read phase and released when the run returns. Uninstall's frozen facts belong to one plan builder call, are released when it returns and never reach the in-lock transition, sync or apply.

lint-run-live-workspace-projection-owner.basis: Each lint run evaluates the projection invariant facts once through a lazy accessor inside its observation read phase and hands the same deep-frozen facts to the projection-ownership and projection-contributor rules. The accessor serves only demands inside that active phase and is released when the run returns, so a demand after the phase has ended evaluates the facts afresh.

scoped-check-requests-convergence-evalua.basis: A scoped check that requests convergence evaluates projection facts once and hands the frozen facts to its convergence assessment while the same read phase, location, graph and participant selection apply.

sync-evaluates-projection-invariant-fact.basis: Sync evaluates the projection invariant facts while planning, again in its pre-acquisition observation check before the no-op decision, and on apply once more under the transition lock, each evaluation observing every selected participant's plans at its own freshness boundary.

unfiltered-check-s-convergence-assessmen.basis: An unfiltered check's convergence assessment observes every aggregate participant to find units with no desired contributor, so it never reuses check's declared-scope facts.

uninstall-preparation-evaluates-projecti.basis: Each uninstall plan builder, for leaf removals and for Pack removals that withdraw exclusive members, evaluates the unfiltered projection invariant facts once, lazily at the first removed target's description, and hands the same frozen facts to every later target in that call, each target filtering them by its own type and enabled change. The facts belong to that plan builder call and never reach the in-lock transition, sync or apply, which keep their own observations.

publishing-distribution.resource: The admitted in-memory publication archive (and its digests, file plan and manifest) of each selected authored package.
publishing-distribution.publication: None locally: each archive is built and admitted in memory and nothing is written; the temporary coordination directory that 'publish --path' creates on apply belongs to the upload.

reads.note: The canonical observation reads the authored manifest and hands over its text; the publish identity is decoded from that text.
Pack dependency expansion reuses the dependencies the identity already decoded; only a source-derived identity reads the pack manifest.
Candidate decoding reads and parses the manifest for lint and publication.

The lint gate of a rule, hook, knowledge, MCP server, subagent or pack candidate evaluates the decoded manifest and probes for the manifest file; a skill candidate's admission runs in the archive instead.
The Knowledge bundle inspection reads each Markdown document under the bundle source once to validate the bundle and keeps its bytes for the archive walk.

The publication ignore observation lists the package tree once with each entry's link target or kind, size and mode, and the archive walk of the same build lists and classifies the tree from that listing.
The archive walk reads the manifest and every included payload file to build the archive, except a Knowledge bundle document the inspection already read, whose bytes it takes instead.
The Git source state of each package is assessed while preparing.

In a repository with a HEAD commit, the Git comparison lists each package's HEAD subtree and hashes each payload entry from what the archive walk observed of it, reading live any entry or bytes the walk did not hand over.

publishing-distribution.existingSharing: The lint gate consumes the decoded manifest in memory; one archive build feeds both digests; publish input normalization reuses the admitted archive's structural admission; versions the Registry already has are skipped before any archive is built.
publishing-distribution.preparedInputs: The publish identity is decoded from the manifest text the canonical observation read, and a pack's decoded dependencies are reused for expansion; the archive digests are computed over the archive owner's own bytes, so preparation makes no extra archive copy. Knowledge preparation hands the bundle document bytes its inspection read to the archive walk, which takes each one once for an included regular file. When an archive build's selection discovers ignore inputs, the publication ignore observation hands the package listing it walked, with each listed entry's link target or kind, size and mode, to that build's archive walk, which lists and classifies the same tree from it. The listing the archive walk takes of a subdirectory to test its emptiness is carried with that subdirectory's pending entry and walked directly. Preparation's archive build hands the Git root its ignore discovery found to the same package's Git source assessment, which compares against that root instead of walking to it again. Preparation's archive walk hands the same package's Git source assessment what it observed of each payload entry it examined itself: a link's target, an empty directory, or a regular file's executable bit with the bytes it archived or read for the manifest, from which the assessment hashes. The sequential source assessment pass hands each repository root's HEAD revision and object format, or the absence of a HEAD commit, from a successful comparison to the later assessments of packages in that repository.
freshChecks: Preparation reads through a documents-only read view with live filesystem ports, so every physical fact it reuses is one this owner hands between its own steps of the same preparation.

The publication ignore observation runs before the archive walk with its own refusals, probes each ancestor and each walked directory that listed no exactly named .gitignore live, and reads every ignore input's contents.
The archive walk examines each .git entry live, and an archive build whose explicit include skips ignore discovery lists and classifies its whole tree live.
A package whose explicit include skips ignore discovery has its source assessment walk for its Git root itself.

In a repository with a HEAD commit, each package's source assessment still lists its own HEAD subtree, reads each excluded regular file's bytes, and reads the link, kind and any regular file bytes of each publication control file and .git entry in the package.

Every archive rebuild observes its tree afresh, and the source reassessment before the first upload detects its Git root, reads HEAD and reads every payload entry live; freshness at apply belongs to the upload owner's revalidation.
publishing-distribution.lifetime: The admitted archive, its digests, file plan, decoded manifest and source assessment are held on each upload candidate of the prepared candidate set until the command completes; the captured manifest text is used only during identity resolution and is never placed on the selected entry; the inspected Knowledge document bytes are created by the inspection inside one candidate preparation and released as the archive takes each one, with any left cleared once the archive is prepared or dropped when that preparation ends; the ignore observation's package listing is created when an archive build resolves its selection and dropped when that build's walk ends, and each subdirectory listing the walk carries lives on its pending entry until that build walks it; the Git root and the walk's payload observations are created by a package's archive build and held beside its prepared candidate only within publish preparation, each observation is taken at most once by that package's source assessment, and any left are released when that assessment settles; the HEAD facts are created by the sequential assessment pass, filled only by a successful comparison, and dropped when the pass ends; nothing is retained across invocations.

after-identity-resolution-candidate-deco.basis: After identity resolution, candidate decoding, the lint gate's manifest probe and the archive walk each read the manifest again, so a manifest changed during preparation is refused at preparation with its own message.
after-identity-resolution-candidate-deco.openQuestion: May publish preparation bind lint input, publish policy, dependencies and the archived manifest to one manifest read, accepting that a manifest emptied, made unreadable or deleted during preparation is refused at apply or with the archive-validation message instead of at prepare with 'Missing manifest' or 'Invalid JSON'?

archive-digests-computed-over-admitted-a.basis: The archive digests are computed over the admitted archive's own bytes, so preparation makes no hashing copy of the archive.

each-publish-candidate-s-manifest-text.basis: Each publish candidate's manifest text is parsed separately by the canonical observation, the identity decode, the candidate decode and the distribution manifest, each into a tree it owns.
each-publish-candidate-s-manifest-text.openQuestion: May publish preparation share one frozen parsed manifest between the canonical observation, the identity decode, the candidate decode and the distribution manifest instead of parsing an independently owned tree for each?

prepared-archive-hashed-twice-once-sha.basis: The prepared archive is hashed twice, once for its SHA-512 integrity and once for the SHA-256 archive digest of its publication descriptor, because the protocol names both identities.

preparing-knowledge-candidate-reads-each.basis: Within one Knowledge candidate preparation, the Knowledge bundle inspection keeps the bytes of each Markdown document it reads in a map private to that preparation, keyed by absolute path, and the archive walk takes each buffer once for an included regular file instead of reading it again. The inspection still runs first with its own refusals, every other file is read from disk as before, and the archive rebuilt when publish revalidates the distribution reads live.

publish-identity-decoded-from-manifest-t.basis: The publish identity is decoded from the manifest text the canonical observation read, and a pack's dependency expansion reuses the dependencies that identity already decoded.

publish-input-normalization-reuses-admit.basis: Publish input normalization reuses the admitted archive's structural admission, and the publish catalog is built from one settings snapshot.

archive-walk-reuses-ignore-observation-p.basis: Within one archive build whose selection discovers ignore inputs, the publication ignore observation keeps the package listing it walked, with each listed entry's link target or kind, size and mode, and the archive walk lists and classifies the same tree from it instead of reading each directory and calling readLink and stat on each entry again; the listing is dropped when that build ends. The ignore observation also probes each exactly named .gitignore it listed from those facts, still runs first with its own refusals, and probes absent nested ignore inputs and ancestors live, while the archive walk examines a .git entry live. An explicit include reads the tree live, and every rebuild, including the one publish revalidation makes, observes its tree afresh.

archive-emptiness-probe-listing-feeds-di.basis: An archive build lists each directory it walks once: a subdirectory's listing, taken when its emptiness is tested, is carried with its pending entry and walked directly, and lives only for that one build. Traversal order, warnings and the refusal mapping are unchanged, and each build, including the rebuild publish revalidation makes, lists its directories live.

source-assessment-reuses-git-root-and-he.basis: Within one publish preparation, each package's Git source assessment starts from the Git root its own archive's ignore discovery found instead of walking to the root again, and the sequential assessment pass holds each repository root's HEAD revision and object format, or the absence of a HEAD commit, filled only by a successful live comparison and dropped when the pass ends. Each package's HEAD subtree listing and payload hashing still run, a package whose explicit include skips ignore discovery walks for its root itself, and the reassessment before the first upload detects its root and reads HEAD live.

source-assessment-takes-archive-walk-pay.basis: Within one publish preparation, the archive walk hands that package's Git source assessment what it observed of each payload entry it examined itself (a link's target, an empty directory, or a regular file's executable bit with the bytes it archived or read for the manifest), and the assessment hashes from it instead of calling readLink, stat and readFile on that entry again. Each observation is taken at most once and released when that assessment settles. Excluded file bytes are still read by the assessment, and archive rebuilds and the reassessment before the first upload read every entry live.

source-assessment-rereads-publication-co.basis: Within one publish preparation, the Git source assessment of a package inside a repository with a HEAD commit reads the link and kind of each publication control file and of a .git entry in the package again, and a regular file's bytes, although the ignore observation and the archive walk already observed them, because the archive walk hands over only the entries it examined as payload.
source-assessment-rereads-publication-co.openQuestion: May the publish source assessment hash each publication control file and .git entry of a package from what the same preparation's ignore observation and archive walk already observed instead of reading it again?

publishing-upload.resource: The prepared archive bytes uploaded to the selected Registry, and for 'publish --path' a temporary coordination workspace.
publishing-upload.publication: Remote upload of the prepared bytes; locally, 'publish --path' creates a scoped temporary coordination workspace so admission state never lands in the published directory.

reads.note: Before the first upload each package's distribution is rebuilt and its digest and selection policy compared with the prepared archive.
Before the first upload each package's Git source state is assessed again and compared with the prepared assessment.
The execution candidate's material fingerprint is checked before and after the revalidation gate.
An upload without an acknowledged response is settled by bounded exact-version readback from the Registry.

publishing-upload.existingSharing: The prepared admitted archive is uploaded verbatim and its integrity was computed once while preparing.
publishing-upload.preparedInputs: A byte-identical rebuild reuses the prepared archive's admission instead of admitting and copying the rebuild; the rebuild is compared by digest over its own bytes.
freshChecks: The workspace transition lock, or for 'publish --path' a temporary coordination workspace's lock.
The material fingerprint before and after the revalidation gate.
The rebuilt distribution digest and selection policy, and the Git source state, compared with the prepared values.
publishing-upload.lifetime: The prepared archive is owned by its upload candidate until the command completes and each upload receives its own copy; the rebuild's bytes live only for its comparison; the 'publish --path' coordination workspace is created only on apply and removed when the resolution's scope closes; nothing is retained across invocations.

before-first-upload-each-package-s.basis: Before the first upload each package's distribution is rebuilt from current sources and its Git source state assessed again, and both are compared with the prepared values.

each-upload-sends-private-copy-admitted.basis: Each upload sends a private copy of the admitted archive, because the admitted archive never lends its bytes by reference.
each-upload-sends-private-copy-admitted.openQuestion: May the publish upload hand the Registry client the admitted archive's own bytes instead of a private copy, giving up the guarantee that the admitted archive never lends its bytes by reference?

revalidation-compares-rebuilt-distributi.basis: Revalidation compares the rebuilt distribution by digest over its own bytes and, when it is identical, reuses the prepared admission, so one admission and only the upload copy remain per candidate.

publishing-visibility-intent.resource: The repository visibility intent of a project package, derived from its authored manifest and the workspace publication default by one resolver shared by publish and visibility, and submitted to the Registry.
publishing-visibility-intent.publication: None locally: visibility status submits the intent for evaluation, visibility reconcile sends a conditional remote visibility update, and publish submits each candidate's intent in its publication-set preview.

reads.note: Settings and the lockfile are decoded once in one document phase that ends before any Registry request.
The canonical observation reads the authored manifest and hands over its text; the visibility intent is decoded from that text.

Publish derives each candidate's intent once from the candidate's decoded manifest visibility and the workspace default, submits it in the publication-set preview, and the upload carries the preview's visibility input instead of deriving it again.

publishing-visibility-intent.existingSharing: Publish already derived each candidate's intent once and carried the preview's visibility input to its upload; visibility status and reconcile shared nothing before prepared inputs were shared.
publishing-visibility-intent.preparedInputs: Visibility status and reconcile decode the intent from the manifest text the canonical observation read, and their document reads share one phase.
freshChecks: Reconcile's remote update is conditional on the Registry revision it observed.
Publish's upload is bound to the publication-set and descriptor digests of its preview.
publishing-visibility-intent.lifetime: The captured text and decoded documents live only inside the intent's document phase, which closes before the Registry request; publish's derived intent is held on its candidate's preview until the command completes; nothing is retained across invocations.

publish-derives-each-candidate-s-visibil.basis: Publish derives each candidate's visibility intent from the manifest visibility its candidate decode already produced and one read of the workspace default inside the preparation read view, and on apply the upload submits the visibility input its publication preview returned instead of deriving the intent again.

repository-visibility-intent-decoded-fro.basis: The repository visibility intent is decoded from the manifest text the canonical observation read instead of a second manifest read.

visibility-intent-derivation-reads-proje.basis: Visibility intent derivation reads the project settings and lockfile inside one document read phase, closed before any Registry request is sent.

registry-requests.resource: Registry requests made through the Registry client factory: index metadata, exact-content admission, archive downloads, discovery, publication, lifecycle and visibility, the identity and token-management requests sent on its authorized wire, together with the per-phase index metadata cache that serves file and remote Registries alike.
registry-requests.publication: None: remote requests and in-memory metadata only; nothing is written locally.

reads.note: Index metadata for one endpoint, credential authority, request policy and identity is requested once per read phase; concurrent requests for one endpoint are batched up to 100 identities per resolution request.
When the endpoint's credential authority changes while a metadata read is in flight, the read is retried under the new authority, at most three times.

Exact-content admission requests check current publisher, integrity and eligibility per logical set before acquisition; the re-admission after confirmation and the one after a contended lock wait are their own requests.

An archive downloaded by a client built without an archive cache is accepted only from a complete response and hashed once against the selected integrity; the CLI's factory always gives remote clients the invocation's archive cache, which hashes instead.
Discover deduplicates Registry endpoints and merges every recommendation naming one endpoint into one discovery submission per endpoint, which the client splits only at the request limits.
Archive, unarchive, deprecate and undeprecate read the current management view once and condition their one write on its revision; nothing repeats.
A visibility update is conditioned on the revision its single read observed, and a publish upload on the condition its publication preview returned.
Verification selects every distinct extension through one batched selection inside one Registry read phase and admits the listed releases once per batch of at most one hundred.
One package detection lists the project directory once, when a detector first asks, and every detector of that detection shares the frozen entries or the same absence.
Each reader with packages to read opens one read per local recommendation read, and the package-manager roots, listings and project package indexes its packages share are read at most once within it.

Dependency resolution reads, parses and validates the installed package.json of each declared dependency once and carries the members the npm reader decodes on the detected package, which the reader checks against the package URL.
The Python reader probes each python* candidate's site-packages under a virtual environment's lib to choose the one it lists, once per local recommendation read.
The Deno reader probes the Deno cache and its jsr.io registry directory once per local recommendation read so that an absent cache costs one probe instead of a failed listing per package.
Installing a named Registry skill or subagent checks each configured host for the extension in order, outside the read phase, and the first host where it exists is matched.

registry-requests.existingSharing: Index metadata reads inside one Registry read phase are shared per endpoint, credential authority, request policy and identity, batched per endpoint, and kept only on success until the phase ends; discover merges the recommendations naming one Registry into one discovery submission per endpoint; exact-content admission is batched per logical set and per Registry endpoint; verification selects all its extensions in one batched selection and admits each batch of listed releases once; with an archive cache configured, equal concurrent archive downloads coalesce through it. Within discover, one package detection lists the project directory once for every detector that asks, dependency resolution carries the installed package.json members the npm reader decodes on the detected package, and each package reader opens one read per local recommendation read in which its packages share the package-manager roots, listings and project package indexes they have in common.
registry-requests.preparedInputs: An archive downloaded by a client built without an archive cache is returned with verification evidence for the buffer the client hashed, so Registry consumers skip their own hash; the factory's remote clients always use the invocation's archive cache, which delivers that evidence instead. One package detection's project directory listing is frozen, or the same absence when listing fails, and is consumed by the gem, NuGet, CocoaPods, Hackage, LuaRocks and opam detectors, which each select and read their own manifests. A resolved npm package carries a deep-frozen copy of the installed package.json members the npm reader decodes, and the npm reader decodes that copy instead of reading the file again. Each package reader with packages to read evaluates its package-independent roots once per local recommendation read, the Python site-packages probes and listing, the Cargo registry and index listings, the Cabal store listing, the opam switch listing, the Deno cache probes, the conda package cache listing and the Zig cache listing, and every package of that read consumes the frozen results. Within the same read, roots derived from a project, the pub package_config.json entries, the Cabal dist-newstyle probe and the pixi environment and conda-meta listings, are shared per path, and the Zig reader shares each visited cache entry's parsed agent-extensions.json.
freshChecks: Each exact-content admission is a fresh request; the re-admissions after confirmation and after a contended lock wait are separate requests.
A read phase ends before a workspace mutation; later metadata queries open a fresh phase, and a failed metadata read is never kept.
A metadata read whose credential authority changed in flight is retried under the current authority.
Archive, unarchive, deprecate, undeprecate and visibility writes are conditioned on the revision observed just before them; a publish upload is conditioned on its preview's condition.
Yank, unyank, identity and token requests are single requests with nothing to share.

Installing a named Registry skill or subagent picks its configured host with an existence check of the extension, a HEAD request on a remote Registry or a stat of its index.json on a file Registry, which the read phase does not serve, before the refs are resolved from that extension's index on the matched host.
The Python reader probes the site-packages of each python* candidate under a virtual environment's lib in turn and lists the first that exists, once per local recommendation read.
The Deno reader probes the Deno cache and its jsr.io registry directory once per local recommendation read before each package lists its own cache directory beneath them.
registry-requests.lifetime: Phase metadata lives in the read phase's scope and is released when the phase closes or is invalidated before a mutation; discovery responses and admission results belong to the call that requested them; an uncached archive and its evidence belong to the caller of that read; the project directory listing lives until its package detection returns; each package reader's shared roots, listings and decoded files are read when a package of a local recommendation read first needs them and are released when that read returns; the npm metadata copy travels on its detected package within one discover call; nothing is retained across invocations.

after-sign-issues-session-identity-read.basis: After a sign-in issues a session, the identity read for the new token is sent once more with the same token when its first attempt fails, before the session is saved. The second attempt runs only after a failure, so it is recovery rather than repeated work, and removing it changes the saved handle and the reported identity; the accepted requirement retains the session when identity is unavailable but does not decide how many identity attempts precede that outcome.
after-sign-issues-session-identity-read.openQuestion: May sign-in save the newly issued session under the unknown handle and report no signed-in identity after a single failed identity read, instead of sending that read once more?

apply-admits-exact-registry-refs-plan.basis: An apply admits the exact Registry refs its plan exposes or acquires in a fresh exact-content admission before acquisition, again after confirmation and again after waiting on lock contention, so a publisher, integrity or eligibility change in between refuses the apply.

each-registry-exposure-check-admits-all.basis: Each Registry exposure check admits all of a plan's distinct exact Registry refs in one logical request per Registry endpoint, split only at the request size limits, rather than once per step.

install-selection-planning-each-run-thei.basis: Install selection and planning each run their Registry index reads in their own Registry read phase, which serves repeated selections within that phase from one response.

one-index-read-serves-whole-document.basis: One index read serves the whole document, and a Hook document reads its package by the exact version and integrity that index named instead of resolving it again.

preparation-s-registry-index-reads-run.basis: Preparation's Registry index reads run in one Registry read phase that serves repeated selections from one response.

recommendations-naming-one-registry-merg.basis: Recommendations naming one Registry are merged into a single discovery request per Registry endpoint.

registry-request-registry-rejects-while-.basis: A Registry request that the Registry rejects while a stored session is presented is sent once more with the renewed session credential.

verification-requests-selection-metadata.basis: Verification requests selection metadata for every distinct selected extension through one batched selection inside one Registry read phase, and admits the listed releases once per batch of at most one hundred, each admission serving its batch's archive reads.

pub-zig-readers-share-ecosystem-files-pe.basis: Within one local recommendation read of discover, the pub reader reads and decodes each project's .dart_tool/package_config.json once, keyed by its path with frozen entries, and the zig reader lists the zig cache once and reads and parses each visited cache entry's agent-extensions.json once. The shared values live only until that read returns; each package still looks up its own entry, reads its own pubspec.yaml, emits its own malformed-JSON and metadata warnings, and stops at the first cache entry whose metadata decodes.

package-readers-share-ecosystem-root-lis.basis: Within one local recommendation read of discover, the packages of one ecosystem share one evaluation of each package-manager root that does not depend on the package: the Python site-packages probes and listing, the Cargo registry and index listings, the Cabal store listing, the opam switch listing, the Deno cache probes and the conda package cache listing, while roots derived from a project's manifest, the Cabal dist-newstyle probe and the pixi environment and conda-meta listings, are shared per project path. Shared listings are frozen and released when the read returns; configuration is still read before any probe, and every per-package metadata read and warning stays per package.

npm-reader-decodes-metadata-resolution-a.basis: Dependency resolution puts a deep-frozen copy of the installed package.json members the npm reader decodes on the resolved observation, so the reader decodes the metadata detection read instead of reading and parsing that file again in the same discover call. The resolution's existence probes, its read, parse and identity validation, and the reader's comparison of name and version against the package URL with its warning stay.

package-detection-lists-project-director.basis: One package detection of discover lists the project directory once, when a detector first asks, and the gem, NuGet, CocoaPods, Hackage, LuaRocks and opam detectors share its frozen entries, or the same absence when the listing fails. The listing lives until that detection returns, and a listing every asker abandoned is not kept; each detector still selects its own manifests and reads each of them itself.

package-readers-list-directories-without.basis: Within one local recommendation read of discover, the Zig, Mojo, Deno and Python readers list the Zig cache, the pixi environments and each environment's conda-meta, each Deno package's cache directory and a virtual environment's lib directly, without probing them first, because a listing that fails, absence included, gives the result the probe gave. The Zig cache, pixi environment, conda-meta and lib listings stay shared within that read as before, and each Deno package lists its own cache directory.

python-reader-probes-each-site-packages-.basis: The Python reader probes the site-packages of each python* candidate under a virtual environment's lib in turn and lists the first one that exists, because the probe chooses between candidates and a selected site-packages that cannot be listed yields no metadata instead of moving on to the next candidate. The probe and the listing are made once per local recommendation read and shared by every package of that read.
python-reader-probes-each-site-packages-.openQuestion: Should the Python reader select the first python* candidate whose site-packages can be listed, instead of probing each candidate's site-packages and then listing the selected one?

deno-reader-probes-cache-roots-once-per-.basis: The Deno reader probes the Deno cache and its jsr.io registry directory, which it never lists, once per local recommendation read before each package lists its own cache directory beneath them, so an absent cache costs one probe instead of a failed listing for every package.
deno-reader-probes-cache-roots-once-per-.openQuestion: Should the Deno reader list each package's cache directory without first probing the Deno cache and its jsr.io registry directory, accepting one failed listing per package when the cache is absent?

named-registry-host-check-precedes-index.basis: Installing a named Registry skill or subagent picks its configured host with an existence check of the extension, a HEAD request on a remote Registry or a stat of its index.json on a file Registry, which the Registry read phase does not serve; resolving the refs then reads the same extension's index on the matched host, for a version range and an exact version alike, with no write, lock or phase end between them. The existence check alone decides which host matches, the failure reasons the probe output reports and the not-found refusal, so a host whose index is unreadable or undecodable matches and then refuses.
named-registry-host-check-precedes-index.openQuestion: May the configured-host lookup for a named Registry skill or subagent pick its host from the extension index read (served by the read phase and reused when the refs are resolved) instead of a separate existence check, accepting three changes: probe failure reasons use the index-read vocabulary, a host whose index is unreadable or undecodable falls through to the next configured host instead of matching and then refusing, and a missing extension reports the index-resolution not-found refusal?

registry-selection.resource: The invocation's selected Registry, derived from the project and user settings and the built-in sources.

reads.note: Project and user settings decoded once by an uninitialized-allowed location construction and handed to a pure snapshot builder.
The construction's layout reads are the selection's only settings reads; the user layout is resolved from paths alone.

registry-selection.existingSharing: The invocation's Registry context decides the selection lazily, at most once, when a command first needs a Registry, and caches the snapshot and both selections for the invocation.
registry-selection.preparedInputs: The project and user settings that the selection's own location construction decodes for its layout are handed to the snapshot instead of being read and decoded again.
freshChecks: The selection is read only when a command first needs a Registry; malformed settings fail at that point with a selection failure naming the file.
A workspace command's own workspace layer builds its location separately and reads its documents again for its own validity boundary.
registry-selection.lifetime: The two decoded settings documents belong to one snapshot construction; the immutable snapshot is held by the invocation's Registry context and released with the invocation.

command-opens-workspace-registry-selecti.basis: On a command that opens a workspace, the Registry selection's own location construction reads and decodes the project and user settings again after the workspace layer's location construction read them. The workspace layer's read ends when its constructor returns, while the selection is read lazily when a command first needs a Registry, possibly after the lock, prompts or settings writes, so it cannot reuse the ended construction read.

invocation-s-registry-context-decides-se.basis: The invocation's Registry context decides the selection at most once, when a command first needs a Registry, and serves the explicit and default selections and every request authorization's default-Registry lookup from that one cached snapshot.

registry-selection-builds-snapshot-from-.basis: The Registry selection builds its snapshot from the project and user settings its own location construction decoded for the layout, instead of reading and decoding both again.

runtime-directories.resource: Runtime directories: the workspace .axm/tmp scratch directory, the coordination namespace and its admission scratch directory, and container parents created through this owner.
runtime-directories.publication: Directory tree: exclusive creation proven against an anchor identity; empty-only removal of proven created directories.

reads.note: Existence walk to the nearest existing ancestor; when nothing is missing one rooted container capture proves the existing directory.

When something is missing, or the rooted capture fails or finds no directory: anchor capture, route assertion and anchor re-verification before each exclusive creation, identity capture of each created directory, final anchor re-verification and rooted capture.
Empty-only removal verifies each created directory's identity first.

runtime-directories.existingSharing: Each call proves its own directory; created-directory identities are handed to the caller's record callback, which the transition-lock hold and the receipt store keep.
runtime-directories.preparedInputs: When nothing is missing, the rooted capture of the existing directory is the single proof; the self-rooted anchor capture and its re-verification, which bracket no creation, are skipped.
freshChecks: Existence walk and rooted capture on every call.
Anchor re-verification before each creation and after the loop when something is created.
Identity verification before each empty-only removal.
runtime-directories.lifetime: Created-directory identities are handed to the caller's record callback (the lock hold or receipt store); proofs are local to one call. Nothing is retained across invocations by this owner.

when-runtime-directory-already-exists-on.basis: When the runtime directory already exists, one rooted capture proves it and the self-rooted anchor capture and its re-verification, which bracket no creation, are skipped; the coordination admission scratch directory is proven this way at every boundary claim.

runtime-ignores.resource: The workspace ignore file (.gitignore) entries for runtime, staging and backup directories.
runtime-ignores.publication: Atomic replacement of .gitignore when a runtime entry is missing.

reads.note: Existence probe of .gitignore: carries the check-target step label and decides the created or modified footprint.
Read-if-present of the existing lines, so existing content and line endings are kept and only missing entries are appended.
Settlement snapshot before the write.
Setup decides at apply, after approval, whether the workspace is Git-managed before ensuring the ignores; the probe made while preparing the preview only describes it.
A first-use settings write probes axm.json and ensures the ignores only when the settings file was absent.

runtime-ignores.existingSharing: The ignore file is read once per call through a read-if-present read after its existence probe; nothing is shared with other owners.
freshChecks: Runs inside the caller's workspace transaction, immediately before its atomic write.
Setup's Git-managed decision and lockfile presence are observed again at apply after the probes made while preparing the preview.
runtime-ignores.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners.

ignore-file-update-probes-existence-befo.basis: The ignore-file update probes .gitignore for existence before reading it, and the probe and the read report different step labels and diagnostic causes for a failure other than absence. The accepted requirements do not decide whether a non-NotFound failure may move from the probe's check-target label and access cause to the read's read-target label and readFile cause.
ignore-file-update-probes-existence-befo.openQuestion: May the ignore-file update drop its existence probe, so that a non-NotFound failure of .gitignore is reported with the content read's step label ("read-target") and readFile cause instead of the probe's "check-target" label and access cause?

setup-decides-apply-after-approval-wheth.basis: Setup decides at apply, after approval, whether axm.lock exists and whether the workspace is Git-managed before writing the lockfile and the runtime ignores; the probes made while preparing the preview only describe it.

when-first-install-sets-up-workspace.basis: When a first install sets up the workspace, setup apply probes the ignore file for existence and then reads it, and the probe keeps its own failure step and diagnostic cause. Dropping the probe keeps the outcome for absent, empty, present and dangling-symlink files but changes the step label and cause of every non-NotFound failure, which the accepted requirements do not decide; the preservation read stays either way.
when-first-install-sets-up-workspace.openQuestion: May the runtime-ignore step label and diagnostic cause for a non-NotFound .gitignore failure during setup apply come from the content read ("read-target", readFile cause) instead of the existence probe ("check-target", access cause)?

self-update.resource: The installed axm executable (its resolved target), the sibling .axm-backup-* rollback file, the staged download and <target>.upgrade.lock; for package-manager installations, the installation the owning manager replaces.
self-update.publication: Atomic replacement of the CLI executable through a staged download and a rollback copy under a per-target upgrade lock; package-manager upgrades are delegated to the owning manager.

reads.note: The executable path is resolved to its real target before the lock is taken.
On lock contention the existing lock is read, its owner's liveness checked, and target and backup existence probed for crash recovery.
The downloaded bytes are hashed once and compared with the release checksum.
The staged executable reports its version before replacement.
The original executable is copied aside (renamed on Windows) before replacement.
The installed executable, and after a failed verification the restored original, report their versions.
Package-manager installations are inspected before mutation and after the manager runs.

self-update.existingSharing: The download is collected once, hashed once and staged without a copy, and the prepared upgrade decision is passed directly to apply.
freshChecks: A per-target upgrade lock with owner liveness and stale-lock recovery is acquired before staging.
The installed executable's real path is resolved again when the upgrade lock is taken, after release selection.
Every executable version check runs after the step it verifies.
self-update.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the staged download and upgrade lock are released when the upgrade settles, and the backup is removed on acceptance or renamed back on restoration, remaining in place with its path reported when install metadata cannot be persisted or restoration fails.

package-manager-upgrade-inspects-install.basis: A package-manager upgrade inspects the installation before mutation and again after the manager runs to verify what it installed.

script-upgrade-hashes-download-copies-or.basis: A script upgrade hashes the download, copies the original aside and runs the staged, installed and restored executables' version checks, each verifying a different step.

script-upgrade-resolves-installed-execut.basis: A script upgrade resolves the installed executable's real path when it takes the upgrade lock; owner detection resolved the same path earlier only when the method came from the resolved executable path, and release selection with its network reads lies between them. The lock-time resolution is the last route check that fixes which file the lock protects and which file is replaced, so a retargeted link is observed, and it reports a failed resolution as an upgrade failure where detection tolerates it.
script-upgrade-resolves-installed-execut.openQuestion: Must a script upgrade resolve its executable's real path again when it takes the upgrade lock, so that a link retargeted during release selection decides which file is locked and replaced, or may it lock the real path that owner detection resolved?

settlement-restoration.resource: Protected workspace paths restored from the rollback store or from retirement quarantine.
settlement-restoration.publication: Atomic replacement through an owned staging sibling and rename (a directory swaps through a trash sibling); identity-preserving in-place reconcile; rename to trash to restore absence; rename of retained originals back from quarantine.

reads.note: Route re-proof before restoring: target entry, native root referent and link value, and the ancestor route (walked once above the root), compared with the snapshot's route baseline.
Current state compared with the snapshot's expected postimage; a divergent boundary is preserved with recovery evidence.
Each retirement store's identity (observed without its entry when the store root matches) and a full observation of each retained original before anything moves.
In-place reconcile reads the backup and the current bytes and compares them directly, writing only files that differ so the retained entry identity survives.
Staged copy hashed against the backup before it is published.
After restoration the target is hashed against the backup and each moved-back original's entry identity is compared.
The backup is hashed again at verification: the only detection of a change to the private rollback store between staging and verification.

settlement-restoration.existingSharing: Restoration takes the route baseline and expected postimage that protection recorded in the ledger snapshot instead of deriving them again.
