settlement-restoration.preparedInputs: The route re-proof walks the ancestors above the native root once; a retirement store whose root matches is observed without its entry, which the next check reads in full; in-place reconcile compares bytes instead of two digests.
freshChecks: Route re-proof per restored snapshot, with the native root's referent and link resolved fresh.
Current-versus-expected comparison per snapshot.
Staged-copy hash before publication.
Backup re-hash at verification.
Restoration stops once the transition is compromised.
settlement-restoration.lifetime: Values are local to one snapshot's restoration inside the rollback's ledger admission; nothing is transferred to another owner or retained across invocations.

verification-after-rollback-hashes-backu.basis: Verification after a rollback hashes the backup again, the only check that the private rollback store did not change between staging and verification.
verification-after-rollback-hashes-backu.openQuestion: Is detecting a change to the private rollback store between staging and verification a requirement?

when-failed-closure-rolled-back-place.basis: When a failed closure is rolled back, the in-place reconcile of a retained entry compares backup and current bytes directly instead of computing two digests.

settlement-retirement.resource: Retired entries held in same-device .axm-retired-* quarantine stores until settlement.
settlement-retirement.publication: Removal: identity-preserving rename into a quarantine store created beside the entry, and removal of that store at settlement; direct removal outside a transaction.

reads.note: Fresh route assertion of the target inside the protection's admission decides the owning snapshot, the entry kind and whether the protection's observation may stand in.

Owner-tree comparison with the snapshot's expected state: the protection's observation stands in when the owner is the entry and the kind matches; a broader owner, an absent target or a changed kind is observed fresh.
The retired entry's original state: a copy of the protection's observation in the exact or miss case, a fresh observation for a descendant retirement.
Quarantine anchor: native and workspace root referents (from the admission's resolution of an ordinary root, else fresh) and device stats up to a mount boundary.
Identity of the newly created quarantine store.
Fresh route assertion and entry observation immediately before the rename.
At settlement, the store (without its entry when the store root matches) and the retained entry are observed before the store is removed; a modified original is preserved.
Recovery reporting observes each retained backup in full and uses only whether its root is absent.

settlement-retirement.existingSharing: The owner-tree check compares against the expected state the protecting snapshot recorded in the ledger, and the quarantine store's identity recorded at retirement is what cleanup and restoration compare against.
settlement-retirement.preparedInputs: Protection and retirement run in one ledger admission: in the exact or miss case the protection's whole-tree observation stands in for the owner-tree observation and, copied, for the original state; the admission's resolution of an ordinary root supplies the quarantine anchors; cleanup's store observation skips the entry, which its fresh entry observation reads.
freshChecks: Route assertion of the target inside the merged admission.
Fresh owner-tree observation for a broader owner, an absent target or a changed kind.
Fresh route assertion and entry observation before the rename.
Before any refusal decided on a reused observation, a fresh owner-tree observation.
Fresh entry observation at cleanup before the store is removed.
settlement-retirement.lifetime: The protection's observation is used only inside the same ledger admission and is copied before it is stored as the retirement's original; the original and store identity live in the owning snapshot's retirement record until cleanup at settlement or restoration. Nothing is retained across invocations.

before-quarantine-store-removed-settleme.basis: Before a quarantine store is removed at settlement, the retained entry is observed fresh and compared with its recorded original so a modified original is preserved.

descendant-retirement-whose-owner-snapsh.basis: A descendant retirement, whose owner snapshot is broader than the entry, observes the entry subtree fresh after the owner-tree observation in the same admission.
descendant-retirement-whose-owner-snapsh.openQuestion: Should a foreign write that lands between the owner-tree check and the entry observation of one retirement admission be refused as a foreign change and preserved, rather than quarantined as the retired original and removed at cleanup?

inside-merged-admission-retirement-asser.basis: Inside the merged admission, retirement asserts the target's route fresh after the protection's copy, which decides whether the protection's observation may stand in, the owner match and the quarantine root.

linked-alias-spelled-absent-native-root.basis: A linked, alias-spelled or absent native root is resolved fresh for the retirement quarantine anchors instead of reusing the admission's selected root address.
linked-alias-spelled-absent-native-root.openQuestion: Is the root address that the admission's route assertion selects for a linked, alias-spelled or absent native root equal to a fresh resolution and link read of that root within the same admission, so it can serve as the rollback route baseline and the quarantine anchor?

owner-snapshot-broader-than-entry-each.basis: For an owner snapshot broader than the entry, each retirement observes the owner tree fresh as a whole-boundary check at its own mutation instant.

protection-retirement-run-one-ledger-adm.basis: Protection and retirement run in one ledger admission, and when the owner snapshot is the entry with an unchanged kind the protection's whole-tree observation stands in for the owner-tree check and, copied, for the retired original.

recovery-reporting-after-failed-settleme.basis: Recovery reporting after a failed settlement observes each retained quarantine backup in full although it uses only whether the backup's root is absent.
recovery-reporting-after-failed-settleme.openQuestion: May an observation whose descendant values are discarded (created-ancestor entries, retirement-store identity probes and recovery-entry reporting) skip reading foreign descendants that no other step of the same boundary reads, so that a planted FIFO, device or very large file there is no longer opened?

settlement-cleanup-observes-matching-qua.basis: Settlement cleanup observes a matching quarantine store without descending into its entry, which the fresh entry observation reads once.

when-target-absent-changed-kind-after.basis: When the target is absent or changed kind after protection, retirement observes the owner tree fresh before deciding, as the last conflict check on that path.

settlement-snapshots.resource: Rollback preimage snapshots: the OS-temporary axm-rollback- store and, in the transaction ledger, each protected target's expected state, preimage and route baseline, updated by every recorded publication.
settlement-snapshots.publication: Copy or link: the rollback store is created at the first copied snapshot and a target's preimage is copied into it before the target's first mutation; while coalescing, earlier child preimages are rewound inside that copy (remove, make directory, symlink, copy).

reads.note: Route assertion of the target before and after its boundary claim, for protections and content claims alike; refuses an alias change during the claim wait.
Exact re-protect of a target the closure already snapshotted observes it again and refuses a foreign change.
Whole-tree observation of a first-touched target (read and SHA-256 per file) recorded as the snapshot's expected state.

Route baseline: identity of each existing ancestor up to the native root, then the root's own ancestors once; an ordinary root's physical spelling comes from the admission's route assertion, other roots are resolved fresh.
Payload classification at the capture point: a link read and an existence probe after the route walk decide symlink, absent or copied.
Copy of the preimage into the rollback store with timestamps preserved; a second read of the bytes the observation read.
Re-observation of earlier descendant snapshots before they are coalesced into a broader or absent boundary.
Postimage route resolution before the ledger admission, then a readback of the published entry inside it that becomes the new expected state.
A file publication's readback reads and digests the entry once; the read bytes are compared with the writer's intended content and its pre-rename entry identity.
Entry observation of each ancestor a publication created inside a protected snapshot, skipping the chain child already read in the same admission; foreign siblings are still observed in full.

settlement-snapshots.existingSharing: First-touch deduplication per closure: a target its closure already protected, or one under a protected target, is not snapshotted again; the atomic writer hands each publication's pre-rename entry identity and content to recording, so recording never re-stats for identity; the native-root witnesses are captured once per transaction scope and serve every admission's route assertion.
settlement-snapshots.preparedInputs: The admission's live route assertion supplies an ordinary native root's physical spelling to the route baseline; the route baseline walks the ancestors above the native root once; a file readback's bytes are compared with the intended content instead of digesting that content again; recording a publication with created ancestors skips the chain child it has just read; a protection hands a copy of its whole-tree observation to the retirement that continues the same ledger admission.
freshChecks: Route assertion before and after every boundary claim, for protections and content claims.
Exact re-protect at each nested join re-observes the target.
Linked, alias-spelled and absent native roots are resolved fresh for the route baseline.
Payload classification (link read, existence) at the capture point.
Descendant re-observation before coalescing.
Postimage route resolution outside, and readback inside, the ledger admission.
A readback that is not the publication's own entry with exactly its intended bytes is refused before it is recorded.
settlement-snapshots.lifetime: The observation handed to a retirement is a copy confined to the same ledger admission; readback bytes are consumed by verification inside the recording admission and only the observed state enters the ledger; expected state and route baselines live in the transaction ledger until their closure settles or rolls back, and the transaction removes the store at settlement. Nothing is retained across invocations.

after-canonical-directory-renamed-into-p.basis: After a canonical directory is renamed into place, settlement observes the new tree as the rollback authority for that target.

after-export-bundle-renamed-into-place.basis: After the export bundle is renamed into place, the transaction walks the new tree to record its postimage, the rollback authority that restoration compares before removing it.

closure-s-first-touch-settings-lockfile.basis: A closure's first touch of the settings and lockfile observes and copies them as its rollback snapshot, a preimage no read outside the transaction can stand in for.

file-publication-verification-compares-r.basis: File-publication verification compares the readback's bytes with the writer's intended content and pre-rename identity, so a recorded publication is digested once instead of twice.

first-touched-target-observed-hashed-the.basis: A first-touched target is observed and hashed, then copied into the rollback store with timestamps preserved; building the copy from the observed bytes would change foreign-edit capture, mode and timestamp fidelity.

foreign-siblings-inside-created-ancestor.basis: Foreign siblings inside created ancestors are still observed in full when a publication is recorded, because no other step of the boundary reads them.
foreign-siblings-inside-created-ancestor.openQuestion: May an observation whose descendant values are discarded (created-ancestor entries, retirement-store identity probes and recovery-entry reporting) skip reading foreign descendants that no other step of the same boundary reads, so that a planted FIFO, device or very large file there is no longer opened?

ordinary-native-root-route-baseline-snap.basis: For an ordinary native root, the route baseline of a snapshot miss and the retirement quarantine anchors take the root's physical spelling from the admission's own route assertion instead of resolving the root again.

protecting-receipt-store-before-write-sn.basis: Protecting the receipt store before a write snapshots it, and file-publication verification reads it back, as the rollback preimage and the postimage check of the closure.

recorded-publication-resolves-route-befo.basis: A recorded publication resolves its route before the ledger admission and reads the entry back inside it, two different validity boundaries.

recording-publication-created-ancestors-.basis: Recording a publication that created ancestors inside a protected snapshot skips re-reading the chain child it has just read, and rollback observes a matching retirement store without its entry, which the next check reads in full.

refusal-path-post-write-verification-sti.basis: On the refusal path, post-write verification still reads a foreign replacement of a just-published file before its identity is compared.
refusal-path-post-write-verification-sti.openQuestion: Should post-write publication verification compare the entry identity before reading, so a foreign FIFO, device or directory that replaced a just-published file is refused without being read?

route-baseline-records-each-ancestor-s.basis: The route baseline records each ancestor's identity for the restoration route re-proof, which the route assertions do not provide.

settlement-readback-publication-establis.basis: The settlement readback of a publication establishes the rollback authority for that target, a different obligation from the owners' own readbacks of the same file.

snapshot-miss-classifies-rollback-payloa.basis: A snapshot miss classifies its rollback payload (symlink, absent or copied) with a link read and an existence probe at the capture point after the route walk.
snapshot-miss-classifies-rollback-payloa.openQuestion: May the rollback payload classification of a snapshot miss be decided from the whole-tree observation instead of a fresh link read and existence probe at the capture point?

snapshot-miss-s-route-baseline-route.basis: A snapshot miss's route baseline, and the route re-proof of each restored snapshot, walk the ancestors above the native root once instead of once per chain.

snapshot-miss-under-linked-alias-spelled.basis: A snapshot miss under a linked, alias-spelled or absent native root resolves the root and reads its link fresh for the route baseline, repeating the admission's own assertion.
snapshot-miss-under-linked-alias-spelled.openQuestion: Is the root address that the admission's route assertion selects for a linked, alias-spelled or absent native root equal to a fresh resolution and link read of that root within the same admission, so it can serve as the rollback route baseline and the quarantine anchor?

target-s-route-asserted-before-after.basis: The target's route is asserted before and after each boundary claim, for protections and content claims alike, to refuse an alias change during the claim wait.

when-broader-absent-boundary-protected-a.basis: When a broader or absent boundary is protected after its children, each earlier descendant snapshot is observed again before it is coalesced, as freshness after the whole-tree copy.

workspace-transaction-s-first-protection.basis: The workspace transaction's first protection of the authored manifest observes its preimage and route, including an existence check, as the rollback snapshot, after the owner's own reads.

settlement-transaction.resource: The transaction's rollback store directory, removed at settlement.
settlement-transaction.publication: Removal of the rollback store when no pending restoration still needs it.

reads.note: Before the transition lock is acquired, the workspace directory and its scratch directory are asserted within the native root.
A top-level transaction asserts the workspace directory within its native root before taking the admission permit.
Declared-target protection before the transition: the settings and lockfile (unless a closure-scoped plan apply opts out) and the declared targets.
A transaction that joins an active closure protects its declared targets again, so default targets the closure already holds are exactly re-protected and re-observed.

settlement-transaction.existingSharing: The invocation-level transition hold is reused instead of acquired again; a nested transaction joins the active closure, its ledger and its boundary claims; closure-scoped plan applies protect the shared files at first touch instead of eagerly; the native-root witnesses are captured once per transaction scope.
freshChecks: Workspace and scratch-directory route assertions before each lock acquisition, and the workspace assertion before each top-level transaction.
Workspace admission permit and transition hold (reused when the invocation holds it).
One boundary-claims lease per top-level transaction.
The transition races the hold's and the lease's compromise signals.
Nested joins re-protect their declared targets.
settlement-transaction.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the ledger and the rollback store live for one top-level transaction.

adding-inline-mcp-server-runs-one.basis: Adding an inline MCP server runs one plan transaction that claims no default targets, and no nested transaction joins its closure, so no target is protected twice at this owner.

nested-transaction-joins-active-closure-.basis: A nested transaction that joins the active closure protects its declared targets again, so default targets the closure already holds are exactly re-protected and re-observed.
nested-transaction-joins-active-closure-.openQuestion: May a nested transaction join skip the boundary claim and exact re-observation of a default target the closure already holds exactly, relying on each writer's own protection?

transaction-claims-default-targets-snaps.basis: A transaction that claims default targets snapshots the settings and lockfile before its transition even when the transition leaves them untouched.
transaction-claims-default-targets-snaps.openQuestion: Should untouched default targets keep rollback copies and recovery evidence in transactions whose transition never writes them?

setup-instruction-source.resource: The project canonical instruction source file (AGENTS.md or the chosen name) and the seeded alias file it replaces, as written by setup initialization, including the interactive first-use setup that install and handoff run before acting in an uninitialized scope.
setup-instruction-source.publication: Create-if-missing plain write of the instruction source file, and removal of the seeded alias it replaces after a byte recheck; each is protected by a settlement snapshot and recorded as a footprint.

reads.note: On an existing project, the settings read that decides whether setup completes an open instruction choice is handed to initialization when no transaction follows.
The candidate instruction files are read in full once for ranking, the seed and, when no source-selection prompt runs, the selected source's presence on the plan's source row.
Plan rows: the recorded instruction rows are read from the lockfile and the instruction projection is observed, including a symbolic-link capability probe.
Plan-time Git-managed status and existence of the lockfile and .gitignore, used for display rows.
After a source-selection prompt, instruction planning probes the selected source's presence again for the plan's source row unless the plan creates it.
After an approval prompt the recorded rows are read again before any write, so an unreadable lockfile version refuses first.
At apply, lockfile presence before creating it, Git-managed status before transient ignores, and source absence before creating it.
The seeded alias and the canonical source are re-read and compared byte for byte before the alias is removed.
Instruction sync at apply observes again, with its own symbolic-link capability probe.
The lockfile is read as the base for committing changed instruction rows after sync.
Footprints record the postimages of the source file and alias for settlement.

setup-instruction-source.existingSharing: The candidate source content read at plan was already passed to apply as the source content and seed. This change also hands that candidate read's source presence to instruction planning when no source-selection prompt runs, the instruction rows decoded at plan to unattended apply, and the settings read that decides an existing project's completion to initialization when no transaction follows.
setup-instruction-source.preparedInputs: Unattended non-preview setup hands the instruction rows decoded at plan to apply as an independent copy instead of re-reading the lockfile; the report's Git-managed check runs only on the branch that uses it; and setup on an existing project decides completion from one settings read, handing it to initialization when no transaction follows. When setup runs no source-selection prompt, as on unattended and preview runs or with an explicitly named source, instruction source resolution hands the selected source's presence from its candidate read to instruction planning, which uses it for the source row instead of probing the file again.
freshChecks: Interactive setup re-reads the recorded rows after approval, before any write.
After a source-selection prompt, instruction planning probes the selected source's presence again unless the plan creates it.
Apply re-checks Git-managed status, lockfile presence and source absence at the mutation boundary.
The seeded alias and canonical source are byte-rechecked before the alias is replaced.
Instruction sync probes symbolic-link capability again at apply.
Non-preview setup runs plan and apply inside one workspace transaction holding the transition lock, and that transaction reads settings again under the lock.
setup-instruction-source.lifetime: Transferred rows are an independent copy for one apply inside the setup transaction and are released when it completes; the candidate read's source presence lives for one project configuration call, is consumed by its instruction planning and never reaches apply; the prepared settings live for one setup call; nothing is retained across invocations.

after-interactive-approval-setup-reads-r.basis: After an interactive approval, setup reads the recorded instruction rows again before any write, so an unreadable lockfile version refuses first.

candidate-instruction-source-content-rea.basis: The candidate instruction source content is read once at plan and passed to apply as the source content and seed.

setup-checks-git-management-plan-display.basis: Setup checks Git management at plan for display and again at apply before transient ignores, across an approval of unbounded length.
setup-checks-git-management-plan-display.openQuestion: Should setup approval freeze the Git-managed status observed at plan, or is the post-approval re-check at apply the contract?

setup-existing-project-decides-completio.basis: Setup on an existing project decides completion from one settings read and hands that value to initialization when no transaction follows; the apply that completes the choice keeps its fresh read under the lock.

setup-no-longer-runs-report-s.basis: Setup no longer runs the report's discarded Git-managed walk, and unattended setup hands its plan-time instruction rows to apply as an independent copy instead of re-reading the lockfile.

setup-reads-project-settings-through-own.basis: Setup reads the project settings through its own read model, for an existing project's instruction-choice decision or a new project's initialization check, after the setup workspace location construction has already read and decoded them, or found them absent, for the layout. The construction's read ends when its constructor returns and is never carried onto the location, and a new project's initialization check runs later under the transition lock, so a change made before the lock is never overwritten.

unattended-setup-plan-reuses-candidate-s.basis: When setup runs no source-selection prompt, as on unattended and preview runs or with an explicitly named source, instruction planning takes the selected source's presence from the candidate read the same planning call just made instead of probing the file again. After a selection prompt the source is probed live, and the apply-time source-absence check and instruction sync's own observation stay fresh.

after-source-selection-setup-probes-sour.basis: After an interactive source-selection prompt, which setup asks when no source is named and the interactive first-use setup that install and handoff run asks whenever instruction sync is on, instruction planning probes the selected source's presence again, unless the plan creates it, instead of taking it from the candidate read made before the prompt.
after-source-selection-setup-probes-sour.openQuestion: May interactive instruction planning take the selected source's presence from the candidate read made before the source-selection prompt?

source-scratch.resource: Scoped temporary directories outside the workspace in which sources are fetched, cloned, extracted, staged and captured.
source-scratch.publication: Directory tree: scoped temporary directories created per fetch, clone, capture or staged Knowledge package and removed by their scope finalizers.

reads.note: A fetched Registry archive, and the official AXM skill compatibility probe's archive, is hashed by the caller only when the client's evidence does not cover that exact buffer and integrity.
A retained canonical directory is re-hashed against its accepted tree integrity before it is reused instead of fetched.
A Git commit fetch compares the fetched package tree with the accepted tree.
Every HTTP artifact download is checked against its digest before it is staged.
An HTTP files inventory is validated once and each path decoded once; staging uses exactly the decoded paths.
Discover checks out each Git URL and revision once per call and shares the read-only checkout.
A Knowledge package is acquired into its own scoped scratch directory and inspected there before the transaction commits it.

list --outdated compares each Git-sourced entry's discovered commit and tree with its accepted resolution, discovering it through the Git provider in a scoped discovery checkout that the assessment shares per Git clone URL and revision.
A configured update sweep lists each Git clone URL's remote refs once and shares the frozen listing across the selectors its entries declare.
A Knowledge sync call restores its locked bundles from one shared read-only Git discovery checkout per clone URL and revision.
A repeat-install request or a Pack member expansion restoring members from accepted state retrieves each accepted Git commit or digest-pinned HTTP artifact once and shares the read-only directory.

One discovery walk lists each directory once for all its AXM manifests, resolves a directory without SKILL.md once for its plugin distribution and marketplace reads, and lets a marketplace root member reuse that directory's first distribution read.
A Codex plugin's skills walk resolves each visited directory once through its containment check, and the distribution read carries its resolved plugin root to plugin MCP discovery.
One convention discovery over a Git checkout reads the checked-out commit once and each package directory's tree once.
An HTTP find measures each acquired tree once, and the offer's convention discovery walks the observation that measure recorded.
A source-switch comparison of a non-Registry proposal with a Registry side replays its ignore walk's listing in the distribution tree digest of the same package root.
Source-switch classification fetches the proposed ref into new scratch and computes its tree integrity for the source-switch preview.
MCP install planning reads and decodes the source mcp.json, and an Agent Plugins connection's root mcp.json, in its own planning read phase after the selection phase's discovery decoded it.

source-scratch.existingSharing: A fetch under the workspace transition already consumed the tree the transition acquired before fetching again, and an accepted retained canonical directory whose tree still matches was reused instead of fetched. This change shares the client's Registry verification evidence, the decoded HTTP inventory paths, one successful Git checkout per URL and revision within discover, a configured update sweep, a list --outdated assessment or a Knowledge sync call, one remote ref listing per Git clone URL within a configured update sweep, and one retrieval of accepted commit or artifact content within a repeat-install request or a Pack member expansion. Within one discovery it shares a directory's listing across its AXM manifests, a plugin directory's resolved root, a marketplace root's first distribution read, the resolved path of each Codex skills directory, a Git checkout's commit and package tree reads, and an HTTP offer's measured tree observation, and one source-switch comparison replays its ignore walk's listing in the distribution tree digest.
source-scratch.preparedInputs: Registry fetches consume the client's verification evidence instead of hashing the archive again; an HTTP files offer decodes each inventory path once and stages exactly the decoded paths; discover shares one Git checkout per URL and revision within its call; a configured update sweep and one list --outdated assessment each share one successful Git discovery checkout per clone URL and revision across their entries, and each entry runs its own discovery on it. A configured update sweep lists each Git clone URL's remote refs once and hands the frozen listing to every entry whose declared Git source carries a selector, which assesses its own selector against it. One Knowledge sync call shares one successful read-only Git discovery checkout per clone URL and revision across the locked bundles its restore loop restores, and each bundle runs its own filtered discovery on it. A repeat-install request, or a Pack member expansion that restores members from accepted state, retrieves accepted content keyed by Git clone URL, transport context and commit, or by digest-pinned HTTP artifact snapshot, once and hands every later fetch of that key the same read-only directory, in which each fetch checks and selects its own package. Within one discovery walk, a directory's own listing serves the inspection of every AXM manifest it holds; a directory without SKILL.md has its real path resolved once, and that root bounds its plugin distribution read and its marketplace read; the plugin distribution read carries that root to portable plugin MCP discovery; a marketplace member at the marketplace root reuses the immutable record of what the directory's first distribution read observed; and each local marketplace member's distribution read is rooted at the physical path its own containment check resolved. Reading a Codex plugin's skills resolves each visited directory once, through its containment check, and that path keys the walk's cycle deduplication. One convention discovery over a Git checkout reads the checked-out commit once and each package directory's tree once, and every Git reference of that discovery carries that commit and its own package directory's tree. Finding an HTTP source hands each offer's convention discovery the immutable observation of the root's existence, directory listings and entry kinds that its tree measure recorded. When source-switch classification compares a non-Registry proposal with a Registry side, the distribution tree digest that walks the same resolved package root replays the listing its ignore observation kept of the fetched package.
freshChecks: The caller hashes the archive when the client gives no covering evidence.
Every Git commit fetch checks the fetched tree against the accepted tree.
Every HTTP download is checked against its digest.
A retained canonical directory is re-hashed before reuse.
A failed clone is not shared and is attempted again.
Each Git-sourced entry that list --outdated assesses compares its own discovered commit and tree against its accepted resolution.
A remote ref listing that awaited a failed or interrupted attempt makes its own unshared attempt.

Each Knowledge bundle a sync restores runs its own filtered discovery and its own commit and tree comparison against its lock entry, and the commit checks the prepared tree integrity before publishing.
A failed or interrupted retrieval of accepted content is not shared, and each fetch of shared HTTP artifact content checks that its own source path exists.
Every AXM manifest of a listed directory is still read and checked for an agents field, and the exported package inspection lists its directory itself.
Every manifest, marketplace member, skills root and SKILL.md keeps its own live resolution and containment check, in the same order.
Every directory and SKILL.md a Codex skills walk visits keeps its live containment and escape check.
The plugin MCP configuration is still probed, resolved, checked for escape, read and strictly decoded live.
A marketplace root member's selection-dependent derivations and the reads of every other member run live.
Each separate convention discovery reads its own checked-out commit, and a failed package tree read is not kept and fails the discovery.
HTTP discovery inspects live the paths its tree measure did not observe and its manifests, and runs its real-path containment checks live.
Every file a source-switch distribution digest includes is read live, contained-link validation resolves each link itself, and a directory missing from the retained listing is observed live.
MCP install planning from a local or Git source reads and decodes the source mcp.json, and an Agent Plugins connection's root mcp.json, again in its own planning read phase.
Source-switch classification fetches the proposed ref into new scratch to compute its tree integrity.
A configured Pack restored from accepted state fetches its own accepted commit or artifact outside the content its member expansion shares.
source-scratch.lifetime: Scratch directories and their contents are released by the scope that created them; a shared discover checkout lives in the scope of the request that first needed it and does not outlive discover; a shared update-sweep or list --outdated checkout is acquired in the scope that sweep or assessment runs in and released with that scope, the record of shared checkouts ends with that call, and a retry after a failed shared attempt lives in the retrying find's own scope. The remote ref listing service is provided by the configured update sweep call and released with it. A Knowledge sync call's shared checkout is held in that call's scope and released with it, so a sync preview and its apply each make their own. Shared accepted content is retrieved in the scope the repeat-install request or the Pack member expansion runs in and released with it. A directory's filtered listing, resolved plugin root and first distribution read record live for that directory's inspection, and a Codex skills walk's resolved paths live for that one distribution read. The commit read and the successful package tree reads of a convention discovery live only for that discovery call. An HTTP offer's tree observation lives for that offer's iteration, in the scope of its scratch directory, and the apply-time measure records none. The retained ignore listing lives for that one source-switch comparison.

configured-update-sweep-resolves-each-gi.basis: A configured update sweep shares one successful shallow discovery checkout per Git clone URL and ref across the entries that declare it, coalescing finds on an attempt in flight, while each entry keeps its own discovery walk, package path and plan. The shared checkout is acquired in the scope the sweep runs in and released with it, a failed or interrupted clone is not shared and is attempted again, and apply acquisition still fetches by commit and refuses a tree mismatch.

discover-shares-one-shallow-git-checkout.basis: Discover shares one shallow Git checkout per URL and revision across the package recommendations of one invocation, with each recommendation keeping its own filtered walk and failed clones not kept.

each-discovered-recommendation-walks-sha.basis: Each discovered recommendation walks the shared checkout with its own filter, because duplicate rejection, MCP parsing and marketplace names depend on the filter.

git-source-cloned-once-into-scoped.basis: A Git source is cloned once into scoped scratch for the whole command; a local source uses no scratch.

git-source-preparation-shallow-clones-re.basis: With a Git source, candidate preparation shallow-clones the repository into scoped scratch to discover the selected package, and apply acquisition fetches the selected commit again into new scratch and checks its package tree against the accepted tree before the package is published. That fetch-time check is the only validation of the published bytes against the remote, and the discovery checkout belongs to candidate preparation, which has ended; checked against that checkout, from which the accepted tree was derived, the check could no longer fail.
git-source-preparation-shallow-clones-re.openQuestion: May apply acquisition publish a Git package from the checkout candidate preparation discovered, although the accepted-tree check would then compare that checkout with the tree derived from it and could no longer fail, instead of fetching the selected commit again?

hook-install-planning-fetches-proposed-e.basis: Hook install planning fetches the proposed exact archive once for its projection and again for its configured-agent outcomes, and each fetch logs the version's lifecycle warnings.
hook-install-planning-fetches-proposed-e.openQuestion: May the hook install plan fetch the proposed exact archive once and pass its tree or manifest to its configured-agent outcomes, and if so should a warning-bearing version still log its lifecycle warning once per former fetch?

http-files-offer-validates-inventory-onc.basis: An HTTP files offer validates its inventory once, decodes each path once and stages exactly the decoded paths.

outdated-each-git-sourced-entry-compared.basis: One list --outdated assessment shares one successful shallow discovery checkout per Git clone URL and revision across the entries it assesses, coalescing finds on an attempt in flight, while each entry keeps its own discovery and its own commit and tree comparison against its accepted resolution. The shared checkout is acquired in the scope the assessment runs in and released with it, a failed or interrupted clone is not shared and each waiting entry attempts its own, and filters other than outdated do no Git work.

planning-fetches-exact-archive-end-their.basis: Planning fetches of an exact archive end with their scoped owner calls before confirmation, and apply acquires the same archive again under the lock, re-admitting and integrity-checking it at that boundary.

registry-fetch-accepts-client-s-verifica.basis: A Registry fetch accepts the client's verification evidence for the exact buffer it receives instead of hashing the archive again before extraction.

configured-update-sweep-lists-remote-ref.basis: A configured update sweep lists each Git clone URL's remote refs once across the entries whose declared Git source carries a selector, sharing the successful listing as a frozen copy through the remote ref listing service that the sweep call provides and releases with it. A listing that awaited a failed or interrupted attempt makes its own unshared attempt, each entry still assesses its own selector against the listing, and reinstalls, entries without a selector and callers outside the sweep list as before.

mcp-install-planning-decodes-source-mani.basis: MCP install planning from a local or Git source reads and decodes the source package's mcp.json in its own planning read phase after the selection phase's discovery decoded it to build the ref. The selection phase has ended before planning starts, so planning observes the source afresh, and its decode refuses an invalid manifest as an install validation failure where discovery fills a missing owner from the source workspace; the planning decode feeds distribution selection, binding requests and native target validation.
mcp-install-planning-decodes-source-mani.openQuestion: May MCP install planning decode the source mcp.json from the selection phase's discovery, which decodes it under the source workspace's default owner, instead of reading it again in its own planning read phase, accepting that discovered refs carry decoded manifests across the source and extension-kind contracts and across the selection-to-planning phase boundary?

source-switch-fetches-proposed-ref-durin.basis: When an install or update proposal leaves an accepted, usable source locator, source-switch classification fetches the proposed ref into new scratch to compute its tree integrity, although planning already retrieved the same content through discovery or, for a Registry Hook, through its projection fetch. That fetch refuses a remote that rejects the commit fetch, a tree mismatch or an integrity mismatch in the source-switch preview and logs a Registry version's lifecycle warnings, and the earlier retrievals belong to discovery or to scopes that have already ended.
source-switch-fetches-proposed-ref-durin.openQuestion: May source-switch classification compute the proposed tree integrity from content planning already retrieved (the Git discovery checkout at ref.location, the HTTP discovery download, or the Hook projection's Registry fetch) instead of fetching the proposed ref again, accepting that a remote refusing commit fetches or a fetched tree or integrity mismatch would be refused only at apply, not in the source-switch preview, and that a warning-bearing Registry version would log its lifecycle warnings once fewer?

discovery-walk-lists-each-manifest-packa.basis: Within one discovery walk, the walk's own listing of a directory serves the inspection of every AXM manifest that directory holds, so a manifest package directory is listed once however many manifests it holds; the filtered copy lives for that directory's inspection and is never mutated. Each manifest is still read and checked for an agents field, and the exported package inspection still lists its directory itself with its own refusals.

codex-skill-walk-resolves-each-directory.basis: Reading a Codex plugin's skills resolves each visited directory's real path once, through its containment check, and that resolved path keys the walk's cycle deduplication for that one distribution read. The skills root is first contained in the walk's first iteration, every directory and SKILL.md keeps its live containment and escape check, and the other plugin formats keep their single containment check of each skills root.

plugin-mcp-check-reuses-resolved-plugin-.basis: The plugin distribution read carries the plugin root it resolved, and portable plugin MCP discovery checks the MCP configuration against that root within the same directory inspection or marketplace-member iteration instead of resolving the root again. The MCP configuration is still probed, resolved, checked for escape, read and strictly decoded live.

git-convention-discovery-reads-checkout-.basis: One convention discovery over a Git checkout reads the checked-out commit once, when the first discovered extension needs it after its tree read, and every Git reference of that discovery carries it; the cached read lives only for that discovery call. Local sources and discoveries with no candidates read no commit, and each separate discovery, such as each entry list --outdated assesses, still reads its own.

git-convention-discovery-reads-each-pack.basis: One convention discovery over a Git checkout reads each package directory's tree once and reuses it for every component of that package, such as each skill or MCP server of one plugin; only successful reads are kept, as strings keyed by repository-relative directory, for that discovery call. A failed read is not kept and fails the discovery as before, and apply acquisition still fetches by commit and checks the accepted tree.

plugin-mcp-install-planning-reads-defini.basis: MCP install planning of an Agent Plugins connection from a local or Git source resolves, reads and decodes the plugin's root mcp.json again in its own planning read phase after the selection phase's discovery read and decoded it to list the plugin's servers. The selection phase has ended before planning starts, so planning observes the file afresh and refuses an escaping, unreadable or invalid configuration as an MCP configuration failure where discovery reports the source as not resolvable; the planning decode feeds native target validation.

knowledge-sync-restores-share-one-git-di.basis: One Knowledge sync call shares one successful read-only Git discovery checkout per clone URL and revision across the locked bundles its restore loop restores, held in that call's scope and released with it, so a sync preview and its apply each make their own. Each bundle still runs its own filtered discovery, its own commit and tree comparison against its lock entry, its own staging and inspection, and the commit still checks the prepared tree integrity before publishing; a failed or interrupted clone is not shared and is attempted again.

accepted-entries-share-one-commit-or-art.basis: Within one repeat-install request, or one Pack member expansion that restores members from accepted state in an ambient scope, a fetch of accepted content keyed by the same Git clone URL, transport context and commit, or by the same digest-pinned HTTP artifact snapshot, retrieves it once in the scope that request or expansion runs in and hands every later fetch of that key the same read-only directory. Each fetch still checks its own package tree against the accepted tree, or checks that its own source path exists, with the same refusals, and a failed or interrupted retrieval is not shared.

pack-own-accepted-fetch-stays-outside-me.basis: A configured Pack restored from accepted state fetches its own accepted commit or artifact when its canonical tree is missing, before its member expansion starts and outside the content that expansion shares across its members, so a Pack whose members were accepted from the same commit or artifact retrieves it once for the Pack and once more for its members. Each retrieval checks its own package tree or source path.
pack-own-accepted-fetch-stays-outside-me.openQuestion: May the accepted fetch of a configured Pack's own content share its retrieval with the member expansion that follows, so that one retrieval serves the Pack and every member accepted from the same commit or artifact, although the shared content would then have to live in a scope that spans both the Pack's resolution and its expansion?

plugin-directory-root-resolved-once-per-.basis: Within one discovery walk, a directory without SKILL.md has its real path resolved once after its listing, with the same refusal, and that resolved root bounds both its plugin distribution read and its marketplace read; each local marketplace member's distribution read is rooted at the physical path the member's own containment check resolved. Every manifest, member, skills root and SKILL.md keeps its own live resolution and containment check, in the same order.

marketplace-root-member-reuses-root-dist.basis: When a marketplace lists its own root as a member, that member's distribution read reuses what the directory's first distribution read in the same inspection observed: its manifest probes, reads and decodes and its skills-root probes and listings, held as an immutable record that lives for that one directory's inspection. Selection-dependent derivations, roots and formats the first read did not reach, and the reads of every other member still run live in the same order with the same refusals.

http-find-discovery-walks-measured-tree-.basis: Finding an HTTP source measures each acquired tree once, with the same limits, link containment checks and failure order, and hands that offer's convention discovery an immutable observation of the root's existence, directory listings and entry kinds, so discovery does not list, link-probe or stat the measured entries again; the observation lives for that offer's iteration, in the scope of its scratch directory. Paths the measure did not observe, manifests and real-path containment checks are still inspected live, and the apply-time measure counts the tree without recording an observation.

source-switch-proposed-digest-replays-ig.basis: When source-switch classification compares a non-Registry proposal with a Registry side and discovers the proposal's ignore inputs, the ignore observation keeps its listing of the fetched package only when the distribution tree digest that follows walks the same resolved package root, and that one comparison replays the listing's directory names, link targets, entry kinds and modes instead of listing, link-probing and stating the tree again. Every included file is still read live, contained-link validation still resolves each link itself, the ignore inputs keep their own checks and refusals, and any directory missing from the listing is observed live.

subagent-sync.resource: Rendered native Subagent files in each agent's subagent directory; one physical file may serve several reader aliases.
subagent-sync.publication: Per physical file under its exclusive write: live re-resolution of every claimant, one read of the prior bytes, the owner's write decision, created-directory capture, rollback protection, parent creation and an identity-preserving write recorded as created or modified; removal re-admits the file, reads its bytes for the owner's removal decision, protects, removes, records and retires created directories.

reads.note: Under the lock every claimant path is re-resolved; an alias retargeted since planning or a non-file entry is a conflict.
One read of the prior bytes under the lock feeds the owner's write decision (record an equal unrecorded file, refuse a differing one) and the change label.
The write authority protects the file before writing or removing it.
Removal re-admits the file under the lock and reads its bytes so the owner's decision retains modified or unowned files.

The Subagent manager's projection observation reads the package once per owner call and compiles the native file once while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased; separate owner calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase read and compile it again.

The refusing destination preflight reads the bytes at every planned native destination to refuse an unrecorded file that differs from the render; a non-Registry materialization's validation of a kept or in-place canonical tree judges from the bytes its source validation read, and a validating projection observation's write judgment decides from the bytes its preflight read while its read phase holds.

Within one projection observation each spelling of every planned file is probed for existence once while its currency is judged, and the write judgment of a file with a recorded projection row reuses that presence, probing again only for a file the probe did not reach or once the read phase has ended, and reads bytes only for a file without a current recorded row; a preview or an inspection makes one such observation per Subagent and writes nothing.

Within one projection observation each planned output's containment comes from its destination preflight's assertion, and every planned output and its readers are located in one native location capture taken at the first output while the read phase holds; an output reached after that phase ends is located live.

One setup report's subagent listing checks the existence of each distinct project subagent location, keyed by its shape and resolved path, once and, for a directory, lists it and stats its entries once, then builds each declaring agent's file list from that scan.

subagent-sync.existingSharing: Prepared rendered bytes are published once per physical file with live claimant re-resolution and a single prior read under the lock; nothing repeated inside this owner's publication. One Subagent manager call now takes its prepared targets and planned files from its destination preflight and the existence of each planned file from its currency probe instead of preparing, planning and probing again; a projection observation also takes each planned output's destination from the containment its destination preflight asserted and locates every planned output and its readers in one native location capture, and one that validates its destinations makes its write judgment from the bytes its refusing preflight read; a non-Registry materialization judges a kept or in-place canonical tree from the bytes its source validation read; a lint run evaluates the projection invariant facts, with each enabled Subagent's projection observation, once per observation read phase; and one setup report's subagent listing scans each distinct project subagent location once for every agent that declares it.
subagent-sync.preparedInputs: Within one Subagent manager call, the targets its destination preflight returns serve that call's configured-agent outcomes or projection observation, and in a projection observation the planned files it returns serve the rest of that observation. Within one projection observation, the presence its currency probe observed for each planned physical file answers the write judgment of a file with a recorded projection row. Within one projection observation, the destination its destination preflight asserted for each planned output answers that output's containment, and the native location capture taken at its first output supplies the readers and location set for every planned output's native location outcome. Within one projection observation that validates its destinations, the bytes its refusing destination preflight read at each planned native file answer the write judgment of a file without a current recorded row when that judgment reads through the preflight's file system. Within one non-Registry Subagent materialization, the bytes its source validation reads at each planned native destination answer a later validation of the canonical path itself when acquisition keeps a cache-hit or retained-binding tree or acquires the source in place. The exclusive write accepts each physical file's rendered bytes, bindings and write decision from the plan of the materialization's validation preflight. Within one lint observation read phase, the frozen projection invariant facts of the first evaluation completed inside that phase answer every later rule that reads them. Within one setup report's subagent listing, the scan of each distinct project subagent location, made by the first agent in registry order that declares it, answers every agent that declares that location with a newly built file list.
freshChecks: Claimant re-resolution under the lock before every write.
The prior read and the owner's write decision under the lock.
Created-directory capture and record, rollback protection and footprint record per write.
Removal re-admission, byte read and removal decision under the lock.

The refusing destination preflight reads every planned native file and refuses an unrecorded file that differs from the render before anything is reported or written, except that a non-Registry materialization's validation of a kept or in-place canonical tree judges from the bytes its source validation read.

The validation of a staged Subagent copy, of a Registry or workspace ref, or under an external reuse request reads every planned native destination live, and any validation reads live a destination its source validation did not plan.

Once the read phase captured at a manager call's start has ended, the call prepares again on live state, and a projection observation also plans again and probes each planned file with a recorded projection row again for its write judgment.
A lint demand for projection invariant facts after its read phase ended evaluates them, with each Subagent projection observation, live.

A projection observation locates live every planned output it reaches after its read phase has ended, and asserts that output's containment again unless its plan was itself made after that phase ended.
The write judgment of a validating projection observation reads the planned file live once its read phase has ended or when it reads through a file system other than its preflight's.
A later setup report's subagent listing scans every project subagent location again, and the single-agent scanAgentSubagentFiles scans its location directly.
subagent-sync.lifetime: The caller's rendered bytes and decision callbacks are used within one call under the exclusive write; nothing is transferred to another owner or retained after the call. The preflight's targets and planned files and the observation's probed presence are created inside one Subagent manager call, used only while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased, and released when the call returns. The refusing preflight's bytes, the output destinations the preflight's plan asserted and the native location capture are created inside one projection observation, used only while the read phase in which they were observed is active or the call is unphased, and released when the call returns. The source-validation bytes and the validation preflight's plan are created inside one materialization call and released when that call returns. The frozen projection invariant facts are created by the lint run's first evaluation inside its observation read phase, reused only while that phase stays the same active phase, and released when the lint run returns. The shared subagent location scans are created inside one scanAllSubagentFiles call of a setup report and released when that call returns.

adding-coding-agents-runs-subagent-proje.basis: Adding coding agents runs the Subagent projection observation of each installed Subagent for the detailed inventory's current configured-agent outcomes and again for the resulting membership while judging its materialization currency, reading the package and compiling its native outputs in each call, with no write between them. The two calls judge different agent sets, possibly from separately resolved refs and source roots, so one observation cannot answer both, and sharing the package read and compile for the agents common to both would need a physical read phase in planning that the accepted read-phase bounds do not provide.
adding-coding-agents-runs-subagent-proje.openQuestion: May agents add planning reuse one read and compile of an installed Subagent's package across the inventory observation for the current configured agents and the currency observation for the resulting membership, although the two manager calls share no physical read phase that could own that value?

check-s-inspection-projection-invariant-.basis: Check's inspection, its projection invariant facts and its convergence assessment each take their own projection observation of a selected Subagent's native files. Each owner resolves the Subagent ref, the configured agents and the source root independently and handles an observation failure differently, and the check assessment view re-verifies the later owners' reads, so the accepted requirements do not decide that the three observations are one equivalent read.
check-s-inspection-projection-invariant-.openQuestion: May check answer its inspection, projection invariant facts and convergence currency from one Subagent projection observation per subagent within its assessment phase, although each owner resolves the ref, configured agents and source root independently, handles an observation failure differently, and the assessment view deliberately re-verifies later owners' reads?

each-subagent-projection-observation-pro.basis: Each Subagent projection observation probes each spelling of every planned native file for existence once while judging its native location's currency, and decides what a reconciliation would write for a file with a recorded projection row from that presence, keyed by the file's physical destination. The presence belongs to the one call and answers only while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased; once that phase has ended each recorded file is probed again on live state, and the exclusive write still re-resolves every claimant and reads the prior bytes under the lock.

lint-run-live-workspace-each-rule.basis: A lint run of the live workspace evaluates the projection invariant facts, and with them each enabled Subagent's projection observation, once per lint observation read phase and hands the same frozen facts to every rule that reads them. The lint run reuses them only while that read phase is still the same active phase, so a demand after the phase ended evaluates live and facts whose evaluation outlived the phase are not kept, and lint --fix plans its repair under its own lock.

one-subagent-manager-call-runs-destinati.basis: The configured-agent outcomes of install planning with destination validation prepare each configured agent's native Subagent implementation once, compiling it and reading any bound package resource in the destination preflight, and report from the targets that preflight returns. The targets belong to that one call and serve it only while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased; once that phase has ended the call prepares again on live state, and the preflight keeps its misconfigured refusal, its reads of planned native files that refuse an unrecorded file and its error mapping.

one-subagent-projection-observation-prep.basis: One Subagent projection observation prepares and renders each configured agent's native implementation and derives the planned files, their containment and their generations once, in its report-mode destination preflight, and judges currency from the targets and planned files that preflight returns. Each value belongs to that one call and is checked separately against the read phase captured at its start; once that phase has ended the call prepares and plans again on live state, and the preflight keeps its misconfigured refusal and its error mapping.

one-subagent-projection-observation-prob.basis: One Subagent projection observation probes each planned native file for existence once: the Subagent manager's projection observation keeps, for the length of the call, the presence its currency probe observes for each planned physical path, and the write judgment of a file with a recorded projection row uses that presence. A file the currency probe did not reach, or any file once the read phase observed at the start of the call has ended, is probed again, and the exclusive write still re-resolves each claimant and reads its prior bytes under the lock.

preview-observes-each-planned-native-sub.basis: A preview observes each planned native Subagent file in one Subagent manager call per subagent and writes nothing.

rendered-subagent-bytes-published-once-p.basis: Rendered Subagent bytes are published once per physical file after one prior read under the lock, with live claimant re-resolution.

separate-subagent-manager-calls-inside-m.basis: Separate Subagent manager calls inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase each read and compile the native Subagent file.
separate-subagent-manager-calls-inside-m.openQuestion: May an owner-call dry-run preimage map share native file bytes inside a mutation's document-only prepare phase?

subagent-install-update-planning-reads-e.basis: Subagent install and update planning reads every planned native Subagent file to refuse an unrecorded differing file before confirmation, and the materialization under the transition lock reads each of those files again before it writes them. The planning read belongs to a read phase that ends before the confirmation and the wait for the lock, so the read under the lock is the fresh refusal and write decision that judges the bytes about to be replaced.

subagent-manager-call-checks-native-dest.basis: A Subagent manager call that checks its native destinations takes each configured agent's compiled and bound targets, and in a projection observation the planned files, from the destination preflight it runs instead of compiling, binding, resolving and planning them again for its own result. These values belong to that one call and serve it only while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased; once that phase has ended the call prepares and plans again on live state, and the preflight keeps its position, its misconfigured refusal and its error mapping.

validated-observation-prepares-in-its-re.basis: A Subagent projection observation that validates its destinations, as the authored native projection of an enabled authored Subagent does, takes each configured agent's prepared targets and planned native files from its refusing destination preflight and runs no reporting preflight after it; an observation that does not validate runs the reporting preflight as before. The preparation and plan belong to that one call and serve it only while the read phase captured at its start is active or the call is unphased, and an unrecorded differing file still refuses before anything is reported.

subagent-materialization-s-validation-pr.basis: A non-Registry Subagent materialization's source validation keeps the bytes it reads at each planned native destination before acquisition, and a later validation of the canonical path itself, when acquisition keeps a cache-hit or retained-binding tree or acquires the source in place, judges those destinations from the kept bytes while it still loads, compiles, plans and decides each one. The kept bytes belong to the one materialization call and are released when it returns; a staged copy, a destination only the canonical plan names, an external reuse request and Registry or workspace refs read fresh, and the exclusive write still re-resolves and reads every destination under its lock.

staged-subagent-copy-validation-rereads-.basis: A staged non-Registry Subagent install or update reads every planned native destination in its source validation before acquisition and again in the validation of its staging copy, and the exclusive write reads each once more as its publication prior. Between the two validations AXM's own recovery of an interrupted replacement, parent creation and staging copy can change a destination that resolves into the package's staging, backup or canonical tree, so judging the staged copy from the earlier bytes would move a SubagentNativeConflict projection-output-unrecorded refusal from before canonical promotion to the exclusive write after it, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
staged-subagent-copy-validation-rereads-.openQuestion: May the staged second validation of a non-Registry Subagent materialization judge each native destination from the bytes the pre-acquisition validation read, although AXM's own recovery, parent creation and staging copy between the passes change those bytes when a destination resolves into the package's own staging, backup or canonical tree, so that an unrecorded-file refusal moves from SubagentNativeConflict projection-output-unrecorded before canonical promotion to a SubagentIoFailed or conflict at the exclusive write after promotion?

when-authored-subagent-enabled-authored-.basis: When an authored Subagent is enabled, the authored native preflight under the lock, the materialization's validation preflight and the exclusive write each read every planned native Subagent file. The authored preflight refuses an unrecorded file from the staged package's render before the scaffold and authored-marking writes; the validation preflight runs after those writes against the render of the canonical package they produced and is the last refusal of an unrecorded differing file, with its unrecorded-output problem, before any native file is written. The exclusive write's prior read is the per-file conflict check under the file lock; the accepted requirements demand that an unrecorded differing file is refused but not which of these checks refuses it.
when-authored-subagent-enabled-authored-.openQuestion: May an enabled authored Subagent leave an unrecorded differing native file that the authored preflight did not see to the exclusive write's conflict decision, which refuses it as an invalid definition without the unrecorded-output problem after other planned files may already be written and rolled back, instead of refusing it in the materialization's validation preflight before any native write?

withdrawing-recorded-subagent-file-resol.basis: Withdrawing a recorded Subagent file resolves its native entry in the agent output inventory, in the native location capture of the removal target, before taking the file's exclusive write and again under it, and the write authority's protection admits it before the removal, with no write to that file between them. The resolution before the exclusive write refuses an escaping, dangling or workspace-conflicting route as an unsafe Subagent removal before any lock, which the native location capture does not check, and the capture is taken before the earlier removals of the same withdrawal. Deciding the route from the capture therefore changes the failure and the exclusive-write key of a non-contained route, while the resolution under the exclusive write and the protection's admission stay as fresh checks.
withdrawing-recorded-subagent-file-resol.openQuestion: May a Subagent file withdrawal take its removal route and exclusive-write key from the pre-removal native location capture, which does not check native-root containment, accepting that a non-contained or dangling recorded route then fails under the exclusive write with that check's message instead of before the lock?

setup-report-scans-each-shared-subagent-.basis: One setup report's subagent listing scans each distinct project subagent location, keyed by its shape and resolved path, once: the first declaring agent in registry order owns the existence check, directory listing and entry stats and names a scan failure, and every agent that declares the location receives a newly built file list from that scan. The shared scan lives for that one scanAllSubagentFiles call, so a later call scans every location again, and the single-agent scanAgentSubagentFiles still scans its location directly.

validated-observation-judges-writes-from.basis: A Subagent projection observation that validates its destinations keeps, for the length of the call, the bytes its refusing destination preflight read at each planned native file, and its write judgment decides from those bytes instead of reading the file again. The bytes serve the judgment only while the read phase captured at the start of the call is active or the call is unphased, and only when the judgment reads through the preflight's own file system; otherwise the file is read live, and the exclusive write still reads its prior bytes under the lock.

projection-observation-takes-output-dest.basis: One Subagent projection observation takes each planned output's destination from the containment its destination preflight asserted, and locates every planned output and its readers in one native location capture taken at the first output, instead of asserting containment and capturing every reader again for each output. Both serve the call only while the read phase in which they were observed is active or the call is unphased; an output reached after that phase ends is asserted and located live, and the exclusive write still re-resolves every claimant under the lock.

projection-observation-inventories-subag.basis: One Subagent projection observation inventories every Subagent container through the agent output inventory to find recorded files of the Subagent outside its plan, after its native location capture has already resolved the same subagent read locations; the inventory classifies ownership from its own resolutions.
projection-observation-inventories-subag.openQuestion: May a Subagent projection observation find its recorded files outside the plan from the subagent read-location resolutions its native location capture made in the same read phase, instead of resolving every Subagent container again in the agent output inventory?

telemetry-identity.publication: A staged identity file written create-only and linked into place create-only; the staged name is removed.

reads.note: The persisted identity is read and validated once per telemetry client.
When the create-only link finds an identity already in place, the concurrent winner is read and adopted.

telemetry-identity.existingSharing: The telemetry client loads the identity once into a deferred value that every send awaits.
freshChecks: The identity is linked create-only, and an already-existing identity is re-read and adopted.
An identity file that holds no identity is never repaired; the client reports without one.
telemetry-identity.lifetime: The deferred identity lives for the invocation's telemetry client and is released with it.

telemetry-client-loads-installation-iden.basis: The telemetry client loads the installation identity once into a deferred value that every send of the invocation awaits.

terminal-diagnostics.resource: ~/.axm/diagnostics/<eventId>.json failure records, retained up to 20 records and 7 days.
terminal-diagnostics.publication: Atomic 0600 replacement of one diagnostic record after ensuring the directory at 0700, then removal of records beyond retention.

reads.note: On the Node dist layout, a built file's inline source map is read and parsed to map AXM-owned frames; one frame collection parses each built file once.
After each record publication, the retention sweep lists the directory and stats each record.
Each record publication encodes the record's text to bytes once, in its atomic write; the size bound counts bytes without allocating them, so the encode is a single execution.

terminal-diagnostics.existingSharing: A later prepare in the same invocation reuses the previous record's event id, occurrence time and causes; each prepare collects its frames again.
terminal-diagnostics.preparedInputs: Within one frame collection, each built file's parsed inline source map, or its deterministic unavailability, serves every frame in that file; the record's byte length is measured without encoding it.
freshChecks: Each prepare collects its frames again, and failed reads are never memoized.
The directory is created and restricted to 0700 before every record publication.
Retention is enforced after every publication.
An in-process single-permit semaphore serializes prepares; there is no filesystem lock.
terminal-diagnostics.lifetime: The source-map memo is local to one frame collection and released when it returns; the current record lives in the process-scoped diagnostics layer.

diagnostics-directory-created-restricted.basis: The diagnostics directory is created and restricted to 0700 before every record publication, so a directory removed between two publications is recreated.

each-diagnostic-prepare-failing-invocati.basis: Each diagnostic prepare of a failing invocation collects its source frames again, resolving the package roots again and, on the Node dist layout, re-reading the built files it needs.
each-diagnostic-prepare-failing-invocati.openQuestion: May terminal-diagnostic source frames be derived once per invocation and reused by later prepares as a pure derivation of the running build, instead of once per prepare?

failure-record-s-byte-length-measured.basis: A failure record's byte length is measured without encoding candidate record strings; only the publication encodes it.

finalization-prepare-appends-request-mat.basis: The finalization prepare appends request-matched remembered causes to the previous record's causes again, so a cause can be recorded and framed twice.
finalization-prepare-appends-request-mat.openQuestion: Should the finalization prepare of a failure record skip remembered causes the record already holds?

one-frame-collection-parses-each-built.basis: One frame collection parses each built file's inline source map once and serves every frame in that file.

retention-sweep-lists-diagnostics-direct.basis: The retention sweep lists the diagnostics directory and stats each record after every record publication, including the finalization rewrite.
retention-sweep-lists-diagnostics-direct.openQuestion: Must the 20-record, 7-day diagnostics bound hold after every record publication, or is a transient 21st record after the invocation's own record was evicted acceptable?

token-resolution.resource: The credential an invocation presents to a Registry: AXM_TOKEN, the file AXM_TOKEN_FILE names, a GitHub Actions identity exchanged for a workload token, or the Registry's stored session.

reads.note: Each explicit-token resolution for the default Registry reads the file AXM_TOKEN_FILE names and refuses it when unreadable or empty instead of falling through to another source.

A signed-in check (requireSignedIn, currentToken or the offline isSignedIn) resolves the credential before any request, so a command that then sends Registry requests resolves it again for each of them.
Each authorized request and each authority probe resolves the presented credential again; a credential that disappears after one was presented fails the operation instead of continuing anonymously.
A GitHub Actions identity is exchanged once per invocation and default Registry; later resolutions present the held workload token and a rejected one is never renewed.
A Registry other than the settings-selected default, or a default with no ambient source, is offered only its own stored session, loaded through the credential store's per-origin memo.

token-resolution.existingSharing: A GitHub Actions identity is exchanged at most once per invocation and Registry through the workload credential cache, a stored session comes from the credential store's per-origin memo, and the runtime decides the ambient source kind once per invocation from environment variables without reading the token file.
freshChecks: Each resolution re-reads the file AXM_TOKEN_FILE names: once per signed-in check, once per authorized request and once per authority probe.
A credential that is no longer available after one was presented fails the operation rather than reading anonymously.
A workload token the Registry rejects is never renewed.
