token-resolution.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; the workload token cache and the per-Registry authority observations live as long as the invocation's layer.

axm-token-file-set-each-signed.basis: With AXM_TOKEN_FILE set, each signed-in check, authorized request and authority probe for the default Registry reads the token file again.
axm-token-file-set-each-signed.openQuestion: May an invocation fix its AXM_TOKEN_FILE credential at first resolution for every signed-in check, authorized request and authority probe, or must each observe the file?

github-actions-identity-exchanged-worklo.basis: A GitHub Actions identity is exchanged for a workload token once per invocation for the default Registry through a cache keyed by Registry origin and identity, and every later signed-in check and authorized request to that Registry presents the held workload token instead of exchanging again.

only-identity-check-existing-session-res.basis: Only the identity check of an existing session resolves the presented credential; the identity read for a new session names its token directly, so no credential source is read twice.

token-show-resolves-credential-once-send.basis: Token show resolves the credential once and sends no authorized request, so an AXM_TOKEN_FILE is read once.

yanking-unyanking-sends-one-remote-write.basis: Yanking or unyanking sends one remote write that is never replayed and runs no signed-in check, so the presented credential is resolved once and a token file named by AXM_TOKEN_FILE is read once.

trace-receipt.resource: The local trace receipt file AXM_TRACE_RECEIPT names, created by this invocation.
trace-receipt.publication: Identity-preserving write: an exclusively created receipt rewritten in place from offset zero and truncated to the document's length.
trace-receipt.existingSharing: None before prepared inputs were shared: every receipt write rewrote the file.
trace-receipt.preparedInputs: The last completely persisted receipt document; a rewrite identical to it is skipped.
freshChecks: The receipt is opened create-only and only this invocation's writer writes its handle.
A failed, short, timed-out or dropped write never updates the remembered document, so the next write runs.
Each write is bounded by a short deadline, and a writer that misses it retires.
trace-receipt.lifetime: The writer retains the last persisted document for the invocation and releases it when the receipt closes.

capture-enabled-each-receipt-write-persi.basis: With capture enabled, each receipt write persists a different completion snapshot.

trace-receipt-rewrite-identical-last-com.basis: A trace receipt rewrite identical to the last completely persisted document is skipped.

transition-lock.resource: Lock directories with a holder.json record: the workspace .axm/tmp/workspace-transition.lock and the coordination namespace's admission and lease locks.
transition-lock.publication: Directory tree: an exclusively created lock directory with a holder placeholder, then the owner-token stamp; removed on release only after an exact token match.

reads.note: Holder token read before release and again after a refused release; holder read for the contention report.
The scratch directory is recreated and proven before every acquisition attempt, since the previous holder may have removed it.

At acquisition the container receipts in the lock's directory are read and matching created-directory proofs adopted for empty-only removal; coordination locks read them too, though nothing writes them there.

transition-lock.existingSharing: Every observed lock adapter shares proper-lockfile's private mtime-precision state, so later acquisitions add no precision probe.
freshChecks: Exclusive lock-directory creation per attempt.
Scratch-directory proof per attempt.
Exact token match before release.
Receipt adoption at every acquisition.
transition-lock.lifetime: No value is transferred between owners; a hold's registry entry and created-directory proofs live for the acquisition's scope.

each-boundary-coordination-lock-acquisit.basis: Each boundary-coordination lock acquisition (admission, lease and liveness contender) reads and adopts the recorded runtime-directory receipts in the lock's directory, as every transition lock does.
each-boundary-coordination-lock-acquisit.openQuestion: May the boundary-coordination transition locks skip recorded-runtime-directory adoption, so that a receipt store planted in the private coordination namespace is ignored instead of decoded, refused when invalid, or adopted?

each-hold-established-holder-placeholder.basis: Each hold is established by a holder placeholder and token stamp and released only after the holder token read back matches.

every-lock-acquisition-attempt-recreates.basis: Every lock acquisition attempt recreates and proves the scratch directory, because the previous holder may have removed it on release.

update-check-cache.resource: The update-check cache document (axm.update-check-cache/v3) under the user's AXM home.
update-check-cache.publication: Atomic replacement after a startup refresh, or after upgrade resolves the latest distribution release.

reads.note: The startup check reads the cache once through a read-if-present read; absent, invalid or superseded content reads as no cache.
A startup refresh writes the cache once after a new network discovery and reads nothing; the write publishes different content and is a single execution.

update-check-cache.existingSharing: The startup check read the cache once per invocation.
update-check-cache.preparedInputs: The cache text, read once by a read-if-present read instead of an existence probe followed by a read; it stays inside the startup check.
freshChecks: No lock: the read is a best-effort snapshot of a document replaced only by atomic rename.
A read failure other than absence is reported as an unavailable update check, which the startup check does not show.
The upgrade command skips the startup check and writes the cache only after resolving the latest distribution release, without reading it.
update-check-cache.lifetime: The text is released when the startup check returns; nothing is retained across invocations.

startup-update-check-reads-cache-once.basis: The startup update check reads the cache once through a read-if-present read instead of an existence probe followed by a read.

workspace-location.resource: The selected workspace's physical location, layout and native directory inputs, resolved from the project and user settings and the selected lockfile when the workspace layer is built.

reads.note: Resolves the selected workspace root to its physical location before anything else is read.
Selected scope's settings for the initialization gate, through the construction-owned loader that the layout read reuses.
Selected lockfile for the newer-version refusal (also beside first-use initial settings), read once per construction through the same loader.
Project and user settings for the layout, one loader per logical scope, so coincident runtime directories keep distinct documents.
Each loader read probes existence, then reads and strictly decodes the document once.
Native directory overrides captured once at the workspace boundary and shared with readers and writers.

Each existing authored root is checked with an existence probe, an lstat and its own fresh real path against the project root's real path, which is resolved once per layout resolution call, after construction already resolved the selected root to its physical location.

workspace-location.existingSharing: Each loader caches its document's bytes and decode for its own lifetime, and readers inside a read phase share the phase's loaders; before prepared inputs were shared, the initialization gate and the layout each built their own loader, so an initialized construction read the selected settings twice and, beside first-use initial settings, the lockfile twice; project layout resolution now resolves the project root's real path once per call instead of once per existing authored root.
workspace-location.preparedInputs: One lazily built loader per logical scope serves the initialization gate, the newer-lockfile refusal and the layout read of one construction, so each settings document and the selected lockfile are read and decoded at most once per construction; the decoded project and user settings are returned with the location, and Registry selection builds its snapshot from them. Each project layout resolution call resolves the project root's real path once, at its first existing authored root and falling back to the resolved path when that fails, and its containment checks compare every existing authored root against that one value.
freshChecks: Readers of the constructed location read their documents fresh or through their own read phase; construction loaders are never placed on the location service, a phase or module scope.
Absent selected settings still fail as an uninitialized workspace, and a newer lockfile beside absent settings is still refused first.
Project and user documents stay distinct when both runtime directories coincide.
Uninitialized-allowed constructions read only the layout documents, once each, as they did before.
Project layout resolution checks the containment of each existing authored root against the project real path of that layout resolution call, not against the physical location construction resolved.
Each existing authored root keeps its own existence probe, lstat, fresh real path and containment check, in the same order.
workspace-location.lifetime: The construction loaders and their decoded documents are local to one location construction and are released when the constructor returns. The project real path of a layout resolution is created lazily inside that call and released when the call returns.

location-construction-serves-initializat.basis: Location construction serves the initialization gate, the newer-lockfile refusal and the layout from one loader per logical scope, so each settings document and the selected lockfile are read and decoded at most once per construction.

project-layout-resolution-resolves-proje.basis: Each project layout resolution call resolves the project root's real path once, lazily at its first existing authored root and falling back to the resolved path on failure, and compares every existing authored root of that call against it; the value lives only for that call. Each root keeps its own existence probe, lstat, fresh real path and containment check in the same order.

layout-resolves-project-real-path-beside.basis: Project layout resolution checks authored-root containment against a real path of the project root resolved within the layout call, after location construction already resolved the project root to its physical location. Construction's native-referent resolution spells paths differently, fails hard instead of falling back and resolves the user home for user-scope constructions, and read-model layout resolutions run in later phases, so substituting it is not decided by the accepted requirements.
layout-resolves-project-real-path-beside.openQuestion: May project layout resolution check authored-root containment against the physical project location that workspace location construction resolved with resolveNativeReferent, instead of an fs.realPath of the project root resolved within the layout call, accepting any spelling or failure-mode differences between the two primitives?

project-layout-validation-checks-each-au.basis: Project layout validation checks that each authored root exists and then lstats the same path, because the existence probe follows links, so a root that does not resolve, a dangling symlink included, counts as absent, while the lstat requires an existing root to be a directory that is not a symlink. One lstat would refuse dangling or looping symlink roots and change the failure message and cause for inaccessible roots, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
project-layout-validation-checks-each-au.openQuestion: May project layout validation decide each authored root's absence and type from one lstat, so that a dangling or looping symlink root is refused as a symlink root instead of treated as absent or reported as an inspection failure, and an inaccessible root's failure carries the lstat cause instead of the existence probe's?

project-scope-selected-lint-read-model.basis: With the project scope selected, the lint read model resolves the project layout again from the settings it reads, probing, inspecting, resolving and listing each authored root that workspace location construction already validated. Lint judges its own selected root and filesystem view, construction's observation ends before lint's observation phase, and the lint read model turns a layout failure into the scanner-io finding that lint reports.

project-scope-selected-read-model-read.basis: With the project scope selected, the read model that a read phase builds for inventory rows resolves the project layout again from the phase settings, probing, inspecting, resolving and listing each authored root that workspace location construction already validated. That validation observes mutable authored-root state, construction's observation ends before the phase begins, and the phase's own validation decides the workspace-layout diagnostic that stops canonical scanning.

workspace-location-construction-resolves.basis: Workspace location construction resolves its project root again as its own validity boundary instead of reusing the execution directory's start-of-process spelling.

workspace-read-views.resource: Phase-scoped observations of workspace documents (settings, lockfile, Pack documents, desired evaluation) and of native files.

reads.note: One decoded settings document and lockfile per scope and one desired evaluation per phase.
Equivalent physical reads coalesce within an observation phase; byte buffers and directory results are independently owned.
A mutation through the observation port invalidates the phase before writing, so the lint instruction symlink probe retires the lint phase; expired ports read live.
Pack document reads share decoding within the active phase.
Install selection and planning capture separate phases around the selection prompt; planning's phase is observed after the prompt.
An explicit agent selection on the root install and on every typed install (and on skills handoff) is checked against configured agents read live before preparation's phase.
Subagent rendering loads the canonical package and reads the settings and lockfile live after the inspection phase closes.
MCP adoption discovery and import preparation run in two consecutive read phases.
Agent membership preparation and step planning read documents outside a shared phase.
View reads the configured agents from the project settings live, outside any read phase, for every document it shows, although only a Hook document's context uses them.
Check's selected-subject lint builds its own lint read model, so the settings and lockfile are read and decoded again inside check's read phase.
An install step's write-free preflight reads the settings, lockfile, Pack documents and desired evaluation through one document-only view that closes before its transaction.
A materialize step collection call evaluates the current desired state once for its prior comparisons.
A detection pass probes each marker that more than one agent declares once.
An agent-settings scan checks each distinct settings path once.
A read model parses the settings text once as plain JSON for the lint rules that need the loose value.
Pre-setup coding-agent detection decides whether a first install or Skills handoff refuses before setup detects the agents again.
The strict settings decode parses the axm.json text separately from the read model's loose parse.

workspace-read-views.existingSharing: Readers inside one read phase share document decoding, desired evaluation, Pack documents and physical observations, and shared decoded documents are frozen; inspection, listing and publish preparation already read inside such phases. This change also shares one desired evaluation across a materialize step collection call, one document-only view across an install step's write-free preflight, one existence probe per shared detection marker within a detection pass and per settings path within an agent-settings scan, and one loose parse of the settings text per read model.
workspace-read-views.preparedInputs: More callers run inside one existing phase: each enabled authored native preflight run, knowledge lint's installed-bundle selection, visibility intent derivation, the lint run (which decides against the phase's settings and lockfile cells instead of a second read model), instruction status, agent listing and instruction preparation, and skills handoff without an agent selection (configured agents are read only inside preparation). The execution review of a plan that exposes a Hook or MCP ref reads the workspace documents through one document-only read phase shared by all of its reader calls and native observations. An active observation phase also holds the outcome of each complete Knowledge package inspection made through its own observation port, by exact package root, for the Knowledge manager's discovery selection and the inventory document, and its records offer the inventory document the Knowledge manifest parses of the read model the phase built. Under the transition lock, an install step's write-free preflight (its prior desired graph, source-authority check, satisfied-install check and prior output authority) takes the settings, lockfile, Pack documents and desired evaluation from one document-only read view, which the satisfied-install check's nested view joins. One materialize step collection call evaluates the committed workspace's current no-option desired state at most once, at its first prior comparison, for its prior MCP graph, prior Hook graph and prior agent output authority; agents add materialization planning makes that evaluation itself and hands it to the call as both the planned desired state and the prior state. Within one detectAgentScopeResults pass, each dir or file marker that more than one agent declares is resolved and checked for existence once through a pass-local cached probe whose outcome every declaring agent evaluates with its own markers, signals and corroboration; agent listing, detected-agent membership, setup's agent selection, first install's observation and the read model's agent presence probe each run such a pass. One agent-settings scan, the read model's cached agent-settings scanner cell, checks each distinct settings path once, and each descriptor settles that outcome in registry order into its own occurrence and scanner-io diagnostic. Each workspace read model holds one lazy cached cell, derived from its raw settings cell, that parses the axm.json text as plain JSON for the unrecognized-key, MCP transport-exclusivity and MCP secret-literal lint rules, while the strict settings decode keeps its own parse.
freshChecks: A write through the documents adapter or the observation port ends the phase; readers after it read live.
A live-observation section closes the enclosing phase.
A phase that has ended is never reused; a new phase retries completed local failures.
Readers under the transition lock outside a phase read and decode per call.
Membership checks for an explicit agent selection read configured agents live before the preparation phase.
Check lints its selected subjects through their own read model rather than the lint run's observation cells.
The execution review's before-review and seal fingerprints run outside its document-only phase, and its package tree hashes, canonical-path existence checks and fetches use live ports.

After an install step's preflight view closes, isInstalled, the transaction's readers and writers and validation read afresh, and inside that view the satisfied-install check's canonical hashing and manifest reads stay live.
Each later detection pass checks every marker again, a project marker is shared only when probed in the pass's own project directory, and single-agent detection checks its markers directly.

When an interactive, non-preview install or Skills handoff runs setup in a scope without settings, setup detects coding agents again with its own live scan after the pre-setup detection has decided whether the command refuses.
A later agent-settings scan checks every settings path again, and every new read model parses the settings text afresh.
workspace-read-views.lifetime: An observation lives for its read phase and is released when the phase ends; the phase's Knowledge package inspections and built read model are cleared with it. The execution review's document-only phase is captured after the review's no-demand check and closed on every exit of the review. An install step's document-only preflight view is opened in that step's own run and closed before its transaction. A step collection call's cached desired evaluation lives only for that call, and the evaluation agents add materialization planning hands in lives only for that planning. A detection pass's shared marker probes live for that one pass, and an agent-settings scan's path outcomes live only for that scan. The read model's loose settings parse lives and is released with its read model.

adoption-discovery-import-preparation-ru.basis: Adoption discovery and import preparation run back to back in two read phases, so the project settings are read and decoded twice.
adoption-discovery-import-preparation-ru.openQuestion: May the adoption discovery and the import preparation of 'mcps import' share one planning read view, accepting that a settings change between them is then reported at apply under the lock instead of during preparation?

after-rule-knowledge-install-resolves-de.basis: After a Rule or Knowledge install resolves, deciding whether its extensions wait on instruction files that are not set up reads and decodes the project settings live, outside any read phase, after the planning read phase already decoded them. The planning phase has ended, and on apply the confirmation, the transition lock and the install's own settings write lie between the two reads, so the expired reader observes live settings and sees an instruction setup made meanwhile.

agent-selection-handler-s-membership-che.basis: With an agent selection, the handler's membership check reads configured agents live before the handoff preparation's own read phase reads them again.
agent-selection-handler-s-membership-che.openQuestion: May the 'skills handoff --agent' membership check read configured agents from the handoff preparation's read phase instead of a separate live read just before it?

check-opens-one-read-phase-inspection.basis: Check opens one read phase that its inspection and its convergence owner reuse instead of capturing their own.

check-s-selected-subject-lint-builds.basis: Check's selected-subject lint builds its own lint read model, so the settings and lockfile are read and decoded again inside check's read phase as identity revalidation of what the assessment observed.

command-s-read-phase-reads-decodes.basis: A command's read phase reads and decodes the settings documents again after the workspace location's construction read and decoded them, and the selected lockfile again when construction read it for an initialized workspace. Construction is its own owner call whose loaders are released when it returns, before the command runs, so the command's phase is a later reader that observes the documents live instead of adopting decodes from an ended call.

each-enabled-authored-native-preflight-r.basis: Each enabled authored native preflight run takes its settings, lockfile and desired evaluation from one document-only read phase, at preparation and again under the lock.

inspection-captures-one-read-phase-every.basis: The inspection captures one read phase and every nested reader reuses it.

install-agent-selection-reads-configured.basis: An install with an agent selection reads configured agents live for the membership usage check before any source access, prompt or planning phase.

install-selection-planning-capture-separ.basis: Install selection and planning capture separate read phases around the interactive selection prompt; planning's phase is the freshness anchor observed after the prompt.

instruction-status-configured-agent-list.basis: Instruction status, the configured-agent listing and instruction planning each run in one documents-only read phase, so their settings and lockfile queries reuse one decode of each document.

instruction-symlink-support-probe-writes.basis: The instruction symlink-support probe writes through the observation port and retires the lint observation phase, so later lint reads of the settings and lockfile are live.
instruction-symlink-support-probe-writes.openQuestion: May a scratch probe whose entry is removed before the phase continues run on live ports without retiring the lint observation phase?

inventory-any-update-lifecycle-assessmen.basis: The inventory and any update or lifecycle assessment read every document through one inspection read phase.

knowledge-lint-selects-installed-bundles.basis: Knowledge lint selects installed bundles inside one document read phase, so the lockfile and settings are read and decoded once for the selection.

lint-run-decides-against-observation-pha.basis: The lint run decides against the observation phase's settings and lockfile cells instead of building a second read model that re-reads and re-decodes both documents.

lint-run-reads-through-one-observation.basis: A lint run reads through one observation phase whose port shares each physical observation (file reads, stats, existence checks, directory listings, link reads and real paths) until the phase ends, so the ownership-issue and agent-output inventories of the same workspace, the official AXM skill assessment and, while the phase lasts, the projection contributor observations reuse the reads the run already made.

listing-reads-every-document-through-one.basis: The listing reads every document through one inspection read phase that nested readers reuse.

membership-preparation-step-planning-rea.basis: Membership preparation and step planning read the settings and lockfile outside a shared read phase, so each planning step reads and decodes them again.
membership-preparation-step-planning-rea.openQuestion: May agents add and remove plan their membership steps from one read phase, so that an extension installed concurrently during planning is refused by the under-lock postcondition check with rollback rather than included in the planned steps?

out-phase-readers-under-lock-decode.basis: Out-of-phase readers under the lock decode the settings and lockfile once per reader call, because decoding is shared only within one read phase.
out-phase-readers-under-lock-decode.openQuestion: May a transaction-scoped decode memo keyed by exact bytes serve out-of-phase readers under the lock while every physical read stays live?

preparation-reads-pack-manifest-text-sta.basis: Preparation reads the pack manifest text for the stale-plan comparison although the phase's pack-document observation already read it, because that observation keeps only the decoded manifest.
preparation-reads-pack-manifest-text-sta.openQuestion: Should the phase pack-document observation retain the raw manifest text so that pack membership preparation can bind its stale-plan comparison to it instead of reading the manifest again?

preparation-runs-one-documents-only-read.basis: Preparation runs in one documents-only read view, so every type's catalog comes from one settings snapshot.

preparation-s-live-checks-retire-read.basis: Preparation's live checks retire its read phase, so sealing the candidate captures and decodes the documents in a new phase.

prepare-runs-one-read-phase-whose.basis: The prepare runs in one read phase whose readers share one observation of each document.

prepare-runs-one-read-phase-whose-2.basis: The prepare runs in one read phase whose readers share one observation of each document.

publish-prepares-candidates-one-read-pha.basis: Publish prepares its candidates in one read phase and its execution candidate in another that opens after the first has ended, so the candidate's lockfile reconciliation check reads and decodes the lockfile again after the canonical observations of the preparation phase decoded it, with no write between them. An ended phase is never reused, and moving candidate preparation into the preparation phase would let an interruption or failure there end preparation instead of being settled into an Interrupted or failed publish outcome, which the accepted requirements do not decide.
publish-prepares-candidates-one-read-pha.openQuestion: May publish prepare its execution candidate inside PublishExtensions.prepare's document read phase, given that an interruption or failure during candidate preparation would then end preparation instead of being settled by previewOrApply into an Interrupted or failed publish outcome?

render-canonical-subagent-package-loaded.basis: With --render, the canonical subagent package is loaded and the settings and lockfile are read live after the local inspection's read phase has closed, so one query takes two captures.
render-canonical-subagent-package-loaded.openQuestion: May 'subagents show --render' take its local inspection and its canonical subagent package load from one local-inspection read view, so a concurrent edit during the query yields one snapshot instead of two?

resolving-bare-name-type-reads-default.basis: Resolving a bare name with --type reads the default Registry, the Registry sources and the desired graph inside one inspection read view.

route-prepares-one-read-phase-whose.basis: The route prepares in one read phase whose readers already share one observation of each document.

skills-handoff-without-agent-selection-r.basis: Skills handoff without an agent selection reads configured agents only inside the handoff preparation's read phase, not again in the command handler.

sync-planning-already-captured-one-obser.basis: Sync planning already captured one observation view that its readers share, and validated it once more without caching.

update-demote-unpack-activation-each-pre.basis: Update, demote, unpack and activation each prepare inside one read view and seal one execution candidate, so their planning reads share one decode of each document.

validation-apply-under-transition-lock-r.basis: Validation and apply under the transition lock run outside any read phase, apart from the write-free preflights of install and authored steps, each of which reads through one document-only view that closes before its transaction. Every other reader call under the lock reads the settings and lockfile again because a write may intervene.
validation-apply-under-transition-lock-r.openQuestion: Should settlement expose a write-completion signal so that reader calls under the transition lock can share one document capture per write-free interval?

view-reads-configured-agents-from-projec.basis: View reads the configured agents from the project settings live, outside any read phase, after the workspace layer and the Registry selection have each read those settings. The workspace location's construction and the Registry selection are owner calls that have returned and released their decodes, so the handler's read is a later reader that observes live state rather than a reuse of an ended observation.

view-reads-configured-agents-for-every-d.basis: View reads the configured agents for every document before the operation starts, although only a Hook document's context uses them. Reading them only for a Hook would let a non-Hook view succeed over unreadable settings and move a Hook view's settings failure into the 'index' progress unit after the Registry fetches, a change of failure and progress outcome the accepted requirements do not decide.
view-reads-configured-agents-for-every-d.openQuestion: May view read the configured agents only after the Registry index identifies a Hook document with no field selected, given that a settings read failure would then no longer fail a non-Hook view and would surface for a Hook inside the 'index' progress unit after the Registry fetches instead of before the operation starts?

when-instruction-observation-probes-symb.basis: When an instruction observation probes symbolic-link capability during a local inspection, the probe writes its temporary directory, file and link in the workspace root through the inspection's observation port and so ends the inspection's read phase, after which every later settings, lockfile, desired-graph and inventory-row read of that inspection reads and decodes the workspace documents again. The probe is a write to the observed state, mutation invalidates observations before writing, and expired ports read live, so the phase cannot keep serving its cached observations past the probe.

when-migration-installs-replacement-live.basis: When a migration installs a replacement, the live checks that end the replacement's install preparation retire the migration's read phase, so preparing the removal of the deprecated extension captures and decodes the settings and lockfile again in a new phase, before the migration's own seal captures them once more. Sharing one phase would require preparing both children before the install child's live checks, which lets an uninstall-preparation refusal take precedence over an install-child live-check failure and has the removal observe documents captured before that independent verification; the accepted requirements do not decide that change.
when-migration-installs-replacement-live.openQuestion: May migrate prepare the replacement's install child and the uninstall child in one read phase and run the install child's live checks (before-review fingerprint, execution review, child-material observation and child seal) only after both are prepared, given that an uninstall-preparation refusal would then take precedence over an install-child live-check failure?

when-plan-exposes-hook-mcp-ref.basis: When a plan exposes a Hook or MCP ref, the execution review reads and decodes the settings and lockfile again after the planning read phase decoded them, because the review runs in its own live-observation section, which retires the planning phase. A fresh verification never reactivates its parent and an expired reader observes live state, so the review stays an independent observation bracketed by live fingerprints.

execution-review-reads-documents-through.basis: The execution review of a plan that exposes a Hook or MCP ref captures one document-only read phase after its no-demand check, so its desired-graph, accepted-entry, accepted-path and settings-entry reads and its native observations decode the settings and lockfile once and evaluate the desired state once. The phase belongs to the review and closes on every exit; the before-review and seal fingerprints stay live outside it, and package tree hashes, canonical-path existence checks and fetches keep using live ports.

install-step-preflight-shares-one-docume.basis: Under the transition lock, an install step's write-free preflight (its prior desired graph, source-authority check, satisfied-install check and prior output authority) takes the settings, lockfile, Pack documents and desired evaluation from one document-only read view, opened in that step's own run and closed before its transaction. The satisfied-install check's nested view joins it while its canonical hashing and manifest reads stay live, and isInstalled, the transaction's readers and writers and validation read afresh after the view has closed.

step-collection-evaluates-current-desire.basis: One materialize step collection call evaluates the committed workspace's current no-option desired state at most once, lazily at its first prior comparison, and uses that frozen evaluation for the prior MCP graph, the prior Hook graph and the prior agent output authority, and it reads the configured agents once for the prior membership. Agents add materialization planning makes that evaluation itself and hands it to the call as both the planned desired state and the prior state, and a handed-in evaluation never accompanies a proposal, settings or a recovery graph. The evaluation lives only for that call, and the membership closure still applies the steps under the transition lock with its own checks.

first-use-detects-agents-before-setup-de.basis: When an interactive, non-preview install or Skills handoff runs setup in a scope without settings, the CLI detects coding agents before setup and discards the result, and setup detects them again for the same root when it selects its agents. The first detection decides whether the command refuses with 'Could not detect coding agents' before the install's selection, prompts and setup output, while setup's detection is its own live scan after that selection and inside the setup transaction.
first-use-detects-agents-before-setup-de.openQuestion: May an interactive, non-preview first install or Skills handoff that runs setup skip its pre-setup coding-agent detection, so that a detection failure no longer refuses before the install's selection with 'Could not detect coding agents' but surfaces later from setup as 'Failed to detect agents', after the setup title note and behind interaction-configuration failures?

detection-pass-probes-each-shared-marker.basis: Within one detectAgentScopeResults pass, each dir or file marker that more than one agent declares, keyed by scope and declared path, is resolved and checked for existence once through a pass-local cached probe, and every declaring agent evaluates its own markers, signals and corroboration from that outcome and maps a failure with its own name. The shared probes live for that one pass and a project marker is shared only when probed in the pass's own project directory, so each later pass, whether agent listing, detected-agent membership, setup's agent selection, first install's observation or the read model's agent presence probe, checks every marker again, and single-agent detection checks its markers directly.

agent-settings-scan-probes-each-settings.basis: One agent-settings scan, the read model's cached agent-settings scanner cell, resolves each descriptor's settings path and checks each distinct path once, so agents that share a root directory share one existence check of its settings.json. Each descriptor then settles that outcome in registry order into its own occurrence and its own scanner-io diagnostic; the outcomes live only for that scan, and a later scan checks every path again.

read-model-parses-settings-text-once-loo.basis: Each workspace read model holds one lazy cached cell, derived from its own cached raw settings cell, that parses the axm.json text as plain JSON and deep-freezes the value, so the unrecognized-key, MCP transport-exclusivity and MCP secret-literal rules of one lint evaluation share one loose parse instead of each parsing the text. The cell lives and is released with its read model; an absent file or text that is not JSON gives no value, the raw read error is kept, and each rule keeps its own object check. The strict settings decode keeps its own parse, and every new read model parses afresh.

strict-settings-decode-keeps-separate-te.basis: Within one workspace read model the axm.json text is parsed by the strict settings decode and again by the shared loose parse. The strict decode refuses unknown properties and withholds the input of a parse failure, while the unrecognized-key and MCP settings rules need the plain parsed value with its top-level keys and retired flat fields, so neither value can serve the other.
strict-settings-decode-keeps-separate-te.openQuestion: Should the strict settings decode take the read model's shared loose parse as its input so that one read model parses the axm.json text once?

reads.note: Settings, lockfile and desired graph from the reader services, shared with the executing phase; without a captured read view, one desired-state evaluation supplies the graph and the accepted resolutions.
Install-root inventory for the expected canonical paths.
Without a captured read view, the scoped read model reads the selected scope's axm.json and axm.lock through its own state loaders, apart from the desired-state evaluation's reads of them.
The human empty-list message probes axm.json presence live after the inventory's read phase has ended.

workspace-records.existingSharing: Within a read view, each type's record rows were already projected once and shared. A records call made without a captured read view now serves its expected canonical paths and its install-root inventory from a frozen copy of the accepted resolutions its desired-state evaluation read, instead of reading the lockfile again for each. An install-root inventory no longer probes the root's existence before listing it; nothing is shared there.
workspace-records.preparedInputs: A records call made without a captured read view freezes the accepted resolutions its desired-state evaluation read, and its expected canonical paths and its install-root inventory consume them. Within a read view, records calls accept the view's cached install-root inventory, and each type's record rows are projected once into a cached cell that every later records call of that view consumes while the view is active.
freshChecks: Outside a read view, each records call derives its rows from the documents its readers observe.

In a records call made without a captured read view, the scoped read model reads the selected scope's axm.json and axm.lock through its own state loaders after the desired-state evaluation of the same call read them.
Each install-root inventory lists the acquired root directly, and under the transition lock that listing is the live observation of the install root.
The list empty-state message decides from a live presence probe, not from the inventory's phase.
Under the transition lock, an install step projects its type's inventory rows again outside any read phase to classify its change as created or updated.
workspace-records.lifetime: Row projections live for the read view that cached them; no value is transferred between owners. The frozen accepted resolutions are created by one records call made without a captured read view and are released when that call returns. The install-root inventory a read view captures lives for that view.

hook-uninstall-decides-whether-target-in.basis: Hook uninstall decides whether its target is installed from the hook inventory rows its preparation projects in the read phase, and under the transition lock, outside any read phase, projects those rows again before withdrawing the target. Preparation's read phase has ended before the lock, and the locked projection is the fresh route check that chooses between withdrawing the target, withdrawing a configured target that has no installed package and reporting it absent, so a package installed or removed after preparation is withdrawn and reported on its state at the lock.

human-empty-list-message-probes-axm.basis: The human empty-list message probes axm.json presence live after the inventory's read phase has already loaded the selected scope's settings.
human-empty-list-message-probes-axm.openQuestion: May the list empty-state message (no workspace versus nothing installed) follow the presence of axm.json observed by the inventory's read phase instead of a live probe made after that phase ends?

rule-uninstall-decides-whether-target-in.basis: Rule uninstall decides whether its target is installed from the rule inventory rows its preparation projects in the read phase, and under the transition lock, outside any read phase, projects those rows again before retiring the target. Preparation's read phase has ended before the lock, and the locked projection is the fresh route check that chooses between withdrawing the target, withdrawing a configured target that has no installed package and reporting it absent, so a package installed or removed after preparation is retired and reported on its state at the lock.

skill-uninstall-expands-selector-against.basis: Skill uninstall expands its selector against the skill rows its preparation projects in the read phase, and under the transition lock, outside any read phase, the uninstall step projects the skill inventory again to decide whether its target is still installed before withdrawing it. Preparation's read phase has ended before the lock, and the locked projection is the fresh route check that chooses between withdrawing the target, withdrawing a configured target that has no installed package and reporting it absent, so a skill installed or removed after preparation is withdrawn and reported on its state at the lock.

subagent-uninstall-matches-selector-agai.basis: Subagent uninstall matches its selector against the Subagent inventory rows its preparation projects in the read phase, and under the transition lock, outside any read phase, its step projects those rows again to decide whether the target is installed before withdrawing it. Preparation's read phase has ended before the lock, and the locked projection is the fresh route check that chooses between withdrawing the target, withdrawing a configured target that has no installed package and reporting it absent, so a Subagent installed or removed after preparation is withdrawn and reported on its state at the lock.

sync-projects-each-touched-type-s.basis: Sync projects each touched type's inventory rows while planning, again in its pre-acquisition observation check and, on apply, once more under the transition lock, and compares each projection with the planning one.

under-transition-lock-install-step-proje.basis: Under the transition lock, an install step projects its extension type inventory rows again outside any read phase to decide whether its target was installed before the write, after install planning already projected those rows in its read phase. The planning read phase has ended, and preview, confirmation, the lock acquisition and, after the candidate freshness check has run, the commits of earlier units in the same closure lie between the two projections, so the projection under the lock observes live state and classifies the change as created or updated from the state at the lock.

out-of-phase-records-call-reads-lockfile.basis: A records call made without a captured read view evaluates desired state once and serves its expected canonical paths and its install-root inventory from a frozen copy of the accepted resolutions that evaluation read, instead of reading the lockfile again for each; the copy lives for that one records call. A call with a captured view keeps its phase-bounded lockfile reader, and every records call still reads its documents live once.

records-read-model-keeps-own-settings-lo.basis: The scoped read model of a records call made without a captured read view still reads the selected scope's axm.json and axm.lock through its own state loaders after the desired-state evaluation of the same call read them. Inside an accepted-resolution batch the evaluation observes the pending resolutions while the read model observes the persisted lockfile, and the two apply different absence and initial-settings mappings.
records-read-model-keeps-own-settings-lo.openQuestion: May an out-of-phase WorkspaceRecords call own one set of state loaders for the selected scope's axm.json and axm.lock that serves both its desired-state evaluation and its scoped read model, given that inside an accepted-resolution batch the evaluation observes the pending closure while the read model observes the persisted lockfile, and the two apply different absence and initial-settings mappings?

install-root-inventory-lists-root-withou.basis: An install-root inventory lists the acquired root directly, and the listing's existing fallback turns an absent or unreadable root into no entries, so no existence probe precedes it. Nothing is shared, and the listing made under the transition lock remains the live observation of the install root.
